name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; prior versions carry 10.60775/fairhub.1 and 10.60775/fairhub.2 A resolvable, version-specific DOI, reused consistently as the record id and as the stem of every file_collection identifier (e.g. doi:10.60775/fairhub.3#retinal_oct), so sub-resources are addressable too. Matches 10.XXXXX/... ; prefix 10.60775 is FAIRhub's registered prefix and is consistent with publisher https://fairhub.io/ and with the citation. No RRID is present, which is expected for a dataset rather than a resource registry entry.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description (~1,700 chars) naming three collection sites, 2280 participants, 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01, 356,343 files, 3.82 TB, twelve modalities, the recruitment balancing design and the removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications from the public release Far beyond the 200-character threshold and specific throughout: counts, dates, sites, modalities, data kinds present and absent ('no unstructured text'), visit structure (2.5-4 hours plus 10 days at home) and scientific framing (salutogenesis). Description content matches the claimed dataset type at every point checked against file_collections, instances and collection_timeframes; the participant count and date window recur identically in three other blocks.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: [Diabetes mellitus, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Electrocardiography, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Retinal imaging, Eye exam] Seven keywords spanning condition, method family and three specific modalities; each is discoverable vocabulary rather than project jargon. Every keyword is corroborated by content elsewhere (ECG in cardiac_ecg, CGM in wearable_blood_glucose, retinal imaging in four collections). Coverage is thinner than the modality list — no keyword for OCT/OCTA, wearables, environmental sensing, OMOP or the AI-READI/Bridge2AI programme itself — but the threshold of five meaningful terms is comfortably met.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; file_collections: ten collections with path, collection_type, file_count, total_bytes and conforms_to, the root_metadata collection nesting nine resources each with id, name, format and file_type A live landing page plus a genuinely hierarchical resource tree: data-type collections with byte and file counts, and a named, typed inventory of the nine root metadata files. Directory structure described in conforms_to (data type / modality / device / participant) matches the collection paths and the device names given in collection_mechanisms.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: related_datasets: is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 (1067 participants, 2024-11-08), is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.1 (204 participants, 2024-05-03), has_part 'AI-READI mini-subset version of the dataset' Typed relationships with target identifiers and per-target notes giving release date and cohort size, so the version lineage is reconstructable from the record alone. Relationship types are used correctly and the source_caveats on the mini-subset explains why a containment rather than derivation relation was chosen and why no DOI is given — the one unidentified target is disclosed rather than fabricated.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: AI-READI Data License Agreement v2.0 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036) with storage limited to institutional servers or BAA-covered cloud, derivative and synthetic data bound by the same terms, NIH GDS security standards, automatic termination on breach; data_use_permission: disease_specific_research; ip_restrictions.restrictions: title and IP remain with the Licensor, models may be distributed if they do not contain the data, copyright '© 2026 AI-READI' An access policy stated at operational detail — what may be stored where, what survives termination, what a derived model may contain — not a licence label. data_use_permission: disease_specific_research is consistent with intended_uses (T2DM-only attestation) and with informed_consent.consent_scope; the licence archive DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17555036 is a well-formed Zenodo DOI.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; regulatory_restrictions: NIH GDS Policy security best practices, watermark-preservation obligation, export-control questions answered by reference to the licence; other_compliance: not FDA-regulated for drug or device, RO-Crate HL7:2N; data_governance.committee_contact: Aaron Lee, ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648, contact@aireadi.org All five evidence slots are populated, including the governance contact the source rubric asks for, with a named person, ORCID and address rather than a generic mailbox. The record explains the tension between the RO-Crate's 'normal' HL7 level and its own 'restricted' classification by reference to verified-ID gating — the classification is reasoned rather than asserted. Counted as a warning, not a failure, because the reasoning is stated.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; data_governance.access_review_process: 'logging in through a verified ID system, agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research, and agreeing to the license terms ... access type PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired ... conditions of access at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access'; external_resources: 'FAIRhub dataset access page'; third_party_sharing.is_direct distribution via FAIRhub under DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3 The dedicated download_url slot is empty, but the sub-element also admits platform access instructions, and these are complete and actionable: the platform, the exact gate (verified ID, attestation, licence assent), the access-conditions URL and the access-type code are all given. A reader can retrieve the data from this record. Flagged as a low-severity completeness issue: a machine client must parse prose to find the retrieval route. The access route is consistent with the restricted confidentiality level and with third_party_sharing.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats: DICOM/application/dicom, CSV/text/csv, JSON/application/json, Markdown/text/markdown, each with a description of which content uses it; file_collections.resources formats MD, JSON, TXT, TSV per metadata file Formats paired with correct IANA media types and mapped onto specific content (imaging to DICOM, OMOP tables to CSV, documentation to Markdown), plus per-file formats for the metadata inventory. Partial mismatch recorded as a warning: WFDB, Open mHealth and the ESDS ASCII environmental files appear in conforms_to and file_collections but have no distribution_formats entry, and no character encoding is stated anywhere. The populated entries are correct; the list is incomplete rather than wrong.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: related_datasets: three typed entries; external_resources: nine, including docs.aireadi.org, https://aireadi.org, the FAIRhub access page, https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, https://github.com/AI-READI, the licence at doi 10.5281/zenodo.17555036, Nature Metabolism doi 10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x, BMJ Open doi 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449 and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048 Both slots are rich, and the external resources carry descriptions and, for the documentation, its own reuse terms (CC-BY 4.0) rather than bare URLs. Both publication DOIs are well formed with plausible registrant prefixes (10.1038 Springer Nature, 10.1136 BMJ); NCT06002048 matches the NCT8-digit pattern; all URLs are structurally valid on plausible domains.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license_and_use_terms: 'non-exclusive, non-transferable license to download, reproduce and use the data and to create derivative works for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes'; intended_uses records the same permission with the T2DM-only attestation for the public version Reuse is affirmatively granted, including commercially and for derivative works, with the boundaries (secondary sharing, model-vendor transfer, storage location) spelled out — a reuser can determine what is permitted without reading the licence. Custom licence rather than a standard CC instrument, so reuse permissions cannot be inferred from a well-known label; the record compensates by restating the grant and the restrictions. The licence-name discrepancy between the FAIRhub API and dataset page is disclosed and adjudicated.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: conforms_to: WFDB for ECG, OMOP CDM for clinical, DICOM for FLIO/OCT/OCTA/photography, Open mHealth for wearables and CGM, NASA ESDS ASCII guidelines for environmental sensors, RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT with FAIRscape profile 0.1; distribution_formats with media types; per-collection conforms_to on all ten file_collections Every modality is mapped to a recognised community format, and the mapping is repeated at collection level so a reuser knows which standard governs which directory. Format choices are domain-appropriate throughout (WFDB for waveforms, DICOM for ophthalmic imaging, OMOP for clinical tables). Character encoding is never stated, which is the one gap against this sub-element's explicit mention of encoding; it is not sufficient to fail an otherwise exemplary standardisation record.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to (prose, naming CDS v0.1.1, WFDB, OMOP CDM, DICOM, Open mHealth, ESDS, RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT, FAIRscape 0.1); conforms_to_standard: [CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS, RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset Conformance is stated three ways — prose, an enumerated standard list, and the schema the datasheet itself conforms to — with versions given for CDS, RO-Crate and FAIRscape. Standard names and version strings are used correctly; the OMOP claim is corroborated by file_collections.clinical_data describing one-to-one CSV mappings to CDM tables and a dqd_omop.json for the Data Quality Dashboard.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: variables: 20 entries, each with variable_name, data_type and description, most with unit (mg/dL, logMAR, %, log contrast sensitivity) and measurement_technique naming the device or laboratory; MoCA total score carries maximum_value 30.0; best-corrected visual acuity carries quality_notes recording that Snellen variables were dropped in 3.0.0 Variable-level metadata is substantive and reuse-relevant: types, units, instruments and, in one case, a version-specific quality caveat. Enough for a reuser to interpret the headline measures of each modality. Recorded as a low-severity gap rather than a failure: no ontology or concept identifiers (LOINC, OMOP concept_id) are attached, variable_name is the only identifier, and source_caveats concedes the authoritative per-domain dictionary was not consulted, so 20 variables stand in for a much larger released schema.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: two categories with usage_notes and an example; prohibited_uses: six reasoned prohibitions (no clinical treatment decisions, no re-identification or contact, no transfer to third-party model vendors for training even under a BAA, no onward conveyance outside the licensee set, publication limited to five figures of representative samples, no watermark removal); other_tasks notes the absence of formal guidelines for user-defined tasks The strongest use-guidance block in the record: each prohibition states its reason, and the model-vendor and watermark clauses give reusers concrete operational rules that are rarely written down. Prohibitions are proportionate to and consistent with the stated re-identification risk and with participant_privacy; no discouraged_uses block, but intended and prohibited uses together answer the sub-element.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews[0]: University of Washington IRB, protocol STUDY00016228, initial approval 2022-12-20, annual renewal within 90 days of expiration, reliance agreements with UAB and UCSD IRBs, approval letter published with the 3.0.0 documentation, contact hsdrely@uw.edu; ethical_reviews[1]: AI-READI ethics team review by Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman and Nicholas Evans; human_subject_research.irb_approval and regulatory_compliance Oversight is documented at the level a replicator would need — protocol number, approval date, renewal cadence, reliance structure, named reviewers and a working contact — and extends beyond the IRB to a standing bioethics review of the release. Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by populated IRB evidence. No data_protection_impacts (DPIA) block exists; the alternative fields carry the sub-element, and the absence is logged as a low-severity gap. The RO-Crate's 'Washington University IRB' label contradicts the UW address and contact it gives; the record flags this rather than silently adopting it.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.method: HIPAA Safe Harbor; identifiable_elements_present: false; identifiers_removed: 'Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule; participant sex; race/ethnicity; medications used'; deidentification_details recording the FAIRhub 'NoDeIdentification' statement, the RO-Crate deidentified statement, the Safe Harbor stripping, and that review was internal rather than externally audited A named method with an explicit removed-identifier list and an honest statement of assurance level (internal review, no formal external audit) — the method field is backed by content, not a label. Method is appropriate to the data type: Safe Harbor plus removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications exceeds Safe Harbor's requirements and is coherent with the imaging and waveform content. The three-way source conflict over whether deidentification was performed at all is counted as a failed consistency check, mitigated by full disclosure.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy.anonymization_method (Safe Harbor removal; participants appear only under study IDs used as folder names); privacy_techniques (removal of sex, race/ethnicity, medications, 5-digit zip, genetic data, past health records, traffic reports; static watermarking; licence prohibitions on identification or contact; verified-ID gating; encrypted servers and locked storage during collection); reidentification_risk ('theoretical risk of future re-identification'); data_linkage (participant-ID linkage across modalities) All four privacy slots are populated, and the risk assessment is candid rather than reassuring: it names a residual risk and future_use_impacts explains the mechanism (AI inference of patient characteristics) and the countermeasures. Consistency check passes — a re-identification risk statement exists alongside the privacy block. data_linkage correctly discloses that per-participant folder structure enables cross-modality linkage, which is the main residual vector for a de-identified multimodal release.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true; consent_type: written, electronically via REDCap e-consent with electronic signature or in person; consent_documentation: signed forms, UW form published with the 3.0.0 documentation; consent_scope: FAIRhub 'ConsentSpecifiedNotElsewhereCategorised', public version limited to T2DM research; withdrawal_mechanism: withdrawal permitted at any time with already-shared data retained, communicated in the consent document; corroborated by collection_consents and consent_revocations Consent is documented end to end — procedure, modality, artifact, scope and the limits of withdrawal — and the consent form itself is published, which is the strongest available evidence for this sub-element. Consistency check passes: IRB approval and consent procedures are both present, as the element's rules require. consent_scope aligns with license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: disease_specific_research and with the T2DM-only access attestation — the consent, the licence and the access gate say the same thing.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: false with special_protections (minors excluded by the 40-year minimum; pregnancy and gestational diabetes excluded; IRB protocol records no recruitment of known prisoners and low likelihood of subjects becoming prisoners); participant_compensation: $200 stipend, transport and rideshare costs covered, paid after devices are returned, not prorated, transport above $25 possibly unreimbursed The false flag is substantiated by the eligibility criteria that produce it rather than asserted, and compensation is documented down to payment timing and the reimbursement ceiling — the level of detail that lets a reader judge undue inducement. at_risk_groups_included: false is consistent with human_subject_research.special_populations (adults 40-85, able to consent, English-speaking) and with the exclusion criteria repeated in preprocessing_strategies. The English-language requirement is separately and correctly surfaced as a selection bias in known_biases rather than hidden here.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations: four entries (self-reported race/ethnicity, biological sex, diabetes status group, age), each with subpopulation_elements_present, identification and distribution — 380 Hispanic, 545 Asian, 519 Black, 836 White; 951 male, 1329 female; 776 no diabetes, 560 lifestyle-controlled, 686 oral/non-insulin, 258 insulin-controlled; mean age 60.8 ± 11.3, eligibility 40-85 Cohort composition is quantified on four axes with inclusion criteria, and the flags honestly distinguish the two axes used for recruitment balancing but withheld at participant level from the two released. All four distributions sum to the stated 2280 instances. subpopulation_elements_present: false for race and sex is correct given those variables were removed from the public release, and is consistent with instances.missing_information and known_limitations.scope_limitation.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances.counts: 2280 with instance_type 'Individual study participant'; total_file_count: 356343; total_size_bytes: 3815969779678; per-collection file_count and total_bytes for all ten collections; splits: 1576 training, 352 validation, 352 test Counts at three granularities — participants, files per collection, and split membership — with sizes in bytes, so a reuser can plan storage and sampling before download. Split counts sum to 2280. The file-count and byte-count discrepancies against the per-directory sums are disclosed in source_caveats and reconcile once the nine root metadata files are added, which is a correctness check the record performed on itself.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: variables: 20 entries with type, unit, description and measurement technique; is_tabular: false; splits.split_details describing the 70/15/15 recommended split assigned per participant in participants.tsv, balanced for sex, race/ethnicity and diabetes status with per-split mean ages (61.1 / 60.3 / 60.5); subpopulations carrying subpopulation_elements_present flags All three components are present, and the split documentation explains the balancing rationale and that the split is new in 3.0.0 and intended to reduce modelling disparities — split provenance, not just split membership. Warning recorded: is_tabular: false coexists with a description stating the modalities 'encompass tabular data' and with OMOP CSV tables in clinical_data. Defensible for a multimodal release but contradictory read in isolation. Note also that the splits are balanced on variables (sex, race/ethnicity) that the public release does not expose, which the record states explicitly and which reusers must understand.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances.data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:43; instance_type: Individual study participant; instances.notes listing the per-participant modality span; description naming T2DM severity strata, diabetic nephropathy biomarkers, peripheral neuropathy testing, cognition, retinal structure and function, glycaemia, activity and home environment The condition under study and the phenotypic domains covered are both explicit, and the topic is bound to a controlled Bridge2AI topic identifier rather than free text alone. B2AI_TOPIC:43 follows a CURIE pattern consistent with the Bridge2AI topic vocabulary; the stated topics are corroborated by variables (HbA1c, urine albumin/creatinine, MoCA, visual acuity) and by the subpopulation strata.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: anomalies: six entries (survey skips, wearable charging gaps every 2-3 days, imaging noise and transfer failures, undilated handheld fundus variability, FLIO discomfort and 1 cm movement tolerance, manual-device modality skips); sampling_strategies with is_sample/is_random/is_representative flags, strategy, source_data and why_not_representative; missing_data_documentation with patterns, causes and handling_strategy Unusually concrete quality documentation: the anomalies are device- and protocol-specific and explain the mechanism of each defect, and missing data is separated into pattern, cause and handling. The three blocks agree with each other and with known_limitations.coverage_limitation; handling_strategy correctly states that filling was limited to values recoverable from the same record under site-PI approval and that no modality-level imputation was performed.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: '3.0.0'; issued: 2025-11-17T00:00:00Z; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3 Semantic version with a release date and a version-specific DOI, so the described artifact is unambiguous. Version string, DOI suffix (fairhub.3), citation year and the 2025-11-17 distribution date all agree.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access.versions_available: 1.0.0 (10.60775/fairhub.1, 2024-05-03, 204 participants), 2.0.0 (10.60775/fairhub.2, 2024-11-08, 1067), 3.0.0 (10.60775/fairhub.3, 2025-11-17, 2280); version_details: all versions listed on the FAIRhub dataset page with their own documentation sets at docs.aireadi.org, 2.0.0 marked no longer accessible Each version is given a DOI, a date, a cohort size and a documentation location, and the record states plainly that one earlier version is no longer retrievable rather than implying all are. Version DOIs match the related_datasets lineage exactly; the cohort sizes increase monotonically, consistent with the stated annual accrual model.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: version_access.version_details: 'version 3.0.0 adds the second and third years of data collection, adds imaging devices relative to the pilot, moves from custom/ad hoc to automated plus custom processing, and drops the Snellen visual acuity variables'; updates.update_details; file_collections root resource CHANGELOG.md described as recording changes from the previous version; variables[best-corrected visual acuity].quality_notes recording the Snellen removal at variable level Substantive change descriptions covering cohort, instrumentation, processing method and a breaking variable removal — and the variable-level note means a reuser upgrading from 2.0.0 would find the removal where they would look for it. No errata block exists; the sub-element's alternative field (updates) carries it, and the absence is logged as a low-severity gap. Change descriptions come from the dedicated update/version fields and the CHANGELOG resource, not from unrelated notes.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.frequency: 'Approximately annually'; updates.update_details: static versions never updated in place, new versions released with additional instances as participants complete visits, enrollment ongoing so future versions are expected to be larger; extension_mechanism: no external mechanism to extend the dataset; maintainers: AI-READI Consortium with contact routes States both the cadence and the update model (immutable versioned releases rather than in-place edits), which is the more consequential fact for anyone citing a version. The annual cadence is consistent with the observed release dates (2024-05, 2024-11, 2025-11) and with collection_timeframes' anticipated completion of 2027-01-01.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: raw_data_sources: (1) EHR at the three sites screened on ICD-10 R73.09 and E11.X, used for recruitment only and not released; (2) device-native exports (.xml ECG, .csv MoCA, .fda Topcon, .sdt FLIO, .FIT Garmin, .csv Dexcom and sensor) with access_details explaining that raw data are retained but unreleased because they are unmapped and may contain PHI in free text; related_datasets version lineage; updates.update_details Provenance runs from recruitment source through device-native capture to the standardised release, and the record explains why the raw tier is withheld and under what circumstance it might later appear in a controlled-access release. No was_derived_from field, but raw_data_sources plus the version lineage satisfy the sub-element's alternatives. The raw formats listed match the conversions described in preprocessing_strategies (.fda/.sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth) — the provenance chain is internally consistent even though the converting software is unnamed.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: four responses (enable AI/ML insight into T2DM including salutogenic pathways; publicly share a multimodal AI-ready dataset balanced for severity across three sites; build a classification-agnostic foundational dataset supporting a temporal atlas of T2DM development and reversal; provide a blueprint for future AI-ready data generation); addressing_gaps: three responses naming the absent evidence base, the AI-readiness gap and the demographic imbalance documented in a 2000-2020 meta-epidemiological review Motivation is stated as scientific rationale plus the specific gaps it answers, with the methodological purpose (a reusable blueprint) distinguished from the scientific one. Purposes align with the funding: the NIH award title 'Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project' matches the salutogenesis framing and the data-generation-blueprint purpose.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: pseudo-time manifold analysis to predict disease trajectories across severity strata from normal to insulin-dependent T2DM; development of AI/ML salutogenesis models and multimodal models across survey, clinical, imaging, waveform, wearable and environmental data; other_tasks: hypothesis-agnostic and unlabelled, so downstream users define their own tasks with no formal guidelines provided Named analytic methods rather than generic 'AI research', and an honest statement that the dataset carries no labels and no task guidance — which tells a modeller what work they must do themselves. Task statements are consistent with instances.label: false and with the recruitment design: a severity-stratified cross-sectional cohort is the right substrate for pseudo-time trajectory inference, which the known_limitations temporal_limitation correctly qualifies.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders: National Institutes of Health (NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program, OT2 other-transaction mechanism, award amount 5,026,499 for FY2022, project period 2022-09-01 to 2025-08-31), Research to Prevent Blindness, Microsoft AI for Good Lab (cloud services) Three funders with the mechanism, programme, amount and period for the principal award, and the nature of the in-kind support for the third. Funding logic passes: the grantor with grant funding carries structured grants, while Research to Prevent Blindness and Microsoft's donated cloud services are recorded as non-grant support with prose notes and correctly carry no grant number.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders[NIH].grants: OT2OD032644 (RePORTER project number 1OT2OD032644-01), P30DK035816, UL1TR003096; source_caveats explaining that tier-1 sources record only OT2OD032644 as the dataset funding reference while the publications add the other two Structured grant numbers with the primary award ordered first and a stated rule for why the publication-only awards were retained rather than dropped or promoted. All three match NIH activity-code patterns and their institute codes are plausible for the work: OT2 + OD (Common Fund, Office of the Director) for the Bridge2AI award, P30 + DK (NIDDK centre) for diabetes, UL1 + TR (NCATS CTSA) for translational infrastructure. The expanded form 1OT2OD032644-01 is a correct application-number rendering.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: AI-READI Consortium with principal_investigator Aaron Lee (ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648, contact@aireadi.org) and nine affiliations with ROR identifiers (WUSTL 01yc7t268, NIH 01cwqze88, CMII 0156zyn36, JHU 00za53h95, OHSU 009avj582, Stanford 00f54p054, UAB 008s83205, UCSD 0168r3w48, UW 00cvxb145); data_collectors with three roles and training/certification detail; maintainers; data_collectors notes crediting OT2OD032644 for personnel effort Creators, contributing institutions, collecting roles and maintainers are all identified, with persistent identifiers on the PI and every affiliation rather than bare names. ORCID and all nine ROR identifiers are well formed. The WUSTL-versus-UW attribution conflict is flagged as a content-accuracy issue: it is disclosed in creators.principal_investigator.source_caveats and dataset-level source_caveats, but leaves the affiliation of record unsupported by the IRB and award evidence.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: twenty entries naming instrument, protocol and setting — Philips PageWriter TC30 12-lead ECG with recorded chair position; OMRON HEM 907XL / Medline MDS4001 / Welch Allyn 6000 BP taken twice; 10 g monofilament at three sites per foot; MoCA Duo on iPad; M&S EVA visual acuity at 4 m photopic and mesopic with a 2.0 ND filter; MARS contrast sensitivity; Heidelberg Spectralis ONH-RC, PPole-H and macular OCTA; Topcon Triton 12x12 and 6x6 OCTA; Maestro2 widefield and 6x6; Zeiss Cirrus 512x512 and 200x200; Dexcom G6 for 10 days at 5-minute intervals with participants masked; Garmin Vivosmart 5 for 10 days at 5-second sampling; LeeLab Anura in-home for 10 days; CLIA-certified local CBC with other assays at the UW NORC The most detailed block in the record. Device make and model, scan geometry, illumination condition, wear duration, sampling frequency, masking and laboratory routing are all specified — a site could reproduce acquisition from this alone. Every device named here reappears in the corresponding file_collection and in variables.measurement_technique; collection_timeframes and the visit structure in the description agree with the 10-day at-home period repeated across three device mechanisms.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods: directly observed measurements (was_directly_observed: true) covering labs, vitals, physical, vision, cognitive, ECG, imaging, CGM, wearable and environmental capture; participant-reported REDCap questionnaires (was_reported_by_subjects: true, was_validated_verified: true) with verification by cross-referencing entered medications against medications brought in or photographed; raw_data_sources giving the device-native export formats; direct_collection.is_direct: true with the EHR-screening recruitment route Acquisition is split into observed and self-reported with the provenance flags set correctly, and the verification procedure for the self-reported tier is concrete rather than asserted. Flags are semantically correct: was_validated_verified: true is attached only to the self-reported entry, and is substantiated by the medication cross-referencing described in the same entry.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies: mapping to OMOP CDM for clinical data and DICOM for imaging, conversion of Topcon .fda and FLIO .sdt to DICOM and Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth before FAIRhub upload, with processing for this release described as automated plus custom in contrast to 1.0.0's ad hoc approach; a second entry stating no instances were excluded at preprocessing and that exclusions arise only from eligibility criteria; cleaning_strategies: REDCap min/max range flagging surfaced in coordinator and data-manager reports, checks for credibility, skip-pattern flow, fillable missing values and omitted or duplicated records, with edits only under site-PI approval; instances.label: false and label_description explaining that no labelling was performed for a hypothesis-agnostic dataset; missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy stating no modality-level imputation Preprocessing and cleaning are both documented as procedures with decision authority named, and the absence of labelling and imputation is explained rather than left blank — which is the right answer for an unlabelled dataset, not a gap. The conversions described match the raw formats in raw_data_sources and the standards in conforms_to. No annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools or imputation_protocols blocks exist, consistently with a record that states no annotation and no imputation occurred.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: No used_software is recorded on preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies or anywhere else, and no tool is named for the steps that produced the release: 'all data were mapped to standardized terminologies ... Topcon .fda and FLIO .sdt files converted to DICOM and Garmin .FIT files converted to the Open mHealth standard' names no converter, package or version. The software that is named sits outside the qualifying roles — REDCap and the MoCA Duo iPad application (collection_mechanisms) are capture instrumentation; FAIRhub hosted on Microsoft Azure (maintainers, data_governance) is hosting and serving; the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard (file_collections.clinical_data, via dqd_omop.json) is validation of the already-released data; https://github.com/AI-READI (external_resources) is an organisation root identifying the publisher, with no repository or tool named. A reader cannot tell what software produced or transformed the distributed DICOM, OMOP CSV and Open mHealth files. The transformation is asserted to have happened and is described at the level of input and output format, but the tooling that performed it is unstated, so neither the conversion nor the OMOP mapping is reproducible or auditable. Scored 0 under the #1059/#1082 threshold. Roles applying here: (a) capture and instrumentation — REDCap, MoCA Duo, device consoles; (b) hosting and serving — FAIRhub on Azure; (d) validation and quality assessment — OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard. The GitHub organisation root is a publisher pointer that neither earns nor forfeits the point. Naming the converters and the OMOP ETL with versions and repositories would satisfy the sub-element.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: nine entries including docs.aireadi.org (with its own CC-BY 4.0 terms and a statement that the dataset is self-contained but relies on the docs for provenance detail), the BMJ Open protocol doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449, the Nature Metabolism comment doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048, the Zenodo community and the archived licence; conforms_to naming seven standards with versions; missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy stating that fillable values were completed from the same record under site-PI approval and that no modality-level imputation was performed Standards, peer-reviewed protocol and outcome publications, a trial registration and a documentation site are all linked, and the imputation question is answered explicitly — that none was performed — rather than left to inference. Publication DOIs are well formed with correct publisher prefixes; the NCT identifier is valid. Imputation is documented through the dedicated missing-data field rather than an imputation_protocols block, which is an acceptable alternative representation for a record stating no imputation occurred.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: five typed entries — representativeness (urban, hospital-based, no Pacific Islanders or Native Americans) with scope_impact on generalizability; coverage (not all modalities for all participants); scope (public release excludes zip, sex, race, ethnicity, genetic data, past records, medications, traffic reports, and raw pre-standardization data); temporal (cross-sectional, one visit, only ~10% returning in year 4); methodological (multiple imaging devices per measure, so make, model and protocol differ across participants and must be modelled) Each limitation is typed, explained and, in the representativeness and methodological cases, accompanied by its consequence for downstream modelling — this is analysis, not a disclaimer. Limitations correspond to facts stated elsewhere: the device heterogeneity to the twenty collection mechanisms, the coverage gap to missing_data_documentation, the scope exclusion to instances.missing_information. No limitation is invented and none of the record's own known weaknesses is omitted, except that the unnamed processing software is not listed as a reproducibility limitation.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases: four entries typed selection_bias (volunteer bias), representation_bias (pilot imbalance, ongoing enrollment, no Pacific Islanders or Native Americans) with mitigation_strategy, sampling_bias (urban hospital-based recruitment) with mitigation_strategy, and selection_bias (English-language requirement impeding Hispanic and Asian recruitment); future_use_impacts describing anticipated downstream social impact Categorised with BiasTypeEnum-aligned types, and three of the four pair the finding with a concrete mitigation — triple-balanced recruitment with under- and oversampling, three geographically distinct sites, uniform protocols, and balanced recommended splits. Bias types are applied correctly to their descriptions (volunteer self-selection as selection bias, missing racial groups as representation bias, recruitment frame as sampling bias). The English-language bias is disclosed here rather than being buried in eligibility criteria, which is the RAI-appropriate placement.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: anomalies: six entries covering survey skips and incomplete responses; wearable improper use, battery failure and the Garmin's 2-3 day recharge gaps; imaging patient uncooperation, obscuring noise, system malfunction and transfer failures; Optomed Aurora undilated handheld variability within and between patients; FLIO's longer acquisition, uncomfortable light levels, last-in-visit placement and sub-centimetre movement tolerance; manual-device operation leading to skipped modalities Device-level and mechanism-level rather than generic: each anomaly explains why the defect arises, which is what a reuser needs to decide whether to filter or model it. The anomaly set is consistent with missing_data_documentation.missing_data_causes, which restates the same mechanisms, and with the methodological limitation about device heterogeneity.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present: false with sensitivity_details (no PHI; sex, race/ethnicity and medications removed); content_warnings.content_warnings_present: false with notes recording the healthsheet's 'No' to offensive, threatening or psychologically risky content; confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present: false with details Explicit negative determinations with reasons attached, which is meaningful documentation rather than an empty field — a reader learns both the answer and the basis for it. Recorded as a failed consistency check at the element-crossing level: these three false flags sit against confidentiality_level: restricted, HIPAA-compliant handling, watermarking, verified-ID gating and an acknowledged theoretical re-identification risk. The flags answer the healthsheet's narrow questions accurately, but a reader taking them at face value would misjudge how governed the release is. Scored 1 because the sub-element is documented with reasons; the tension is reported as an issue.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews: the UW IRB approval record and a named AI-READI ethics team review (Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman, Nicholas Evans) with ELSI considered at every stage under bioethicist guidance; future_use_impacts: no unfair-treatment uses currently anticipated but a theoretical future re-identification risk, with AI inference of patient characteristics identified as the mechanism and a dissemination system, strict licence and watermarking as the mitigations for both public and controlled sets Both halves of the sub-element are answered: institutional review and a forward-looking social impact analysis that names a risk mechanism and the specific controls addressing it. The impact analysis is coherent with participant_privacy.reidentification_risk and with the licence prohibitions on re-identification and model-vendor transfer — the ethical reasoning and the legal controls point the same way. No conflicts of interest are declared either way.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: publisher: https://fairhub.io/; third_party_sharing: distributed for public use through the FAIRhub platform under DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3; maintainers: hosted on FAIRhub through Microsoft Azure A recognised domain repository for Bridge2AI data generation projects, identified by URL and corroborated by the DOI prefix, the access route and the hosting arrangement. Publisher, DOI prefix 10.60775 and landing page domain all agree; the status field confirms 'published'.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: citation: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3'; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; external_resources additionally give two citable publications with DOIs A complete, version-pinned DataCite-style citation with creator, year, title, version, resource type, publisher and resolvable DOI — nothing a citing author would need to reconstruct. Citation year 2025 matches issued 2025-11-17; the version in the citation matches version: '3.0.0'; the DOI in the citation matches the doi field.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to naming CDS v0.1.1, WFDB, OMOP CDM, DICOM, Open mHealth, NASA ESDS ASCII guidelines, RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT and FAIRscape profile 0.1 with one subcrate per data type; conforms_to_standard enumerating all seven; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; per-collection conforms_to Conformance to seven community standards, stated with versions and bound to specific content, plus RO-Crate packaging that makes the release machine-actionable to external tooling. Standard identifiers and version strings are used correctly and are internally consistent between the prose, the enumeration and the ten per-collection declarations.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: external_resources: docs.aireadi.org covering citation, access and training prerequisites, per-domain documentation, the Healthsheet, controlled variables and AI-readiness; https://aireadi.org with team and contact pages; the FAIRhub access page; the Zenodo community; the GitHub organisation; two publications; the ClinicalTrials.gov record; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; maintainers giving contact routes at aireadi.org/contact and docs.aireadi.org/docs/3/contact A full documentation and outreach surface — versioned documentation site, project site, community archives, publications and named contact routes — with the documentation's own CC-BY 4.0 licence stated. The documentation URL is version-aware (docs/3/), consistent with the record's statement that each version has its own documentation set. All URLs are structurally valid on plausible domains.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: related_datasets: is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2; is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.1; has_part 'AI-READI mini-subset version of the dataset' with a source_caveat explaining that no identifier is published and that a containment relation was chosen because the sources state a FAIRhub parent/child entry without a derivation direction Typed relationships with resolvable targets for the two versions and an explicit, reasoned account of why the third target is named descriptively — the relationship type is justified rather than guessed. Relationship types are used in their correct sense and agree with version_access.versions_available; the record declines to assert a derivation direction it cannot support, which is the correct handling of an underdetermined relation.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3 A single persistent identifier is used consistently as the dataset id, the doi slot, the citation target and the latest-version pointer, and prior versions carry their own DOIs (10.60775/fairhub.1, .2). Matches 10.XXXX/... . Prefix 10.60775 is the FAIRhub DataCite prefix, which is plausible and corroborated by publisher https://fairhub.io/ and by the FAIRhub citation. No RRID is claimed, so no RRID pattern check applies.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description of roughly 1,500 characters covering cohort size (2,280 adults aged 40+), three sites, collection window, every modality and format, the balanced-recruitment design and the public/controlled split. Far beyond the 200-character threshold and specific throughout: it names the sites, the version, the date range, the standards per modality and the salutogenesis goal, and it states what the public version withholds. The description is semantically appropriate to a multimodal observational clinical dataset and its claims are corroborated elsewhere in the record (counts by instances, formats by distribution_formats, sites by collection_mechanisms and sampling_strategies).

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: [Diabetes mellitus, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Electrocardiography, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Retinal imaging, Eye exam] Seven keywords spanning the disease domain, the AI/ML purpose and three of the principal acquisition modalities; meets the five-keyword expectation. Every keyword is substantiated by dataset content: ECG by cardiac_ecg, CGM by wearable_blood_glucose, retinal imaging by four retinal directories. No keyword stuffing or unsupported terms.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; file_collections gives ten collections with ids, paths, file_count, total_bytes and per-standard conformance, and the root collection enumerates nine resources with format, media_type and file_type. Both halves of the sub-element are satisfied: an accessible platform landing page and a genuinely hierarchical resource structure (datatype directory, then modality, then device, then participant) with per-collection counts and sizes. The landing page domain matches the declared publisher and the DOI prefix registrant; the resource hierarchy matches the CDS v0.1.1 layout described in conforms_to.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: related_datasets: three entries with relationship_type is_new_version_of (doi:10.60775/fairhub.2), is_new_version_of (doi:10.60775/fairhub.1) and is_source_of (AI-READI mini subset for pipeline development); was_derived_from names the AI-READI observational study. Typed relationships with resolvable DOI targets for the two predecessor versions, plus notes explaining what changed and that the older versions are no longer accessible through FAIRhub. Relationship types are used correctly and the version lineage is consistent with version_access and distribution_dates. The mini-subset target lacks a DOI, which the record states rather than fabricating.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: disease_specific_research, with license_terms describing the AI-READI Data License Agreement v2.0 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036), the grant of rights, Authorized Group provisions, derivative-data treatment, model distribution terms and warranty/liability; ip_restrictions lists four restrictions including retention of title by the Licensor and reservation of unstated rights. An unusually operational access policy: a reader can determine who may license, what they may do, what happens on breach and who owns the underlying rights. The license DOI prefix 10.5281 is Zenodo, consistent with the record's statement that the Zenodo community was used to publish the license terms. The permission enum 'disease_specific_research' is consistent with consent_scope and with the T2DM-only prohibition in prohibited_uses.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; regulatory_restrictions lists NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy security standards, applicable-law compliance and watermarking; other_compliance records the study as not FDA-regulated for drugs or devices with no human subject exemption claimed. Confidentiality classification, HIPAA status and named external frameworks are all present, and the record volunteers that the two enum values are its own mapping rather than sourced statements. The dedicated data_governance.committee_contact slot is empty, so the governance-contact component of this sub-element is met only indirectly, via maintainers (contact@aireadi.org, https://aireadi.org/contact) and the IRB Reliance Team address hsdrely@uw.edu. Five of the six listed evidence paths are substantively populated, so the sub-element passes with that noted gap.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: distribution_formats access_urls: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 and https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access; data_governance.access_review_process: 'logging in through a verified ID system, agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research, and agreeing to the license terms', with FAIRhub access type PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired. The sub-element asks for a direct download link or platform access instructions; the instructions here are step-by-step, name the access type, publish the conditions-of-access URL, and add that the controlled tier is reached through a data use agreement. The dedicated download_url slot is not populated, which is recorded as a low-severity completeness issue; the access route is nonetheless unambiguous and actionable from the populated slots, so the sub-element's purpose is served.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats: application/dicom, JSON/application/json, CSV/text/csv, MD/text/markdown; file_collections.resources give format and media_type per file (MD/text/markdown, TXT/text/plain, JSON/application/json, TSV/text/tab-separated-values); per-collection conforms_to names WFDB, OMOP CDM, ESDS, DICOM and Open mHealth. Formats are given both as release-level distribution entries and per file collection, with MIME types throughout and a note on why DICOM appears as a media type only. Media types are correctly paired with their formats and the per-datatype standards match the modalities they are attached to (WFDB for ECG, DICOM for the four retinal directories, Open mHealth for wearables). No mismatch detected.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: related_datasets: three typed entries; external_resources: seven entries including https://docs.aireadi.org/, https://aireadi.org/, https://github.com/AI-READI, https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, https://doi.org/10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x, https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449 and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048. Both halves are richly populated, and each external resource carries a note explaining its role (documentation, project site, code organization, license publication, associated publication, protocol publication, trial registration), with reuse restrictions stated for the documentation. Publisher DOI prefixes 10.1038 (Springer Nature) and 10.1136 (BMJ) match the named journals; the NCT identifier matches the NCTXXXXXXXX pattern.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license: 'AI-READI custom license v2.0'; license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'grants the Licensee a non-exclusive and non-transferable license to download, reproduce and use the Data and to create derivative works of the Data, for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes'. Reuse is permitted and the permission is bounded explicitly rather than vaguely: derivative and synthetic data inherit the terms, licensee-trained models may be distributed if they do not contain the Data, and attribution and citation obligations are stated. Not a standard Creative Commons instrument, but the custom license is identified by DOI and its operative terms are reproduced, so a prospective reuser can assess permissions without retrieving the text. Restrictiveness is proportionate to the human-subjects origin.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: conforms_to specifies WFDB for cardiac_ecg, OMOP CDM for clinical_data, NASA ESDS for environment, DICOM for the four retinal directories and Open mHealth for the two wearable directories; distribution_formats and file_collections.resources give formats and media types. Every datatype is bound to a recognised community format, and the record explains the conversions performed to reach those formats from device-native exports. The encoding component of the sub-element is not populated on any file resource. This is a minor omission for formats that are largely binary (DICOM, WFDB) or conventionally UTF-8 (CSV, TSV, JSON, MD); the standardisation requirement is otherwise met in full.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to describes the Clinical Dataset Structure v0.1.1 layout and per-datatype standards plus an RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT package on the FAIRSCAPE profile 0.1; conforms_to_standard: [CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, ESDS, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset. Conformance is stated at three levels: the directory structure, the per-file data standards, and the metadata schema of the datasheet itself, with a version pinned for each. OMOP CDM conformance is made concrete ('each CSV file in this directory is a one-to-one mapping to an OMOP CDM table') rather than asserted, and a dqd_omop.json supports the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard, which is credible corroboration of the claim.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: variables: 13 entries including participant_id (data_type identifier, is_identifier true, derivation stated) and analytes such as HbA1c (float, %, whole-blood test, reference range 4.0-6.0) and Troponin-T (float, ng/L, sex-specific reference ranges). Entries carry name, type, unit, measurement technique, provenance of the measurement and, where the laboratory supplied one, a reference range; the MoCA entry even records scoring caveats and the contrast-sensitivity entry the computation rule. Coverage is illustrative rather than exhaustive against an OMOP-mapped clinical directory, and participants.json is the actual data dictionary. The identifier requirement is met explicitly by participant_id with is_identifier true, so the sub-element passes with a coverage warning.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: three categories with usage_notes and examples (T2DM AI/ML research, disease trajectory modeling, use of the recommended splits); prohibited_uses: eight entries each with a prohibition_reason, covering clinical decision-making, re-identification, third-party model-vendor sharing, onward conveyance, bulk reproduction in publications, non-T2DM research, watermark removal and non-compliant storage. Among the most actionable use-guidance sections possible: each prohibition states not only the rule but the protective rationale, and the intended uses tie back to the stated scientific purposes. No discouraged_uses entries, but the intended/prohibited pair is comprehensive and internally consistent with license_and_use_terms and consent_scope. The T2DM-only restriction appears in three places without contradiction.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews: University of Washington IRB protocol STUDY00016228, initial approval 20 December 2022, reliance agreements covering UAB and UCSD, annual renewal within 90 days of expiration, approval letter published with the documentation; a second entry naming four ethics reviewers; a third naming an 11-person Community Advisory Board that evaluates consent forms and protocols. human_subject_research.irb_approval and ethics_review_board repeat the protocol number and give the IRB contact hsdrely@uw.edu. Named board, protocol number, dated approval, multi-site reliance arrangement, renewal obligation and a standing community oversight body — well past what the sub-element requires. Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects true and IRB approval is populated. The record discloses that the RO-Crate labels the board 'Washington University IRB' while giving a University of Washington address, and does not silently resolve the conflict. data_protection_impacts has no structured entry; the notes field states that no DPIA has been conducted, which is a disclosed negative rather than an omission, and the IRB evidence alone carries the sub-element.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.method: 'No active de-identification was necessary because no identifiers were collected... The public set is stripped of Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule via the "Safe Harbor" method'; identifiers_removed enumerates PHI, sex, race/ethnicity and medications; deidentification_details records the FAIRhub deIdent flags and the anti-stigmatisation rationale. A named method (HIPAA Safe Harbor), an explicit list of what was removed, the reason for removing more than HIPAA requires, and an acknowledged residual risk with mitigations. Consistency check passes: a deidentification claim is accompanied by both a method and an identifiers_removed list. The 'NoDeIdentification' deIdentType alongside the Safe Harbor claim is flagged as a low-severity tension; the record's explanation (no identifiers to remove) reconciles it. Safe Harbor plus suppression of sex and race is appropriate to multimodal imaging and physiological data.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy.anonymization_method; privacy_techniques listing study-ID folder naming, static watermarking, the two-tier public/controlled release, licence prohibitions on re-identification and contact, privacy-preserving device selection (no video, audio or GPS; no syncing to participant devices) and BAA-bound storage; reidentification_risk: 'A theoretical risk of future re-identification is acknowledged; AI algorithms can infer individual patient characteristics'; data_linkage describing Risk Level 3 separation of identifiers from study data. The risk assessment is explicit and technically literate about the AI-specific threat model, and each stated protection is a concrete mechanism rather than an assurance. Consistency check passes: a privacy section is present and reidentification_risk is assessed rather than left implicit, and the assessment is echoed coherently in future_use_impacts and is_deidentified.notes.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent: consent_obtained true; consent_type 'Written informed consent, obtained either electronically before the visit (e-consent with an electronic signature through REDCap) or in person'; consent_documentation (approved UW form published, reliance sites using the same form); consent_scope (FAIRhub consent metadata, T2DM-only restriction on the public version); withdrawal_mechanism ('Participants were permitted to withdraw consent at any time'). collection_consents and consent_revocations add the pre-visit e-consent flow and the statement that data already shared remain in the dataset. Type, mechanism, documentation, scope, withdrawal and the limits of withdrawal are all covered, including the candid disclosure that withdrawal does not retract already-released data. Consistency check passes: IRB approval and consent procedures are both documented, as the cross-field rule expects. consent_scope's T2DM-only limitation is consistent with license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission and with prohibited_uses.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included false with special_protections detailing exclusion of prisoners, minors (age floor 40), pregnant women, fetuses, neonates and adults unable to consent, and the absence of tribe-directed recruitment; participant_compensation: USD 200 stipend, not pro-rated, paid from grant funds once devices are returned, plus parking/transit/rideshare cost coverage and a note that fees above USD 25 are unreimbursed. A false at-risk flag that is substantively justified by the IRB eligibility criteria rather than left bare, paired with compensation documented down to amount, timing, rationale and the boundary between reimbursement and incentive. The exclusion list is consistent with human_subject_research.special_populations and with the eligibility limitation recorded in known_limitations. The notes correctly separate a project-level tribal consultation commitment from the content of this release.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations: three entries (race/ethnicity, biological sex, diabetes severity) each with identification, distribution counts across all 2,280 participants and a subpopulation_elements_present flag; subsets carry is_data_split with per-split demographic breakdowns; sampling_strategies records the eligibility base and recruitment targets. Demographics are given as exact counts, the recruitment design behind them is explained, and the record distinguishes which subpopulation variables are released publicly (diabetes status) from which are held under controlled access (sex, race/ethnicity). All subpopulation totals reconcile exactly against the three split breakdowns. The subpopulation_elements_present flags are used correctly: false for the two withheld variables, true for diabetes status, matching the stated release policy.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances.counts: 2280, with instance_type defining an instance as one individual patient across all modalities; subsets give 1,576 / 352 / 352 with is_data_split true; total_file_count 356,343 and total_size_bytes 3,815,969,779,678; per-collection file_count and total_bytes for all ten collections. Counts are reported at participant, split, file and byte level, and the notes record the historical counts of 204 and 1,067 for the earlier versions. 1,576 + 352 + 352 = 2,280, matching instances.counts. The nine datatype file counts sum to 356,334, and the nine root metadata files reconcile the stated 356,343. The byte total exceeds the directory sum by 419,614 bytes, a discrepancy the record itself discloses and which is flagged as a low-severity content-accuracy issue.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: variables: 13 documented variables with types, units and measurement techniques; is_tabular: false; subsets: three entries with is_data_split true; subpopulations carry subpopulation_elements_present flags; splits.split_details explains the 70/15/15 design and the balancing rationale. All three required components are present, and the split documentation goes beyond the flag to explain how validation and test sets were balanced for sex, race/ethnicity and diabetes status despite those variables being withheld from the public release. is_tabular false is semantically correct for a release dominated by DICOM and WFDB content, and does not conflict with the OMOP CSV tables in one of ten collections. The split flags agree with splits.split_details and with participants.tsv as the carrier.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances.data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:43; instance_type enumerates the survey, clinical, retinal imaging, environmental sensor, CGM and wearable modalities per participant; subpopulations define the four diabetes severity categories; description names type 2 diabetes mellitus and salutogenesis as the subject matter. The conditions represented are unambiguous: T2DM across four severity strata in adults aged 40-85, with the excluded conditions (type 1 diabetes, gestational diabetes, pregnancy) stated in known_limitations. The coded topic B2AI_TOPIC:43 is an opaque reference carrying no human-readable label, so the point rests on the prose, which is specific and consistent. A label alongside the code would make the coded value independently interpretable.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: anomalies: five entries (survey skips, wearable battery and malfunction gaps, imaging noise and uncooperation, data collisions, undilated handheld fundus image variability); sampling_strategies with is_sample, is_random, is_representative flags, wave-based strategy, source_data and why_not_representative; missing_data_documentation with patterns, causes and handling_strategy. Quality issues are named per modality with their physical causes, and the missing-data entry states both what is missing and what was done about it, including that no instances were excluded at preprocessing. The anomaly entries agree with the coverage limitation in known_limitations and with instances.missing_information. The record resolves a genuine source conflict about whether the dataset is a sample, setting is_sample true on the registered 'Non-Probability Sample' and the documented wave recruitment, and records the conflict rather than hiding it.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: 3.0.0; title-level and description-level references to 'Version 3.0.0'; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3. A semantic version number that is used consistently across the description, the citation, the DOI and the documentation references. Follows MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and is consistent with the 1.0.0 and 2.0.0 predecessors listed in version_access and related_datasets.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access: latest_version_doi; versions_available listing all three versions with DOI, release date and participant count; version_details explaining that each version has its own DOI and documentation set navigable from a version dropdown, and that 1.0.0 and 2.0.0 are no longer accessible through FAIRhub; notes giving the earlier healthsheet URLs. Not merely a list of versions but an honest account of which remain retrievable, which is exactly what a user trying to reproduce an earlier analysis needs to know. Version DOIs follow the same FAIRhub prefix and increment coherently; release dates are ordered and match distribution_dates.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: updates.update_details: 'Changes between the current version and the previous one are provided in detail in the CHANGELOG file included in the dataset and visible at docs.aireadi.org'; version_access.version_details names the substantive changes (Snellen visual acuity variables dropped so only logMAR remains, number of image devices increased, a recommended data split added); the root metadata collection includes CHANGELOG.md. Specific, consequential changes are named in the record itself rather than only pointed at, and the dropped-variable change is repeated on the affected variable entry so a reuser encounters it in context. No errata slot is populated, and none is claimed; the changelog route is real and the enumerated changes are consistent with the variables and subsets sections. Scored on the change-description half of the disjunctive requirement.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.frequency: 'Approximately once a year'; update_details: 'The dataset is released as static versions and is not updated in place. Instead, new versions are released with additional data from participants who have been enrolled since the last version release; enrollment is ongoing and future versions are expected to include larger numbers of participants.' States both the cadence and the update model, which matters more than the cadence: static immutable versions rather than in-place mutation. The stated annual cadence is corroborated by the actual release dates (May 2024, November 2024, November 2025), and the growth model is corroborated by the participant counts 204, 1,067, 2,280.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: was_derived_from: the AI-READI observational study; raw_data_sources: two entries (prospective collection from participants; EHRs of the three health systems, with access_details noting the derived records are controlled-access only); raw_sources describing the device-native exports (.xml, .fda, .sdt, .FIT, .csv, REDCap exports) and their retention and non-sharing policy; updates.update_details for release-specific notes. Provenance is traced from parent study through raw device exports to standardised release, including an explicit statement of what raw material exists, why it is not shared, and that it may appear in future controlled releases. The raw-source inventory matches the conversions described in preprocessing_strategies (.fda and .sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth, ECG .xml to WFDB), so the provenance chain is internally coherent end to end.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: three entries (enable AI/ML insight into T2DM including salutogenic pathways; permit downstream pseudotime manifold analysis to reconstruct a temporal atlas of T2DM development and reversal; establish FAIR standards and best practices as a blueprint for future data generation projects); addressing_gaps: three entries naming the absence of AI-ready multimodal T2DM datasets, the documented under-representation of higher-burden racial and ethnic groups, and the infeasibility of such analyses with claims or EHR data. Purpose and the research gap it addresses are stated separately and specifically, with the diversity gap supported by reference to a meta-epidemiological review of T2DM studies from 2000 to 2020. The stated purposes align with the funding award title 'Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project', satisfying the funding-to-purpose alignment check.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: pseudotime manifold analysis to predict disease trajectories across severity strata from normal to insulin-dependent T2DM; development of AI/ML models on a hypothesis-agnostic multimodal dataset using the recommended 70/15/15 split. Concrete analytical methods rather than generic aspirations, and the second task ties directly to an artifact shipped with the release (participants.tsv split assignments). Consistent with instances.label_description, which states no labels are provided because the dataset is hypothesis-agnostic; the tasks do not presuppose labels that do not exist. Consistent also with intended_uses.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders: National Institutes of Health, with notes identifying the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program and the award title 'Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project'; a second grantor, Research to Prevent Blindness; notes records in-kind support from Microsoft AI for Good Lab (cloud services), device loans from Topcon, Optomed, iCare World and Carl Zeiss, and research discounts from Heidelberg, Dexcom and Garmin. Both the funding agency and the specific mechanism (NIH Common Fund Other Transaction under Bridge2AI) are identified, with award amount, fiscal year and project period given for the principal award. The in-kind and discount support is correctly documented without grant numbers; per the funding rule, an absent grants block for non-grant support is not flagged.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders.grants: OT2OD032644 (application 10471118, project number 1OT2OD032644-01, FY2022, USD 5,026,499, 2022-09-01 to 2025-08-31), P30DK035816, UL1TR003096. Three award numbers with provenance for each, and the record distinguishes the one award named in the dataset's own funding reference from the two named only in the protocol publication. All three match NIH structural patterns for their stated agency: OT2 + OD + 032644, P30 + DK + 035816, UL1 + TR + 003096. The record notes the healthsheet's transcription 'OT2ODO32644' as a transcription of the correct number rather than propagating the typo, and discloses that two NIH RePORTER project-detail identifiers (10885481, 10471118) appear for the same core project.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: AI-READI Consortium with affiliation Washington University in St. Louis (ROR:01yc7t268) and principal_investigator Aaron Lee (ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648, contact@aireadi.org) with two affiliations; source_caveats enumerates fifteen further study principal investigators and seven collaborating organizations; license_and_use_terms records the acknowledgement obligation; notes records in-kind acknowledgements. Creators carry persistent identifiers (ORCID, ROR), the distinction between dataset creator and study personnel is reasoned rather than assumed, and the attribution conflict between two tier-1 sources is represented rather than silently resolved. The ORCID matches the 16-digit pattern and both ROR identifiers are well formed. Recording both the University of Washington and Washington University in St. Louis attributions is the correct handling of a genuine source disagreement, and it is disclosed at the point of use.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: thirteen entries. Examples: 'Philips PageWriter TC30 Cardiograph... a 12-lead ECG performed while the participant sits in a reclining chair or lies supine, with the position recorded as 0, 30, 60 or 90 degrees relative to supine'; 'Dexcom G6... worn continuously for 10 days... readings in mg/dL every five minutes... Participants were masked to the results'; 'Garmin Vivosmart 5... non-dominant wrist for 10 consecutive days... sampling frequency is 5 seconds'; plus a consolidated entry for in-clinic instruments with test distances, filters and luminance ranges. Replication-grade detail: device manufacturer and location, acquisition protocol, participant positioning, duration, sampling rate, lighting conditions and output format for each modality, with collection_timeframes giving the 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 window. Each mechanism maps onto a device directory named in file_collections (philips_tc30, dexcom_g6, garmin_vivosmart5, leelab_anura, the four OCT devices), so the described collection and the released structure corroborate each other.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods: one entry with was_directly_observed and was_validated_verified true, describing verification by cross-referencing entered medications against medications physically brought in or photographed; a second with was_reported_by_subjects true, enumerating the survey domains. raw_data_sources gives the two source types with access details. The flags are accompanied by concrete verification procedure, and the split between observed and self-reported acquisition is made explicit domain by domain. Consistent with data_collectors, which names who performed each acquisition role and describes their certification, and with the central and local laboratory arrangements for assays.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies: five entries (OMOP/DICOM standardisation for AI-readiness; device-format conversions; HIPAA Safe Harbor removal plus suppression of sex, race/ethnicity and medications; CDS v0.1.1 organisation with manifest.tsv and root metadata files including dqd_omop.json for the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard; the shift from ad hoc v1.0.0 handling to automated and custom processing). cleaning_strategies: two entries describing REDCap range-check flagging, credibility checks for skip-pattern errors, duplicates and fillable gaps, PI-approved editing and PI review of uncorrectable values, plus site data-manager QC before upload. The pipeline is traceable from device export to released file, and the cleaning entry is specific about the decision authority for edits, which is unusual and useful. Labeling is addressed by an explicit negative: instances.label false with label_description stating no labeling was performed because the dataset is hypothesis-agnostic and that no software was used to label instances. annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are unpopulated, but the disjunctive requirement is satisfied by the preprocessing and cleaning evidence.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: No software producing or transforming the released data is named. preprocessing_strategies states that Topcon Maestro2 and Triton .fda exports were 'converted to DICOM', Heidelberg FLIO .sdt 'converted to DICOM', Garmin .FIT 'converted to the Open mHealth standard', ECG 'converted to WFDB', and that clinical data were 'mapped to standardized terminologies... notably the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model' — in every case without naming the converter or mapper. The nearest thing to a pipeline description is 'a combination of automated and custom processing'. external_resources gives https://github.com/AI-READI, an organization root. A reader cannot tell what software produced the distributed DICOM, WFDB, OMOP CSV or Open mHealth files, which is precisely the question this sub-element asks. This is the only sub-element not met, and the gap is narrow: the processing steps are described in detail, only their implementing tools are anonymous.
