The format claims themselves are internally consistent across description, file_collections, distribution_formats and raw_data_sources.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to: 'Structured electronic health record data (demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets and diagnoses) are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, with published metadata in the OMOP schema and, for nursing flowsheets, the OMOP schema with extensions. Imaging from PACS follows DICOM. Waveform telemetry follows WFDB ... EEG waveforms use EDF+ and Persyst. Clinical notes are extracted and tokenized against the OHNLP open source schema.' conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema ; conforms_to_class: Dataset ; instances carry ontology-coded data_topic (B2AI_TOPIC:9, 15, 32, 37) and data_substrate (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11, 43, 49) terms. Conformance is stated per data element class rather than as a blanket claim, including the honest qualification that flowsheet metadata extends the standard schema. Ontology term identifiers on instances add machine-resolvable semantic typing beyond the prose. Standard names are used correctly and match the modalities they are attached to. Extension points (OMOP with flowsheet extensions, PhysioNet schema extended) are declared, which is exactly what a harmonizing reuser needs to know; the specific extension content is not documented.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: No variables field anywhere in the record. The closest content is instance-level typing ('Row of electronic health record data standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model', data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:9) and prose enumeration of domains covered: 'demographics, medication administration time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration, procedures documented by providers, high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation, and diagnoses documented by providers'. No variable-level metadata, no data dictionary, no field identifiers, units or value sets, for a release whose principal component is 1.6 billion rows of tabular data. OMOP conformance substitutes by reference for standard tables but leaves the declared CHoRUS extensions and the waveform, EEG and token outputs undocumented at variable level. Domain-level prose is real information but operates at a coarser granularity than this sub-element requires; crediting it would also duplicate the evidence scored under sub-element 3 and Element 5 sub-element 4.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: three entries with use_category and usage_notes — 'Machine learning model development for acute and critical care' ('models can be built to improve the care and outcomes of patients requiring critical care, using multi-modal EHR, waveform, imaging and text data harmonized under unified standards'), 'External validation of AI models' (with source_caveats 'The source documents do not report that this holdout set has been released'), and 'AI/ML workforce training and education' (AIM-AHEAD trainees developing use cases in the enclave). existing_uses records training activities and publications as of the September 2025 webinar. Intended uses are categorized, described concretely, and calibrated: the holdout-validation use is explicitly marked as not yet realized rather than advertised as available. A reuser can tell which uses the dataset supports today. prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses are both absent, which for controlled-access critical-care data is a meaningful omission — no prohibition on re-identification attempts, on removing data from the enclave, or on clinical deployment of models trained on it is recorded, even though those constraints are implied by the access regime described elsewhere. The rubric satisfies this sub-element on any of the three fields, and the intended_uses content is substantive enough to pass; the missing prohibitions are logged as an issue.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews[0].review_details: 'Ethics is one of three project pillars (Ethical and Trustworthy AI). The project performs community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing, evaluates community perspectives on clinical care AI ... establishes a legal framework for collecting data at scale, and analyzes the existing legal and regulatory landscape.' ethical_reviews[0].source_caveats: 'The source documents do not name an IRB or ethics committee of record for the dataset and do not report an approval number or determination.' human_subject_research.source_caveats repeats that no IRB approval, ethics review board of record, or regulatory compliance determination is stated. No data_protection_impacts field; no governance committee contact. What is documented is a project ethics workstream — focus groups, legal-landscape analysis, community engagement — not review or approval of this dataset. For a 14-site retrospective extract of critically ill patients including minors and neonates, a reuser cannot identify the reviewing body, the approval or determination, the reliance arrangement across sites, or any DPIA. The field is populated with genuine content that does not answer the oversight question the sub-element asks. Fails the stated consistency check: involves_human_subjects=true requires IRB or equivalent oversight evidence, and none is present. The gap is one the record itself discloses twice, so this is an absence in the documented dataset governance rather than an evaluator inference.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.method: 'Tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text, transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification, and de-identification of imaging prior to release.' is_deidentified.deidentification_details: 'As of August 2025, 1000 images were available with de-identification in process for a larger imaging cohort. Supporting tooling in the chorus-ai organization includes a privacy scan tool for medical records and a CTP-deid repository.' source_caveats: identifiers removed are not enumerated, no standard is stated for structured data, and no residual risk assessment is reported. The method is described per modality with named implementing tooling — OHNLP tokenization for notes, CTP-deid (a recognized DICOM de-identification toolkit) and a privacy scan tool for imaging and records — and the state of completion is dated. That is specific and actionable, above the boilerplate threshold, even though it is not a formal standard. Method is appropriate to the data types: tokenization is the right control for free-text notes and pixel/header de-identification via a CTP-based pipeline is the right control for DICOM. Two gaps remain: no HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination claim for the structured OMOP data, and no identifiers_removed enumeration, both flagged as a medium consistency issue. The enclave-only access model partially compensates for the weaker structured-data claim.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy[0].anonymization_method: 'Tokenization of unstructured electronic health record data and transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification, with clinical notes retained at the contributing site.' participant_privacy[0].reidentification_risk: 'The project states that data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification; no quantitative residual risk is reported in the source documents.' notes: 'Patient-focused efforts within the project determine the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health.' Corroborated by confidential_elements (note text not releasable) and regulatory_restrictions (all modalities controlled access). Concrete, verifiable protections are documented and layered: notes never leave the contributing site, only tokens enter the enclave, analysis happens inside the enclave, and every modality is controlled access. This is a substantive privacy architecture rather than an assertion of care. The reidentification_risk slot is populated but reports a qualitative claim and an explicit absence of quantification rather than an assessment — a real weakness for high-resolution waveform and imaging data, which are known to carry re-identification potential even after header scrubbing. The honest negative statement is credited as documentation of the risk position; the missing quantitative assessment is logged as an issue rather than treated as an empty field.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: No informed_consent field anywhere in the record. direct_collection[0].is_direct: false, 'Data are acquired retrospectively from clinical systems at contributing hospitals rather than gathered directly from patients for this project'. human_subject_research.source_caveats notes that no IRB approval or determination is stated; at_risk_populations.source_caveats states the sources 'describe no assent procedures, guardian consent, or special protections'. Nothing is documented about the legal basis on which patient data left 14 hospitals: no consent procedure, no broad consent for secondary use, no waiver determination, no opt-out mechanism, and no withdrawal route. Retrospective collection makes a waiver likely, but likelihood is not documentation, and a reuser of a controlled-access critical-care dataset needs the basis stated. Fails the stated consistency check: involves_human_subjects=true is expected to be accompanied by documented consent procedures. Combined with the absent IRB record under sub-element 1, the two failures compound — neither the oversight body nor the consent basis can be identified.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: true ; notes: 'Admissions from pediatric intensive care units and neonatal intensive care units are part of the current released dataset.' human_subject_research.special_populations: 'The released dataset includes admissions from pediatric and neonatal intensive care units, so minors and neonates are represented.' source_caveats: 'The value is an inference from the reported PICU and NICU admissions; the source documents do not characterize the cohort as including at-risk or vulnerable populations and describe no assent procedures, guardian consent, or special protections.' No participant_compensation field. The record affirmatively identifies the vulnerable groups present and names them specifically (minors, neonates), tying the determination to the reported PICU and NICU admissions and marking it as inference. For a reuser planning analyses or applying for access, knowing that pediatric and neonatal records are in scope is the operative fact, and it is documented in two mutually consistent fields. Identification is present and non-trivial; protections are absent, and participant_compensation is absent without comment — defensible for retrospective record collection, where no participant interaction occurs, but not stated. Scored 1 on the strength of the specific, cross-corroborated identification, with the missing protections logged as a medium consistency issue rather than double-counted here.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations: three entries each with subpopulation_elements_present: true and identification — 'Admissions to intensive care units (ICU)', 'Admissions to pediatric intensive care units (PICU)', 'Admissions to neonatal intensive care units (NICU)' — each carrying source_caveats: 'The released figure of 50,000 patient admissions is reported for ICU, PICU and NICU combined; no per-setting breakdown is given.' Contributing cohort context: '14 contributing hospitals drawn from a network of 20 academic centers'. Three clinically meaningful subpopulations are identified and flagged, spanning adult, pediatric and neonatal critical care, with the site network described. This is real cohort structure, and the repeated caveat that counts are combined is accurate rather than evasive. No demographic characterization at all — no age, sex, race, ethnicity, payer or geography distribution — and no inclusion or exclusion criteria, for a project whose stated purpose is equitable AI and whose keywords include social determinants of health. The subpopulation identification passes the threshold; the demographic silence is logged as a high-severity completeness issue and echoed in the record's own representativeness_limitation.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances: 'Hospital admission of a critically ill patient' counts: 50000; 'Row of electronic health record data standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model' counts: 1600000000; 'Hospital admission with associated radiology imaging' counts: 7642; 'Bedside monitor waveform telemetry record' (no count, notes '23 Tb of waveform data; no record or file count is given for the waveform modality'); plus tokenized clinical note and EEG instance types. Anticipated final dataset: 100,000 admissions across 9 modalities. Counts are specific, per instance type, and given with their units, distinguishing admissions from rows from terabytes. Where no count exists (waveform records, notes, EEG) the record says so explicitly instead of leaving the reader to guess, and the released-versus-anticipated distinction is maintained. One unresolved discrepancy: source_caveats records the webinar figure of 'over 45K unique admissions' against the website's 50,000, and imaging is counted as 7,642 admissions in one source and 1,000 available images in another. The record ranks its sources and reports both figures rather than silently reconciling them, which is good practice, but the released cohort size remains ambiguous — logged as a content_accuracy issue.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: No variables field. No is_tabular field. No is_data_split or is_subpopulation flags on dataset subsets (subpopulation_elements_present appears on subpopulations, not as a subset flag). splits[0].split_details: 'The award abstract states that the project will sequester holdout datasets and will provision a holdout test set accessible for model external validation', with source_caveats: 'This is described in the award abstract as a planned capability; the source documents do not report the size or availability of the holdout partition.' The primary ask — variable-level metadata or a data dictionary — is entirely absent for a release dominated by 1.6 billion rows of tabular OMOP data, and the tabular flag is unset. The only split content is a planned holdout with no size, no composition and no availability, which cannot orient a user to a role any subset currently plays. Scoring 0 despite the populated splits field: the field describes a future capability rather than a realized partition, and no variable or flag evidence exists to combine with it. Consistent with Element 3 sub-element 4, which fails on the same absent variables field.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances carry ontology-coded topics and substrates: data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:9 (EHR admissions and OMOP rows), B2AI_TOPIC:15 with data_substrate B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11 (radiology imaging), B2AI_TOPIC:37 with B2AI_SUBSTRATE:49 (waveform telemetry and EEG), B2AI_TOPIC:32 with B2AI_SUBSTRATE:43 (tokenized clinical notes). Content domains enumerated: 'demographics, medication administration ... procedures documented by providers, high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation, and diagnoses documented by providers'; sensitive_elements adds social determinants of health and geographic distance to the nearest hospital. Six instance types cover the represented topics with machine-resolvable ontology identifiers plus prose enumeration of the clinical content domains, so a reuser can tell which modalities and which classes of clinical information are present. Ontology term identifiers are consistently applied and modality-appropriate (imaging substrate on the imaging instance, waveform substrate on both telemetry and EEG). Specific disease conditions or phenotypes are not enumerated — no diagnosis distribution or condition list — which limits topical discovery to the setting and modality level rather than the clinical-condition level.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: instances[2].missing_information: missing 'Imaging beyond the approximately 1,000 images reported as available in August 2025', why_missing 'De-identification was in process for a larger imaging cohort.' instances[4].missing_information: missing 'Full clinical note text', why_missing 'Clinical notes are stored locally at contributing sites; only tokens leave the site.' sampling_strategies[0].strategies: 'Sampling to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies. Federated access is intended to enable sampling methods that ensure a balanced and diverse cohort', with source_caveats that both statements describe intended approaches and the sampling actually applied is not reported. Missing data is documented where it exists, per instance type, with the reason for the absence — a structural gap (notes never leave the site) and a temporal one (imaging de-identification in progress). Combined with the sampling strategy entry, a reuser can anticipate the principal holes in the release. No anomalies field and no missing_data_documentation block; the missing-information content sits on instances, which the rubric's field list for this sub-element reaches via missing_data_documentation's concept. The sampling entry is aspirational and marked as such. Sufficient for this sub-element, but the absence of any data-quality anomaly reporting is scored against Element 9 sub-element 3 rather than forgiven there.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: No version field. status: 'partially released'. The nearest temporal anchors are narrative: 'as of August 2025' in collection_timeframes and updates, and 'the current released dataset' in description and updates.update_details. No version identifier of any kind for a dataset the record describes as actively growing from 50,000 toward 100,000 admissions with two modalities still being ingested. Work performed against the August 2025 state cannot be distinguished from work performed against a later state, which undermines reproducibility of any analysis built on it. The 'partially released' status is a lifecycle stage, not a version. Dated snapshot language ('as of August 2025') is used consistently and is the closest functional substitute, but it is prose rather than an assigned, citable version.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: No version_access field. data_governance.access_review_process describes how to obtain access to the dataset but says nothing about obtaining a particular state of it; updates.source_caveats: 'The source documents do not state a release cadence or versioning policy for the dataset itself.' With no versions assigned, there is correspondingly no mechanism documented for retrieving a prior state, pinning an analysis to a snapshot, or determining which state an enclave workspace holds. This is a compounding gap for an enclave-hosted dataset where users cannot keep their own copy. Consistent with sub-element 1: the absence is structural rather than an oversight in one field, and the record states the policy gap explicitly.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: updates.update_details: 'Data acquisition is ongoing. The current released dataset covers 50,000 patient admissions, while the anticipated final dataset is 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals. Imaging de-identification for a larger cohort and EEG extraction were in process as of August 2025. Contributing sites provide regular status updates on their progress in creating and curating a CHoRUS-specific clinical data extract.' Corroborated by known_limitations (coverage_limitation) and instances[2].missing_information. The dedicated update_details field carries actual release-state information: what is in the current release, what the target is, and which two modalities are mid-ingestion as of a stated date. A reuser can tell how the content differs now from what it will contain, which is the substance of a change description even without a formal changelog. No errata field and no per-version change log; nothing is recorded about corrections to previously distributed data, which matters because characterization reports returned to sites (cleaning_strategies) imply that site resubmissions occur. Credited on the strength of substantive, dated release-state documentation, not on the mere presence of an updates block.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.source_caveats: 'The source documents do not state a release cadence or versioning policy for the dataset itself.' The only cadence language is 'Data acquisition is ongoing' and 'Contributing sites provide regular status updates on their progress', which describes site reporting to the consortium, not dataset releases to users. No schedule, frequency, or next-release expectation for the dataset. A user cannot plan around whether the imaging and EEG modalities arrive in a month or a year, nor learn how they would be notified. Correctly distinguished from sub-element 3: an account of what is changing is present, an account of when it will be published is not. The record's own caveat confirms the absence rather than leaving it to inference, and the internal site-reporting cadence is not repurposed as a release cadence.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: was_derived_from: 'Clinical source systems at the 14 CHoRUS data contributing hospitals, comprising electronic health records, PACS imaging archives, bedside monitors with gateway/middleware, and hospital EEG databases.' raw_data_sources: five structured entries — hospital EHR systems (site-native formats mapped to OMOP before delivery; only the standardized extract is delivered), unstructured note text (free text; notes stay local, only OHNLP tokens available), PACS (DICOM), bedside monitors with gateway/middleware (waveform telemetry converted to WFDB), hospital EEG database (EDF+ and Persyst). created_by: CHoRUS Consortium. The strongest element of the record: every released modality is traced to its originating clinical system, with the native format, the transformation applied before delivery, and the access condition on the source stated per entry. A reuser can reconstruct the chain from bedside instrument to distributed file. raw_data_sources aligns one-to-one with was_derived_from, file_collections, distribution_formats and the preprocessing_strategies that perform each conversion — no orphan source and no modality lacking a source. Formal PROV-O structure is absent but the rubric accepts structured text, and the entity-activity relationships are recoverable from the text as written.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: four responses — 'Generate data for ML/AI applications aimed at characterizing acute and critical care illness, predicting complications, and measuring treatment response'; 'Develop a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset while ensuring the methods promote privacy, accountability, and clinical benefit'; 'Provision a holdout test set accessible for model external validation, to aid marketplace adoption'; 'Create ethically sourced datasets and tools around artificial intelligence and establish best practices for AI in health'. addressing_gaps: three responses including 'There is an urgent need for infrastructure to support artificial intelligence and machine learning in critical care' and 'Unified standards are needed to harmonize multi-modal EHR, waveform, imaging, and text data across institutions'. Purpose is stated at both the scientific and the infrastructural level, and addressing_gaps articulates the specific research gap the dataset exists to close. Together they explain not just what the dataset is for but why it needed to be built. Purposes align with the funding mechanism (Common Fund Bridge2AI, whose stated aim is ethically sourced AI-ready data) and with the tasks, intended_uses and description — no divergence between the motivation claimed and the dataset delivered.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: 'Characterizing acute and critical care illness'; 'Predicting complications and clinical deterioration among patients with acute or critical illness'; 'Measuring treatment response among patients with acute or critical illness'; 'External validation of AI-developed models against a sequestered holdout test set, which the award abstract states the project will provision.' Four distinct, well-formed analytic objectives spanning characterization, prediction and treatment-response estimation, phrased concretely enough to map onto modelling problems. The fourth is attributed to the award abstract and marked as a project commitment. Tasks are consistent with the modalities actually released (high-frequency flowsheet and waveform data support deterioration prediction; OMOP structured data supports treatment-response measurement). No task requires data the record says is unavailable, except the holdout validation task, which is correspondingly flagged as not yet released in intended_uses.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders[0].grantor: 'National Institutes of Health, Common Fund Bridge2AI program'; grant notes record 'fiscal year 2022, award amount 5880300, project start 2022-09-01 and project end 2026-11-30' and 'The project website states that the project is funded by the NIH under award number OT2OD032701.' The funder is named at both agency and program level, with the mechanism evident from the award type, the award amount, and the full project period. notes also record the disclaimer that website content does not necessarily represent official NIH views. Funder identity is corroborated independently by the RePORTER URL in external_resources (project-details/10472824, matching the application ID recorded here) and by the Bridge2AI keyword. The OT2 other-transaction mechanism is the one the Common Fund uses for Bridge2AI data generation projects, so agency, program and mechanism are mutually consistent.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders[0].grants[0].grant_number: 'OT2OD032701'; notes: 'NIH RePORTER lists project number 1OT2OD032701-01, application ID 10472824, fiscal year 2022, award amount 5880300, project start 2022-09-01 and project end 2026-11-30.' A structured grant_number is supplied together with the fully qualified project number, the application ID, and the award period, so the award can be verified against RePORTER without ambiguity. Format check passes for NIH: OT2 (other transaction activity code) + OD (Office of the Director, correct for Common Fund awards) + six digits 032701, and the qualified form 1OT2OD032701-01 correctly adds the application type prefix and support-year suffix. The grantor named is NIH Common Fund, so agency and number pattern match. Application ID 10472824 matches the RePORTER URL in external_resources.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: seven entries — Eric Rosenthal (Massachusetts General Hospital, with principal_investigator block and id https://chorus4ai.org/#person-eric-rosenthal, sourced to both the webinar leadership slide and the RePORTER record), Azra Bihorac and Yulia Strekalova and Parisa Rashidi (University of Florida), Xiaoqian Jiang (UTHealth Houston), Manlik Kwong (Tufts University), and 'CHoRUS Consortium' ('More than 60 CHoRUS consortium members across 20 different institutions'). maintainers: program manager at MGH and GitHub organization access contacts. data_collectors: Data Acquisition centers and CHoRUS sub-teams. Named individuals with affiliations, an explicit PI designation, the collective consortium credit, and separately documented maintainer and collector roles. Each attribution carries a provenance note stating where the name was found, which is unusually traceable. Creator affiliations are consistent with the accountable_organization (MGH) and with the RePORTER organization recorded under funders ('MASSACHUSETTS GENERAL HOSPITAL'). One recorded contact address, cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu, has a suspect domain that the record flags verbatim; it affects contactability, not attribution, and is logged as a low-severity correctness issue. No ORCIDs are present.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: 'Contributing sites create and upload a CHoRUS Data Extract using the tooling in the chorus-extract-upload repository, following an interactive workflow diagram with links to validated standard operating procedure documents'; 'Bedside monitors with gateway/middleware supply waveform telemetry'; 'Imaging is drawn from hospital PACS'; 'EEG waveforms are drawn from hospital EEG databases in EDF+ and Persyst formats'; 'Clinical notes are extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit'. collection_timeframes: retrospective collection, snapshot 'as of August 2025, covering 14 different hospitals', with a caveat distinguishing the award period from the encounter period. direct_collection: is_direct false, with details. Mechanisms are given per modality and name the actual tooling and workflow a site follows, including the SOP-driven extract-and-upload path. The settings are specified (14 contributing hospitals, ICU/PICU/NICU, retrospective) and the timeframe caveat prevents a reader from misreading the award dates as the encounter window. Consistent with raw_data_sources and acquisition_methods, which describe the same five pathways from the source side. One genuine gap, disclosed rather than hidden: the calendar range of included clinical encounters is nowhere stated, which limits assessment of practice-era drift.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods: was_directly_observed true — 'Retrospective acquisition of clinical data recorded in the course of care ... including provider documentation of procedures and diagnoses, high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation, medication administration time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration, PACS imaging, bedside monitor telemetry and hospital EEG recordings'; was_inferred_derived true — tokenization of unstructured text and OMOP standardization 'so that delivered records are derived from rather than identical to the site source records'; was_validated_verified true — 'Semantic mappings ... are validated, and standard operating procedures used by contributing sites undergo an internal validation and review process within the Chorus_SOP repository'. raw_data_sources adds five entries with source_type and raw_data_format. Acquisition is described with the schema's provenance flags set correctly and each flag justified in prose, covering observation, derivation and validation. The instrument and system classes are named (bedside monitors with gateway/middleware, PACS, hospital EEG databases, EHR systems), and the granularity of medication timestamping is specified. The three flags are mutually consistent and match the pipeline described in preprocessing_strategies. Specific device manufacturers, monitor models and EHR vendors are not named, which limits exact replication of the capture stage but does not leave the acquisition method unstated.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies: OMOP standardization 'using validated semantic mappings that connect clinical data in various source formats to international standards; pooled tabular mappings and their documentation are maintained in the chorus-mapping repository'; note extraction and tokenization with the OHNLP toolkit plus transformation limiting re-identification; waveform conversion 'using the conversion scripts and documentation maintained in the chorus_waveform repository, with supporting materials in chorus_waveform_resources'. cleaning_strategies: 'Characterization reports are produced and returned to contributing sites following their data submissions, using the CHoRUSReports repository'; validated semantic mappings with 'a clinical validation standard operating procedure' and internally reviewed site SOPs. labeling_strategies: annotation environment described, with source_caveats that it is future tense and no labels are reported in the current release. The pipeline is documented stage by stage and each stage points at the repository that implements it, so the transformations between site source records and distributed files are traceable and, in principle, inspectable. Quality control is genuine — characterization reports fed back to sites and a clinical validation SOP for mappings. Labeling is honestly marked as not yet realized rather than claimed, and no annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools or imputation_protocols are recorded. The preprocessing and cleaning content is substantive enough to carry the sub-element; the forward-looking labeling entry is logged as a low-severity tense issue rather than credited as delivered.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: Named software in processing roles, carried by preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, is_deidentified and external_resources: the 'OHNLP toolkit', which extracts and tokenizes the clinical notes that are the distributed note artifact; the 'chorus_waveform' conversion scripts, which convert waveform data for release into WFDB; 'chorus-mapping', holding the pooled tabular semantic mappings by which site data are standardized to OMOP; 'CTP-deid' and a 'privacy scan tool', which de-identify imaging and records before release; and 'CHoRUSReports', which generates the characterization reports driving site resubmission. A reader can tell what transformed the data being distributed. Each named tool is tied to the modality it acts on — OHNLP to notes, chorus_waveform to telemetry, chorus-mapping to OMOP structured data, CTP-deid to imaging — and each is locatable within the chorus-ai organization named in external_resources. Threshold satisfied on processing-role software, not on capture, hosting, packaging or validation tooling: the Azure deployment and dockerized container applications (hosting, role b), the OHDSI tool stack and Jupyter Notebooks used by trainees in the enclave (analysis by consumers), and chorus-extract-upload (site-side capture and transfer, role a) are present but were not relied on. No version numbers, commit pins or software DOIs are given for any tool, and the individual repository URLs are not listed — the pointer identifies the organization root only — which weakens reproducibility; the sub-element asks whether the tooling is disclosed, and it is, by name.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: the chorus-ai GitHub organization with 28 named repositories and its licensing note; https://chorus4ai.org/ with its documentation pages; www.bridge2ai.org/chorus; https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824; the AIM-AHEAD cohort-2 informational webinar PDF. conforms_to: per-modality standards statement (OMOP CDM with extensions, DICOM, WFDB with extended PhysioNet metadata schema, EDF+/Persyst, OHNLP). extension_mechanism.contribution_url: https://github.com/chorus-ai, with the chorus-mapping contribution path and Standards / Data Acquisition discussion spaces. External standards and supporting resources are both well covered: the standards are named per modality, the implementing SOPs and code are pointed at, the funder record is linked, and a contribution route is documented for external collaborators to extend the semantic mappings. No imputation_protocols field, and the record does not state whether imputation was applied or deliberately avoided — a real gap for high-frequency flowsheet and waveform data where gaps are ubiquitous. The standards and resource evidence is strong enough to carry the sub-element; peer-reviewed publications describing the dataset are also absent from the resource list.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: four typed entries — coverage_limitation ('as of August 2025 imaging was limited to about 1,000 available images with de-identification in process for a larger cohort, and EEG extraction was still in process', scope_impact 'Analyses requiring imaging or EEG at scale are not yet supported by the released data'); integration_limitation (note text remains local, only tokens in the enclave); representativeness_limitation (14 of 20 centers contribute; achieved demographic, geographic and clinical distribution unreported); scope_limitation (ICU/PICU/NICU settings only). Limitations are categorized by type, described concretely, and at least one carries an explicit scope_impact telling a reuser which analyses are foreclosed. They cover the four dimensions that actually matter here — modality coverage, data locality, representativeness and clinical scope — and none is boilerplate. Each limitation is corroborated elsewhere in the record rather than asserted in isolation: coverage by instances[2].missing_information, integration by confidential_elements and raw_data_sources, representativeness by the sampling_strategies caveat, scope by subpopulations. The representativeness entry is notably candid in conceding that the achieved distribution is unknown.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: No known_biases field. No future_use_impacts field. The nearest content is known_limitations[2] (representativeness_limitation, noting that the distribution achieved is not reported) and participant_privacy[0].notes ('Patient-focused efforts within the project determine the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'). No bias is identified, let alone categorized. For a 14-site academic-center dataset explicitly framed around equitable AI, the expected biases — academic-center selection, geographic concentration, documentation-practice variation across sites, device and monitor heterogeneity, differential missingness in flowsheet data — are entirely unenumerated, and no demographic composition is reported against which representativeness could be judged. No BiasTypeEnum categorization and no rai:dataSocialImpact content. A prose acknowledgement that bias must be managed, and a limitation noting that the distribution is unreported, are not a bias analysis; scoring 1 here would credit the absence of the analysis as its presence.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: No anomalies field. Adjacent content addresses other concerns: instances[].missing_information (gaps in coverage), source_caveats (disagreement between source documents about cohort and imaging counts), cleaning_strategies (characterization reports returned to sites, which implies quality findings exist). Nothing is documented about the quality of the data itself — no outliers, no artefact rates in the telemetry, no implausible physiologic values, no site-to-site mapping inconsistencies, no OMOP concept mapping failure rates — even though the record states that characterization reports are generated per submission and would surface exactly these. The metadata discrepancies noted in source_caveats concern the documentation, not the data. Distinguished from Element 5 sub-element 5, which passes on missing-data documentation and sampling strategy: those describe what is absent from the release, whereas this sub-element asks about defects in what is present. The existence of CHoRUSReports makes the silence a reporting gap rather than an inherent one.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present true, 'The dataset comprises hospital clinical data on critically ill patients, including demographics, diagnoses, procedures, medication administration, nursing flowsheets, clinical notes, imaging, telemetry and EEG waveforms, and social determinants of health, together with contextual factors such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital. Every data type listed in the project\'s data inventory is under controlled access.' confidential_elements: confidential_elements_present true, 'Clinical note text is treated as not releasable: notes are stored locally at contributing sites and only tokens are held in the enclave alongside OMOP and telemetry data.' Sensitivity is enumerated at the level of specific data classes rather than asserted generically, and it identifies the two subtle re-identification vectors a reuser might overlook — social determinants of health and geographic distance to the nearest hospital. The confidentiality entry states an operative restriction, not a label. Consistent with regulatory_restrictions (confidentiality_level restricted), is_deidentified and participant_privacy. No content_warnings field, which is defensible for clinical record data where sensitivity rather than distressing content is the concern, and the sensitive_elements content covers the ground.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews[0].review_details: 'Ethics is one of three project pillars (Ethical and Trustworthy AI). The project performs community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing, evaluates community perspectives on clinical care AI to increase trustworthiness of provenance and privacy, establishes a legal framework for collecting data at scale, and analyzes the existing legal and regulatory landscape.' participant_privacy[0].notes: patient-focused efforts determine ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias 'while accounting for social determinants of health'. purposes: 'ensuring the methods promote privacy, accountability, and clinical benefit'. A structured ethics programme is documented with named activities that bear directly on societal impact: community focus groups deciding what is appropriate to share, evaluation of public perspectives on clinical AI, and analysis of the legal and regulatory landscape. That is more than a compliance statement and is useful to a reuser assessing the dataset's social positioning. Scored differently from Element 4 sub-element 1 by design: that sub-element asks for oversight of record (IRB, approval, DPIA), which is absent, whereas this one asks for ethical review activity and social impact analysis, which is present in substance. The analysis remains process-level — no future_use_impacts field, no anticipated downstream harms or mitigations for deployed models trained on the data — which is logged as part of the bias and impact completeness issue.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: No publisher field. Hosting is described only in prose within description and distribution_formats: 'OMOP and telemetry data are worked with inside the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud enclave' and 'CHoRUS services are deployed on Azure through dockerized container applications'. No PhysioNet, Dataverse, Zenodo or institutional repository record exists for the dataset. No publishing organization or repository of record is declared. The Bridge2AI enclave is named as the analysis environment, but a reuser cannot identify who publishes the dataset, under whose curation it sits, or where a catalogue record would be found — which also removes the long-term stewardship guarantees a recognized repository would supply. An accountable_organization (Massachusetts General Hospital) is recorded under data_governance, which addresses accountability rather than publication; it is credited there, not repurposed here. The waveform metadata is described as 'the PhysioNet schema extended', which indicates standards borrowing, not PhysioNet publication.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: No citation field. No doi field. The only citable handles are the NIH award (OT2OD032701) and its RePORTER record (https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824), plus the project homepage used as id. notes records the NIH disclaimer language but no attribution or citation instruction. A user who publishes on this dataset has no recommended citation, no DOI, and no versioned handle to reference — for a federally funded resource whose purpose includes external validation and marketplace adoption of models, so that credit and reproducible reference matter directly. Citing the grant number is not citing the dataset. Consistent with Element 1 sub-element 1, which fails on the same absent persistent identifier; the two failures are the same underlying gap observed against different requirements (unique identification versus citable cross-reference) and are each scored once.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to: OMOP Common Data Model for structured EHR (with extensions for nursing flowsheets), DICOM for PACS imaging, WFDB with an extended PhysioNet metadata schema for telemetry, EDF+ and Persyst for EEG, and the OHNLP open source schema for tokenized notes. conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]. conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema ; conforms_to_class: Dataset. file_collections repeat the conformance per collection. Conformance to five distinct community standards, declared per modality and repeated consistently at collection level, plus conformance of the metadata record itself to the Bridge2AI data sheets schema. This is the dataset's strongest ecosystem link and is what makes cross-institutional harmonization plausible. Standards are correctly named and correctly matched to their modalities, and the two declared extensions (OMOP flowsheet extensions, extended PhysioNet waveform metadata) are disclosed rather than hidden behind a bare conformance claim — important, because an extended schema is not interchangeable with the base standard. The extension content itself is not specified.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: page: https://chorus4ai.org/ with pages 'on the team, project overview, tools, data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset, and learning resources'. external_resources: the AIM-AHEAD cohort-2 informational webinar PDF describing the dataset snapshot and trainee access route; the chorus-ai GitHub organization with SOP repositories (Chorus_SOP, data_acq_SOP) and a developer web guide (chorus-developer); the NIH RePORTER record. extension_mechanism: contribution route via chorus-mapping plus Standards and Data Acquisition discussion spaces. Documentation and outreach are genuinely multi-channel: a landing site with a learning-resources section, a training-programme webinar, SOP and developer documentation repositories, and open discussion spaces where contributing sites raise issues. A newcomer has several viable entry points. All links are plausible and purpose-annotated; one entry lacks a URI scheme ('www.bridge2ai.org/chorus'). The notes field quotes a site banner indicating the content is under review for potential modification, a stability caveat on these links that the record surfaces rather than suppresses.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: No related_datasets field. The description positions the project as 'one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded Bridge2AI consortium', and splits refers to a planned sequestered holdout, but neither is expressed as a typed relationship to another dataset. No relationship of any type — supplements, is version of, derives from, is part of — is recorded. The consortium siblings, the planned holdout partition, and the relationship between the current 50,000-admission release and the anticipated 100,000-admission dataset are all left as prose a machine cannot traverse. Same underlying absence as Element 1 sub-element 5, evaluated here against ecosystem integration rather than discovery hierarchy. was_derived_from records provenance to clinical source systems, not to other datasets, so it does not supply the missing typed dataset relationships.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: id: https://chorus4ai.org/ ; no doi field; no RRID anywhere in the record. page: https://chorus4ai.org/ is the identical string. No persistent identifier. The only identifier is the project homepage URL, reused verbatim as the landing page, which identifies the programme rather than this dataset; the record's own source_caveats notes the site is 'under review for potential modification', undercutting any persistence claim. conforms_to_schema carries a w3id PURL, but that identifies the metadata schema, not the dataset. DOI pattern 10.XXXX/... : absent. RRID pattern RRID:SCR_/AB_ : absent. URI resolves but is not dataset-specific and is not registered with a persistence authority; subset ids are fragments under the same homepage.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI'; description of ~1,500 characters naming 14 contributing hospitals within 20 academic centres, per-modality standards (OMOP, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+/Persyst, OHNLP), released volumes (50,000 admissions, 1.6B OMOP rows, 7,642 admissions with radiology, 23 Tb waveform), and the project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30. Far beyond the 200-character threshold and dense with specifics rather than boilerplate: it states what the data are, where they came from, how they are standardized, how much exists now versus anticipated, and what is still in process (imaging deidentification, EEG extraction). Description content is semantically appropriate for a multimodal critical-care EHR dataset and is consistent with keywords, instances, subsets and distribution_formats; no overclaiming — released and anticipated figures are distinguished.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: critical care; intensive care unit; acute illness; electronic health record; OMOP Common Data Model; waveform telemetry; electroencephalography; medical imaging; clinical notes; social determinants of health; AI-ready dataset; Bridge2AI; multimodal data; controlled access (14 terms). Well above the 5-keyword threshold and spanning four distinct facets: clinical domain, data modality, standard, and access regime. Each term is discriminating rather than generic. Every keyword is corroborated elsewhere in the record (OMOP in conforms_to, EEG in subsets, SDOH in purposes/preprocessing geocoding, controlled access in license_and_use_terms), so keywords are not decorative. 'Bridge2AI' supplies the programme context from a quoted value rather than from filename or prior knowledge.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://chorus4ai.org/ ; external_resources describes the site as having 'pages on the team, project overview, tools, data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset, and learning resources'; nine hierarchical subsets with ids such as https://chorus4ai.org/#subset-waveform-telemetry. An accessible, well-structured landing page is given, and hierarchical structure is expressed through nine typed modality subsets each carrying its own id, description and standard. The dedicated resources slot is unused, but subsets carry equivalent hierarchical content. URL is well-formed and the domain matches the project name and title. Noted in issues: the same URL doubles as the dataset id, which is why sub-element 1 fails while this one passes.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: No parent_datasets field; no related_datasets field. description states CHoRUS is 'one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded Bridge2AI consortium' and external_resources links a Bridge2AI project page, but no dataset-to-dataset relationship is typed. Programme membership is narrated in prose but no parent, sibling or derived dataset is declared as a structured relationship. The three sibling Bridge2AI data generation datasets, which the description itself invokes, are not linked. Prose mention of a consortium is not a typed relationship; no relationship predicate (isPartOf, supplements, isVersionOf) appears anywhere in the record.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Controlled access to all data types. Participants must sign a licensing agreement, included in the registration form, before gaining access... a ".edu" email address is required'; ip_restrictions.restrictions: 'chorus-ai GitHub organization's software is released under the MIT License, with individual repositories also listing Apache-2.0; dataset access is separately governed by a licensing agreement'. The access regime is stated concretely (controlled access, signed agreement bundled into registration, institutional email requirement) and the record makes the non-obvious but correct distinction between the MIT/Apache licensing of project code and the agreement governing the clinical data. Consistent with confidential_elements ('Every data type is listed with controlled access'), data_governance.access_review_process, and third_party_sharing.is_shared=true. The software-vs-data licence separation is semantically correct and explicitly caveated rather than conflated.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: data_governance.committee_contact: {id: https://chorus4ai.org/#person-jared-houghtaling, name: Jared Houghtaling, email: jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org}; data_governance.accountable_organization: Massachusetts General Hospital; data_governance.access_review_process describes request routing to dbold@emory.edu or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org and a registration/provisioning workflow; confidential_elements.confidentiality_details: 'Every data type is listed with controlled access. OMOP and telemetry data sit in the enclave; clinical notes are not placed in the enclave but stored locally at contributing sites, with only tokens shared.' The governance-contact evidence path enumerated for this sub-element is fully populated with a named, contactable person plus an accountable organization and a described review process, and confidentiality is classified unambiguously and per-modality. What is absent is the regulatory layer itself. Fails the regulatory half: regulatory_restrictions, confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant and other_compliance are all absent for PHI-derived data from US hospitals — flagged as a high-severity content_accuracy issue. Scored 1 on the strength of the governance-contact and confidentiality evidence the sub-element explicitly enumerates; the missing HIPAA determination is recorded as an issue rather than double-counted here.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: No download_url field. The only URLs in the record are page (https://chorus4ai.org/), external_resources (https://github.com/chorus-ai, www.bridge2ai.org/chorus) and extension_mechanism.contribution_url (https://github.com/chorus-ai). Access is described only in prose: 'Access requests are directed to the contacts published in the chorus-ai GitHub README: dbold@emory.edu or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org.' No download link and no link to an access portal, application form, or enclave sign-in. Controlled access does not excuse this: a request form or portal URL is the expected artifact, and the record instead routes users to two email addresses. Prose instructions exist but the sub-element asks for a retrievable locator. Consistent with the controlled-access posture, so this is a documentation gap rather than a contradiction; but combined with the absent DOI and publisher, there is no machine-actionable route to the data from this record.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats: five entries — DICOM ('Imaging drawn from PACS'), WFDB ('Waveform telemetry... held in the enclave'), 'EDF+ and Persyst' (EEG), 'OMOP Common Data Model' (structured EHR), 'OHNLP' (tokenized notes), each with notes; per-subset conforms_to on all nine subsets. Three genuine, specific file formats (DICOM, WFDB, EDF+/Persyst) are named and bound to the modalities they carry. The two remaining entries are standards rather than formats, and the record says so itself in per-entry source_caveats. Format names are used correctly for their modalities (DICOM for PACS imaging, WFDB for monitor telemetry, EDF+/Persyst for clinical EEG) — technically appropriate choices. No media_type or encoding on any entry; OMOP/OHNLP mis-typed as formats, disclosed in source_caveats and recorded as a low-severity issue.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: external_resources: three entries — CHoRUS project website (https://chorus4ai.org/) with page inventory; chorus-ai GitHub organization (https://github.com/chorus-ai) describing 28 repositories and naming thirteen of them (chorus-container-apps, privacy_scan_tool, chorus_waveform, chorus_waveform_resources, Chorus_SOP, data_acq_SOP, CTP-deid, UF-Geocoding, CHoRUSReports, chorus-extract-upload, chorus-apps-internal, cloud_public, CADA) with a licence restriction note; CHoRUS page on the Bridge2AI website. External resources are exceptionally well developed: named repositories mapped to functions (deidentification, privacy scanning, waveform conversion, geocoding, SOPs), which is what makes the processing chain in Element 8 auditable. related_datasets is absent, but this sub-element is satisfied by either field and external_resources carries substantial content. Repository names are internally consistent with the tools cited in preprocessing_strategies and collection_mechanisms (chorus_waveform, UF-Geocoding, Chorus_SOP, chorus-extract-upload), so the link inventory is corroborated rather than decorative. One locator, 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus', lacks a URI scheme.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: controlled access, a signed licensing agreement included in the registration form, and a '.edu' email requirement with administrator assistance; source_caveats separating the MIT licence of the code repositories from the dataset's access agreement. Specific and non-boilerplate: a reader learns exactly what gate stands between them and the data and who is eligible. What is not conveyed is the substance of the agreement — redistribution, publication, and commercial-use rights are unstated — so downstream rights cannot be determined from the record alone. No conflict between the software licence and the data terms; the record actively prevents the common error of reading the repository MIT licence as covering the clinical data. Restrictiveness is consistent with the sensitivity documented in sensitive_elements and is_deidentified.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats: DICOM, WFDB, EDF+ and Persyst, OMOP Common Data Model, OHNLP; conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]; each of the nine subsets carries conforms_to and conforms_to_standard (e.g. Waveform telemetry → WFDB; Imaging → DICOM; Clinical notes → OHNLP). Every modality is bound to a recognized community standard, and the binding is repeated at subset granularity so a reuser knows which standard governs which slice. Character encoding is nowhere specified, and no media types are given. Format-to-modality assignments are technically correct and mutually consistent across conforms_to, conforms_to_standard, distribution_formats and subsets. The OTHER enum is used honestly for EDF+/Persyst and OHNLP, which have no dedicated enum value.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to: 'OMOP Common Data Model for structured EHR data (demographics, medication administration, procedures, diagnoses and nursing flowsheets); DICOM for imaging; WFDB for waveform telemetry; EDF+ and Persyst for waveform EEG; OHNLP for extracted and tokenized clinical notes'; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; conforms_to_standard enum list. Conformance is stated at four levels — prose mapping per modality, controlled enum values, the metadata schema URI, and the schema class — which is materially more than a bare standard name and directly supports integration with other OMOP or DICOM holdings. OMOP CDM is the semantically appropriate standard for the structured content types listed, and the per-modality assignment is internally consistent with subsets and preprocessing_strategies (which names chorus-mapping's validated semantic mappings as the route to OMOP). The w3id PURL is well-formed.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: No variables field anywhere in the record. subsets name content categories (Demographics, Medication administration, Procedures, Nursing flowsheets, Diagnoses, Clinical notes, Imaging, Waveform telemetry, Waveform EEG) but define no variables, identifiers, units, value sets or permissible values. For a dataset of 1.6 billion rows the absence of any variable-level metadata is the single largest interoperability gap. A reuser cannot determine which OMOP tables and fields are populated, which vocabularies are used for concept codes, or which flowsheet measures are present. Conformance to OMOP is asserted, which implies an external specification exists, but the record does not state which CDM version, which tables are instantiated, or what site-specific extensions exist — so the standard reference does not substitute for variable metadata.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: three use_category entries — 'Clinical AI/ML model development' (characterizing critical illness, predicting complications, measuring treatment response), 'External model validation' (against a sequestered holdout), 'Education and workforce development' (AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI training programme, with usage_notes clarifying that as of the source webinar no trainees had been selected); existing_uses; other_tasks (canonical Jupyter notebooks, OHDSI tool-stack workshops). Intended use is documented with unusual precision, including a usage_note that correctly distinguishes an announced programme from a use in progress. prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses are both absent, which for critically ill patients including minors under a signed agreement is a genuine omission recorded as an issue. Intended uses align with tasks and purposes and do not overclaim beyond what the access regime permits. No prohibition on re-identification is stated anywhere, which sits awkwardly with is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present=true.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews.review_details: 'The project performs community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing, and evaluates community perspectives on clinical care AI to find ways to increase trustworthiness of provenance and privacy in AI'; human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: true with special_populations naming PICU and NICU admissions; data_governance.accountable_organization: Massachusetts General Hospital; data_governance.committee_contact: Jared Houghtaling with email; data_governance.access_review_process describing the access review workflow. Scored on the institutional-oversight and governance-contact evidence the sub-element explicitly enumerates: a named accountable organization, a named and contactable governance representative, a described access review process, and a documented ethics workstream. This is substantive and specific, not boilerplate. It is nonetheless not IRB documentation, and the record says so plainly in its own source_caveats. Semantic check triggered (involves_human_subjects=true) and the field is populated, but with ethics activities rather than oversight of collection: no IRB, no protocol number, no waiver, and data_protection_impacts absent entirely for a multi-site PHI enclave. Recorded as a high-severity consistency issue. The record's explicit refusal to assert a reviewing organization it cannot evidence is the correct handling of the gap.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: true; is_deidentified.method: 'Extraction and tokenization of unstructured EHR text with the OHNLP toolkit; de-identification of imaging, in process for the larger cohort as of September 2025; transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification'; is_deidentified.deidentification_details: 'De-identification is combined with controlled access rather than relied on alone... Identifiable source material remains at the contributing sites, where clinical note text is stored locally and only tokens are shared.' Two concrete mechanisms are named — OHNLP tokenization of note text and the architectural control that identifiable source text never leaves the contributing site — plus honest reporting that imaging deidentification was still in process. That is specific technique, not a generic claim. Coverage is the weakness: nothing is said about the structured OMOP data, and no standard of record is named. Method appropriateness is partially assessable: tokenization is a suitable technique for free text and is consistent with the local-retention architecture described across five other fields. But identifiable_elements_present=true with no Safe Harbor/Expert Determination determination and no stated treatment of dates, geography (the record geocodes Locations via DeGauss) or rare diagnoses leaves the residual identifiability of the largest component unexplained — recorded as a medium-severity content_accuracy issue.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy.anonymization_method: 'Tokenization of clinical note text, imaging de-identification, and transformations designed to limit re-identification'; participant_privacy.privacy_techniques: 'A privacy scan tool for medical records is maintained by the project, alongside controlled access to all data types' (corroborated by the privacy_scan_tool repository listed in external_resources); participant_privacy.reidentification_risk: 'The project describes transforming data using approaches that limit re-identification, and patient-focused efforts to determine ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy.' Protections are real and named — a maintained privacy scan tool, tokenization, imaging deidentification, controlled access — and the tool is independently traceable to a repository. The risk-assessment half is not delivered: the reidentification_risk value restates mitigation rather than characterizing residual risk. Scored 1 because the sub-element's primary field carries substantive, corroborated technique; the vacuous risk statement is recorded as an issue. Consistency check: data_protection_impacts is absent, so the DPIA→risk-assessment expectation cannot be evaluated; the standalone risk statement is circular. No re-identification vector analysis despite three vectors visible in the record itself (geocoded Locations, high-resolution waveform timing, rare-diagnosis ICU cohorts).

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: No informed_consent field in the record. The nearest content is direct_collection.is_direct: false — 'Data are not collected from individuals for the purpose of this dataset; they are retrospectively extracted from clinical source systems' — and human_subject_research.notes, which describes retrospective assembly from clinical records but says nothing about consent, waiver, or authorization. Entirely undocumented. Retrospective EHR research normally proceeds under an IRB waiver of consent and a HIPAA waiver of authorization; either would be straightforward to state, and neither appears. A reader cannot determine on what legal basis 50,000 patients' records, including those of neonates and children, were assembled and shared. Consistency check FAILED: involves_human_subjects=true → consent procedures expected. Compounded by at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included=true covering PICU and NICU admissions, where parental permission or its waiver is the relevant construct and is likewise unaddressed. High-severity issue.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: true; special_protections: 'All data types are under controlled access; clinical notes remain at the contributing sites except for tokens, and data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification'; notes: 'Pediatric and neonatal intensive care admissions are within scope, and the population consists of acutely and critically ill patients'; corroborated by human_subject_research.special_populations and by three subpopulations entries (adult ICU, PICU, NICU). participant_compensation absent. Vulnerability is identified precisely and on two independent axes — developmental (paediatric, neonatal) and clinical (acute critical illness, a population unable to consent contemporaneously) — and concrete protections are attached rather than asserted generically. The absence of participant_compensation is semantically appropriate, not a gap: direct_collection.is_direct=false establishes that no one was recruited or enrolled, so there is nothing to compensate. Consistency check PASSED (at_risk_groups_included=true → special_protections present). The identification of vulnerable groups without any corresponding consent or assent documentation is scored against sub-element 4, not repeated here.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations: three entries, each with subpopulation_elements_present: true and an identification rule — 'Adult intensive care unit (ICU) admissions, identified by the care setting of the admission', likewise PICU and NICU; subsets carry explicit is_subpopulation: false on all nine modality slices; description and instances confirm ICU/PICU/NICU as the cohort frame. Subpopulations are enumerated with an explicit identification criterion (care setting of admission) rather than merely named, and the false subpopulation flags on the nine modality subsets correctly signal that those slices are modality partitions, not cohort strata. Missing: demographic composition and per-subpopulation counts. Care-setting-based stratification is semantically coherent for a critical-care dataset and is consistent across description, subpopulations and human_subject_research.special_populations. For a project titled 'for Equitable AI' with SDOH in keywords, the absence of any demographic distribution is a notable omission, recorded as a low-severity issue.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances: 'Patient admission from an ICU, PICU or NICU setting' counts: 50000; 'Row of OMOP-standardized electronic health record data' counts: 1600000000 with a description noting the website states '1.6 Billion' and that the integer is that magnitude expanded to units; 'Admission accompanied by radiology imaging data' counts: 7642; 'Bedside monitor waveform telemetry recording' with '23 Tb of waveform data'. Four instance types with three exact counts, each tied to a defined unit of observation, plus an explicit note on how an approximate published figure was converted to an integer. Volume is reported per modality rather than as a single headline number, which is what a reuser needs. Counts are mutually plausible: 7,642 radiology admissions is a subset of 50,000 admissions; 1.6B rows across 50,000 admissions is ~32,000 rows per admission, consistent with high-frequency nursing flowsheet and medication-administration data. The 50,000 vs. 45K discrepancy between sources and the admissions-vs-images unit mismatch for imaging are disclosed in source_caveats rather than hidden — a documented low-severity inconsistency handled transparently. The waveform entry carries volume but no recording count.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: variables: absent. is_tabular: absent. subsets.is_data_split: false on all nine subsets; subsets.is_subpopulation: false on all nine. splits.split_details: 'The project states that the dataset will also provision a holdout test set... sequestering holdout datasets for external validation is described as a planned project activity rather than a released partition.' Two of the three named components are entirely missing. The explicit false flags are meaningful documentation and are credited as such — they correctly state that no released subset is a split or a stratum — but they convey only negative information, and the one split that is contemplated is explicitly not released. With no variable metadata and no tabular flag for 1.6 billion rows of tabular OMOP data, a reader cannot understand the dataset's internal structure. The false split flags are semantically consistent with splits.split_details describing the holdout as planned — no contradiction. But is_tabular is unset despite the structured OMOP component being paradigmatically tabular, and no data dictionary, CDM version, or vocabulary specification is offered. High-severity completeness issue.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances carry data_topic codes B2AI_TOPIC:4, B2AI_TOPIC:9, B2AI_TOPIC:15, B2AI_TOPIC:37 and data_substrate codes B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37 (EHR rows), B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11 (imaging), B2AI_SUBSTRATE:49 (waveform); instance_type values name admissions, OMOP rows, radiology-accompanied admissions and telemetry recordings; description and keywords cover critical care, acute illness, SDOH; nine subsets enumerate the content domains (demographics, medications, procedures, flowsheets, diagnoses, notes, imaging, telemetry, EEG). Topic coverage is expressed both as controlled ontology codes and as human-readable content domains across nine subsets, which together make the represented subject matter clear. No disease or phenotype breakdown is offered — the cohort is defined by care setting rather than by condition — so a user cannot tell which clinical conditions are represented or in what proportion. Substrate codes are assigned consistently with the modality of each instance type. The CURIEs are unresolved and unlabelled with no link to the B2AI vocabulary, reducing human readability — recorded as a low-severity issue.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: anomalies: absent. missing_data_documentation: absent. sampling_strategies is present (is_sample: true; 'Sampling to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies; federated access is intended to enable sampling methods that ensure a balanced and diverse cohort') but carries its own source_caveats: 'The bundle states the sampling intent but does not describe the executed sampling frame, inclusion criteria, or any verification of representativeness.' None of the three things this sub-element asks for is documented. The only populated field describes sampling intent and then explicitly disclaims knowledge of what was actually executed, so it does not tell a user anything about the quality of the data they would receive. For retrospective EHR, flowsheet and waveform data, missingness, device artifact and charting irregularity are the defining quality characteristics and none are addressed. Inconsistent with cleaning_strategies, which states that 'Characterization reports are produced and returned to contributing sites following their data submissions, allowing sites to identify and resolve issues in their extracts' — quality findings demonstrably exist within the project but none are surfaced to data users. Medium-severity completeness issue.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: No version field anywhere in the record. status: released; distribution_dates.release_dates describes 'A released dataset... available to approved users as of August 2025... a Current Released Dataset alongside an Anticipated Final Dataset', but no version string, tag or edition label is given. A released, growing, controlled-access dataset with no version identifier. Because the content demonstrably changes over time (imaging deidentification in process, EEG extraction in process, admissions growing toward 100,000), the absence of a version makes it impossible for a user to state which state of the data an analysis used. Consistency check FAILED: status=released with distribution_dates populated but no version. The record's own 'Current Released Dataset' versus 'Anticipated Final Dataset' distinction presupposes versioned states that are never labelled.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: No version_access field. No statement anywhere about whether prior states of the dataset remain retrievable, whether the enclave preserves snapshots, or how an approved user would request a specific past state. Entirely absent. This compounds the missing version number: not only is the current state unlabelled, there is no indication that any earlier state is preserved or reachable, which is a reproducibility problem for the training programme and publications the record says are already using the data. Consistency check FAILED against existing_uses ('The datasets are being used for training activities and publications') — published analyses are being produced against an unversioned, unsnapshotted moving target.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: errata: absent. updates.update_details describes forward-looking growth ('The dataset is growing toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities... imaging de-identification was in process for a larger cohort and EEG extraction was in process; contributing sites provide regular status updates on their extract progress'), but no change log, no description of what changed between states, and no corrections. The record documents change that is underway but nothing that has happened: no history of what the released dataset contained at earlier points, what was added or corrected, or what errors have been found and fixed. Given that cleaning_strategies describes characterization reports driving site-level corrections, corrections evidently occur and none are reported. The updates content is credited under sub-element 4 (update schedule/plan), which is the purpose it actually serves; it does not constitute change descriptions or errata. No contradiction, but a real gap for a dataset already in published use.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.update_details: 'The dataset is growing toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals. As of the September 2025 webinar, imaging de-identification was in process for a larger cohort and EEG extraction was in process; contributing sites provide regular status updates on their extract progress, tracked on the Standards and Data Acquisition project boards.' Bounded by the funded project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 in funders.grants. A substantive maintenance plan rather than a cadence: it states the target end-state (100,000 admissions, 9 modalities), which modalities are actively expanding, the mechanism by which progress is tracked (named project boards), and — via the funding period — the horizon within which growth is expected.
