text: license: 'Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License'; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: general_research_use; intended_uses: 'intended solely for commercial and non-commercial research purposes by Authorized Researchers'. Reuse is permitted for both commercial and non-commercial research, with the boundary conditions stated (no resale, no re-identification, duplication for the project permitted, no fees). The permission (general_research_use) is consistent with informed_consent.consent_scope, which states the consent does not restrict use to non-commercial purposes or to a research type — an unusually well-closed consent-to-license chain.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats: TSV, JSON, Apache Parquet described as 'an open-source column-oriented data file format'; file_collections.resources.format: TSV with media_type text/tab-separated-values; every data file paired with a JSON data dictionary sharing its file stem. All three formats are open and standard, and the dictionary-per-file convention makes the tables self-describing. Character encoding is nowhere stated, which is a real gap for TSV interchange; it is outweighed here by the format specificity and the dictionary convention, and is recorded as a low-severity completeness issue.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry ontology CURIEs data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:25 / B2AI_TOPIC:36 and data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41 / B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30; labeling_strategies.data_annotation_protocol: 'Per Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10 codes'. Conformance is stated at three levels — the metadata record's own schema, Bridge2AI topic/substrate ontology terms on instances, and ICD-10 for diagnostic labels. Partly qualified: source_caveats states that the 3.1.0 release 'does not state conformance to any data standard, so no standard is asserted for this release', explicitly declining to carry the earlier BIDS v1.9.0 claim forward. The stated conformances are real and correctly scoped; the honest non-assertion of a data standard is recorded as a low-severity semantic issue rather than a fabrication.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: variables: participant_id (identifier, is_identifier: true), session_id (identifier, is_identifier: true), task_name (categorical), n_frames (integer), each with a description; file_collections describes 'a JSON data dictionary sharing its file stem, giving a description of each column, the question asked of the participant where applicable, and the data type'. The linking keys — which are what cross-file and cross-dataset integration depends on — are defined with explicit identifier flags, and the per-file dictionaries are documented as the route to column-level semantics. participant_id and session_id are consistently referenced in distribution_formats, file_collections and participant_privacy.data_linkage, so the declared keys match the described linkage. Coverage is thin relative to the phenotype tables (low-severity completeness issue).

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses (two entries, research, with examples AI model pretraining/fine-tuning/benchmarking/validation); discouraged_uses ('hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustments, or any form of surveillance'); prohibited_uses (three entries: re-identification attempts, uses causing harm or stigmatization, IP claims restricting access). All three categories are populated and each prohibition carries a stated reason rather than a bare rule. Guidance is internally coherent with future_use_impacts, which names the same misuse scenarios, and with ip_restrictions, which encodes the third prohibition contractually.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews.reviewing_organization: University of South Florida Institutional Review Board, with review_details covering the Single IRB process, subsite IRBs and separate Canadian REB applications; human_subject_research.irb_approval repeats this and ethics_review_board names USF IRB; data_governance names the Data Access Compliance Office. Oversight is described at the level a replicator needs: which IRB, which mechanism (Single IRB), how non-US sites were handled, and where approval copies were filed. Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by populated IRB detail. A content-accuracy warning is recorded because data_protection_impacts states that no impact analysis on data subjects was conducted, which is a governance gap for biometric and mental-health data even though the IRB record is strong.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.method: 'HIPAA Safe Harbor, supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers and of non-identifying but highly sensitive fields, and by withholding of all raw audio'; identifiers_removed enumerates the Safe Harbor categories plus state/province, household composition, income, mental health status and traumatic life experiences; deidentification_details records transcript review, removal of recordings with external voices, and 'K-anonymization with k of two or more is not achieved'. A named method, an explicit list of removed identifier classes, and a candid statement of the residual limitation — the strongest sub-element in the record. Method is appropriate to the data type: Safe Harbor addresses tabular phenotype data, and withholding raw audio addresses the biometric channel that Safe Harbor cannot. The is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present=false boolean reads more absolutely than the k<2 admission (low-severity consistency warning).

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy.anonymization_method, privacy_techniques (four listed, including removal of transcripts and derived representations of free speech), reidentification_risk: 'Voice is unique to the speaker and cannot be fully de-identified ... K-anonymization with k of two or more is not achieved for the released tables', data_linkage describing the participant identifier and EHR access for gold-standard validation. A genuine risk assessment rather than an assurance: it names the residual risk, the reason it cannot be eliminated, and the contractual control (recipients barred from contacting subjects) that substitutes for technical mitigation. Consistency check passes: data_protection_impacts present and reidentification_risk assessed. The assessment is proportionate to sensitive_elements, which flags voice as a biometric identifier.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true; consent_type: prospective written consent on paper, via REDCap e-consent, or by video of the participant reading the statement, with assent where applicable; consent_documentation: REDCap storage for a minimum of five years; consent_scope covering registered vs controlled sharing and the absence of commercial/geographic/method restrictions; withdrawal_mechanism; plus collection_consents, consent_revocations and collection_notifications. Consent is documented end to end, including the operationally important boundary that data cannot be removed once voice collection is complete and that withdrawal before completion excludes the data. Consistency check passes: IRB documented and consent procedures also described. consent_scope matches license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission (general_research_use) — the permission granted downstream does not exceed the permission obtained upstream.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations.special_protections (adults only, 18-120; pediatric participants released separately; assent option for adults unable to consent; discomfort risk in mood/psychiatric instruments) and assent_procedures; participant_compensation: electronic gift cards, '40 US dollars for a session under 90 minutes and 80 US dollars for over 90 minutes ... maximum compensation of 120 US dollars'. Compensation is quantified with its schedule and cap, and the at-risk discussion identifies the specific populations at issue (cognitive impairment, dementia, mood and psychiatric diagnoses) rather than asserting none. at_risk_populations is consistent with human_subject_research.special_populations, which states the same age bounds and the same assent provision; source_caveats correctly declines to assert whether assent-enrolled participants appear in this release.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations.subpopulation_elements_present: true; identification: 'Age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status are recorded, and participants are assigned to disease cohort categories — voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders — or to the control group'; distribution: 'do not contain an equal distribution of the disease categories, and the dataset has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors'; sampling_strategies gives per-diagnosis inclusion/exclusion screening. Cohort structure and the recorded demographic dimensions are explicit, and the skew is disclosed. Actual counts or proportions per cohort are not given, which limits a reader's ability to judge fit before download. Consistent with known_biases.representation_bias, which states the same skew, and with the phenotype directory listing, which enumerates the per-condition diagnosis tables that carry the cohort assignment.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances[0].counts: 833 human participants; instances[1].notes: 'torchaudio pitch 32,522; sparc periodicity and sparc pitch 31,872 each; sparc loudness 31,855; phonetic posteriorgrams 29,289; spectrogram, Mel spectrogram and MFCC 29,278 each; sparc EMA 28,640'; per-file counts repeated in file_collections.resources. Counts are given at both participant and recording-derivative level, with an explanation of why feature counts differ and an explicit refusal to invent a single recording total. Counts are internally consistent between instances.notes and the eleven file_collections resource descriptions. The 833 figure is attributed to 3.1.0 but sourced from v3.0 documentation per source_caveats (low-severity content-accuracy issue).

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: variables (4 entries with data_type and is_identifier); splits: 'No recommended train, validation or test splits are predefined. Researchers are encouraged to create their own data splits'; subpopulations.subpopulation_elements_present: true; relationships describes the session-within-participant grouping and multiple rows per participant. The split question is answered explicitly rather than left blank, and the session/participant nesting — which is exactly what an incautious modeller would get wrong — is called out. is_tabular is not set, although the record distributes TSV phenotype tables and dense Parquet tensors, a mixture that would have been worth flagging explicitly (low-severity completeness issue).

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances[*].data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:25 and B2AI_TOPIC:36; data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41 and B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30; file_collections phenotype description enumerates eighteen diagnosis tables (airway stenosis, ALS, anxiety, benign lesions, bipolar disorder, cognitive impairment, control, COPD and asthma, depression, glottic insufficiency, laryngeal cancer, laryngeal dystonia, laryngitis, muscle tension dysphonia, Parkinson's disease, precancerous lesions, unexplained chronic cough, unilateral vocal fold paralysis) and fourteen questionnaire instruments. Condition coverage is enumerated at the level of individual diagnoses and validated instruments, not just cohort families. The enumerated conditions map coherently onto the four cohort families named in description and subpopulations; ontology CURIEs are used in the correct slots.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: anomalies (three entries: differing site configurations and protocol change over time; noise artifacts and diagnostic-practice variation; headset distance variation and single-clinician diagnosis); sampling_strategies (is_sample true, is_representative false, why_not_representative); missing_data_documentation with missing_data_patterns, missing_data_causes and handling_strategy ('a missingness table is included with the dataset'); cleaning_strategies releases audio_quality_metrics.tsv. Missing-data documentation distinguishes structural absence (cohort-specific branching, optional items) from incidental loss (collection irregularities, features that could not be generated), which is the distinction a reanalyst needs. missing_data_patterns is consistent with the differing per-feature record counts in instances.notes — the stated cause (features that could not be generated, sensitive records withheld) explains the observed count spread.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: '3.1.0'; title-level and page-level agreement (https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/); issued: 2026-05-01. Semantic version, pinned in the landing page URL and matched to a release date. Version, page path, issued date and the last entry of distribution_dates all agree.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access.versions_available lists five releases with dates and DOIs where known ('1.1 — 17 January 2025 — doi:10.13026/249v-w155' ... '3.1.0 — 1 May 2026 — doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'); version_details: 'Each version ... has a unique DOI, and by default older versions continue to be supported ... The files for version 1.1 are no longer available from PhysioNet. Version 1.0 was published on the Health Data Nexus platform under doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84'. Both the policy (older versions supported by default, publishers reserve removal rights) and the actual exception (1.1 files withdrawn) are stated, which is more useful than the policy alone. Failed consistency check: latest_version_doi (doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42) matches none of the listed version DOIs and conflicts with the record's own 3.1.0 DOI. The sub-element still documents version access substantively, so the defect is recorded as a medium-severity issue rather than a zero.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: errata.erratum_details: 'Version 2.0 reprocessed the spectrograms to fix minor issues ... and removed all spectrograms and MFCCs derived from free-speech files. Version 2.0.1 corrected the authorship list. Version 3.1.0 fixed broken parquet files carried over from the previous release, updated validated diagnosis information ... rearranged some phenotypic files and renamed certain gold standard variable names.' Per-version, change-level detail including breaking changes (renamed gold-standard variables, rearranged phenotype files) that would silently break downstream code. source_caveats correctly notes that the project healthsheet claims no erratum exists and that these entries were reconstructed from per-version release notes — the provenance of the claim is disclosed.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.update_details: 'further versions ... will be released on a semi-annual (twice a year) basis ... with users notified through news items on the hosting platform ... that statement is a plan written against the Health Data Nexus platform and an earlier release, not an observed cadence', followed by the list of six published versions with dates. Both the stated cadence and the observed release history are given, with an explicit warning not to read the plan as an observation. The observed history (Jan 2025, Apr 2025, Aug 2025, Dec 2025, May 2026) is roughly consistent with the semi-annual plan for major versions; notification channel is named.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: was_derived_from: 'Raw audio recordings ... captured by the Bridge2AI-Voice tablet application, together with questionnaire and clinical data captured in REDCap, collected under the Bridge2AI Voice Data Acquisition protocol'; raw_data_sources (two entries with source_type, raw_data_format and access_details, including the Synapse accession); updates.update_details carries the release history; related_datasets.derives_from syn72370534. The derivation chain is complete and traversable: raw WAV and REDCap export, named preprocessing library, released feature tables, with the raw tier's access route given. was_derived_from, raw_data_sources and the derives_from relationship name the same source consistently; b2aiprep appears as the transforming agent in all three places.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes (three entries, including 'To generate a large multi-institutional, ethically sourced and diverse voice dataset linked to multimodal health biomarkers'); addressing_gaps (three entries naming the specific deficiencies: small sample sizes, absent collection standards, no linkage to multi-modal health data). Motivation is paired with an explicit gap analysis, so the rationale is falsifiable rather than aspirational. Purposes align with the funding programme named in funders (NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI, whose stated aim is AI-ready datasets) — the funding-to-purpose consistency check passes.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: 'Training machine-learning models for disease detection and classification using voice data, with labels drawn from diagnostic categories ...' and 'Screening, diagnosis and monitoring of health conditions through voice biomarkers'; other_tasks.task_details describes cohort selection from the phenotype tables. Tasks are specific enough to be actionable (named label families, named downstream use of the phenotype tables). Tasks are consistent with intended_uses.examples (pretraining, fine-tuning, benchmarking, validation) and with the labelling described in labeling_strategies.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders.grantor: 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund, Bridge2AI Program'; grants[1].notes identifies the parent award as held at the University of South Florida with Yael Emilie Bensoussan as PI, 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30, FY2025 award 4,660,942 US dollars. Agency, programme, mechanism (Other Transaction OT2), holding institution, period and award amount are all present. The OT2 activity code is consistent with the Common Fund Bridge2AI programme's use of other-transaction awards; grantor and grant prefix agree.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders.grants: grant_number 3OT2OD032720-01S1 (PhysioNet acknowledgement) and OT2OD032720 (NIH RePORTER core project); source_caveats records the RePORTER application 3OT2OD032720-01S3 and dismisses the corrupted documentation variants '3Tf-OTOD03272001S2' and '3TF-OT2ActfOD032720Projectf01S1'. Two award identifiers with their distinct roles (supplement cited in the release acknowledgement vs core project), plus an audit trail for the conflicting transcriptions. Both identifiers match the NIH pattern: amendment prefix 3, activity code OT2, institute code OD, serial 032720, support-year/supplement suffix -01S1. Grant-number format validation passes.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: sixteen entries with affiliations and roles (co-PIs, module co-leads, cohort leads), including principal_investigator with id, email yaelbensoussan@usf.edu and department-level affiliation; the consortium entry notes 'over 50 other investigators, clinicians, scholars and trainees contributed'. Roles are differentiated rather than a flat author list, and two name-spelling discrepancies between sources are resolved explicitly in per-creator source_caveats. Creator affiliations are consistent with the five North American collection sites named in description and with data_collectors; the citation author order matches the creator roster's first and senior authors.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: 'A custom Bridge2AI-Voice application running on a tablet, with a head-mounted headset and microphone ... iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) with an Avid AE-36 microphone connected through an Apple dongle; distinct iPad devices were used at each site' and REDCap for questionnaires; collection_timeframes (12 months, with a caveat); direct_collection.is_direct: true; data_collectors (three roles). Hardware, software, setting, personnel and directness are all specified to the model level — enough to reason about device-related acoustic confounds. The per-site device detail is consistent with known_biases.measurement_bias, which identifies exactly that confound; collection_timeframes carries an honest caveat that the 12-month figure predates 3.1.0.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods: first entry (was_directly_observed, was_reported_by_subjects, was_validated_verified all true) describing the standardized session and clinician confirmation via audio/imaging review, EHR or prescriptions; second entry (was_inferred_derived: true) stating that released features are computed from audio rather than observed; raw_data_sources gives WAV audio and REDCap export as the two sources. The acquisition flags are used correctly and the record separates what was observed from what was derived — a distinction many datasheets collapse. The derived-feature entry is consistent with preprocessing_strategies and with the scope_limitation stating that raw waveforms are not in this release.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies (six entries with parameters: mono conversion and 16 kHz resampling with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter; STFT with 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT; 60 Mel bins and 60 MFCCs; sparc articulatory traces at 50 Hz; ppgs posteriorgrams at 100 Hz over 40 phoneme categories; Whisper Large transcription); cleaning_strategies (audit protocol and released audio_quality_metrics.tsv); labeling_strategies (clinician gold standard, annotations_per_item: 1, annotator_demographics, ICD-10 protocol); machine_annotation_tools.tool_accuracy: 'off-the-shelf models that have not been audited for correctness'. Parameter-level reproducibility for every released feature family, plus an explicit and unflattering statement of annotation quality limits. Stated parameters match the per-file dimensions in file_collections (201 x T spectrogram from a 400-point FFT; 60 x T Mel and MFCC; 40 x T posteriorgrams; 12-dimensional EMA), so the pipeline description and the distributed artifacts corroborate each other. imputation_protocols is absent and no statement of non-imputation is given (low-severity gap).

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: machine_annotation_tools.tools: OpenAI Whisper Large, openSMILE, Praat, parselmouth, torchaudio, Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc), ppgs, b2aiprep, SenseLab, with tool_descriptions assigning each a role; external_resources: 'b2aiprep, the library used to organize and preprocess the dataset, to process the raw audio into the released features ... at https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep; version 3.0.0 generated this release'; preprocessing_strategies names the same tools inline. Evidence carried by machine_annotation_tools, preprocessing_strategies and external_resources together. Threshold met: the named software produced or transformed the data being distributed — b2aiprep (with generating version 3.0.0 and repository) built the release, and torchaudio, sparc, ppgs, openSMILE, Praat and parselmouth computed the specific distributed feature files. This is processing-role software, not capture, hosting, packaging or validation tooling; the capture application and PhysioNet hosting are documented separately and neither supplies nor detracts from the point.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: b2aiprep and SenseLab (Apache-2.0); the REDCap data dictionary at github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap archived at Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.12760724 (MIT); the documentation source at github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs archived at Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.13834653 (MIT); Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles; Bensoussan et al., Interspeech 2024, with URL. Five resource groups, each with a license and a stated role, and each pointing at something a reuser would actually need (the instruments, the preprocessing code, the protocol paper). Zenodo DOIs are well formed under the 10.5281 prefix and the archived repositories match the tools named in preprocessing. imputation_protocols is unpopulated; the record documents missing-data patterns and handling but never states whether imputation was performed, which the sub-element's own wording invites (recorded as a low-severity completeness issue, outweighed by the external-resource evidence). source_caveats candidly notes the healthsheet's contrary 'self-contained' answer.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: five typed entries — representativeness_limitation (non-probability sample, limited geography, with scope_impact on generalization), coverage_limitation (English-only eligibility, Spanish under development, with recommended_mitigation), scope_limitation (features not raw audio), temporal_limitation (diagnostic-practice drift), integration_limitation (laryngoscopy, genomics and spirometry not in this release). Each limitation is typed, described and — for two of the five — paired with an impact statement or mitigation; the integration_limitation pre-empts the common misreading that the multimodal protocol implies multimodal data in the release. Limitations agree with sampling_strategies.is_representative=false, with language: English, and with file_collections, which contains only features, phenotype and metadata.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases: selection_bias ('recruited at a small number of high volume expert clinics; groups that have less trust in the medical system or in AI ... less likely to be recruited'), representation_bias (cohort and site skew), measurement_bias ('participants with different labels also had their data collected on different devices, confounding label with recording apparatus and site', with affected_subsets); each with a mitigation_strategy; future_use_impacts describes downstream unfair treatment. Enumerated bias_type values from the taxonomy, each with a concrete mechanism rather than a generic caution, and the measurement_bias entry identifies a confound that directly threatens published results. bias_type values align with BiasTypeEnum categories; the biases are corroborated by sampling_strategies and collection_mechanisms (distinct iPad devices per site).

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: anomalies: 'Different sites have different collection configurations, and the collection protocol changed over the course of the study'; 'Noise artifacts, variations in diagnostic practices, inaccurate questionnaire responses and underreporting are possible confounding factors'; headset-distance variation between sessions and single-clinician or record-based diagnosis. Three distinct anomaly classes (protocol drift, signal artifacts, measurement variability), reinforced by the released per-recording audio_quality_metrics.tsv that lets users check quality themselves. Anomalies are consistent with errata (broken parquet files fixed in 3.1.0) and with missing_data_documentation (features that could not be generated).

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements: three entries flagging race and ethnicity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic and health information, and 'Voice itself is a biometric characteristic capable of identifying the speaker'; content_warnings.content_warnings_present: true with warnings on free-speech transcription content and on mental-health and trauma questionnaire content, plus a source_caveat narrowing the free-speech exposure for 3.1.0. Warnings address both the participant-protection dimension and the researcher-exposure dimension, and the caveat prevents an over-broad warning from being carried forward incorrectly. sensitive_elements is consistent with is_deidentified.identifiers_removed, which lists exactly the sensitive fields (income, mental health status, traumatic life experiences) that were withheld.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews (USF IRB, Single IRB process, Canadian REB handling); future_use_impacts: skew-driven 'unfair treatment of individuals or groups' and misuse in 'hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustments or surveillance'; data_governance.notes records an ethics memorandum justifying controlled access to raw voice and that 'the fields treated as sensitive and removed from the release were identified by a team of ethicists'. Social-impact analysis is linked to enforcement — the anticipated harms are the ones the access agreement prohibits — and the ethics module's role in field-level redaction is documented. future_use_impacts matches discouraged_uses and prohibited_uses one-to-one. A gap remains that data_protection_impacts reports no formal impact assessment on data subjects was conducted; that is recorded as a content-accuracy issue against Element 4 sub-element 1 rather than negating the social-impact analysis present here.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: publisher: https://physionet.org/; page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; maintainers records 'PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology'; raw audio served via Synapse. A recognized domain repository, with the platform migration history (Health Data Nexus for 1.0, PhysioNet from 1.1) disclosed in maintainers.source_caveats and distribution_dates. Publisher, DOI prefix (10.13026) and landing-page domain are mutually consistent.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: citation: full author list with 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66. A complete, version-pinned recommended citation carrying both the DOI and the platform RRID. Citation DOI, top-level doi and id agree; the version in the citation matches version: 3.1.0 and the page path.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema with conforms_to_class: Dataset; external_resources lists 'Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker, published by the project'; labeling_strategies uses ICD-10; instances use B2AI_TOPIC and B2AI_SUBSTRATE ontology CURIEs. Community-standards engagement is real and multi-layered (a w3id metadata schema, published FHIR profiles, ICD-10 coding, a project ontology). Scored consistently with Element 3 sub-element 3 on the same evidence. The qualification applies here too: conforms_to is unpopulated and source_caveats declines to assert BIDS conformance for the 3.1.0 layout, so no data-level standard is claimed for the release itself.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: external_resources references the project documentation site https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/ with its source at github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs and Zenodo archive; existing_uses records use of a restricted raw-audio version 'in the Bridge2AI Summer School and hackathon'; page gives the PhysioNet landing page; extension_mechanism gives https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep with issue and pull-request routes for community contribution. Documentation, training/outreach activity and a concrete community contribution channel are all named. Documentation URLs are well formed and the archived Zenodo copies give them persistence; the outreach claim is attributed to a specific programme rather than asserted generically.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: related_datasets: is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68 ('added data for 391 participants over version 2.0.1 and reorganized the phenotype files'); derives_from syn72370534; references 10.13026/h995-bt35 (pediatric release, 23,533 recordings from 300 participants aged 2 to 18); is_documented_by 10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926. Four relationships spanning version lineage, source derivation, a sibling cohort and the documenting publication, each with an explanatory note. Relationship types are semantically correct for their targets, and the Synapse accession is used where the record states no DOI exists rather than inventing one.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; id: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; citation carries 'RRID:SCR_007345'; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42 (concept DOI) A resolvable version DOI, a URI identifier, and a concept DOI for the version series are all supplied; identification is unambiguous at both version and series level. DOI matches 10.XXXX/... and the prefix 10.13026 is PhysioNet's, agreeing with publisher and citation. RRID matches RRID:SCR_XXXXX; SCR_007345 identifies PhysioNet (the platform) rather than the dataset, noted as a low-severity scope issue but not disqualifying since the DOI carries dataset-level identity.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description of roughly 1,700 characters naming 833 adult participants, five North American sites, four adult condition categories plus controls, the feature-only scope (spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, SPARC articulatory measures, PPGs, pitch contours, openSMILE/Praat/parselmouth static features), the phenotype directory contents, Parquet/TSV distribution, and the credentialed access condition Far beyond the 200-character threshold and semantically dense: the description states what is in the release, what is deliberately not (raw waveforms), how it was collected, and on what terms it can be obtained. Description is internally consistent with instances (833), file_collections (feature/metadata/phenotype layout), distribution_formats (Parquet, TSV) and license_and_use_terms (credentialed). No drift between summary and structured fields.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: [health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice] Four keywords, below the five-term guideline, and all of them broad program- or domain-level terms. None names a condition (Parkinson's disease, ALS, laryngeal cancer, depression, chronic cough), a modality or feature type (spectrogram, MFCC, acoustic features, speech), a population (adult), or a study design — all of which are documented elsewhere in the record and would carry the retrieval load. Discovery by a user searching for, say, a dysphonia or neurodegeneration voice corpus would fail on these tags. Terms present are relevant and correctly used; the failure is coverage, not correctness. The gap is measurable against the record's own phenotype inventory of eighteen conditions.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://b2ai-voice.org/; distribution_formats.access_urls: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; file_collections describes three named collections (features, metadata, phenotype) each with an id, path, collection_type and contents Both a project landing page and the platform content page are given, and the internal resource hierarchy is described down to individual file names and the phenotype subdirectory structure (confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaire, task). URLs are well-formed with plausible domains; the collection ids are constructed as fragments of the dataset URI, which is internally consistent.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: related_datasets: is_supplemented_by 10.13026/h995-bt35 (pediatric companion, 300 participants at SickKids); is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68 (version 3.0.0); is_version_of 10.13026/37yb-1t42 (concept DOI); derives_from syn72370534 (raw audio on Synapse) Four typed relationships, each with a resolvable target and substantive notes explaining what the related resource contains and how it relates. The derives_from edge to the withheld raw audio is the key provenance link for a feature-only release and is made explicit. Relationship types are used correctly and non-redundantly (version-of for the concept DOI, new-version-of for the immediate predecessor). parent_datasets is unused, but the same structural information is carried by the typed relationships.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: general_research_use; license_terms describing credentialed access under the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement, the separate controlled-access route for raw audio (Data Access Request Form, DUA, DACO review, institutionally signed DTUA), and the absence of non-commercial/geographic/research-type restrictions; ip_restrictions lists five specific terms including no transfer of IP rights, duplication permitted but sale prohibited, no IP claims that would block access, Fort Lauderdale Agreement adherence, and no third-party IP encumbrances Access policy and IP terms are both operationally specific: a prospective user learns exactly which credential and which signature are required, what may be duplicated, and what may not be sold or patented in a blocking manner. Policy restrictiveness matches the sensitivity claims elsewhere (biometric voice data, Certificate of Confidentiality) without over-claiming: commercial research is explicitly permitted because the consent did not restrict it, which is consistent with informed_consent.consent_scope.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; regulatory_restrictions list ('No export controls apply', credentialed-access restriction, institutional sign-off for raw audio); other_compliance describing a Certificate of Confidentiality that must be asserted against subpoenas and the DTUA's characterization of the data as PII under OMB Memorandum M-07-16; governance contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org recorded in maintainers (Bridge2AI-Voice Consortium Data Access Compliance Office) Classification, export-control status, HIPAA status, an additional statutory protection, and a reachable governance contact are all present. The source_caveats candidly state that neither classification term is used verbatim by a source and explain the inference from PhysioNet's credentialed policy and the healthsheet's HIPAA answer. Enum values are used correctly and cohere with the access policy. The governance contact sits in maintainers rather than data_governance.committee_contact; the substantive requirement (a contact for the responsible governance body) is met, with the slot placement noted.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: distribution_formats[].access_urls: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ (given for both the Parquet and the TSV distribution); raw_sources.access_url: https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; license_and_use_terms states the credentialing and agreement steps required to obtain the files The dedicated download_url slot is empty, but the sub-element asks for a download link or platform access instructions and both are present and actionable: the PhysioNet content URL is the download point for this release, the Synapse URL is the controlled-access route for raw audio, and the steps to qualify for each are spelled out. URLs are well-formed and the domains match the declared publisher and the stated controlled-access repository. Flagged as a low-severity slot-placement completeness issue rather than an absence of information.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats: 'Parquet' (dense binary feature files, loadable by any Parquet library) and 'Tab-separated values with JSON data dictionaries'; file_collections names the nine Parquet feature files individually (ppgs.parquet, sparc_ema.parquet, sparc_loudness.parquet, sparc_periodicity.parquet, sparc_pitch.parquet, torchaudio_spectrogram.parquet, torchaudio_mfcc.parquet, torchaudio_pitch.parquet, torchaudio_mel_spectrogram.parquet) plus static_features.tsv and audio_quality_metrics.tsv Formats are specific, standard, and resolved to the level of individual file names, with the pairing convention (each file accompanied by a JSON data dictionary sharing its stem) stated explicitly. Formats are appropriate to the content: columnar Parquet for dense time-varying tensors, delimited text for per-recording tables. MIME types and character encoding are not declared, a minor gap that does not obscure the file types.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: related_datasets with four typed, DOI- or accession-identified targets; external_resources listing docs.b2ai-voice.org, github.com/sensein/b2aiprep (Apache-2.0), github.com/sensein/senselab, github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap (MIT), github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs (MIT), and the Synapse raw-audio location, with future_guarantees and access restrictions stated Links are numerous, typed, licensed where applicable, and accompanied by an explicit statement that they are supporting materials rather than dependencies because the dataset is self-contained — which tells a user what breaks if a link rots. All URLs are structurally valid with plausible domains. The restrictions attached to the Synapse link are consistent with the controlled-access policy stated in license_and_use_terms and third_party_sharing.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license: Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: general_research_use; 'intended solely for commercial and non-commercial research purposes by Authorized Researchers; the consent does not restrict use to non-commercial purposes, to a geographic location, to a type of research, to genetic research, or away from methods and algorithm development' Reuse permissions are stated affirmatively and with the unusual precision of naming what is not restricted, which is what a downstream reuser actually needs in order to clear a project. The per-organization application requirement is also stated. The permission enum, the prose terms and the consent scope agree; the license is bespoke rather than a standard CC instrument, which is disclosed rather than misrepresented as an open license.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: distribution_formats: Parquet ('an open-source column-oriented data file format, and can be loaded with any library that supports Parquet') and tab-delimited plain text with companion JSON data dictionaries whose keys match the table column names All three formats used (Parquet, TSV, JSON) are open, widely supported and appropriate to their content, and the dictionary-to-table key correspondence is a genuine interoperability affordance rather than a nominal claim. Character encoding is not declared for the delimited text, the one gap in this sub-element; format standardization itself is unambiguous and machine-actionable.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry ontology term identifiers (B2AI_TOPIC:36, B2AI_TOPIC:37, B2AI_TOPIC:31, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:80); labeling_strategies.data_annotation_protocol: 'Labeling followed the Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10 codes' A resolvable schema URI with a named class, plus controlled-vocabulary term identifiers on instances and an ICD-10 coding statement for diagnostic labels. Scored on the source rubric's field pair (conforms_to, conforms_to_schema), of which the second is populated with a genuine schema. Semantic caveat recorded: conforms_to_schema governs this metadata record rather than the released data tables, and conforms_to is deliberately omitted because the BIDS 1.9.0 conversion applies to the audio dataset's layout, not this feature-only release. The ontology term IDs and ICD-10 statement are what carry data-level conformance here, and they are thinner than the schema URI suggests. This same omission is scored against Element 10 sub-element 3, whose source-rubric field list is conforms_to alone.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: variables: participant_id (identifier, is_identifier true), session_id (identifier, is_identifier true, 'A participant may have more than one session'), task_name (categorical), n_frames (integer); file_collections states every table is 'paired with a JSON data dictionary whose entries carry a description, the question put to the participant where there was one, and the data type of the response' The variables actually declared are the join keys that make the release integrable — participant_id, session_id and task_name are precisely what links feature tensors to metadata to phenotype rows, and relationships restates that linkage explicitly. Coverage of analytic columns is thin relative to the dozens of distributed tables, but the record names the authoritative source for those (the shipped JSON dictionaries) rather than leaving them undocumented. Identifier flags are used correctly and the cardinality caveat (a participant may appear on multiple rows because sessions repeat, and responses need not agree across sessions) is a substantive integration warning. Thin coverage recorded as a low-severity completeness issue.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses: three categories (clinical ML research, AI model pretraining/fine-tuning, voice biomarker research) with examples and usage notes; prohibited_uses: four (re-identification attempts, foreseeable harm or stigmatization, IP protections that restrict access, contacting subjects without IRB approval and written provider approval); discouraged_uses: two (non-research applications such as hiring, insurance pricing and surveillance; uses assuming representativeness) All three registers are populated, each with reasons attached rather than bare prohibitions, and the discouraged-uses entries connect directly to documented properties of the data (the skews recorded in subpopulations and known_biases). Prohibitions are consistent with the Registered Access Agreement described in license_and_use_terms and with the re-identification risk assessed in participant_privacy; no permission granted here contradicts a restriction stated elsewhere.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews: reviewing_organization 'University of South Florida Institutional Review Board', review_details noting US sites joined through the Single IRB process with subsite approvals; human_subject_research.ethics_review_board and irb_approval repeating the approval and recording that the study is not for a drug or device and no data monitoring committee was appointed; governance contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org Oversight is named at the institution level, the mechanism (single IRB with subsite approvals) is identified, and the scope of approval covers both collection and sharing. The absence of a formal DPIA is the only gap in an otherwise complete oversight record. Consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects is true and IRB approval is populated, as required. data_protection_impacts is absent, but its substance is partly carried by participant_privacy.reidentification_risk, which is assessed rather than omitted.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.method: 'HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification, supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers and of highly sensitive non-identifying elements, and by withholding the raw audio waveform'; identifiers_removed enumerates eighteen categories including names, geographic locators, sub-year dates, SSNs, MRNs, device and biometric identifiers, with country retained; deidentification_details adds transcript review, removal of recordings with identifying information or external voices, date rebasing, narrative-field removal, and the disclosure that 'k-anonymization with k of at least two was not achieved' One of the strongest sub-elements in the record: a named standard, an enumerated identifier list, the supplementary measures beyond the standard, and an explicit statement of a de-identification guarantee that was *not* achieved. Negative disclosure of that kind is rare and materially useful. Method appropriateness check passes: for biometric voice data, Safe Harbor alone would be insufficient, and the record's primary control is withholding the waveform and releasing derived features — a measure matched to the actual re-identification vector it names.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy.anonymization_method (Safe Harbor identifiers plus indirect/sensitive field removal, derived features in place of waveforms); privacy_techniques (controlled-access raw audio, manual transcript review, password-protected REDCap behind institutional HIPAA firewall, access limited to HIPAA-trained approved personnel, HTTPS transmission to HIPAA-compliant NIH STRIDES cloud storage); reidentification_risk ('a person's voice is unique to them and to their health at that time, so it is always possible, even if unlikely, that someone could recognize a participant by voice'); data_linkage (EHR access for gold-standard validation; linking datasheets kept within collecting institutions) Protections are described at both the technical and the administrative layer, and the risk assessment is honest about residual risk rather than declaring it eliminated. The linkage disclosure tells a user exactly what identifiable material exists and where it stays. Consistency check passes: where a re-identification vector is named, a corresponding mitigation is named (waveform exclusion, prohibition on re-identification in prohibited_uses). Risk level stated is plausible for feature-only release of biometric-derived data.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true; consent_type covering paper signature, in-app or REDCap electronic consent, and a video consent in which the participant reads a statement aloud (also used to verify the acoustic data belongs to the consented individual); consent_documentation (paper uploads stored in REDCap, retained at least five years); consent_scope (sharing of non-directly-identifying data, registered vs controlled access tiers, EHR access permission, re-consent before each longitudinal session); withdrawal_mechanism (withdrawal any time; data excluded if withdrawal precedes completion; recordings cannot be removed after collection completes); plus collection_consents, collection_notifications and consent_revocations corroborating Consent is documented end to end — modality, documentation, retention, scope, re-consent and the precise boundary at which withdrawal stops being effective. That last point is the one most datasheets omit and the one participants and reusers most need. Consistency check passes: IRB approval documented and consent procedures documented together. The consent scope's permission of commercial research matches the license terms; the tiered-sharing language matches the actual two-tier access model.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: human_subject_research.special_populations: participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, other dementias, ALS and Parkinson's disease; participants with depression, bipolar disorder, anxiety, PTSD and ADHD. participant_compensation: compensation_provided true, type 'Electronic gift cards', amount '40 US dollars for a data collection session lasting under 90 minutes and 80 US dollars for a session lasting over 90 minutes, for no more than three sessions and a maximum total of 120 US dollars', with a caveat that the scheme changed over the protocol's life Both halves are substantively documented: the at-risk groups are named at diagnosis level rather than as a generic category, and compensation is given with tiering, caps and a change caveat. The canonical at_risk_populations slot is unused, which is a placement rather than a content defect. Cohorts named as special populations match the disease categories in subpopulations and the eighteen diagnosis tables in file_collections — no population is claimed that the data does not contain. Compensation amounts are plausible for the session burden described and are not so large as to raise an undisclosed undue-inducement concern.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations[0]: subpopulation_elements_present true, identification 'Age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status are recorded, together with race and sexual orientation', distribution noting skews by disorder category, site and demographics with advice to consider the multivariate distribution; subpopulations[1]: the five disease cohort categories, with distribution noting this adult release covers four plus controls and that categories are not equally distributed Both demographic and clinical stratifications are identified, and the distributional caveat is specific enough to act on. What is missing is quantitative breakdown — no counts or proportions per subgroup are given — which limits assessment of fitness for a given subpopulation question. Consistent with sampling_strategies (is_representative false), known_biases (representation and selection bias) and discouraged_uses (uses assuming representativeness). The pediatric-category exclusion matches the separate pediatric dataset in related_datasets.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances[0].counts: 833 (Participant); instances[1] notes per-feature record counts: '29,278 spectrogram, Mel spectrogram and MFCC records; 32,522 torchaudio pitch records; 28,640 articulatory records; 31,855 loudness records; 31,872 periodicity and Speech Articulatory Coding pitch records; and 29,289 phonetic posteriorgram records'; related_datasets records 833 participants at 3.0.0; version_access gives the cohort trajectory 306 -> 442 -> 833 Counts are given at participant level and at per-feature record level, and the record explains why the feature counts differ from each other (some recordings could not yield some features; dense features withheld for sensitive records) rather than presenting a single misleading total. Cross-field count consistency passes: 833 appears in description, instances and the 3.0.0 relationship note. source_caveats discloses that no total recording count is stated for 3.1.0 and that per-feature counts cannot be summed because they count overlapping recordings — a correct and necessary caveat.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: variables: four entries with data_type, is_identifier flags and descriptions; file_collections: every table tab-delimited and 'paired with a JSON data dictionary whose entries carry a description, the question put to the participant where there was one, and the data type of the response'; splits.split_details: 'Researchers are encouraged to create their own data splits based on their specific requirements'; notes: 'No recommended train, validation or test splits are supplied with the release'; subpopulations entries carry subpopulation_elements_present true The split status is documented as a positive statement of absence in two places, which is the useful answer when no canonical split exists; the tabular character of the phenotype and static-feature files is evident from the format description; data dictionaries are documented as shipped with every table. The is_tabular flag itself is unset and the variables list is thin, so this sub-element passes on substance rather than on completeness of slots. No contradiction between the split statement and any other field. Structural description (dense Parquet tensors plus delimited tables) is coherent with both distribution_formats and the feature inventory.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances carry data_topic and data_substrate ontology identifiers (B2AI_TOPIC:36, B2AI_TOPIC:37, B2AI_TOPIC:31; B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:80); file_collections.phenotype enumerates eighteen diagnosis tables — airway stenosis, ALS, anxiety, benign lesions, bipolar disorder, cognitive impairment, control, COPD and asthma, depression, glottic insufficiency, laryngeal cancer, laryngeal dystonia, laryngitis, muscle tension dysphonia, Parkinson's disease, precancerous lesions, unexplained chronic cough, unilateral vocal fold paralysis; description names the four adult condition categories Conditions are represented at three levels of granularity — coded topic identifiers, the five-category scheme, and the per-condition diagnosis tables — so a user can determine precisely which phenotypes are present. The eighteen named conditions map cleanly onto the four declared categories plus controls; no condition appears in one place and is absent from another. Ontology identifiers are well-formed CURIEs in the project's own namespace.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: anomalies: four entries (differing site configurations and protocol change over the study; noise artifacts, inter-site diagnostic variation, inaccurate questionnaire responses and underreporting; off-the-shelf models such as transcription not audited for correctness; some audio unable to yield certain features); sampling_strategies (non-probability, not random, not representative, with why_not_representative); missing_data_documentation with missing_data_patterns (row present only if at least one column is non-missing; disease-specific fields systematically absent outside the cohort), missing_data_causes and handling_strategy ('Missing values are left as missing rather than imputed'; a missingness table is distributed) Quality documentation is unusually complete: known anomalies, their causes, the structural pattern of missingness, the non-imputation decision, and the fact that a missingness table ships with the data so a user can verify it themselves. Consistent with instances[].missing_information and with the per-feature count discrepancies explained in instances[1]. The non-imputation statement substitutes coherently for the absent imputation_protocols slot.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: 3.1.0; id and access URLs both embed /3.1.0/; citation states '(version 3.1.0)' A semantic version number, consistently repeated across the identifier, the access URL and the citation so that a retrieved file can be matched to this record. Version string is well-formed and agrees with issued/last_updated_on (2026-05-01) and with the 3.1.0 entry in version_access.versions_available.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access.versions_available lists six releases with dates and contents (1.0 on Health Data Nexus, 12,523 recordings from 306 participants; 1.1 adding MFCCs; 2.0.0 adding 136 participants; 2.0.1 authorship correction; 3.0.0 adding 391 participants and separating phenotype files; 3.1.0 adding data for existing participants); version_details: each version has a unique DOI, a concept DOI resolves to the latest, older versions remain listed but 1.1 files are no longer available, and publishers reserve the right to remove access to older versions A user can determine what each version contained, which are still retrievable, and by what identifier to request one — including the candid statement that 1.1 files have been withdrawn. One mismatch recorded: latest_version_doi holds 10.13026/37yb-1t42, which related_datasets identifies as the concept DOI, not the 3.1.0 version DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66. Scored 1 because the access methods themselves are documented thoroughly and the concept/version distinction is explained elsewhere in the record; the slot mismatch is reported as a correctness issue.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: errata: 3.1.0 fixed broken Parquet files carried over from the previous release, updated validated diagnosis information with back-filled data, rearranged some phenotype files and renamed certain gold-standard variables; 2.0 reprocessed spectrograms and removed free-speech spectrograms and MFCCs; 2.0.1 corrected the authorship list; updates.update_details describes the new-version-not-in-place-edit policy Errata are release-specific, name the defect and the remedy, and include changes that break downstream code (renamed gold-standard variables, rearranged files) — precisely the changes a reuser must know about. source_caveats discloses that the project documentation claims there is no erratum and that these corrections were drawn from PhysioNet release notes; the conflict is surfaced rather than hidden. Errata align with the version_access change list for the same releases.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.frequency: 'Semi-annual, that is twice a year'; update_details: further versions released as new versions with their own DOIs, users notified through platform news items and standard channels, 'the dataset itself is released as static versions rather than being dynamically updated' A stated cadence, a notification mechanism and a versioning policy are all present, and the record caveats that the cadence statement was written against the previous hosting platform. Consistency failure recorded: the observed release history (2025-01, 2025-04, 2025-08, 2025-12, 2026-05) is denser and more irregular than semi-annual. Scored 1 because the schedule and mechanism are stated and caveated, but the mismatch is reported as a medium-severity issue.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: was_derived_from: 'Raw voice, speech and respiratory audio recordings and questionnaire responses collected under the Bridge2AI Voice Data Acquisition protocol and exported from REDCap'; raw_sources.raw_data_details describing the withheld waveforms, the separate controlled-access dissemination, and the BIDS 1.9.0 conversion that applies to the audio dataset's layout; raw_sources.access_url https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; related_datasets derives_from syn72370534; updates.update_details carrying the release-to-release derivation narrative The derivation chain is complete and traceable: named raw sources, the transformation that produced the release, a resolvable location for the raw material, and a typed relationship encoding the same edge machine-readably. Release-specific notes were read from updates.update_details and the errata entries, both of which carry actual release and derivation information rather than unrelated commentary. The BIDS scoping caveat is correctly confined to raw_sources rather than asserted of this release.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes: three responses (an ethically sourced, demographically diverse voice dataset linked to health information as a foundation for voice AI; development, benchmarking and validation of clinically applicable ML models across vocal, neurological, psychiatric, respiratory and pediatric disorders; integration of voice as a biomarker into clinical care); addressing_gaps: four responses naming small prior sample sizes, absent measurement standards, the opacity of industry-held voice data, and the scarcity of voice linked to accurate clinical and demographic information Motivation is stated both positively (what the dataset is for) and negatively (which specific deficiencies in the prior literature it addresses), including the causal claim that data scarcity explains the absence of an FDA-approved voice AI diagnostic. Purposes align with the funder's programmatic aims (NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI, Precision Public Health grand challenge) and with the intended_uses declared later; no purpose is claimed that the released content could not serve.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks: 'Training machine-learning models for disease detection and classification from voice data, using diagnostic labels spanning vocal pathologies, neurological disorders, psychiatric conditions and respiratory disorders' and 'Pretraining, fine-tuning, benchmarking and validation of AI models for the screening, diagnosis and monitoring of health conditions using voice as a non-invasive, cost-effective biomarker' Tasks are specified as concrete ML problem types tied to the label taxonomy the dataset actually carries, not as generic aspirations. Tasks are supported by the data described: diagnostic labels exist per participant (labeling_strategies), and derived acoustic features are the model inputs. Consistent with intended_uses and with the discouraged non-research applications.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders.grantor: 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund, Bridge2AI Program'; description names the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program and the Precision Public Health grand challenge; maintainers records separate NIBIB/NHLBI/OD support for PhysioNet under U24EB037545 and R01EB030362 The funding agency, the specific programme and the mechanism (Common Fund other-transaction award) are identified, and infrastructure funding for the hosting platform is separately and correctly attributed rather than conflated with dataset funding. Funder identity is consistent across funders, description and notes (organization study identifier OT2OD032720). Funding goals align with the stated purposes, satisfying the funding-alignment check.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders.grants: grant_number 3OT2OD032720-01S1 (PhysioNet acknowledgements, with the full project title quoted) and grant_number OT2OD032720 (NIH RePORTER core project number and the study's organization identifier); source_caveats records the variants 3OT2OD032720-01S3, '1OT2OD032720-01' from the feasibility publication, and two garbled documentation forms, with the PhysioNet form preferred Structured grant numbers in the canonical slot, with both the supplement-level and core project forms given, and the conflicting variants across sources catalogued with a stated preference rule rather than silently collapsed. NIH pattern check passes: OT2 is a valid Common Fund other-transaction activity code, OD is the Office of the Director, 032720 is a six-digit serial, and the 3...-01S1 prefix/suffix convention (type 3 supplement, support year 01, supplement S1) is well-formed. The RePORTER details (project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30, FY2025 award 4,660,942) are plausible for an OT2 Common Fund award of this scope.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators: University of South Florida with PI Yael Bensoussan and affiliation, Weill Cornell Medicine with PI Olivier Elemento and affiliation, and the Bridge2AI-Voice Consortium with twelve named member institutions; source_caveats explaining that the roughly 120 PhysioNet authors are represented at institution and consortium granularity and noting the diaeresis discrepancy in a PI's name; citation carrying the full author list; maintainers naming MIT LCP and the consortium DACO Attribution is complete at the level the record chose, that choice is declared, and the two co-PIs are individually identified with affiliations. Acknowledgement of platform support and of the consortium's disciplinary composition is also present. Creator institutions overlap consistently with the five collection sites implied elsewhere (USF, Weill Cornell, OHSU, SickKids, Mount Sinai among the affiliation list) and with the pediatric site named in related_datasets. No attribution conflicts with the citation string.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: collection_mechanisms: the Bridge2AI-Voice tablet application ('Data were collected on iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) using an Avid AE-36 microphone connected through an Apple dongle', head-mounted where possible, collecting breathing and cough sounds, voice, speech and linguistic tasks plus surveys) and REDCap for clinical, diagnostic and questionnaire capture; direct_collection records in-clinic collection in the United States and Canada; data_collectors describes site research teams and site clinicians with their roles Hardware down to device generation and microphone model, the software stack, the setting, the personnel and their roles are all specified — enough for a reader to judge comparability with another corpus or to attempt replication. Device specificity is what makes the measurement-bias disclosure in known_biases verifiable (distinct iPads per site, variable headset distance); collection description and bias description are mutually consistent.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods with was_directly_observed, was_reported_by_subjects, was_inferred_derived and was_validated_verified all true, and acquisition_details distinguishing directly observed acoustic tasks, self-reported demographics and questionnaires, clinician-verified diagnoses, and the derived character of the released values ('features computed from the recorded waveforms rather than the waveforms themselves'); raw_sources identifying the REDCap and audio origins with a Synapse access URL The four acquisition modes are not merely flagged but disaggregated by which part of the dataset each applies to, including the important observation that everything released is derived rather than observed. Flags and prose agree, and both agree with the feature-only scope declared in description and file_collections. No acquisition mode is flagged true without a corresponding element of the data.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: preprocessing_strategies: monaural conversion and 16 kHz resampling with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter; STFT with 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, downsampled by two in time for 201 frequency bins; 60 MFCCs and a 60-bin Mel spectrogram; SPARC kinematic traces for six articulators with loudness, periodicity and pitch at 50 Hz; PPGs over forty phoneme categories at 100 Hz; Whisper Large transcription; b2aiprep 3.0.0 and senselab. cleaning_strategies: an audit protocol generating missingness tables, checking distributions and outliers, validating categorical responses against the schema, and running audio QC on silence, duration and passage fidelity. labeling_strategies: clinician diagnosis with cohort-specific gold standards (laryngoscopy and stroboscopy, spirometry and flow-volume loops, brain CT and MRI, EHR plus psychiatrist diagnosis and medication history), annotations_per_item 1, annotator demographics, protocol and platform. machine_annotation_tools.tool_accuracy: off-the-shelf models such as transcription 'have not been audited for correctness' The strongest element in the record. Parameters are given at the level a reimplementation would need, cleaning is described as an auditable protocol, labeling includes the gold standard per cohort, and annotation quality is stated honestly including its unaudited components and the single-labeler limitation. Signal-processing parameters are internally coherent (25 ms window at 16 kHz with a 400-point FFT gives the stated 201 bins). The healthsheet's 'No' answer to preprocessing-for-cleaning is disclosed in source_caveats as contradicted by the audit steps recorded elsewhere — surfaced rather than suppressed.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: Evidence carried by machine_annotation_tools.tools (OpenAI Whisper Large; openSMILE; Praat via parselmouth; torchaudio; Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc); phonetic posteriorgrams (ppgs); b2aiprep; senselab) with per-tool descriptions of what each produced, corroborated by preprocessing_strategies ('Processing was performed with the b2aiprep library, version 3.0.0 for this release, and the senselab audio processing toolkit') and by external_resources, which gives repository URLs and licenses for b2aiprep and senselab Every named tool is in a producing or transforming role for the data actually distributed: torchaudio produced the spectrogram, Mel spectrogram, MFCC and pitch Parquet files; sparc produced the articulatory, loudness, periodicity and pitch tensors; ppgs produced the posteriorgrams; openSMILE and Praat/parselmouth produced static_features.tsv; b2aiprep and senselab orchestrated the pipeline and merged the phenotype files. A version is pinned for b2aiprep (3.0.0) and repositories are linked for the two consortium libraries, exceeding the naming threshold. Threshold check passes on producing/transforming software, not on excluded roles: the tablet application (capture, role a), PhysioNet (hosting, role b) and REDCap (capture and label recording, role a) are also documented but were not relied on for this score. Tool-to-output mapping is verifiable against the nine Parquet file names in file_collections.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources: project documentation at docs.b2ai-voice.org (protocols, healthsheet, study metadata, AI-readiness assessment), b2aiprep (Apache-2.0), senselab, bridge2ai-redcap (MIT), bridge2ai-docs (MIT), Synapse raw audio, each with future_guarantees and access restrictions; missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy: 'Missing values are left as missing rather than imputed', with a missingness table distributed alongside the data External materials are numerous, licensed, typed by purpose and accompanied by an honest statement that no persistence guarantee is offered and that they are supporting rather than load-bearing. The imputation question is answered in the negative explicitly, which is the documented answer the sub-element accepts. The imputation_protocols slot is unused; its substance is carried by missing_data_documentation, which states non-imputation rather than leaving it unaddressed. conforms_to is absent, with the BIDS scoping reason disclosed. Standards coverage is therefore the weakest of the three strands here but the sub-element is satisfied by resources and the imputation statement.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations: five typed entries — coverage_limitation (fluent English speakers only, non-English speakers excluded, with Spanish protocols noted as under development and a source caveat about IRB revisions); representativeness_limitation (non-probability sample from high-volume expert clinics at five sites, with scope_impact on generalization); scope_limitation (derived features only, waveform analyses impossible on this release, mitigated by controlled-access raw audio); temporal_limitation (protocol changed over the study, diagnostic practice drift as a source of distribution shift); coverage_limitation (unequal disease-category distribution, pediatric category omitted, multimodal imaging/genomic/respiratory data not included) Limitations are typed, each carries a described consequence, and three carry recommended mitigations. The set covers language, sampling, modality scope, time and content coverage — no obvious dimension is left unaddressed. Each limitation is corroborated elsewhere: the sampling limitation by sampling_strategies, the scope limitation by raw_sources and description, the coverage limitation by subpopulations and related_datasets (pediatric released separately). No limitation contradicts a capability claimed in intended_uses.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases with bias_type values selection_bias, representation_bias, measurement_bias and annotation_bias, each with a bias_description and, for the first three, a mitigation_strategy or affected_subsets ('Disease cohort categories, which are confounded with collection site and device'); future_use_impacts adds two downstream impact statements on multivariate skew and on models learning site or device signatures Four distinct taxonomy categories are used correctly rather than as synonyms, and the measurement-bias entry identifies a genuine and non-obvious confound between cohort, site and recording device. The social-impact strand required by the RAI alignment is carried by future_use_impacts. Bias types map to recognizable BiasTypeEnum categories. The representation-bias description (five sites in the US and Canada, fluent English only) is numerically consistent with the description and known_limitations; the annotation-bias entry is consistent with labeling_strategies.annotations_per_item of 1.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: anomalies: four entries covering differing site configurations and a protocol that changed over the study; noise artifacts, inter-site variation in diagnostic practice, inaccurate questionnaire responses and underreporting; unaudited off-the-shelf models for derived products such as transcription; and audio files that could not yield certain features and are absent from the corresponding bundled files Anomalies are concrete and each has a traceable effect on the released artifact — the last one directly explains the unequal per-feature record counts reported in instances. Anomaly set is consistent with missing_data_documentation.missing_data_causes and with the per-feature count discrepancies; the record does not claim a data quality it elsewhere disclaims (the notes even report the AI-readiness self-assessment scoring Characterization 80 percent 'with the data quality criterion not met').

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present true, with race and ethnic origin, sexual orientation, socioeconomic and health information named and the observation that 'Voice itself is a biometric characteristic; the derived features are released in place of the waveform for that reason', plus a source_caveat recording the conflict with the version 3.0.0 removal account; content_warnings: content_warnings_present false with a warning text explaining that the healthsheet's offensive-language warning concerns free-speech transcripts removed at 1.1 and excluded from the feature-only 3.0.0/3.1.0 releases Sensitive attributes are enumerated, the biometric rationale for the release design is stated, and the superseded content warning is carried with an explanation of why it no longer applies rather than being silently dropped. Two low-severity coherence issues recorded: content_warnings_present false alongside a populated warnings list, and the acknowledged healthsheet-versus-deidentification conflict about which sensitive fields survive in 3.1.0. Both are disclosed by the record itself, so the user is not misled; they are reported as issues rather than scored against this sub-element, whose substance is amply present.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
