text: ethical_reviews: USF IRB review of collection and sharing, with US sites joining through the Single IRB process and subsite approvals; future_use_impacts: skews by disorder category, site and demographics with the warning to consider the multivariate distribution 'to avoid unfair treatment of individuals or groups through stereotyping or quality-of-service failures', and the risk that models learn site or device signatures rather than disease signatures; discouraged_uses names hiring, insurance pricing and surveillance as harms to avoid Ethical oversight and anticipated downstream social impact are both documented, and the impact analysis is specific about the mechanism of harm (stereotyping, quality-of-service failure, spurious site signatures) rather than gesturing at fairness generally. Conflicts of interest are not documented, the one gap in scope. The social-impact statements are consistent with known_biases and with the prohibitions in prohibited_uses, and the ethics review is the same one recorded in Element 4 sub-element 1, used here for its social-impact pairing rather than duplicated as new evidence.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: publisher: https://physionet.org/; id and access URLs under physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; maintainers records the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology as the platform maintainer with its own NIH support grants PhysioNet is a recognized domain repository for physiological and clinical data, the publisher field resolves to it, and the maintaining institution is separately identified. Publisher, DOI prefix (10.13026, PhysioNet's) and access URLs all agree — a three-way consistency that confirms the platform claim rather than merely asserting it.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: citation: full author list ending 'Ghosh, S. (2026). Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; version_access.latest_version_doi supplying the concept DOI for citing the series A complete, conventionally formatted citation with authors, year, title, version, publisher, platform RRID and a resolvable DOI, plus a concept DOI for version-independent reference. The DOI in the citation matches the top-level doi field and the version it describes. The RRID is PhysioNet's rather than the dataset's, noted as a low-severity scope observation; the dataset-level identifier in the citation is the DOI, which is correct.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: conforms_to is absent. source_caveats states: 'the BIDS version 1.9.0 conversion described in the project documentation concerns the audio dataset's folder layout, and is noted in raw_sources rather than asserted as a property of this release, which is why conforms_to and conforms_to_standard are omitted.' The only standards signals for the released artifact are ICD-10 mentioned within labeling_strategies.data_annotation_protocol and conforms_to_schema, which declares the datasheet's own schema rather than the data's. No community data standard is claimed for this release. The omission is deliberate and honestly reasoned — asserting BIDS conformance would have been inaccurate for a feature-only release — but the sub-element asks whether the dataset connects to community standards, and for the distributed tables the answer given is effectively none. A reader cannot determine whether the phenotype tables follow any shared clinical data model (OMOP, FHIR, CDISC) or only a project-internal convention. Scored strictly on the source rubric's field for this item (conforms_to), which is empty. Element 3 sub-element 3 scores 1 because its field list also admits conforms_to_schema, which is populated; the divergence is deliberate and reflects the two items' different scopes, data-level standards here versus schema conformance there.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: page: https://b2ai-voice.org/; external_resources: docs.b2ai-voice.org carrying protocols, healthsheet, study metadata and AI-readiness assessment, plus four public code repositories with licenses; existing_uses notes the Bridge2AI Summer School and hackathon and lists training opportunities at https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/; extension_mechanism.contribution_url https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep with discussion forums, issue pages and pull requests accepted Documentation, training and community-contribution channels are all linked, and the contribution route is described operationally (forums, issues, pull requests against the preprocessing code), which is genuine ecosystem integration rather than a bare homepage. All URLs are well-formed with plausible domains consistent with the project and its GitHub organizations (sensein, eipm). The scholars and summer-school references corroborate the outreach claim with concrete instances.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: related_datasets: is_supplemented_by 10.13026/h995-bt35 (pediatric dataset v1.1.0, 23,533 recordings from 300 participants aged 2-18 at SickKids under REB approval, raw audio at syn73617068); is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68 (v3.0.0, published 16 December 2025); is_version_of 10.13026/37yb-1t42 (concept DOI); derives_from syn72370534 (adult raw audio under controlled access) Four relationships, each typed with a standard vocabulary term, each pointing at a resolvable identifier, and each annotated with enough detail (counts, sites, ethics approval, access route) for a user to decide whether to pursue it. Relationship semantics are used correctly and the targets are mutually consistent: the pediatric companion is supplementary rather than a version, the immediate predecessor is a version predecessor, and the raw audio is a derivation source, matching was_derived_from and raw_sources.

name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
text: doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66; citation carries 'RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; version_access.version_details gives per-version DOIs 10.13026/249v-w155 (1.1), 10.13026/k81f-qr68 (3.0.0), 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 (3.1.0) and 10.13026/37yb-1t42 (latest). A resolvable persistent identifier is present, and the versioning discipline around it is unusually good: each release has its own DOI and a separate concept DOI resolves to the latest. The identifier is repeated consistently in four places without drift. Format check passes: matches 10.XXXX/... The 10.13026 prefix is PhysioNet's registered prefix and is plausible given publisher: https://physionet.org/ and the physionet.org landing page, so the prefix-plausibility test passes rather than merely the syntax test. RRID:SCR_007345 matches RRID:SCR_XXXXX and is correctly scoped to the hosting resource.

name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
text: title: 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description of approximately 1,500 characters naming 833 adult participants, five clinical sites in the US and Canada, four disease cohorts plus controls, the acoustic-task protocol and tablet-plus-headset instrument, the exact feature families released (spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, articulatory and phonetic posteriorgram features, static acoustic features, audio quality metrics, per-recording metadata, phenotype tables), and the statement that 'Raw audio waveforms are withheld from this release and disseminated separately under controlled access'. Far beyond the 200-character threshold and, more importantly, specific rather than promotional. It states what is in the release, what is deliberately not, and why the dataset exists, so a prospective user can decide fitness without opening another field. Description is semantically coherent with the claimed dataset type and consistent with downstream fields: the 833 count matches instances.counts, the five-site claim matches known_limitations.representativeness_limitation, and the raw-audio withholding matches raw_data_sources.access_details and the derives_from relationship.

name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
text: keywords: [health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice] - four terms in total. Below the five-keyword threshold and thin in substance. Every term is either the programme name or a one-word abstraction; none reaches the disease cohorts the dataset is organized around (voice disorders, Parkinson's disease, ALS, dementia, depression, COPD, chronic cough), the modalities (speech, breath, cough), the feature families (spectrogram, MFCC, posteriorgram) or the methodological framing the record itself coins under purposes ('audiomics'). A searcher looking for a Parkinson's voice corpus would not retrieve this record on its keywords. The keywords are individually accurate and none is misleading, so this is a coverage failure rather than a correctness failure. Note that the same keywords were read as evidence for the Element 4 human-subjects condition only in combination with description; 'health' alone would not have carried it.

name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
text: page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; file_collections define three hierarchical collections (features, metadata, phenotype) with paths, collection_type values and, for features, eleven enumerated resources each with its own id, name, file_type and description. Both limbs are met. The landing page is version-pinned rather than generic, and the resource hierarchy is genuinely navigable, descending from collection to named file with per-file dimensions and record counts. URL structure is well-formed and the version segment matches version: 3.1.0. Resource identifiers use the dataset DOI as a base with fragment suffixes, which is internally consistent.

name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
text: related_datasets contains seven entries with explicit relationship_type values: is_supplemented_by (pediatric release, doi 10.13026/h995-bt35), derives_from (raw audio via Synapse syn72370534), is_new_version_of (Health Data Nexus version 1.0, doi 10.57764/qb6h-em84), is_described_by (REDCap dictionary on Zenodo), is_documented_by (Interspeech 2024 protocol paper, doi 10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926) and two is_referenced_by publications. No parent_datasets slot is used, but the relationship graph more than substitutes for it: the derives_from edge to the controlled-access raw audio and the is_new_version_of edge to the platform predecessor together place this release precisely in its lineage, each with a resolvable identifier and an explanatory note. Relationship types are used correctly rather than interchangeably: the featurized release genuinely derives from the raw audio, the pediatric cohort genuinely supplements rather than derives, and the Health Data Nexus release is genuinely an earlier version. Note that the feasibility-study reference is annotated as contributing no data, preventing a false provenance reading.

name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License. Users must be credentialed on PhysioNet and sign the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement... sale of all or part of the data on any media is not permitted'; data_use_permission: general_research_use; ip_restrictions.restrictions lists six distinct clauses covering copyright reservation, prohibition on IP claims over the data, prohibition on using IP protection to block access, permission to obtain downstream IP subject to non-obstructive licensing, prohibition on sale, and a no-warranty statement on third-party rights. The access policy is actionable (a reader knows exactly what to sign and with whom) and the IP position is genuinely articulated rather than gestured at, including the unusual and substantive downstream-licensing condition drawn from the Fort Lauderdale Agreement. Restrictiveness is coherent with the ethics posture: a registered-access tier for low-risk derived features alongside the controlled-access tier for raw audio matches the re-identification reasoning in is_deidentified.source_caveats. No contradiction between the licence's permissiveness on commercial research and the consent scope.

name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
text: regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions: 'No export controls apply... Data transfer... governed by a Data Transfer and Use Agreement with the University of South Florida Board of Trustees, which requires appropriate administrative, technical and physical safeguards, restricts access to named authorized persons, prohibits contacting data subjects without IRB approval... and requires notification of any unauthorized use or disclosure within five business days'; hipaa_compliant: compliant; confidentiality_level: restricted; other_compliance cites a Certificate of Confidentiality, PII status under OMB Memorandum M-07-16, and PhysioNet requirements. Governance contact: data_governance.committee_name 'Data Access Compliance Office (DACO)' with the address DACO@b2ai-voice.org given in access_review_process and repeated under maintainers. All four limbs of the sub-element are served, including the governance-contact limb that the source rubric adds. The export-control position is stated negatively and explicitly, which is more useful than silence, and the Certificate of Confidentiality is correctly framed as something that must be asserted against compulsory legal process. confidentiality_level: restricted is proportionate to the content: derived features with health, mental-health and demographic linkage, deidentified but acknowledged as not k-anonymous. The contact is carried by data_governance.committee_name plus access_review_process rather than by a dedicated committee_contact slot; the substance is present and resolvable.

name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
text: distribution_formats[0].access_urls: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; page gives the same URL; data_governance.access_review_process specifies the full retrieval path for each tier ('Registered access to the featurized data requires registration on PhysioNet, confirmation of identity and signature of the Bridge2AI-Voice Registered Access Agreement'; controlled access via a Data Access Request Form and DUA submitted to DACO@b2ai-voice.org); raw_data_sources.access_details names the Synapse endpoint https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/. The dedicated download_url slot is empty, but the criterion admits platform access instructions and these are exemplary: a reader knows the platform, the credentialing step, the agreement to sign, the contact address for the second tier and the endpoint each tier resolves to. The information is actionable, which is the test. Both access endpoints are well-formed and platform-plausible (physionet.org for the featurized release, synapse.org with a syn-prefixed accession for raw audio). The two-tier routing is consistent with the withholding described in description and limitations.

name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
text: distribution_formats describes 'Derived features and phenotype tables distributed as Apache Parquet and tab-delimited text with JSON data dictionaries'; file_collections.resources give format: TSV and media_type: text/tab-separated-values for static_features.tsv and audio_quality_metrics.tsv; nine parquet resources are named with .parquet extensions and per-file tensor dimensions (for example ppgs.parquet, '40 by T at a frame rate of 100 Hz', 29,289 recordings). Formats are specific, standard and stated at file granularity rather than as a single blanket claim, and each file is paired with a JSON data dictionary sharing its stem. MIME types are supplied for the TSV resources. Apache Parquet is a semantically appropriate choice for dense per-frame feature tensors and TSV for recording-level summaries; the format assignment matches the data shape described for each file. Warning: media_type is not declared for the nine parquet resources (application/vnd.apache.parquet), and no character encoding is declared anywhere.

name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
text: Seven related_datasets entries with resolvable DOIs or accessions, plus six external_resources: Bridge2AI Voice REDCap (github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap, MIT licence, archived at zenodo.org/records/14989503, archival: true), b2aiprep (github.com/sensein/b2aiprep), SenseLab (github.com/sensein/senselab), the documentation site and dashboard (docs.b2ai-voice.org, archived at zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653, archival: true), FHIR profiles, and the Bridge2AI Voice Scholars training programme (b2aivoicescholars.org). Both limbs are richly populated, and the archival flag distinguishes Zenodo-archived resources from live repositories, which is exactly the distinction a long-term reuser needs. The Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.13834653 carries the correct Zenodo prefix 10.5281, matching the stated registrar. All repository URLs follow plausible GitHub organization/repository structure.

name: License Terms Allow Reuse
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms permits 'Duplication as reasonably required to carry out the research project'; data_use_permission: general_research_use; notes: 'The registered access agreement permits both commercial and non-commercial research by Authorized Researchers; the consent does not restrict use to non-commercial purposes, to a geographic location, to a specific type of research, to genetic research, or against methods and algorithm development.' Reuse permissions are stated affirmatively and the boundaries are enumerated rather than left to inference. The explicit statement that consent does not restrict methods and algorithm development is precisely what a machine-learning reuser needs and is frequently absent from comparable records. Not a standard Creative Commons identifier but a named bespoke agreement, which is appropriate for a credentialed health-data release; the permissions are described in enough substance that the absence of an SPDX identifier does not impede a reuse decision. Licence permissiveness is consistent with the consent scope recorded independently under informed_consent.

name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
text: Apache Parquet described as 'an open-source column-oriented data file format' for dense per-frame features; TSV with media_type text/tab-separated-values for recording-level summaries; JSON data dictionaries accompanying every data file; raw_data_sources records WAV for the upstream audio and 'REDCap export converted to tab-delimited tables with JSON data dictionaries'. Every format in use is open and standard, and the choice is matched to the data shape. The paired JSON dictionary convention (a dictionary sharing each file's stem) is itself an interoperability affordance. Format naming is technically correct throughout. Warning: the encoding limb of this sub-element is unmet - no character encoding is declared for the TSV tables or JSON dictionaries, which matters for the phenotype free-text and multi-institution name fields. Scored 1 because the format limb is satisfied comprehensively and encoding is the lesser of the two.

name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
text: conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema with conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry ontology CURIEs data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:36 and data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:69; labeling_strategies.data_annotation_protocol: 'Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10 codes, with disorder-specific gold standard validation methods'; external_resources lists 'Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles'. Scored on the field pair the source rubric assigns to this item. conforms_to_schema resolves to a real w3id-namespaced schema, and content-level standardization is evidenced independently by ICD-10 coding of diagnoses and by B2AI ontology terms on instances. Qualified pass with a recorded reservation: conforms_to_schema describes the metadata record's own schema rather than the distributed data, and source_caveats states that 'no conforms_to value is asserted for this release' because BIDS 1.9.0 applies to the raw-audio distribution instead. ICD-10 and the B2AI CURIEs are what carry genuine content-level conformance here. The narrower Element 10 sub-element 3, whose field list is conforms_to alone, is scored 0 on this same reading.

name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
text: variables defines participant_id (data_type: identifier, is_identifier: true, 'present in every feature file and in the phenotype tables', quality_notes noting it is pseudonymous and not reversible), session_id (is_identifier: true, noting participants may hold multiple sessions), task_name (categorical, enumerating the fourteen acoustic tasks) and n_frames (integer). file_collections adds that 'Every table is paired with a JSON data dictionary whose keys match the table's column names and whose values give a one-sentence description, the question asked of the participant where applicable, and the data type of the response.' The four documented variables are precisely the cross-file join keys on which all integration depends, and each carries an identifier flag, a data type, a description and, where relevant, a re-identification caveat. The mechanism for the remaining columns is disclosed concretely. Coverage is the weakness and is flagged as a medium-severity completeness issue: four entries against hundreds of phenotype and static-feature columns. Scored 1 because the content present is non-trivial, correctly typed and sufficient for the integration task the sub-element exists to support, not because the field is merely non-empty.

name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
text: intended_uses gives two use_category entries (Research; Cohort selection and phenotyping) with usage_notes and examples; prohibited_uses gives three entries each with a prohibition_reason, covering re-identification attempts, uses foreseeably causing harm or stigmatization, and IP protection used to block access; discouraged_uses names 'hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustments, or any form of surveillance that could lead to discrimination or harm'. All three limbs are populated with reasoned content. Pairing each prohibition with its rationale rather than a bare list lets a downstream user apply the principle to cases the list does not enumerate, which is the more useful form of guidance. Use guidance is coherent with the ethics and bias fields: the discouraged surveillance and insurance uses follow from the representation and measurement biases documented under known_biases, and the re-identification prohibition follows from the acknowledged residual risk in participant_privacy.reidentification_risk.

name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
text: ethical_reviews lists three reviewing organizations: the University of South Florida IRB ('submitted and approved by the USF single IRB and by subsite IRBs through the single IRB process'), Canadian institutional REBs ('Mount Sinai Hospital, the Hospital for Sick Children and the University of Toronto... applied for separate Research Ethics Board approvals... copies of the approvals were submitted to the University of South Florida IRB'), and a Bridge2AI-Voice ethics working group whose memorandum on restricting raw voice to controlled access is published alongside the documentation. human_subject_research.irb_approval and ethics_review_board repeat the USF approval; regulatory_compliance records HIPAA de-identification and HIPAA-compliant storage via NIH STRIDES. Oversight is documented at a level that lets a reader trace which body approved what and how the cross-border complication was handled, rather than asserting that approval exists. The consistency check that involves_human_subjects: true must be matched by populated oversight passes decisively. Fails the data-protection-impact limb: no data_protection_impacts entry exists, and source_caveats discloses that 'no analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted'. Recorded as a failed consistency check given the sensitive content and the acknowledged residual re-identification risk. Scored 1 because the source rubric's field list is disjunctive and the ethics-review limb is satisfied comprehensively; the DPIA gap is carried as a medium-severity issue rather than absorbed silently.

name: Deidentification Method Described
text: is_deidentified.method: 'HIPAA Safe Harbor, with additional removal of indirect and highly sensitive elements'; identifiers_removed enumerates the Safe Harbor set plus 'state and province of collection, with country retained', indirect geographic and demographic identifiers, household composition and cultural identity, 'non-identifying but highly sensitive elements such as household income, mental health status and traumatic life experiences', narrative text fields and free-speech transcripts, and all raw voice waveforms; deidentification_details adds that 'Dates were rebased or replaced by integers', that transcripts were reviewed and recordings containing identifying information or external voices removed, and that 'K-anonymization at k greater than or equal to two is not achieved'. A named standard, an enumerated removal set that goes beyond that standard, the operational detail of how dates and geography were handled, and a candid statement of what the method does not achieve. This is the strongest field in the record. Method appropriateness check passes: Safe Harbor is the correct baseline for US health data, and the additional removals respond to the specific re-identification vectors of a voice corpus. The source_caveats admission that 'a person's voice is unique to them' is semantically consistent with, and is the stated cause of, the two-tier access design recorded independently under raw_data_sources and related_datasets. The is_deidentified-implies-method and implies-identifiers_removed checks both pass.

name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
text: participant_privacy.anonymization_method (Safe Harbor plus state and province removal, narrative and transcript removal, waveform withholding); privacy_techniques enumerating direct-identifier removal, indirect-identifier removal where combination with public data creates risk, date rebasing, geographic generalization, transcript review, and 'two-tier dissemination, with derived features under registered access and raw audio under controlled access'; reidentification_risk: 'Residual risk is acknowledged. Voice is inherently identifiable, so raw audio is disseminated only through controlled access; K-anonymization at k greater than or equal to two is not achieved in the released tables'; data_linkage describing EHR access for diagnosis validation and stating that 'Identifiable linkage tables are held within each collecting institution and are not shared'. The re-identification risk limb is explicitly assessed rather than asserted away, and the assessment is negative in the right direction: it names a specific unmet anonymity property. The data_linkage entry closes the loop on where the re-identification key lives. Fully consistent with is_deidentified and with the access tiers in E2. The data_protection_impacts check that a DPIA should accompany an assessed re-identification risk fails here as recorded under sub-element 1, but the risk assessment itself is present and substantive, which is what this sub-element asks for.

name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
text: informed_consent.consent_obtained: true; consent_type names four modalities (paper signature, electronic within the collection application, REDCap survey form, or video recording in which the participant reads a statement aloud, 'used to verify that the acoustic data submitted belongs to the consented individual'); consent_documentation (REDCap storage, retained at least five years); consent_scope (covers EHR access for gold-standard validation and onward sharing of de-identified data, and informs participants of the registered and controlled tiers); withdrawal_mechanism ('Participants may withdraw at any point... once voice data collection is complete the recordings cannot be removed'). Reinforced by collection_consents, collection_notifications ('Approximately thirty minutes was spent explaining the study... potential participants were asked to explain back what they had understood') and consent_revocations (re-consent before each longitudinal session). Exceptional. The teach-back procedure and the honest statement of the limits of withdrawal are both the kind of detail that is usually omitted, and the consent scope is mapped onto the actual dissemination tiers the dataset uses. The IRB-implies-consent check passes. Consent scope and licence terms are mutually consistent on commercial use and algorithm development. The video-consent mechanism is semantically apt for a voice corpus, tying consent to voice identity.

name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
text: at_risk_populations.special_protections: 'Enrollment in this dataset is restricted to participants aged 18 years or older. Pediatric participants are enrolled only through the pediatric sites, under a separate protocol, and are released as a separate dataset', with source_caveats recording that the IRB protocol identifies only children as vulnerable and notes that psychiatric instruments 'may cause discomfort or trigger negative emotions'. participant_compensation: compensation_provided: true, type 'Electronic gift cards', amount '40 US dollars for a data collection session lasting under 90 minutes and 80 US dollars for a session lasting over 90 minutes, for no more than three sessions and a maximum total of 120 US dollars', with rationale and the amendment history. Both limbs are met. Compensation is quantified with its cap and its protocol-amendment provenance, which supports an undue-inducement judgement rather than merely disclosing that payment occurred. The age restriction is a real protection, verified against the separate pediatric release under related_datasets. Consistent with human_subject_research.special_populations (18 to 120) and with the pediatric relationship, whose note independently records parental consent and child assent for that cohort. Flagged as a low-severity content-accuracy issue: the record declines to determine whether the cognitive-impairment and psychiatric cohorts are at-risk groups, which is correct source discipline but leaves a live protection question for participants with dementia.

name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
text: subpopulations.subpopulation_elements_present: true; identification: 'Demographic sub-populations are identified by age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status, collected through a detailed demographic questionnaire'; distribution: 'The distribution across sub-populations is uneven... groups with less trust in the medical system or in AI, and groups less proximal to the collection sites, were less likely to be recruited. Participants were screened for different disorders depending on site, so demographic composition, disorder category and recording device are entangled.' Five subsets each carry is_subpopulation: true with detailed clinical inclusion criteria and per-cohort gold-standard validation methods. Inclusion and exclusion criteria are documented to an unusual depth at cohort level, naming specific diagnoses and the imaging or physiological evidence used to confirm each. The distribution statement offers a causal account of the skew rather than a disclaimer. Consistent with known_biases.representation_bias and with sampling_strategies.why_not_representative, which give the same account independently. Warning: the characterization is entirely qualitative - no counts or percentages are given for any demographic stratum or cohort, so subgroup sizes cannot be determined from the datasheet.

name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
text: instances[0]: instance_type 'Human participant', counts: 833; anomalies give per-feature record counts 'ranging from 28,640 for articulatory estimates to 32,522 for pitch'; file_collections state exact counts per file (29,278 spectrograms, 32,522 pitch, 28,640 sparc_ema, 31,855 loudness, 31,872 periodicity, 29,289 ppgs); subsets carry is_data_split: false. Counts are specific at both the participant and the recording level, and the per-file counts are given individually rather than as a single headline, which matters because they legitimately differ. The differing per-feature counts are not an inconsistency: anomalies explains that 'Some audio files... could not generate certain features'. The record also discloses, rather than reconciles, the discrepancy between a ~61,937 recording figure quoted for version 3.0 and the 3.1.0 per-feature range - correct handling of an unresolvable source conflict, carried as a warning.

name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
text: variables defines four typed variables with is_identifier flags; subsets carry is_data_split: false and is_subpopulation: true on all five entries; splits.split_details: 'The release provides no predefined recommended data splits for training, validation or testing. Researchers are encouraged to create their own splits based on their specific requirements, taking the multivariate distribution across disorder category, site and demographics into account.' Three of the four evidence paths are populated, and the split position is stated affirmatively with the methodological warning a user needs: because site, device and disorder are entangled, a naive random split would leak. That guidance is worth more than a supplied split would be. Low-severity gap: is_tabular is absent from the record although the phenotype and static-feature files are explicitly tab-delimited tables. The is_data_split: false flags are consistent with the splits block, so the two representations agree rather than conflict.

name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
text: instances carry data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:36 and data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:69; subsets enumerate conditions in clinical detail across four cohorts (laryngeal cancer, muscle tension dysphonia, spasmodic dysphonia, unilateral vocal fold paralysis, presbyphonia; airway stenosis by site, bilateral vocal fold paralysis, unexplained chronic cough, COPD, asthma; mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, other dementias, ALS, Parkinson's disease; anxiety, bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder with enumerated comorbidities); the phenotype collection lists one diagnosis table per condition across eighteen conditions. Condition coverage is documented three times over at increasing granularity - cohort, diagnosis table and validation method - so a user can determine not only which conditions are present but how each label was established. The prose enumeration is rich and internally consistent. Low-severity issue: the ontology CURIEs B2AI_TOPIC:36 and B2AI_SUBSTRATE:69 are opaque, carrying no label and no resolvable prefix, so the machine-readable topic assertion is not independently interpretable.

name: Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented
text: anomalies gives four entries (site-varying collection configurations and protocol drift over time; feature-generation failures explaining the differing per-file counts; version 2.0 spectrogram reprocessing and version 3.1.0 parquet repair; noise artifacts from variable headset distance). sampling_strategies records is_sample: true, is_random: false, is_representative: false with source_data, strategies and why_not_representative. missing_data_documentation gives missing_data_patterns, missing_data_causes and handling_strategy ('A missingness table is included with the dataset... No imputation was performed'). All three limbs are substantively populated, and the anomalies are tied to their observable consequences in the released files rather than listed abstractly. The shipped missingness table is a concrete artifact, not a promise. The three fields agree with each other and with instances.missing_information, which gives the same three causes of missingness independently. The explicit negative on imputation is consistent with the absence of imputation_protocols and correctly satisfies that limb in Element 8 sub-element 5.

name: Dataset Version Number Provided
text: version: 3.1.0; corroborated by page https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ and by version_access.versions_available. A precise semantic version, not a date or a vague label, and it is the version the whole record is scoped to. Matches the MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH pattern and is consistent across version, page, versions_available, version_details and the citation string.

name: Version Access Methods Documented
text: version_access.versions_available lists 1.1, 2.0.0, 2.0.1, 3.0.0, 3.1.0; latest_version_doi: doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42; version_details: 'Each version of the dataset has a unique DOI: version 1.1 is 10.13026/249v-w155, version 3.0.0 is 10.13026/k81f-qr68 and version 3.1.0 is 10.13026/8xbn-nq66, with 10.13026/37yb-1t42 resolving to the latest version... By default older versions continue to be supported, hosted and made available, though the publishers reserve the right to remove access to older versions.' A user can reach any specific version by DOI and knows the retention policy for old versions, including the caveat that it is not guaranteed. The concept-DOI-versus-version-DOI distinction is made explicit. All four DOIs carry the PhysioNet 10.13026 prefix consistently. The divergence between latest_version_doi and the record's own doi is explained by version_details and is correct by design, though flagged as a low-severity readability issue.

name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
text: errata.erratum_details: 'version 2.0 reprocessed spectrograms to fix minor issues identified in version 1.1 and removed all spectrograms and MFCCs derived from free-speech recordings; version 2.0.1 corrected the authorship list; version 3.1.0 fixed broken parquet files carried over from version 3.0.0 and back-filled validated diagnosis information across conditions', with notes recording that the project documentation states there is no erratum as such but that a changelog is published per version. Per-version corrections are itemized and attributed to the release that made them, including a defect (broken parquet files) that reflects poorly on a prior release. Recording a known-bad prior state is a mark of genuine erratum discipline. Consistent with anomalies, which lists the same version 2.0 reprocessing and 3.1.0 parquet repair independently, and with version_access.version_details. The notes field honestly reconciles the terminology mismatch between 'erratum' and 'changelog' rather than forcing one.

name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
text: updates.frequency: Semi-annual; update_details: 'Further versions of the dataset will be released twice a year, distributed as new versions on the hosting platform. Users will be notified through news items on the platform as well as through standard communication channels. Updates correct labeling errors, add new instances and reorganize files; the collection is released as static versions rather than being dynamically updated.' A stated cadence, a notification channel, the kinds of change to expect, and the static-versioning model - the four things a downstream pipeline maintainer needs to plan around. The semi-annual claim is corroborated by distribution_dates: five releases from 2025-01-17 to 2026-05-01, an observed cadence of roughly four to five months, consistent with the stated schedule. Temporal ordering across the five dates is strictly increasing.

name: Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources
text: was_derived_from: 'Raw voice, speech, breath and cough audio recordings, together with questionnaire responses retrieved from ReproSchema-UI or exported from REDCap, collected prospectively from consented participants'; raw_data_sources gives three entries with source_description, source_type, raw_data_format and access_details (prospective audio collection as WAV via Synapse; REDCap electronic data capture converted to tab-delimited tables with JSON dictionaries, published at github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap and archived on Zenodo; retrospective multimodal EHR and imaging extraction, not released); updates.update_details and version_access.version_details supply the release-specific notes. Provenance is traceable end to end: from the instrument that captured each stream, through the system it was held in, to the derived artifact distributed here, with the parts deliberately not released identified and explained. The third raw source is included precisely to record what was collected but withheld. Release-specific notes are read from the dedicated updates.update_details field and from version_access.version_details, both of which carry actual derivation and release information rather than unrelated commentary. Consistent with the derives_from relationship to the Synapse raw-audio distribution recorded under related_datasets.

name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
text: purposes gives four responses: creating an ethically sourced flagship dataset so voice can be developed as a biomarker and integrated into clinical care; enabling development, benchmarking and validation of clinically applicable models across vocal, neurological, psychiatric, respiratory and pediatric disorders; introducing and standardizing 'the field of audiomics by developing new standards of acoustic and voice data collection and analysis, creating benchmarks of diversity metrics, and minimizing the risk of algorithmic bias'; and supplying an openly documented resource supporting ethical voice AI research. addressing_gaps adds three specific gaps: prior studies with samples too small or lacking key metadata, absence of collection standards preventing pooling, and industry-held voice data that is privately held and therefore unauditable for fair representation. Motivation is stated as a response to named deficiencies in the prior literature rather than as generic aspiration, and the addressing_gaps entries make the scientific rationale falsifiable. Purposes align with the funding goals: the description identifies the dataset as the flagship deliverable of the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Precision Public Health grand challenge, and the standards-and-bias purposes map directly onto that programme's stated aims. The funding-implies-purpose-alignment check passes.

name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
text: tasks gives three responses: 'Detection and classification of disease from voice, speech, breath and cough, across vocal pathologies, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, and respiratory disorders'; 'Screening, diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring of health conditions using voice as a non-invasive, low-cost biomarker'; and methodological work on 'acoustic feature extraction, voice bioinformatics standards and diversity benchmarking for voice AI'. Tasks are specific enough to be recognizable as machine-learning problem statements and map onto the cohort structure and the released feature families, so a user can tell which released artifact serves which task. Task list is consistent with intended_uses ('AI model pretraining, fine-tuning, benchmarking and validation') and with the four subsets, and does not overclaim relative to known_limitations, which independently constrains generalization.

name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
text: funders[0].grantor: 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund, through the Bridge2AI program'; the grant description identifies the award to the University of South Florida with a project period of 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 and a fiscal year 2025 amount of 4,660,942 US dollars. maintainers additionally records the funders of the hosting platform: NIBIB, NHLBI and the NIH Office of the Director under U24EB037545 and R01EB030362. The funding agency, the specific programme within it, the recipient institution, the project period and the award amount are all present - well beyond naming an agency. Agency and mechanism are correctly paired: the OT2 activity code is an Other Transaction award, which is the mechanism the NIH Common Fund actually uses for Bridge2AI, and OD is the correct administering institute for Common Fund programmes. The project period is internally consistent with the 2025 and 2026 release dates.

name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
text: funders[0].grants lists grant_number OT2OD032720 ('Core project number for Bridge2AI: Voice as a Biomarker of Health'), 3OT2OD032720-01S1 ('Administrative supplement cited by the PhysioNet data releases as the funding source') and 3OT2OD032720-01S3 ('Application 11376382 in NIH RePORTER, fiscal year 2025'). source_caveats records that 'Sources cite different award identifiers for the same core project: the PhysioNet releases give 3OT2OD032720-01S1, NIH RePORTER gives 3OT2OD032720-01S3, the feasibility publication gives 1OT2OD032720-01, and the project documentation footer gives a garbled 3Tf-OTOD03272001S2. The core project number OT2OD032720 is consistent across all sources.' Award numbers are present in structured grant_number slots rather than buried in prose, and the conflict between sources is surfaced and adjudicated to the stable core number instead of one variant being silently chosen. NIH pattern check passes. OT2OD032720 decomposes as activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032720, matching [Type][Number][Institute][Digits]. The supplements 3OT2OD032720-01S1 and -01S3 carry the canonical application type 3 prefix with support year 01 and supplement suffix. The garbled variant is correctly identified as garbled rather than recorded as a fourth award. Platform grants U24EB037545 and R01EB030362 also parse correctly.

name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
text: creators lists the consortium plus fifteen named individuals with affiliations and roles, including two co-principal investigators with structured principal_investigator entries carrying identifiers and affiliations (Yael Bensoussan, University of South Florida Health Morsani College of Medicine; Olivier Elemento, Weill Cornell Medicine) and module leads for ethics, informatics, each disease cohort and the processing pipeline. notes records that 'over 50 other investigators, clinicians, scholars and trainees contributed, and the PhysioNet author list for version 3.1.0 names more than one hundred individuals'. maintainers names three maintaining bodies with contact details. Attribution is role-resolved rather than a flat author list: a reader can tell who led the ethics module, who led each cohort and who built the pipeline. The acknowledgement of the wider contributor body is quantified and the discrepancy with the fuller PhysioNet list is disclosed. Name-spelling conflicts between sources are surfaced rather than silently resolved: the record notes 'Jennifer Sui' versus 'Jennifer Siu' and 'Frank Rudzizc' versus 'Frank Rudzicz', preferring the PhysioNet forms as the higher-ranked source and recording the alternative. Affiliations are plausible and internally consistent with the five-site and cross-border structure described elsewhere.

name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
text: Three collection_mechanisms entries: the custom Bridge2AI-Voice tablet application hosting the acquisition protocols, acoustic tasks, demographic and confounder surveys and validated questionnaires; the hardware configuration 'iPads of the 9th or 10th generation and iPad Air of the 5th generation, with an Avid AE-36 microphone connected through an Apple dongle. Distinct iPad devices were used at each site'; and REDCap capture of clinical, diagnostic and multimodal data, 'from which the dataset was exported and converted using an open source library developed by the consortium'. Supplemented by direct_collection (in clinic, with a trained research assistant), data_collectors (two role entries) and collection_timeframes. Settings are specified down to the microphone model and dongle, which is the level at which acoustic collection is actually reproducible. The per-site device variation is disclosed here rather than only in the bias section. The device detail here is what makes known_biases.measurement_bias verifiable: the confound between site, device and diagnostic label is stated in both places consistently. source_caveats correctly excludes remote collection as a mechanism for this release on the ground that it was IRB-approved but did not occur. Warning: collection_timeframes gives only a twelve-month duration with no absolute dates, and the record itself flags that this may not describe the window for all 833 participants.

name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
text: acquisition_methods sets was_directly_observed, was_reported_by_subjects, was_inferred_derived and was_validated_verified all true, with acquisition_details mapping each flag to its stream: 'Voice, speech, breath and cough were directly observed and recorded during the session; demographics, confounders and validated questionnaires were reported by subjects; the released features are derived from the recorded waveforms. Clinical diagnoses were verified by clinicians reviewing audio or imaging data, consulting electronic health records, or checking medication prescriptions, against established gold standards for each disorder.' raw_data_sources supplies three source entries with formats and access paths. Rather than setting four booleans and leaving them uninterpreted, the record says which data stream each flag refers to, so the acquisition modality of every released component is determinable. The four flags are each independently corroborated: direct observation by collection_mechanisms, subject report by the questionnaire inventory in file_collections, derivation by preprocessing_strategies, and verification by labeling_strategies and the per-cohort validation methods in subsets.

name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
text: Five preprocessing_strategies entries with exact parameters: monaural conversion and 16 kHz resampling with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter; spectrograms by short-time FFT with '25 ms window size, 10 ms hop length and a 400-point FFT', downsampled by two in time, with sixty MFCCs and a 60-bin Mel spectrogram on the same parameters; articulatory features via Speech Articulatory Coding producing kinematic traces at 50 Hz and posteriorgrams at 100 Hz; openSMILE acoustic features with Parselmouth and Praat prosodic measures; Whisper Large transcription with free-speech transcripts removed before release. cleaning_strategies states that no cleaning-motivated preprocessing was performed and describes the audit protocol instead (missingness tables, distribution and outlier checks, schema validation of categorical responses, audio QC including silence, duration and comparison of produced speech against the intended passage). labeling_strategies gives annotations_per_item: 1, a data_annotation_protocol referencing Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10, and annotator_demographics. machine_annotation_tools lists eight tools with descriptions. This is replication-grade documentation for the preprocessing limb: another group could recompute the spectrograms from the stated parameters. The annotation-quality limb is honest about its weakness, recording a single annotator per item and noting that off-the-shelf models 'have not been audited for correctness, so no accuracy figures are available'. No annotation_analyses or imputation_protocols slots exist, but the substance of both is carried: annotation quality is discussed in labeling_strategies.notes and machine_annotation_tools.notes, and missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy states that no imputation was performed. The claim that no cleaning was done is consistent with instances.missing_information, which attributes missingness to protocol optionality and collection irregularities rather than to exclusion.

name: Software and Tools Documented
text: Evidence carried by machine_annotation_tools.tools and tool_descriptions, corroborated in preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies and external_resources: 'Whisper Large generated transcriptions; openSMILE extracted acoustic features capturing temporal dynamics; Praat through the Parselmouth interface produced phonetic and prosodic measures of fundamental frequency, formants and voice quality; torchaudio produced spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs and pitch contours; sparc produced electromagnetic articulography estimates...; ppgs produced high-fidelity neural phonetic posteriorgrams. b2aiprep organized and preprocessed the dataset and SenseLab processed the audio files; this release was generated with b2aiprep version 3.0.0.' external_resources gives b2aiprep at https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep as 'The library used to organize and preprocess the dataset, to convert the raw audio waveforms into the parquet feature files' and SenseLab at https://github.com/sensein/senselab. Well above the threshold. Every named tool occupies a processing or transformation role with respect to the distributed data, each is tied to the specific released artifact it produced, and the orchestrating library is pinned to a version and a public repository, so the release is reconstructible in principle. Role test applied explicitly. The Bridge2AI-Voice app and REDCap are capture and instrumentation software (role a) and PhysioNet is the serving platform (role b); neither was relied on for this score. The point rests on openSMILE, Praat/Parselmouth, torchaudio, sparc, ppgs, Whisper Large, b2aiprep 3.0.0 and SenseLab, all of which produced or transformed the data being distributed.

name: External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols
text: external_resources gives six entries with URLs, licences and archival status, including the REDCap dictionary (MIT licence, archived at zenodo.org/records/14989503) whose description notes that 'The dictionary encodes which data elements are sensitive, which drove field removal at de-identification', the documentation site archived at zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653, FHIR profiles, and the Voice Scholars training programme. Imputation: missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy states 'A missingness table is included with the dataset and missingness tables are generated as part of the audit protocol. No imputation was performed.' External resources are not merely linked but characterized by their function, and two are archived with DOIs so the link rot risk is addressed. The imputation limb is satisfied by an explicit negative, which the sub-element expressly accepts. The Zenodo DOI prefix 10.5281 is correct for that registrar. The conforms_to limb is unmet by design and is treated as the basis for the Element 10 sub-element 3 zero rather than penalized twice here; the external-resources and imputation limbs are independently satisfied.

name: Known Limitations Documented
text: known_limitations gives six typed entries: representativeness_limitation (five sites, not representative of any wider population) with scope_impact and recommended_mitigation; coverage_limitation ('Data collection and participant communication were conducted in English; only fluent English speakers were eligible'); scope_limitation (raw waveforms not included; free-speech-derived dense features additionally withheld); methodological_limitation ('Diagnostic labels rest on a single clinician's assessment per instance, and validation practices differ by disorder'); temporal_limitation (diagnostic-criteria drift and protocol change as sources of distribution shift); integration_limitation (multimodal imaging, laryngoscopy and genomic data uploaded to REDCap but not released). Limitations are typed, non-overlapping and each identifies a distinct failure mode a user could actually encounter. The English-only eligibility constraint and the single-clinician labelling admission are both consequential disclosures that weaker records omit. Each limitation is corroborated elsewhere rather than free-standing: the representativeness claim by sampling_strategies, the scope claim by is_deidentified and raw_data_sources, the methodological claim by labeling_strategies.annotations_per_item: 1, and the temporal claim by anomalies.

name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
text: known_biases gives four entries using distinct BiasTypeEnum categories. selection_bias: recruitment 'from high volume expert clinics within academic institutions on the basis of an existing diagnosis, using a non-probability sampling method', with a mitigation_strategy and affected_subsets listing four subset URIs. representation_bias: skews by disorder category, site and demographics, noting that 'Groups with less trust in the medical system or in AI... were less likely to be recruited'. measurement_bias: 'Distinct iPad devices were used at each site and participants were screened for different disorders depending on site, so diagnostic label and recording device are confounded.' annotation_bias: 'A single labeler provided the diagnostic label for each instance... Diagnostic practice varies between clinicians and sites.' future_use_impacts records anticipated downstream effects on generalization. Four genuinely distinct bias mechanisms, each with a causal account, two with mitigation strategies, and one with machine-readable links to the affected subsets. The measurement_bias entry identifies a device-label confound that would materially mislead a naive classifier, which is the most useful single disclosure in the record for a modelling reuser. Taxonomy use is correct: each category is applied to a mechanism that genuinely belongs to it rather than the labels being applied loosely. affected_subsets URIs resolve against the subset identifiers declared in the same record, so the cross-reference is internally valid.

name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
text: anomalies gives four entries: heterogeneous site configurations and protocol change over time; feature-generation failures producing per-file count variation 'ranging from 28,640 for articulatory estimates to 32,522 for pitch'; version 2.0 spectrogram reprocessing and version 3.1.0 parquet repair; and 'Noise artifacts are present in the recordings; the head-mounted headset microphone could sit at slightly different distances between participants.' Anomalies are quantified where quantification is possible and are tied to observable properties of the released files, so a user encountering the differing row counts will find them explained rather than suspect corruption. Disclosing the microphone-distance variation is a candid acoustic-quality admission. The per-file counts cited here match those in file_collections.resources exactly, and the version-fix anomalies match errata. The record does not conflate anomalies with limitations: these are properties of the data as collected, while known_limitations concerns fitness for use.

name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
text: sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present: true, with details covering 'race and ethnic origin information, sexual orientation information, and socioeconomic and health information' and the statement that fields encoded as sensitive in the REDCap dictionary and non-identifying but highly sensitive elements 'such as household income, mental health status and traumatic life experiences, were removed before release'. content_warnings: content_warnings_present: true with two warnings (free-speech transcription may contain offensive or distressing material; phenotype tables record mental health status, psychiatric history and trauma-related responses) and source_caveats noting that in 3.1.0 free-speech transcripts were removed so 'the residual exposure in this release is reduced'. confidential_elements records confidential_elements_present: false with its own reconciling caveat. Both limbs populated, and the content warning is version-aware: it states the warning as inherited from the documentation and then narrows it to what actually remains in 3.1.0, rather than carrying forward a stale warning or dropping it. Consistent with is_deidentified.identifiers_removed, which lists the same highly sensitive elements as removed. The confidential_elements_present: false claim is not contradicted by the Certificate of Confidentiality in regulatory_restrictions, because the record explicitly distinguishes the released dataset from the underlying source data - the potential contradiction is anticipated and resolved in source_caveats.

name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
text: ethical_reviews gives three reviewing bodies including a Bridge2AI-Voice ethics working group whose published memorandum sets out 'the ethical justification for restricting raw voice data samples to controlled access' and records that 'Best ethical practices developed through ethical inquiry guided the voice collection protocol and dissemination practices'. future_use_impacts.impact_details warns that 'models trained on it may not generalize to populations, languages or recording conditions absent from the collection'. Anticipated social harms and their mitigation appear in discouraged_uses (hiring, insurance premium adjustment, surveillance 'that could lead to discrimination or harm') and prohibited_uses (any purpose 'that could foreseeably cause harm or stigmatization to research participants, their families, communities, or specific populations'). The ethical-review limb is exceptionally strong, including a dedicated ethics module with named leads and a published reasoned memorandum rather than a bare approval number. The social-impact limb is met through the anticipated-harm analysis in the use-guidance fields, where specific downstream harms are named and mitigated by prohibition. Recorded shortfalls, both carried as issues rather than absorbed: no conflict-of-interest statement appears anywhere despite the sub-element asking for one, and no data protection impact assessment exists, with source_caveats disclosing that no analysis of impact on data subjects has been conducted. Scored 1 because the ethical-review limb and a substantive anticipated-harm analysis with mitigations are both present; the conflicts and DPIA gaps are the reason this is a qualified rather than an unqualified pass.

name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
text: publisher: https://physionet.org/; page https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; distribution_formats[0].name 'Registered access featurized release on PhysioNet'; maintainers names the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology as the platform maintainer; regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance requires adherence to PhysioNet requirements. PhysioNet is the canonical domain repository for physiological and clinical signal data, so this is a domain-appropriate rather than merely generic archive. Platform identification is corroborated across five independent fields. Platform identity is consistent with the DOI prefix 10.13026 and with the RRID in the citation. source_caveats honestly notes that the publisher value was inferred from the hosting platform and the citation's journal field because 'the bundle makes no explicit publisher statement' - a disclosed inference rather than a silent one.

name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
text: citation gives a complete formatted reference: 'Bensoussan, Y., Sigaras, A., Rameau, A., Elemento, O., Powell, M., Dorr, D., ... Ghosh, S. (2026). Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66. Both limbs present. The citation is version-pinned, names the publisher, carries the platform RRID and resolves the DOI as a URL, so it can be pasted into a reference manager without reconstruction. Citation year 2026 is consistent with issued: 2026-05-01 and with the fifth release date in distribution_dates. Version 3.1.0 in the citation matches the version field. The DOI in the citation matches the doi field exactly.

name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
text: No conforms_to value is present. source_caveats states the position explicitly: 'Brain Imaging Data Structure conformance is stated in the project documentation for the audio-plus-questionnaire distribution organized under a b2ai-voice-audio root, not for the PhysioNet featurized release described here, which is organized into features, metadata and phenotype folders; the BIDS fact is therefore recorded against the raw audio collection under related_datasets and no conforms_to value is asserted for this release.' Scored against this sub-element's field list, which is conforms_to alone. No community data standard - OMOP, FHIR, BIDS, schema.org, Dublin Core - is claimed for the distributed features and phenotype tables. conforms_to_schema is populated but points at the datasheet's own metadata schema, which does not evidence conformance of the data to a community standard. The consortium's FHIR profiles appear under external_resources as a published artifact but are not asserted as applicable to this release. The abstention is well-reasoned and correctly scoped, but the sub-element asks whether conformance is stated, and for this release it is deliberately not. This is a correctly-reasoned absence, not an error, and is recorded as a failed consistency check rather than a correctness fault. The same underlying facts were read more favourably at Element 3 sub-element 3, whose field list includes conforms_to_schema and where ICD-10 and the B2AI ontology CURIEs carry content-level standardization; the divergence between the two scores follows from the difference in the source rubric's field lists, not from inconsistent judgement.

name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
text: external_resources includes the 'Bridge2AI-Voice documentation and dashboard' at https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/ with source at github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs and a Zenodo archive, and the 'Bridge2AI Voice Scholars training program' described as 'Training opportunities for using the dataset, at https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/'. page gives the PhysioNet landing page. extension_mechanism adds contribution_url https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep with discussion forums, issue pages and pull requests for public contribution. Both limbs are met and the outreach limb is met substantively rather than by a bare documentation link: a dedicated training programme, a documentation and dashboard site, and open contribution channels for the processing code together constitute genuine community-facing infrastructure. All URLs are well-formed and the domains are plausible and consistent with the consortium naming used throughout the record. The documentation site is Zenodo-archived, which addresses the durability of the outreach link.

name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
text: Seven related_datasets entries, each with an explicit relationship_type: is_supplemented_by (pediatric release, doi 10.13026/h995-bt35, latest 10.13026/mf9s-5r03), derives_from (raw audio, Synapse syn72370534), is_new_version_of (Health Data Nexus version 1.0, doi 10.57764/qb6h-em84), is_described_by (REDCap dictionary v3.23.0 on Zenodo), is_documented_by (Rameau et al., Interspeech 2024, doi 10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926) and two is_referenced_by entries (Moothedan et al., Front Digit Health, doi 10.3389/fdgth.2025.1514971; Bensoussan et al., JAMA Otolaryngol, doi 10.1001/jamaoto.2023.4807). Every relationship is typed, every target is identified by a resolvable DOI or accession, and most carry an explanatory note. The pediatric note independently documents that cohort's separate REB approval and assent procedure, and the feasibility-study note records that it 'contributed no data to this dataset' - annotations that prevent incorrect provenance inferences. Relationship types are semantically apt in each case and the DOI prefixes are registrar-plausible throughout: 10.13026 PhysioNet, 10.57764 Health Data Nexus, 10.21437 ISCA, 10.3389 Frontiers, 10.1001 JAMA Network. The derives_from and is_new_version_of edges agree with was_derived_from and version_access.version_details respectively.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated: id (doi:10.60775/fairhub.3); title ('Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'); description (~1,600 chars); keywords (7); license_and_use_terms (AI-READI Data License Agreement v2.0, data_use_permission: disease_specific_research); doi (10.60775/fairhub.3); page (https://fairhub.io/datasets/3); creators (AI-READI Consortium with PI Aaron Lee, ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648, nine ROR-identified affiliations); purposes (4 entries); instances (2280, data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:43); variables (20 entries with data_type, unit, measurement_technique); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level ('restricted'); resources (nine metadata_file entries nested under the root_metadata file collection). Absent: parent_datasets. 13 of 14 named fields carry meaningful content (~93%). Only parent_datasets is empty, and the version lineage it would express is captured by typed related_datasets entries (is_new_version_of to 10.60775/fairhub.2 and .1). Content is substantive rather than placeholder throughout. Field values are semantically appropriate to their slots: id and doi agree, page resolves to the publisher named in publisher, and confidentiality_level 'restricted' is consistent with the DUA-gated access mechanism described in data_governance. The resources list appears nested rather than at top level, which satisfies the hierarchical sub-resource intent but is a structurally weaker placement than a top-level list.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description is approximately 1,600 characters and is specific rather than generic: it names the three collection sites, the 2280-participant count, the 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 window, 356,343 files, 3.82 TB, and enumerates thirteen modalities. Each of the four purposes entries exceeds 200 characters, e.g. 'To collect and publicly share a multimodal, AI-ready dataset for studying the pathogenesis and salutogenesis of T2DM, uniformly balanced for T2DM severity across a diverse group of participants recruited at three geographically distinct sites.' Average narrative length far exceeds the 200-character threshold, and length here reflects genuine information density rather than padding. The description carries quantitative specifics that are independently checkable against other fields (participant count matches instances.counts; file count and byte total match the stated totals; date range matches collection_timeframes), so its length corresponds to verifiable content. It also proactively discloses what was removed from the public release.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: keywords: 'Diabetes mellitus', 'Machine Learning', 'Artificial Intelligence', 'Electrocardiography', 'Continuous Glucose Monitoring', 'Retinal imaging', 'Eye exam' — 7 unique terms, all distinct with no near-duplicates. Seven keywords place the record at the top of the 3-7 band, one short of the ≥8 threshold. The set is genuinely diverse, spanning the disease, the analytic method and four acquisition modalities, which is why it scores above the band anchor rather than at it. The keyword set under-represents the record's own modality coverage: OCT angiography, FLIO, wearable activity monitoring, environmental sensing and OMOP conformance are prominent in description and file_collections but absent from keywords, so discoverability lags the actual content. No supplementary condition list or ontology-coded disease field is present to offset the count, though conforms_to_standard supplies standard-level terms.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists 4 entries each with a media type: DICOM (application/dicom), CSV (text/csv), JSON (application/json), Markdown (text/markdown). Additional formats appear in resources (TXT, TSV, MD) and raw_data_sources (.xml, .fda, .sdt, .FIT). total_file_count: 356343. file_collections enumerates 10 collections with per-collection file_count and total_bytes, e.g. retinal_octa (173,721 files; 1,155,908,809,724 bytes), retinal_oct (56,478), retinal_photography (93,921). Well above the >3 threshold, and the enumeration is granular: each collection carries its own path, collection_type, description, file count, byte total and conformance standards. Format variety corresponds to genuine multimodality rather than incidental file-type spread — DICOM for imaging, CSV for OMOP tables and sensor streams, WFDB for waveforms — and the record documents the unifying participant-ID directory scheme that makes the modalities integrable, which is the Bridge2AI multimodality criterion. Only the root_metadata file_count is the record's own enumeration rather than a source-stated value, which it discloses.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: total_size_bytes: 3815969779678; total_file_count: 356343; instances.counts: 2280; per-collection total_bytes for all nine data-type collections; splits giving 1576/352/352; subpopulation distributions with counts for diabetes status, sex and race/ethnicity. Size metadata is present at both dataset and collection granularity, and dimensional metadata is present at participant, split and subpopulation level — comfortably exceeding the pass condition. The stated totals are 9 files and 419,614 bytes larger than the sum over enumerated directories, a gap the record itself surfaces and which the nine root-level metadata files account for exactly. This does not affect the pass determination, since numeric size and count metadata are unambiguously present, but it is logged as a consistency finding.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; publisher: https://fairhub.io/. Prior versions carry their own DOIs (10.60775/fairhub.2, 10.60775/fairhub.1), and the license text is separately archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036. Both halves of the identification requirement are satisfied: a registered persistent identifier and an explicitly named hosting platform, with per-version DOIs rather than a single floating identifier. The 10.60775 prefix is FAIRhub's DataCite registrant and is consistent with the named publisher and landing page, so the identifier and the platform corroborate one another. No RRID is present, which is unremarkable for a dataset record of this kind.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders: NIH with grant_number OT2OD032644 (award title 'Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project', NIH RePORTER project 1OT2OD032644-01, $5,026,499 FY2022, project period 2022-09-01 to 2025-08-31), plus P30DK035816 and UL1TR003096; additional grantors Research to Prevent Blindness and Microsoft AI for Good Lab (cloud services). creators: AI-READI Consortium with principal_investigator Aaron Lee (ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648, contact@aireadi.org) and nine ROR-identified affiliations. data_collectors notes that collection effort was supported by OT2OD032644 by percentage of effort. Meets the top band on both limbs. Grant detail extends beyond award numbers to title, amount and period, and creator affiliations are machine-identified by ROR rather than free text. All three NIH numbers match agency format (OT2/OD, P30/DK, UL1/TR with correct institute codes), and the funding purpose aligns with purposes, which repeatedly invoke salutogenesis — the exact term in the award title. The record also discloses and adjudicates a tier-level disagreement about how many grants support the work, preferring the tier-1 funding reference while retaining the publication-sourced grants as research support. The unresolved Washington University in St. Louis versus University of Washington attribution affects the affiliation semantics but not the completeness of the funding record.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: UW IRB protocol STUDY00016228, initial approval 2022-12-20, annual renewal within 90 days of expiration, reliance agreements with UAB and UCSD IRBs, approval letter published with v3.0.0 documentation, contact hsdrely@uw.edu; second entry records release-level ethics review by Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman and Nicholas Evans. human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects true, ethics_review_board, regulatory_compliance (not FDA-regulated, no DMC, HL7:2N), special_populations (age 40-85, consent-capable, English-speaking; pregnancy, gestational diabetes and T1DM excluded). is_deidentified: method 'HIPAA Safe Harbor', identifiers_removed, internal review for PII. participant_privacy: anonymization_method, privacy_techniques (variable removal, watermarking, license terms, encrypted servers and locked storage during collection), reidentification_risk, data_linkage. participant_compensation: $200 stipend, transport support, disbursement conditions. at_risk_populations: false, with prisoner and minor exclusions recorded. informed_consent: obtained true, e-consent or in-person, documentation, scope, withdrawal_mechanism. collection_consents, collection_notifications and consent_revocations all populated. regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant: compliant. Absent: data_protection_impacts. Nearly every protection area is documented, and several to an unusual depth — the consent pathway, the withdrawal rule that already-shared data remain in the dataset, the compensation disbursement conditions, and the explicit prisoner and minor exclusions. Two gaps hold it below 5: no data_protection_impacts entry, and re-identification risk treated in a single qualitative sentence rather than as an assessment. Cross-field logic passes on the main gates: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by populated ethical_reviews, informed_consent and participant_compensation, and is_deidentified is matched by a named method and listed privacy protections. Two semantic problems reduce the score. First, is_deidentified simultaneously asserts HIPAA Safe Harbor stripping and reports FAIRhub's 'NoDeIdentification' finding that no identifiers were collected; these describe incompatible processing. Second, and more seriously, sensitive_elements_present=false and confidential_elements_present=false are implausible for retinal imaging, CGM and wearable biometric data whose release the record itself gates behind verified-ID login, license assent and watermarking, and for which it concedes a theoretical re-identification risk. Safe Harbor is an appropriate method for the clinical and survey strata, but the record does not address its known limits for high-dimensional imaging and continuous physiological signals, which is where a DPIA would have done the work.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
