The confidentiality_level 'restricted' is the record's own substitution contradicting the sourced 'HL7:2N (normal)', and it sits beside confidential_elements_present false; this is a genuine cross-field inconsistency. It is not deducted here because the record states the substitution, its reason and its conflict with the source in regulatory_restrictions.notes, so a reader learns exactly what the source said and what was asserted instead — the disclosure preserves the field's usability, which is what the question measures. The licence-scope divergence (grant covering commercial use versus the disease-specific access attestation) is likewise disclosed.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to names eight standards with their roles: CDS v0.1.1 organisation, RO-Crate 1.2 packaging, DICOM for ophthalmic imaging, OMOP CDM for clinical data, WFDB for ECG, Open mHealth for wearables and CGM, NASA ASCII Earth Science guidelines for environmental sensing. conforms_to_standard enumerates CDS, RO_CRATE, DICOM, OMOP_CDM, WFDB, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS; conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; conforms_to_class 'Dataset'. Each file_collection repeats its own conforms_to and conforms_to_standard. related_datasets carries four typed links (is_new_version_of ×2, is_source_of, is_supplemented_by). external_resources includes the CDS specification URL 'https://cds-specification.readthedocs.io/en/v0.1.1/'. Integration keys: variables declares participant_id with is_identifier true; file organisation is 'one directory per data type, then modality, then device, then participant'; clinical CSVs are 'a one-to-one mapping to an OMOP Common Data Model table'; participants.tsv carries the split assignment. Top band met on all three components. Standards are declared at both dataset and collection granularity, schema conformance is a resolvable w3id URI, and integration capability is concrete rather than aspirational: a participant identifier common across every modality directory, an OMOP mapping that makes the clinical tables harmonisable with other OMOP sources, and a documented directory contract in a versioned external specification. The standards are used where they belong, which distinguishes real interoperability from standards name-dropping: DICOM appears on exactly the four imaging collections, WFDB on the ECG collection only, Open mHealth on the two wearable streams, and the Earth Science format on the environmental sensor. The RO-Crate packaging plus a dqd_omop.json for the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard indicates machine-actionable rather than merely declared conformance. The is_source_of and is_supplemented_by targets (the mini-subset and the controlled-access release) lack DOIs; the record names them in prose and says explicitly that no identifier is given in the declared sources, which is the correct handling and does not undercut the typed-relationship evidence.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies (3): mapping to OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB and Open mHealth; format conversion — 'Topcon Maestro2 and Triton exports (.fda) and Heidelberg FLIO exports (.sdt) were converted to DICOM, and Garmin exports (.FIT) were converted to the mHealth standard'; and a version-level note that v3.0.0 was produced by 'a combination of automated and custom processing', with a CHANGELOG-derived account of how processing evolved from 'custom, ad hoc processing' at v1.0.0. cleaning_strategies (2): REDCap range flagging with coordinator and data-manager review, checks for 'credibility against prespecified ranges, incorrect flow through prescribed skip patterns, missing data ... and the omission or duplication of records', editing only under site PI approval; plus site data-manager QC before upload and a central check that no PII was included. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling_strategy ('No imputation was applied'). instances.label_description: 'No labels or targets are provided. No specific labeling was performed'. Absent: labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses and imputation_protocols as fields; no software name, version number or repository URL for any conversion or QC step. Strategy documentation is genuinely comprehensive in coverage — preprocessing, cleaning, missing data, and reasoned explicit negatives for labelling and imputation — and the cleaning account is specific enough to be auditable (who flags, who reviews, who authorises edits). What the top band additionally requires is missing: not one piece of data-preparation software is named. The .fda-to-DICOM, .sdt-to-DICOM and .FIT-to-mHealth conversions are the most consequential transformations in the release and are described without a tool, a version or a link, even though the project runs a public GitHub organisation that is cited generically in external_resources. A reuser cannot reproduce the conversions from this record. Hence 4, not 5. The instruments named throughout collection_mechanisms (Philips TC30, Dexcom G6, Garmin Vivosmart 5 and so on) are acquisition devices, not preparation software, so they do not satisfy the software-transparency requirement; counting them would misread the question. The explicit negatives are semantically correct rather than evasive: 'no imputation' is consistent with missing_data_documentation's handling strategy, and 'no labelling' is consistent with the hypothesis-agnostic design stated in purposes and known_limitations. REDCap and the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard (dqd_omop.json) are named as platforms, but without versions, and REDCap is a capture system rather than a preparation tool.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods (2) with typed flags: was_directly_observed true for laboratory, vital, vision, imaging, ECG, monofilament, CGM, wearable and environmental data; was_reported_by_subjects true with was_validated_verified true for survey data, including the verification method ('cross-referencing entered medications against medications physically brought in or photographed'). collection_mechanisms (20) at protocol-parameter depth: 'Optomed Aurora IQ ... 50 degree field of view, 5 Mpix sensor; used undilated in a dark room'; 'Heidelberg Spectralis HRA+OCT ... optic nerve head radial circle high resolution, posterior pole macula 61-line high resolution, and 20x20 macular OCTA'; 'Topcon Maestro2 ... 12.0x9.0 mm widefield, 6.0x6.0 mm 3D macula and 6.0x6.0 mm OCTA at a 50 kHz scan rate'; 'Mars Letter Contrast Sensitivity ... background luminance of 60 to 120 cd/m2 and illuminance of 189 to 377 lux'; 'Dexcom G6 ... the transmitter records readings every five minutes'; 'Garmin Vivosmart 5 ... at a five-second sampling frequency'; site-varying blood pressure devices and lensometers enumerated by model. data_collectors (3): named site teams with role 'clinical research site', staff composition, and the note that 'The UAB data manager also trained research personnel at all three sites'. collection_timeframes: start_date 2023-07-19, end_date 2025-05-01, with timeframe_details and a caveat recording BMJ Open's conflicting 18 July 2023 start. direct_collection and raw_sources additionally describe EHR-based recruitment screening and raw-export retention. This is a full protocol at the level a reader would need to replicate acquisition: every instrument identified by manufacturer, model and city, with scan protocols, sampling rates, luminance conditions and ordering constraints (FLIO 'is performed last in the visit because it takes longer ... and exposes participants to uncomfortable light levels'). Collectors, sites, dates and the recruitment pathway are all specified. Comfortably the top band. The protocol detail is corroborated elsewhere in the record rather than free-floating: the ten-day wear period appears consistently in description, file_collections, collection_mechanisms and anomalies; the site-varying blood pressure and lensometer models named here are precisely what the measurement_bias entry identifies as confounded with site, so the collection account and the bias account are mutually consistent. raw_sources is recorded under that name rather than the schema's raw_data_sources slot, a naming divergence noted but with content fully present. Timeframe ordering is consistent with the 2022-12-20 IRB approval preceding the 2023-07-19 start.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version '3.0.0'; issued '2025-11-17'. version_access.versions_available lists all three releases with their own DOIs and dates: '1.0.0 (DOI 10.60775/fairhub.1, 3 May 2024), 2.0.0 (DOI 10.60775/fairhub.2, 8 November 2024) and 3.0.0 (DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3, 17 November 2025)', with latest_version_doi and the note that each version has its own documentation set selectable from a version dropdown, and that 2.0.0 'is marked ... as no longer accessible'. updates: frequency 'approximately annually', static-version release model, 'Changes between versions are recorded in detail in the CHANGELOG file'. maintainers: AI-READI Consortium, role academic_institution, with hosting details (FAIRhub on Microsoft Azure, 'developed for this project'), contact routes and README pointers. Sustainability: persistent DOI; domain-appropriate repository (FAIRhub, a biomedical data-sharing platform); governance via data_governance (accountable_organization, committee_contact, stewardship_roles, access_review_process); commitment via retention_limit ('There are no limits on the retention of the data') and ongoing enrolment implying further versions. related_datasets records the v1 and v2 lineage with participant counts (204; 1,067). All four sustainability indicators the question names are evidenced — persistent identifiers, a governance plan with a named accountable organisation and contact, a domain-appropriate repository built for this project, and a retention and maintenance commitment — alongside comprehensive versioning with per-version DOIs, dates, counts and a changelog. The one enumerated field genuinely absent is errata, for which the CHANGELOG is referenced but not enumerated; against a slot list of seven this does not pull the assessment below the top band. Two facts the record reports are adverse to sustainability and are flagged as issues rather than scored as documentation failures, because the question measures whether the maintenance picture is documented and here it is documented including its negatives: version 2.0.0 holds a registered DOI yet is recorded as no longer accessible, which is in tension with DOI persistence expectations, and the notes field reproduces the FAIRhub and documentation-site notice that 'This repository is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives'. A record that hid either of these would look more sustainable and be less trustworthy. Version numbering is semantically coherent: major-version increments accompany substantive content changes (the v3.0.0 drop of Snellen acuity variables is recorded under known_limitations as an integration_limitation).

name: Associated Publications
text: citation: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3' — a formal dataset citation identifying the dataset by title, version, publishing organisation and DOI. external_resources holds seven distinct entries, including two DOI-linked publications: 'AI-READI Consortium (2024). "AI-READI: rethinking AI data collection, preparation and sharing in diabetes research and beyond." Nature Metabolism 6:2210-2212, https://doi.org/10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x' and 'Owsley C, Matthies DS, McGwin G, et al. "Cross-sectional design and protocol for Artificial Intelligence Ready and Equitable Atlas for Diabetes Insights (AI-READI)." BMJ Open 2025;15:e097449, https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449'; plus the documentation site, the project website, the GitHub organisation, the Zenodo community and the CDS specification. The licence separately imposes an acknowledgement obligation on publications reporting use of the data. Both conditions for the top band are met with margin: a formal dataset citation naming title, authors/organisation, version and DOI, and well beyond two distinct references, two of which are peer-reviewed publications with resolvable DOIs. Scored at 5 per the exact-value rule for this question. The two publication DOIs have well-formed, registrar-plausible prefixes (10.1038 Nature Portfolio; 10.1136 BMJ) and the cited venues, volumes and article identifiers are internally consistent with those publishers. The seven external resources are genuinely distinct targets rather than repeated links to one resource. The record notes that the BMJ Open title expands the acronym differently from the FAIRhub metadata and records both readings in source_caveats instead of silently harmonising them.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: instance_type 'individual study participant', counts 2280, with missing_information recording which modalities are absent and why. subpopulations (4): race/ethnicity '380 Hispanic, 545 Asian, 519 Black, 836 White'; sex '951 male, 1,329 female'; diabetes status '776 with no diabetes, 560 pre-diabetes or lifestyle-controlled, 686 controlled by oral or non-insulin injectable medication, 258 insulin-controlled'; age 'Mean age ... 60.8 years (standard deviation 11.3)' with eligibility 40–85. subsets: three is_data_split subsets each with its own full demographic composition (e.g. validation '88 each of Hispanic, Asian, Black and White; 176 male and 176 female'). Inclusion/exclusion: adults 40+, able to read and speak English; pregnancy, gestational diabetes and type 1 diabetes excluded; at_risk_populations.special_protections on minors, prisoners and adults unable to consent. missing_data_documentation populated. known_limitations records that the cohort 'does not include Pacific Islanders or Native Americans' and that recruitment was 'predominantly urban and hospital-based'. Demographics are given as exact counts across four independent stratifications, repeated per split, with eligibility criteria, exclusion criteria and an honest statement of who is not represented. This is the top band by a clear margin. Every demographic figure reconciles arithmetically, both within stratification (each of the four sums to 2,280) and across splits (per-group split counts sum to the cohort counts; for example insulin-controlled 105 + 67 + 86 = 258). The record also carries a genuine representational tension without hiding it: subpopulation_elements_present is false for race and sex because those values are withheld from the public release and held under controlled access, so the published aggregates are README summary tables rather than per-instance labels — the notes field says exactly that, and known_limitations states the consequence, that users 'cannot stratify analyses by sex or race/ethnicity, and cannot audit models for disparities across those groups directly'. Documenting the demographics fully while flagging that they are not individually usable is the most informative available handling.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: doi 10.60775/fairhub.3; id doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; publisher https://fairhub.io/; access route https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access; documentation https://docs.aireadi.org; project site https://aireadi.org; code https://github.com/AI-READI; https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi; consent form PDF at docs.aireadi.org; CDS specification at cds-specification.readthedocs.io; publication DOIs 10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449. Passes on every axis: a version-level DOI, a landing page, a documentation site, a code repository and DOI-linked publications. All URLs are structurally valid with plausible domains, and the documentation URLs are version-scoped (the record directs readers to 'Dataset v3.0.0' on docs.aireadi.org), which is what makes findability durable across releases. One adverse signal is recorded rather than scored here: version 2.0.0's DOI is reported as no longer resolving to accessible content, which bears on the persistence of the identifier series even though this version's identifiers are intact.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: data_governance.access_review_process: 'Access to the release requires logging in through a verified ID system, agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research, and accepting the license terms ... The access route is published at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access. Access is granted by self-attestation rather than committee review: the FAIRhub access type for this release is PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired.' distribution_formats enumerates the five obtainable media types with what each contains. license_and_use_terms sets out the obligations a requester accepts. third_party_sharing.is_shared true, with onward-sharing limits. related_datasets records a mini-subset 'made available for pipeline development', and version_access notes Azure Storage access is covered in the v3.0.0 documentation. Note: no download_url field is populated; the access URL appears within data_governance. Every element of the top band is specified: the platform (FAIRhub), the authentication step (verified ID login), the policy step (use attestation plus licence acceptance), the named access tier, the URL where the route begins, and the formats obtained. The record explicitly distinguishes self-attestation from committee review, which is the access-tier distinction the rubric warns against blurring, and it does not misdescribe a gated release as 'public' in the unrestricted sense. Scored from content rather than slot occupancy, per the instrument: the absent download_url is a serialisation gap, not an information gap, since the access URL, tier and procedure are all stated. Accessibility is consistent with the governance and licence declarations — a self-attestation gate matches a release from which sex, race, ethnicity, medications and ZIP have been withheld to a separate controlled tier, and the pipeline-development mini-subset is a coherent low-friction on-ramp. The one caveat is that the mini-subset has no identifier in the declared sources, which the record states rather than inventing one.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms in operative detail (grant scope, derivative-data treatment, model-distribution conditions, acknowledgement, termination, warranty disclaimer). intended_uses (2) with use_category, examples and usage_notes, including that data are 'AI-ready' so research 'can begin without further reformatting'. prohibited_uses (7), each with notes and a prohibition_reason: no clinical treatment decisions; no re-identification or group-membership inference; no sharing with third-party model vendors for training even under a BAA, though 'Short-term interaction such as prompting or querying ... is permitted for analysis'; no onward conveyance outside identically bound licensees; publication limited to 'small representative samples in up to five images or figures per paper'; storage limited to institutional or BAA-covered infrastructure; no removal of watermarking. future_use_impacts (2): no currently anticipated unfair-treatment harms plus an acknowledged theoretical re-identification risk; and the fairness impact that 'users of that release cannot directly stratify or audit model performance across those groups', mitigated by a recommended split 'balanced as well as possible for sex, race/ethnicity and diabetes status, with the stated aim of reducing disparities in models developed from the dataset'. discouraged_uses is not populated. Use guidance is exceptionally operational: each prohibition states what is forbidden and why, and the boundaries are drawn at a level of specificity a compliance officer could apply (the vendor-sharing prohibition distinguishes training from prompting; the publication limit gives a number). The social impact analysis is not generic — it names a concrete harm created by the project's own design choice and pairs it with a concrete mitigation. discouraged_uses is empty, but the seven-entry prohibited_uses list covers the territory that field would occupy, so the top band is met. The use guidance is consistent with the ethics and governance declarations: the re-identification prohibition tracks participant_privacy.reidentification_risk, and the storage limits track regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance. One divergence is recorded as an issue rather than a deduction: the licence grant covers commercial use while data_use_permission is disease_specific_research, a difference the record attributes to the access attestation and discloses. The future_use_impacts entries are also unusual in candour — the second effectively concedes that a transparency measure taken for privacy reasons degrades fairness auditability, which is the kind of trade-off datasheets usually omit.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: Present: version_access (three versions with DOIs and dates, latest_version_doi, version_details); updates (static-version model, CHANGELOG, approximately annual); missing_data_documentation (patterns, causes, handling_strategy); subsets with is_data_split true ×3 and splits.split_details describing the 70/15/15 assignment in participants.tsv; raw_sources describing retained device and REDCap exports and why they are not shared. Lineage in text: preprocessing_strategies traces device-native exports (.fda, .sdt, .FIT, XML, CSV) through conversion to DICOM and mHealth and mapping to OMOP, DICOM, WFDB and Open mHealth; cleaning_strategies names the agents at each stage ('The data manager at each collection site was responsible for the quality control of all data before upload to FAIRhub. After transfer to the central project team, the dataset was additionally reviewed internally'); related_datasets gives the derivation chain v1.0.0 → v2.0.0 → v3.0.0 via is_new_version_of and is_source_of for the mini-subset; anomalies documents modality-specific quality failure modes; known_limitations records the v3.0.0 removal of Snellen acuity variables. Absent: errata; was_derived_from; parent_datasets; no PROV-O or other graph serialisation. This is clearly more than the version history that defines the 3 band: there is an end-to-end textual account of how raw device output became released files, who performed each transformation, and how releases derive from one another, plus quality documentation at modality level. It falls short of the 5 band because the lineage is narrated at the level of strategies rather than resolved into entity–activity–agent relationships over identified artifacts: no was_derived_from links a released collection to the raw export it came from, no activity is identified as an addressable node, and the derivation path exists only as a relationship type between version DOIs. Errata is also absent. The instrument accepts text in place of a PROV-O serialisation where the text provides complete lineage, so the question is whether the lineage is complete, not whether it is RDF. It is not quite complete: a reader can say that .sdt files became DICOM and that site data managers ran QC, but cannot determine which activity produced a given released collection, in what order the mapping and conversion steps ran, or which agent performed the central standardisation. The RO-Crate packaging noted in conforms_to would be a natural carrier for exactly this graph, which makes its absence from the record conspicuous rather than unavoidable. Integrity-side evidence is strong and independently checkable — the file-count and byte-total reconciliations and the split arithmetic all hold — which is why this sits at 4 rather than 3.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases (4), each typed with a BiasTypeEnum value: selection_bias ('Participants are volunteers, so the cohort is subject to volunteer bias ... The protocol publication states this as a limitation and describes no measure taken against it'); representation_bias ('recruitment was predominantly urban and hospital-based ... does not include other races/ethnicities such as Pacific Islanders and Native Americans. Eligibility required the ability to read and speak English'), mitigated by three-site geographic selection; sampling_bias, with affected_subsets naming 'Version 3.0.0 as a whole; the recommended validation and test partitions are balanced ... while the training partition is not', mitigated by uniform protocols across sites; measurement_bias ('blood pressure monitors and lensometers differ by site, and retinal imaging is acquired on multiple manufacturers' instruments — so device make and model may be confounded with site'), mitigated by documenting device make, model and scan modality. Fairness analysis in future_use_impacts: the inability to stratify by sex or race in the public release, mitigated by demographically balanced validation and test splits aimed at 'reducing disparities in models developed from the dataset'. known_limitations adds representativeness, coverage, temporal, scope, methodological and integration limitations. Top band met: four biases categorised with schema-standard type values, each with a substantive description, three with mitigation strategies and one with affected subsets identified, plus a fairness analysis that connects a documented bias to a concrete design mitigation. The categorisation is systematic rather than a single undifferentiated 'limitations' paragraph. The bias types are applied correctly, which is the semantic test that matters here: measurement_bias is used for a device-versus-site confound rather than for a sampling problem, and representation_bias and sampling_bias are distinguished sensibly (who is absent from the cohort versus how the realised distribution departs from the balanced target). The selection_bias entry carries no mitigation and says so explicitly, which is more credible than a fabricated one. No AIO ontology URIs are attached, but the rubric names BiasTypeEnum as an acceptable standard taxonomy and the enum values are used throughout. The bias claims corroborate the numbers elsewhere: the assertion that training is unbalanced while validation and test are balanced is verifiable from the split composition figures.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated (10 of 14): id 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; title 'CHoRUS Dataset'; description (~1,450 chars); keywords (13); license_and_use_terms.license_terms (controlled access + signed licensing agreement); page 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; creators (7 entries, 6 with affiliations); purposes (4 responses); instances (6 instance types with counts 50000 / 1600000000 / 7642); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted'. Absent (4 of 14): doi, resources, parent_datasets, variables. 10/14 = 71% of the enumerated mandatory fields carry meaningful content, landing squarely on the 70% band. The populated fields are substantive rather than token-filled. The four absences are not equally weighted in practice: doi is the consequential one, and variables is a real gap for a 1.6-billion-row OMOP release where no variable-level documentation is offered beyond modality-level narrative. Field presence and field meaning agree throughout the populated set; no placeholder or self-referential filler. The one semantic defect is that id and page hold the identical project-homepage URL, so the record technically populates id while providing no dataset-level identifier — presence without identifying function. Counted as present for the proportion but penalized at Q6/Q16/Q13.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description is roughly 1,450 characters and carries specific figures (14 contributing hospitals from a network of 20 academic centers, 50,000 admissions from ICU/PICU/NICU, 1.6 billion OMOP rows, 7,642 admissions with radiology, 23 Tb of waveforms, 100,000 anticipated admissions across 9 modalities). purposes holds four responses of roughly 180–260 characters each, e.g. 'Generate data for ML/AI applications aimed at characterizing acute and critical care illness, predicting complications, and measuring treatment response...' and 'Provision a holdout test set accessible for model external validation...'. Far above the 200-character threshold, and the length is carrying information rather than padding: the description states modality-specific standards, the access model (enclave for OMOP and telemetry, local retention for notes), and the released-versus-anticipated distinction in a single pass. Length here correlates with semantic density rather than diluting it — nearly every clause is a checkable factual claim, and the claims agree with instances, file_collections and distribution_formats elsewhere in the record. The description also correctly hedges the holdout test set as an award-abstract statement rather than a released artifact.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: 13 unique keywords: critical care; intensive care; acute illness; electronic health records; OMOP Common Data Model; waveform telemetry; electroencephalography; medical imaging; clinical notes; multimodal clinical data; Bridge2AI; AI-ready dataset; social determinants of health. Comfortably above the 8-keyword threshold with no duplicates or near-duplicates beyond the acceptable 'critical care'/'intensive care' pair, and the set spans three useful axes: clinical domain, data modality, and program/standard. Keywords are semantically faithful to the content: every modality keyword (waveform telemetry, electroencephalography, medical imaging, clinical notes) maps to an actual file_collection, and 'OMOP Common Data Model' maps to conforms_to_standard. 'social determinants of health' is the one keyword whose backing is thin — SDOH appears only in sensitive_elements and participant_privacy.notes, with no SDOH variables or collection described, so it slightly oversells coverage. The 'Bridge2AI' and program-affiliation signals are drawn from keywords and funders as permitted.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists 5 entries: OMOP Common Data Model; OHNLP; DICOM; WFDB; EDF+ and Persyst. file_collections enumerates 5 matching collections with ids (#collection-omop, #collection-waveform-telemetry, #collection-imaging, #collection-clinical-notes, #collection-eeg), each with collection_type 'processed_data' and its own conforms_to. total_file_count is absent. Five distinct formats, well past the >3 band, and each is documented with its access posture and metadata-publication status rather than merely named. The unmet part of the field set is enumeration proper: total_file_count is unset and no per-collection file counts are given, so 'how many files' remains unanswerable even though 'what kinds' is answered well. Format variety genuinely reflects multi-modality as corroborated by description ('imaging from PACS in DICOM, bedside telemetry in WFDB, EEG in EDF+ and Persyst') and by the modality keywords, so the variety is substantive and not an artifact of listing serialization variants of one thing. Each format is the conventional standard for its modality, which is the correct semantic pairing.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: instances[].counts gives 50000 (hospital admissions of critically ill patients), 1600000000 (OMOP EHR rows) and 7642 (admissions with radiology imaging). description and the waveform collection both state '23 Tb of waveform data'. subpopulations identifies ICU/PICU/NICU strata and splits describes a planned holdout partition. total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes are unset. Passes on instance counts, which are explicit, numeric and present for three of six instance types. Two of the six (waveform records, EEG recordings) carry no count — the record says so directly for waveforms: 'no record or file count is given for the waveform modality'. The counts are mutually plausible: 1.6 billion OMOP rows across 50,000 ICU/PICU/NICU admissions is about 32,000 rows per admission, which is a realistic order of magnitude for high-frequency nursing flowsheet and medication-administration documentation in critical care. 23 Tb across a waveform cohort of this scale is likewise plausible for continuous bedside telemetry. Counted as pass with a warning that the 23 Tb figure and all size information live in prose rather than in total_size_bytes, so sizes are readable but not computable; the 50,000 versus 45K cohort discrepancy is disclosed in source_caveats and does not affect the pass.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: id: 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; page: 'https://chorus4ai.org/'. No doi field. No publisher field. Stable third-party links exist in external_resources: 'https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824' (the NIH RePORTER award record) and 'https://github.com/chorus-ai' (the 28-repository code organization). Passes only on the fail-band's literal wording — 'Fail: No persistent ID or link' — since durable links plainly exist, including a RePORTER record keyed to application ID 10472824. It is a weak pass: there is no DOI, ARK, Handle, RRID or accession, and the identifier that occupies the id slot is the organization homepage. Correctness check on identifier function rather than syntax: id and page are byte-identical, so the record's dataset identifier does not distinguish the dataset from the project that produced it and will not resolve to a versioned landing page. doi_format is recorded as not_present rather than invalid, and persistent_identifier as not_present. This is the single change with the widest downstream effect in this record, since the same absence depresses Q13 (no persistent ID for sustainability) and constrains Q14 (no dataset DOI to anchor a formal citation).

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health, Common Fund Bridge2AI program' with grants[0].grant_number 'OT2OD032701' and notes recording project number 1OT2OD032701-01, application ID 10472824, fiscal year 2022, award amount 5880300, project start 2022-09-01 and end 2026-11-30. creators: Eric Rosenthal (Massachusetts General Hospital, with principal_investigator block and an id), Azra Bihorac (University of Florida), Xiaoqian Jiang (UTHealth Houston), Yulia Strekalova (University of Florida), Parisa Rashidi (University of Florida), Manlik Kwong (Tufts University), plus a CHoRUS Consortium entity entry describing 60+ members across 20 institutions. data_governance.accountable_organization: Massachusetts General Hospital. Both halves of the 5-band are met and exceeded: a named funder with a grant number, award amount, and full project period, and six named creators each with an institutional affiliation plus an explicitly designated principal investigator. Provenance for each attribution is stated (leadership-team slide, RePORTER record). Grant format validation passes as valid_nih: OT2 is the correct Other Transactions activity code for Common Fund Bridge2AI data generation awards, OD is the Office of the Director, and the 1OT2OD032701-01 expansion is a well-formed type-1 year-01 project number consistent with the fiscal-year-2022 start. Funding-to-purpose alignment also holds — purposes recite Bridge2AI programme goals (AI-ready data, ethically sourced datasets, coordination with the other data generation projects), which is what this award funds. Minor gaps not sufficient to reduce the band: no ORCIDs, and only one creator carries an id.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: Present: ethical_reviews.review_details ('Ethics is one of three project pillars (Ethical and Trustworthy AI)... community-facing ethics focus groups... establishes a legal framework for collecting data at scale'); human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects true with special_populations noting PICU/NICU minors and neonates; is_deidentified.method (tokenization, transformation limiting re-identification, imaging de-identification) with deidentification_details citing privacy_scan_tool and CTP-deid; participant_privacy.anonymization_method and .reidentification_risk; at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included true; confidential_elements and sensitive_elements both populated. Absent: informed_consent, participant_compensation, data_protection_impacts, regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant, regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance, regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact. ethical_reviews.source_caveats states the sources 'do not name an IRB or ethics committee of record for the dataset and do not report an approval number or determination'. Roughly six of twelve ethics elements carry content, and the breadth is real — de-identification, privacy method, residual-risk discussion, vulnerable-population identification, confidentiality classification and an ethics programme are all addressed. But the 3-band is defined as IRB plus de-identification, and the IRB half is missing outright: there is an ethics programme without an approval of record. Informed consent and any waiver are absent, and no compliance determination is recorded. Held at 3 rather than 4: breadth compensates for the missing IRB only up to the basic band, and the two strongest protections a reader would check for are the two that are not there. Three cross-field consistency rules fail here. (1) involves_human_subjects=true should imply populated ethical_reviews with an approval — ethical_reviews is populated but with programme description, not approval. (2) involves_human_subjects=true should imply a described informed_consent — absent entirely, with no waiver named either. (3) at-risk minors and neonates are identified with no assent, guardian permission or subpart D determination. One rule passes: is_deidentified is present and both a method and participant_privacy protections are documented. Content-accuracy check on de-identification appropriateness returns indeterminate rather than pass — tokenization is a defensible choice for note text and CTP-deid is the conventional DICOM tool, but with no standard named, no identifier set enumerated, and no residual-risk assessment, the method's sufficiency for high-dimensional waveform and imaging data cannot be judged. Ethics-claim restrictiveness does align with access posture: controlled access on every modality and confidentiality_level 'restricted' are consistent with sensitive clinical content, so the record does not overclaim openness. The record's own source_caveats disclose each gap accurately, which is why these are scored as genuine source absences rather than extraction errors.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Access to the dataset is controlled and conditioned on a signed licensing agreement... a ".edu" email address is required for dataset access. The chorus-ai GitHub organization states that its project code is licensed under the MIT License.' regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: 'restricted'; regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions: 'Every data type in the project's data inventory is listed with controlled access control' and 'Clinical notes may not leave the contributing site; only tokens are shared.' data_governance.accountable_organization: Massachusetts General Hospital; data_governance.access_review_process describes registration form, signed licensing agreement, .edu requirement and provisioning email, plus access-request contacts dbold@emory.edu and jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org; data_governance.stewardship_roles lists three roles. Absent: ip_restrictions, data_protection_impacts, hipaa_compliant, other_compliance, governance_committee_contact. Two of the three components of the 5-band are fully met — restrictions are enumerated per modality and a confidentiality classification is asserted — and the governance surrounding them is better than typical, with an accountable organization, a described review route, named contacts and three stewardship roles. The third component fails: no license governs the dataset. Scored 4 rather than 5 for the missing data license and absent compliance determinations, and not 3 because the governance documentation substantially exceeds 'license only'. Content-accuracy check catches a scope error that the record itself catches first: the MIT License is stated of the GitHub code, and source_caveats correctly warns that 'the MIT License statement is made about the GitHub software project, not about the data'. Crediting MIT to the dataset would have been a significant misread; the record avoids it. Restrictiveness alignment passes — controlled access, .edu gating, a signed agreement, 'restricted' classification and the notes-stay-local rule form a coherent and mutually reinforcing posture with no contradiction. The residual weakness is that the described terms are the AIM-AHEAD training-program route, which the record flags, so the governing instrument for a general research user is unnamed.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: distribution_formats: OMOP Common Data Model, OHNLP, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+ and Persyst. conforms_to_standard enum: OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER. conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; conforms_to_class: 'Dataset'. conforms_to narrative maps each modality to its standard, noting nursing flowsheets use 'the OMOP schema with extensions' and waveform metadata 'the PhysioNet schema extended'. Each of the 5 file_collections carries its own conforms_to and conforms_to_standard. Integration: preprocessing_strategies describes 'validated semantic mappings that connect clinical data in various source formats to international standards' with 'pooled tabular mappings and their documentation maintained in the chorus-mapping repository'; instances carry ontology CURIEs (B2AI_TOPIC:9, B2AI_TOPIC:15, B2AI_TOPIC:32, B2AI_TOPIC:37, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:43, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:49). Absent: related_datasets, file_collections.compression. All three components of the 5-band are satisfied with substance. Formats are the recognized standard for each modality rather than bespoke exports; schema conformance is declared at both document level (w3id LinkML schema, class Dataset) and per collection; and integration capability is the strongest element in the record — harmonizing 14 hospitals onto OMOP CDM via validated, version-controlled semantic mappings is precisely the cross-site harmonization this question asks about, and the mapping artifacts are publicly inspectable. Awarded 5 despite the related_datasets gap, which is logged as a low-severity issue: the band's three stated requirements are each met at a high level, and downgrading for an unpopulated linkage field would understate genuinely excellent standardization. Standards-to-modality matching validates as correct in all five cases, with no mismatched pairing (a common error would be claiming DICOM for waveforms or WFDB for EEG; neither occurs, and EEG is correctly given EDF+/Persyst rather than folded into WFDB). The record is also honest about the limits of standardization, marking nursing-flowsheet and waveform metadata as extended rather than pure, and listing published metadata for the notes and imaging modalities as planned — an overclaim of full schema conformance would have been easy here and is avoided. The unmet element is cross-platform linkage: related_datasets is empty though CHoRUS is described as one of four Bridge2AI data generation projects, so integration is demonstrated within the dataset but not expressed as typed relationships to sibling datasets.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies (3): OMOP standardization via 'validated semantic mappings' with 'pooled tabular mappings and their documentation maintained in the chorus-mapping repository'; text 'extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit', with data 'transformed using approaches that limit re-identification'; waveforms 'converted for release using the conversion scripts and documentation maintained in the chorus_waveform repository, with supporting materials in chorus_waveform_resources'. cleaning_strategies (2): 'Characterization reports are produced and returned to contributing sites following their data submissions, using the CHoRUSReports repository'; validated mappings under 'a clinical validation standard operating procedure' with SOP internal review. labeling_strategies (1): a visualization and annotation environment 'will label data with targets important for prediction', with source_caveats that this is future tense and 'do not report labels present in the current release'. Further tooling: privacy_scan_tool, CTP-deid, chorus-extract-upload, chorus-container-apps, OHDSI tool stack, Jupyter Notebooks, Azure dockerized containers. Absent: machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, imputation_protocols, missing_data_documentation. All three core strategy families are documented with named, publicly locatable software and repository URLs, which is well past the 3-band. Held at 4 rather than 5 on two counts: no version, tag or commit is pinned for any tool, so the pipeline is locatable but not reconstructible; and four of the seven fields — annotation tooling and analyses, imputation protocols, and missing-data documentation — are empty, with labeling itself explicitly not yet applied to the release. Tool-to-task pairing validates as correct throughout: OHNLP is the appropriate toolkit for clinical NLP tokenization, CTP is the standard DICOM de-identification pipeline, OHDSI tooling is the natural companion to OMOP CDM, and WFDB conversion for bedside telemetry is conventional. No tool is credited with a capability it does not have. The record also resists a common inflation: labeling is reported in the future tense with an explicit caveat rather than being presented as delivered annotation. Missing-data handling is partially recoverable from another element — instances[].missing_information documents absent imaging and full note text with why_missing — but missing_data_documentation proper is unset and no imputation is described, so a modeler cannot tell whether missingness is structural or incidental.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: was_directly_observed true ('Retrospective acquisition of clinical data recorded in the course of care... medication administration time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration, PACS imaging, bedside monitor telemetry and hospital EEG recordings'); was_inferred_derived true (tokenization and OMOP standardization so 'delivered records are derived from rather than identical to the site source records'); was_validated_verified true (validated semantic mappings, SOP internal validation). collection_mechanisms (5): chorus-extract-upload tooling with 'an interactive workflow diagram with links to validated standard operating procedure documents'; bedside monitors with gateway/middleware; PACS; hospital EEG databases in EDF+/Persyst; OHNLP tokenization. data_collectors: 'Fourteen of the twenty academic centers... contribute as Data Acquisition centers. Data site managers at each contributing site extract and submit a CHoRUS-specific clinical data extract following the step-by-step workflow and standard operating procedures maintained in the Chorus_SOP repository'; plus Standards/Data Acquisition/Tooling sub-teams. raw_data_sources: 5 sources with source_type, raw_data_format and access_details. collection_timeframes: 'built from retrospective data collection. The snapshot described in the cohort-2 informational webinar is stated as of August 2025, covering 14 different hospitals', with source_caveats that the sources 'do not state the calendar range of the clinical encounters included in the dataset'. direct_collection.is_direct false. sampling_strategies present but intent-only. Methods, mechanisms, collectors and raw sources are all documented at a level that would let another site replicate the extraction workflow, and the SOP and tooling are publicly available. The 5-band requires methods, collectors and timeframes together; the timeframe element is populated but tells a reader only when the snapshot was reported, not what period of care the data covers — for a retrospective critical-care cohort that is the single most important temporal fact, and its absence blocks the top band. Scored 4. A temporal-correctness trap is present and correctly avoided: the record explicitly warns that 'the 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 dates on the NIH RePORTER record are the award period, not the encounter period', refusing a substitution that would have silently misrepresented the data period. direct_collection.is_direct=false is semantically consistent with retrospective extraction from clinical systems, and its source_caveats honestly notes the value is an interpretation rather than sourced language. sampling_strategies is correctly demoted to intent — 'Both statements describe intended sampling approaches; the source documents do not report the sampling actually applied to the released 50,000 admissions' — which is the right call and simultaneously flags a representativeness gap that resurfaces at Q15 and Q20.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: Present: updates.update_details ('Data acquisition is ongoing. The current released dataset covers 50,000 patient admissions, while the anticipated final dataset is 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals. Imaging de-identification for a larger cohort and EEG extraction were in process as of August 2025'); maintainers (2 entries — Ciera McCrary, Program Manager, MGH, with contact; and the chorus-ai GitHub organization directing access requests to named addresses); status 'partially released'; data_governance.accountable_organization Massachusetts General Hospital; funders award period through 2026-11-30 with amount 5880300. Absent: version, version_access, errata, doi, publisher. updates.source_caveats: 'The source documents do not state a release cadence or versioning policy for the dataset itself.' The 3-band requires a version number, basic access info and a persistent ID; two of those three are absent outright, so the score sits below 3. It is above 0 because this is clearly not 'single version only, no sustainability plan': named maintainers with contacts, an accountable institution, an active update trajectory with concrete milestones, and funding committed through November 2026 are all documented. Scored 2. The sustainability checklist returns four partial results and no complete one. (1) Persistent identifier: absent — no DOI, ARK or Handle, and id duplicates the homepage. (2) Long-term governance: partial — data_governance names an accountable organization, an access review process and three stewardship roles, but no post-award custody plan. (3) Domain-appropriate repository: partial — the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud enclave on Azure is a named access platform rather than an archival repository with a preservation commitment, and the enclave's fate after the award period is unaddressed. (4) Institutional commitment: partial — MGH accountability and a dated, funded award period are recorded, but no preservation funding beyond it. The consistency failure that most affects usability is the combination of status 'partially released' with an actively changing corpus and no version identifier: a user cannot name which snapshot they analyzed, and the record's own 50,000-versus-45K discrepancy is a direct symptom of unversioned snapshots being described side by side.

name: Associated Publications
text: external_resources holds four distinct reference groups: (1) 'https://github.com/chorus-ai' — the code organization with 28 named repositories; (2) 'https://chorus4ai.org/' — the project website, plus 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus'; (3) 'https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824' — the NIH RePORTER record for the supporting award; (4) 'https://www.aim-ahead.net/media/jnzdnid3/bridge2ai-for-clinical-care-informational-webinar-cohort-2.pdf' — the AIM-AHEAD cohort-2 informational webinar describing the dataset snapshot and trainee access route. The citation field is absent and no doi is present anywhere in the record. Well past the 3-band: at least four distinct references, counting repeated links to the project website once. The 5-band additionally requires a formal citation for this dataset — one identifying it by title together with its authors or publishing organization — and no such citation exists, nor is there a dataset DOI that could anchor one. Per the rubric's explicit instruction, multiple non-publication external resources without a formal dataset citation earn 3, not 5. Scored 3. Reference quality is better than the bare count suggests: the RePORTER link is a durable third-party record that independently corroborates the funding claims, and the webinar PDF is the traceable provenance for the August 2025 snapshot figures used throughout the record. What is absent is any peer-reviewed publication — no methods paper, cohort description, or preprint is cited, which is notable for a consortium of this scale and suggests the source bundle predates or omits them. The missing formal citation is downstream of the missing DOI recorded at Q6: with no persistent identifier, the record has nothing to build a citation string around, so a single remediation (mint a DOI) would unblock both items.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: 6 types, including 'Hospital admission of a critically ill patient' counts 50000 with the note that this covers ICU, PICU and NICU and that the anticipated final dataset is 100,000. subpopulations: three entries — ICU, PICU and NICU admissions — each with subpopulation_elements_present true and each carrying the identical source_caveat that 'The released figure of 50,000 patient admissions is reported for ICU, PICU and NICU combined; no per-setting breakdown is given.' at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included true, notes that PICU and NICU admissions 'are part of the current released dataset', with source_caveats that the sources 'do not characterize the cohort as including at-risk or vulnerable populations and describe no assent procedures, guardian consent, or special protections'. splits: a planned holdout partition with no size. human_subject_research.special_populations records minors and neonates. Absent: any age, sex, race, ethnicity or geographic distribution; any inclusion or exclusion criteria; missing_data_documentation; subsets.is_data_split. Solidly at the 3-band and no higher. Human subject involvement is unambiguous and the population is characterized by care setting with three named strata and an at-risk flag, which is more than 'general human data'. But the 5-band needs detailed demographics and inclusion/exclusion criteria, and the record has neither: not one demographic attribute is reported, the three subpopulations carry no counts, and no eligibility rule is stated for which admissions at a contributing site entered the extract. The subpopulation entries are semantically thin in a specific way — they identify strata without quantifying them, so 'subpopulation_elements_present: true' asserts structure that the content does not fill; each entry's own caveat concedes this. The at_risk_populations value is flagged by the record as an inference drawn from reported PICU/NICU admissions rather than a source characterization, which is the correct epistemic marking but also means the vulnerable-population determination is the evaluator-facing reconstruction, not the project's. The demographic void interacts badly with the project's stated equity framing: purposes and addressing_gaps promise 'the most diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready data set' while known_limitations.representativeness_limitation concedes the achieved 'demographic, geographic or clinical distribution' is unreported. The record is internally honest about this — it does not fabricate diversity — but the claim of diversity remains unevidenced, and the same absence caps Q20.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page: 'https://chorus4ai.org/'. external_resources: 'https://github.com/chorus-ai', 'https://chorus4ai.org/', 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus', 'https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824', 'https://www.aim-ahead.net/media/jnzdnid3/bridge2ai-for-clinical-care-informational-webinar-cohort-2.pdf'. extension_mechanism.contribution_url: 'https://github.com/chorus-ai'. conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'. No download_url; no doi. Passes clearly on link presence: five or more distinct external URLs across documentation, code, funding record and training materials, covering both project-controlled and third-party-controlled locations. URL validity returns some_invalid rather than all_valid: 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' lacks a URI scheme and will not resolve as given, and the maintainer contact 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' carries a probable domain misspelling that the record flags as transcribed exactly from the source. Domains are otherwise plausible and well formed, and reporter.nih.gov and w3id.org are genuinely durable — the w3id.org schema URI is the most persistent identifier anywhere in the record, though it identifies the metadata schema rather than the dataset. The pass is on links; the absence of any dataset-level persistent identifier is penalized at Q6 and Q13 rather than double-counted here.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: distribution_formats documents the working environment per modality: OMOP data 'worked with inside the enclave supporting the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud, where trainees use Jupyter Notebooks and the OHDSI tool stack; CHoRUS services are deployed on Azure through dockerized container applications'; telemetry 'worked with inside the enclave alongside the OMOP data'; notes 'stored locally at contributing sites rather than in the enclave; only tokens are available'. license_and_use_terms requires a signed licensing agreement and a '.edu' email address. data_governance.access_review_process: 'participants complete a registration form giving name, email and institution, and must sign a licensing agreement included in that registration form before gaining access... program administrators assist with this access where needed. Once access is granted and compute is provisioned, an email is sent to the participant', plus access-request contacts dbold@emory.edu and jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org. download_url absent. Three of the four things a prospective user needs are specified: the platform (a named cloud enclave with its analysis stack), the credentialing mechanism (registration, signed agreement, .edu requirement, provisioning notification), and the policy (controlled access on every modality, notes non-exportable). Short of 5 because the one fully specified route is the AIM-AHEAD training-program path, which the record itself flags as program-specific; a general research user is left with two individual email addresses, no application form, no review criteria, no turnaround expectation and no DUA text. Scored 4 rather than 3 because substantially more than a partial mechanism is documented. The access description is internally consistent with the restrictive posture asserted elsewhere — an analysis-in-enclave model with no download endpoint is the semantically correct pattern for controlled-access clinical data, and the absence of download_url is appropriate here rather than an omission. The record does not overclaim: source_caveats states plainly that 'the access terms described are those of the training program registration route'. The FAIR consistency rule that a reusable license implies specified distribution formats holds in the reverse direction too — formats are specified per modality with their access posture — but the rule that a DOI implies an accessible landing page cannot be evaluated, since no DOI exists.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: intended_uses (3): 'Machine learning model development for acute and critical care' with usage_notes on multi-modal model building; 'External validation of AI models' against the planned holdout, with source_caveats that 'The source documents do not report that this holdout set has been released'; 'AI/ML workforce training and education' via the AIM-AHEAD program. license_and_use_terms as at Q9 (controlled access, signed licensing agreement, .edu email; MIT scoped to code). Supporting context: known_limitations (4 typed entries), participant_privacy.notes ('determine the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'), ethical_reviews (community-facing ethics focus groups 'to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing', evaluation of 'community perspectives on clinical care AI'). Absent: prohibited_uses, discouraged_uses, future_use_impacts. The 3-band is met — access terms plus genuine, well-differentiated use guidance across three use categories with usage notes. The 5-band fails on both of its additional requirements: three of the five fields are empty, so no use is anywhere prohibited or discouraged, and there is no social impact analysis with mitigation strategies. For a controlled-access critical-care dataset intended for clinical AI, the absence of prohibited uses is a substantive omission — nothing in the record forbids re-identification attempts, clinical deployment without validation, or redistribution. Intended uses are semantically coherent with the dataset's actual content and with purposes and tasks, and the second one is correctly hedged as depending on an unreleased holdout rather than presented as available. Social-impact material exists but is misplaced and partial: the ethics pillar describes community engagement and a legal framework, and known_limitations types four real constraints including representativeness, but neither is framed as downstream-use risk with mitigations, and future_use_impacts — the field the rubric names for exactly this — is unset. The equity framing in the project name and keywords ('Equitable AI', 'social determinants of health') raises the expectation of a fairness-risk discussion that the record does not deliver, which is the same gap that caps Q15 and Q20.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: was_derived_from: 'Clinical source systems at the 14 CHoRUS data contributing hospitals, comprising electronic health records, PACS imaging archives, bedside monitors with gateway/middleware, and hospital EEG databases.' raw_data_sources: 5 entries each with source_description, source_type, raw_data_format and access_details (e.g. 'Continuous bedside physiologic monitoring at contributing hospitals' / 'Bedside monitors with gateway/middleware' / 'Waveform telemetry, converted to WFDB'). Activities: acquisition_methods (observed / derived / validated), preprocessing_strategies (OMOP semantic mapping via chorus-mapping, OHNLP tokenization, chorus_waveform conversion), cleaning_strategies (CHoRUSReports characterization returned to sites; clinical validation SOP). Agents: data_collectors ('Data site managers at each contributing site extract and submit...'; Standards, Data Acquisition and Tooling sub-teams), created_by 'CHoRUS Consortium'. Quality/missingness: instances[].missing_information with why_missing for imaging ('De-identification was in process for a larger imaging cohort') and notes ('Clinical notes are stored locally at contributing sites; only tokens leave the site'); known_limitations (4 typed). updates populated; splits describes a planned holdout. Absent: version_access, errata, parent_datasets, missing_data_documentation, subsets.is_data_split. The rubric permits provenance as text, and as text this is close to complete: for each of the five modalities a reader can trace source system to acquisition mechanism to transformation tool to released collection, with the responsible agent named and the validation step identified. That is entity–activity–agent lineage with derivation paths. Held at 4 rather than 5 because the lineage is narrative and unidentified — no collection carries a machine-readable derivation link to its inputs or to the activity that produced it — and because the integrity half of the question is weak: version_access, errata and parent_datasets are all absent, so there is no mechanism to learn that a released record changed or was corrected. Scoring here inverts the usual pattern the bands anticipate: version history is nearly absent while lineage is strong, the opposite of the 3-band description. The 4 reflects the rubric's explicit allowance that 'provenance may be represented as text OR as W3C PROV-O graphs'. Quality assurance is genuinely evidenced rather than asserted — characterization reports returned to contributing sites form a feedback loop, and semantic mappings pass through a clinical validation SOP with internal review. Missingness is documented where it exists, at instance level with reasons, though not in the field the rubric names. The provenance narrative also correctly captures a subtle point: acquisition_methods.was_inferred_derived explains that 'delivered records are derived from rather than identical to the site source records', which is exactly the derivation semantics PROV-O would encode.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases: absent. future_use_impacts: absent. Bias-adjacent content appears only elsewhere: known_limitations.representativeness_limitation — 'Data are contributed by 14 hospitals drawn from a network of 20 academic centers; the source documents state that sampling and federated access are intended to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort but do not report the demographic, geographic or clinical distribution achieved in the released dataset'; known_limitations.coverage_limitation (imaging ~1,000 images, EEG extraction in process); participant_privacy.notes ('manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'); sampling_strategies.source_caveats ('the source documents do not report the sampling actually applied to the released 50,000 admissions or the resulting distribution'). Both fields the question scores are empty. What exists is an acknowledgement, inside a limitations element, that the achieved distribution is unknown — that identifies an unexamined risk rather than a bias, names no bias type, and offers no fairness analysis. Scored 2 rather than 3 because the 3-band expects bias identification, however untaxonomized, and this record never states that any specific bias is present; scored above 0 because the representativeness and coverage limitations are typed, specific and directly relevant to how a model trained on this data would fail. The gap is conspicuous against the record's own framing: the project is 'CHoRUS for Equitable AI', keywords include 'social determinants of health' and 'AI-ready dataset', and addressing_gaps claims the aim of 'the most diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready data set'. Equity is thus a stated objective with no bias inventory and no fairness measurement behind it. Several biases are strongly implied by content documented elsewhere and would be straightforward to state: selection bias from 14 academic medical centers (not community or rural hospitals); coverage and missingness bias across modalities, where imaging is available for a small fraction of admissions and EEG extraction is incomplete; measurement bias in high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation; and the ICU/PICU/NICU scope limitation. The record identifies each of these facts in known_limitations and instances without ever naming them as biases, so the raw material for a taxonomized bias section is present and merely unassembled. No AIO or BiasTypeEnum mapping appears anywhere, and no fairness analysis is attempted.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated (9/14): id 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; title 'Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI'; description (~1,700 chars); keywords (14); license_and_use_terms.license_terms 'Controlled access to all data types. Participants must sign a licensing agreement...'; page 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; creators (7, all with affiliations); purposes (5); instances (4, with counts 50000 / 1600000000 / 7642). Absent (5/14): doi; resources; parent_datasets; variables; regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level (the regulatory_restrictions class is absent entirely). 9 of 14 counted fields populated (64%), sitting just below the ≈70% anchor. The populated fields are of high quality rather than nominal — creators carry affiliations, instances carry integer counts, purposes are substantive. The five absences are not incidental: doi and confidentiality_level are the two that a released controlled-access clinical dataset most needs, and variables is absent for a dataset of 1.6 billion OMOP rows, leaving the actual data elements uncharacterized. Counted on meaningful content, not key presence. Partial credit was considered and declined for near-misses: data_governance.committee_contact supplies a governance contact but is not regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level, and conforms_to_schema is not a variables listing. Scored 3 rather than 4 because the missing fields cluster on identification and composition.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description ≈1,700 characters, covering consortium context, 14 contributing hospitals within 20 academic centers, per-modality standards (OMOP/DICOM/WFDB/EDF+/Persyst/OHNLP), released volumes (50,000 admissions, 1.6B OMOP rows, 7,642 imaging admissions, 23 Tb waveform), access posture and the 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 project period. purposes: 5 entries, each a full sentence of 150–300 characters ('To develop the most diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready data set to answer the grand challenge of improving recovery from acute illness'). Far beyond the >200 character threshold, and the length carries information density rather than padding: the description alone supplies volumes, modalities, standards, storage locations and per-modality completion status. Length is matched by specificity — named standards, integer volumes and dated states rather than generic prose. The description also honestly qualifies its own figures ('reported by the project website', 'As presented in September 2025'), so length does not come at the cost of overclaiming.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: 14 unique keywords: critical care; intensive care unit; acute illness; electronic health record; OMOP Common Data Model; waveform telemetry; electroencephalography; medical imaging; clinical notes; social determinants of health; AI-ready dataset; Bridge2AI; multimodal data; controlled access. Comfortably above the ≥8 threshold with no duplicates or near-duplicates. The keyword set spans four distinct discovery axes — clinical domain (critical care, acute illness), modality (waveform telemetry, electroencephalography, medical imaging, clinical notes), standard (OMOP CDM), and access/programme context (controlled access, Bridge2AI) — and every term is corroborated by content elsewhere in the record, so none is decorative. 'social determinants of health' is the weakest: it appears in purposes and future_use_impacts as intent but no SDOH variables are documented.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists 5 entries: DICOM ('Imaging drawn from PACS, under controlled access'); WFDB ('Waveform telemetry from bedside monitors, held in the enclave'); 'EDF+ and Persyst' (EEG); 'OMOP Common Data Model' (structured EHR); OHNLP (tokenized notes). Nine subsets each carry conforms_to and conforms_to_standard. raw_data_sources independently records raw_data_format per source. Four genuine file/media formats (DICOM, WFDB, EDF+, Persyst) exceed the >3 threshold on their own, before counting the two standards entries. Format variety is corroborated as real multimodality by the description and by nine modality subsets, not asserted by a bare list. Two of the five entries (OMOP, OHNLP) are data standards rather than delivery formats — the record flags this itself in per-entry source_caveats, which is honest but leaves the 1.6-billion-row structured component with no stated delivery format or packaging (logged as a semantic_understanding issue). The band is met by the four true formats regardless. total_file_count and file_collections are absent, so file enumeration proper is undocumented; this does not affect the type-variety band but is noted.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: instances[0].counts: 50000 (patient admissions, ICU/PICU/NICU); instances[1].counts: 1600000000 (rows of OMOP EHR data); instances[2].counts: 7642 (admissions with radiology data); instances[3].description: '23 Tb of waveform data in the current released dataset'. subsets (9) and subpopulations (3) present with is_data_split / is_subpopulation flags. Passes on multiple independent grounds: three integer instance counts plus an aggregate storage volume for the waveform component. instances[1] transparently explains its own derivation ('The project website states the figure as "1.6 Billion"; the integer recorded here is that approximate magnitude expanded to units') — the count is an order-of-magnitude expansion, correctly disclosed rather than presented as exact. total_size_bytes is absent, so the 23 Tb figure is prose rather than a machine-readable size, and no per-modality byte counts exist. Sufficient for pass; the disclosed 50,000-vs-45K discrepancy is recorded as a separate content_accuracy issue.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: id: 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; page: 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; external_resources include 'https://github.com/chorus-ai' and the Bridge2AI project page. doi: absent. publisher: absent. No RRID. Passes against the stated fail condition ('No persistent ID or link') because an identifying, resolvable landing page is present. This is the weakest possible pass: the identifier is a project homepage, not a persistent identifier, and the same URL serves as id and page so there is no independent resolution path. Semantically this is a marginal pass and the margin matters. No DOI, ARK or Handle exists; no publisher or hosting repository is named; and the record's own source_caveats reports the homepage carries a banner stating it 'is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives' — the sole identifier is documented as unstable. For a dataset declared released and shared, this is the record's most consequential FAIR gap and it is logged as a high-severity consistency issue. Pass/fail granularity cannot express the deficit, so it is reflected in Q13 (no persistent ID for sustainability) rather than manufactured here.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders[0].grantor: 'National Institutes of Health, Common Fund Bridge2AI program'; grants[0].grant_number: 'OT2OD032701' with description 'project number 1OT2OD032701-01, application ID 10472824, fiscal year 2022 award amount 5,880,300 USD, awarded to Massachusetts General Hospital for the project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30'. creators: 7 entries, each with affiliations — Eric S. Rosenthal (Massachusetts General Hospital, named principal_investigator with structured PI block), Azra Bihorac (University of Florida), Xiaoqian Jiang (UTHealth Houston), Yulia Strekalova (University of Florida), Parisa Rashidi (University of Florida), Manlik Kwong (Tufts University), and CHoRUS Consortium ('more than 60 consortium members across 20 different institutions'). Both band-5 conditions are met in full and exceeded: the grant carries not only an award number but the application ID, award amount, awardee institution and project period, and every creator carries an institutional affiliation with the PI identified as such. Grant number validated against NIH format: OT2 (other-transaction activity code, the correct instrument for Common Fund Bridge2AI awards) + OD (Office of the Director, the correct administering institute for Common Fund) + serial 032701; the '1...-01' project-number form is also well-formed. The awardee institution (MGH) matches both the PI's affiliation and data_governance.accountable_organization, so funding, leadership and accountability are mutually consistent. The stated project period matches the temporal claims in the description and collection_timeframes.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: Present: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=true with special_populations 'Includes pediatric (PICU) and neonatal (NICU) intensive care admissions as well as adult critically ill patients'; is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present=true with method 'Extraction and tokenization of unstructured EHR text with the OHNLP toolkit; de-identification of imaging, in process for the larger cohort as of September 2025' and deidentification_details noting de-identification is 'combined with controlled access rather than relied on alone'; participant_privacy with anonymization_method, privacy_techniques ('A privacy scan tool for medical records is maintained by the project') and reidentification_risk; at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included=true with special_protections; ethical_reviews describing community ethics focus groups; data_governance.committee_contact (Jared Houghtaling, jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org). Absent: informed_consent; participant_compensation; data_protection_impacts; regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant; regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance. Breadth is real — six protection areas are populated with substantive, modality-aware content — but the two declarations most load-bearing for a US clinical PHI dataset are missing. ethical_reviews is populated yet names no IRB (its own source_caveats concedes this), so the band-3 anchor 'IRB + deidentification' is met only on the deidentification half; informed_consent is absent entirely despite pediatric and neonatal subjects; and no DPIA or HIPAA status exists. The privacy content that is present is good enough to hold the score at 3 rather than below it. Two cross-field checks fail (human_subjects=true → informed_consent expected; human_subjects=true → IRB-bearing ethical_reviews expected) and both are logged high-severity. reidentification_risk is present as a field but semantically thin: it restates intent ('describes transforming data using approaches that limit re-identification') rather than assessing residual risk, so it does not supply the band-5 element. Deidentification method appropriateness is otherwise sound for the data type — site-local note text with only tokens released, imaging de-identification before transfer, and an enclave — and the governance contact is credited although it sits under data_governance rather than regulatory_restrictions. Scoring was not reduced for the record's honest disclosure that no IRB is named in its sources; the absence itself, not its disclosure, is what caps the score.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Controlled access to all data types.
