Participants must sign a licensing agreement, included in the registration form, before gaining access to the dataset; under the training program route a ".edu" email address is required'. ip_restrictions.restrictions: 'The chorus-ai GitHub organization's software is released under the MIT License, with individual repositories also listing Apache-2.0; dataset access is separately governed by a licensing agreement'. data_governance.accountable_organization: Massachusetts General Hospital; committee_contact: Jared Houghtaling with email; access_review_process naming two request addresses (dbold@emory.edu, jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org) and the registration/provisioning flow. confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present=true: 'Every data type is listed with controlled access.' Absent: regulatory_restrictions in full (confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant, other_compliance), data_protection_impacts. Substantially beyond 'license only': the record supplies license terms, IP restrictions, an accountable organization, a named governance contact, a described access-review process and per-data-type confidentiality assertions. It falls short of 5 because there is no formal confidentiality classification and no regulatory compliance statement — the structured governance metadata that would let the controlled-access posture be machine-read. The strongest single element is correct scoping of the MIT license to software rather than to the clinical dataset, with the reasoning recorded in source_caveats — a conflation that would have been a material correctness error is explicitly avoided. Governance asymmetry is also disclosed: two co-equal access addresses exist, one carried in the single-valued committee_contact and the other in access_review_process, with the modelling compromise stated. Against this, an absent regulatory_restrictions class on a HIPAA-governed PHI dataset is a genuine consistency gap (logged medium), since restrictiveness asserted in prose is never classified.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to: narrative mapping each modality to its standard ('OMOP Common Data Model for structured EHR data...; DICOM for imaging; WFDB for waveform telemetry; EDF+ and Persyst for waveform EEG; OHNLP for extracted and tokenized clinical notes'). conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]. conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; conforms_to_class: Dataset. Each of the 9 subsets carries its own conforms_to and conforms_to_standard. Instances carry ontology-coded data_topic/data_substrate terms (B2AI_TOPIC:4, B2AI_TOPIC:9, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:49, B2AI_TOPIC:15, B2AI_TOPIC:37). preprocessing_strategies cites 'validated semantic mappings for connecting clinical data in various source formats to international standards' with 'pooled tabular mappings and an associated clinical validation SOP... in the chorus-mapping repository'. external_resources: 3, including the chorus-ai GitHub organization (28 repositories). Absent: related_datasets; file_collections.compression. Standardization is genuinely excellent — every modality is bound to an internationally used standard, schema conformance is declared by URI, subsets are individually typed, and instances carry ontology term identifiers. Integration capability is real but incomplete: semantic mappings with a clinical validation SOP are documented, and OMOP is itself a harmonization target, but no typed related_datasets exist and, decisively, the join key across modalities is never stated. Standard usage is technically correct throughout, including the appropriate fallback to OTHER for EDF+/Persyst and OHNLP, which have no enum value — a small but telling sign the enum was applied rather than guessed. Held to 4 rather than 5 for one substantive reason: for a multimodal AI-ready dataset, integration turns on the identifier linking an admission's OMOP rows, waveforms, images and note tokens, and that identifier appears nowhere (logged as a completeness issue). The absence of related_datasets also means no typed linkage to the sibling Bridge2AI datasets the description situates this one among. The OMOP/OHNLP-as-format conflation noted in Q4 slightly weakens computability as well, since no delivery encoding is stated for the structured component.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies (5): OMOP standardization with 'validated semantic mappings... pooled tabular mappings and an associated clinical validation SOP... in the chorus-mapping repository'; OHNLP tokenization 'so that only tokens leave the contributing site'; 'transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification' with imaging de-identification in process; waveform conversion 'using the documentation and conversion scripts maintained in the chorus_waveform repository'; 'Geocoding of OMOP Location entities via DeGauss, using open source code maintained in the UF-Geocoding repository'. cleaning_strategies (2): 'Characterization reports are produced and returned to contributing sites following their data submissions'; SOPs that 'undergo an internal validation and review process before publication'. Named tools: OHNLP toolkit, DeGauss, chorus_waveform scripts, chorus-extract-upload, privacy_scan_tool, CTP-deid. Absent: labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, imputation_protocols, missing_data_documentation. Well past band 3 ('at least one strategy or tool listed'): seven strategies across preprocessing and cleaning, each tied to a named tool or a named repository, and the cleaning loop (characterization reports returned to sites for correction) is a real quality-control mechanism rather than a generic assertion. Short of 5 on two counts — no software version numbers anywhere, and five of the seven listed field areas are empty, including all annotation and missing-data documentation. Tool-to-task matching is correct and non-generic: OHNLP is a recognized clinical NLP toolkit appropriate for note tokenization, DeGauss is a recognized de-identifying geocoder appropriate for OMOP Location entities, and CTP-deid corresponds to DICOM de-identification — each tool suits the modality it is applied to. Versions are the specific band-5 element missing; notably the maintainers entry mentions 'a package status page lists versions... about CHoRUS packages' without recording any version, so version information is acknowledged to exist but is not captured. Repository names are given but only the organization URL is provided, not per-repository URLs. The absence of labeling and annotation documentation is a substantive gap given purposes explicitly claims a labeling capability.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods (2): retrospective extraction from 'EHR, PACS, bedside monitors and gateway or middleware, and the hospital EEG database' with was_directly_observed=true; derived content via OHNLP tokenization and DeGauss geocoding with was_inferred_derived=true. collection_mechanisms (3): bedside monitors with gateway/middleware converted by chorus_waveform scripts; the OHNLP toolkit; 'site data extracts created and uploaded using the chorus-extract-upload tooling, following standard operating protocols published on the centralized Chorus_SOP documentation site'. data_collectors (2): '14 data contributing hospitals' (role: data acquisition center) and 'Site data managers at contributing sites' who 'follow the interactive Chorus_SOP workflow... and provide regular status updates... through GitHub or a Google Form'. raw_data_sources (5) with source_type, raw_data_format and access_details each. direct_collection.is_direct=false. collection_timeframes (1): 'Retrospective collection of previously recorded clinical data at contributing hospitals; as presented in September 2025, the assembled dataset reflected a state as of August 2025'. Methods and collectors are documented to band-5 depth — acquisition is split into directly-observed and derived with correct provenance flags, mechanisms name the actual tooling and SOP site, collectors are identified by role with their reporting workflow, and five raw sources are individually characterized. The timeframe element of band 5 is the weak limb: an as-of date is given but no clinical date range. One cross-check is notable and passes: direct_collection.is_direct=false is semantically consistent with the retrospective design and with was_directly_observed=true on the acquisition method — 'directly observed' refers to clinical documentation at the point of care, not to collection from participants for this dataset, and the record keeps that distinction straight. Two gaps hold the score at 4: the admission years covered are never stated (logged low-severity), so temporal comparability and practice-drift assessment are impossible; and sampling_strategies concedes in its own source_caveats that the executed sampling frame and inclusion criteria are undocumented, so who entered the 50,000-admission cohort remains unspecified.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: Present: updates.update_details — 'The dataset is growing toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals. As of the September 2025 webinar, imaging de-identification was in process... contributing sites provide regular status updates on their extract progress, tracked on the Standards and Data Acquisition project boards'; maintainers (3) — CHoRUS Consortium ('more than 60 consortium members across 20 different institutions'), Ciera McCrary (Program Manager, MGH, with contact), chorus-ai GitHub organization ('a package status page lists versions, maintainers and other metadata about CHoRUS packages'); data_governance.accountable_organization Massachusetts General Hospital; funders establishing support through 2026-11-30; extension_mechanism with contribution_url. Absent: version; version_access; errata; doi; publisher. Band 3 requires 'version number + basic access info + persistent ID' and two of those three are absent: the dataset carries no version identifier of any kind and no persistent identifier. What is present is genuine maintenance infrastructure — named maintainers, a concrete update trajectory, status tracking on project boards, an accountable institution and a contribution pathway — which is more than band 0's 'no sustainability plan'. Scored 2 to sit between the two anchors. Sustainability was assessed against all four indicators: persistent identifiers — absent; long-term governance plan — partial, since governance is documented but tied to the NIH project period ending 2026-11-30 with no stated post-award custodianship; domain-appropriate repository — absent, as the data reside in a project cloud enclave rather than a durable biomedical repository such as PhysioNet, and no publisher is named; institutional commitment — partial via MGH as accountable organization and awardee. The versioning gap is aggravated by the dataset being explicitly in motion: imaging and EEG are still arriving, so without a version or dated snapshot identifier a user cannot name which state of the dataset they analysed. That the GitHub package status page versions the software while the dataset itself is unversioned sharpens the contrast.

name: Associated Publications
text: external_resources: 3 distinct entries — 'CHoRUS project website' (https://chorus4ai.org/), 'chorus-ai GitHub organization' (https://github.com/chorus-ai, 28 repositories), 'CHoRUS page on the Bridge2AI website' (www.bridge2ai.org/chorus). existing_uses.examples: 'The datasets are being used for training activities and publications' — no publication is identified. citation: absent. doi: absent. Three distinct non-publication references are documented, satisfying the band-3 condition. The band-5 condition is not met: there is no formal dataset citation (no title-plus-authors/publishing-organization citation string) and no DOI to serve even as a bare reference. Per the Q14 rule, three external resources without a formal citation earn exactly 3. Scored on the {0, 3, 5} scale as required. The three resources are genuinely distinct targets rather than repeated links to one destination, so all count toward the ≥2 references limb — but that limb alone cannot reach 5 without the citation. The gap is conspicuous in context: existing_uses asserts that publications using the data exist, yet none is cited, so the record acknowledges a literature it does not reference. With no DOI either, a reuser has no supported way to cite this dataset, which is the specific failure Q14 exists to detect.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: 50,000 patient admissions (ICU/PICU/NICU), 7,642 admissions with radiology data. subpopulations (3): 'Adult intensive care unit (ICU) admissions, identified by the care setting of the admission'; the same formulation for PICU and NICU. at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included=true, notes 'Pediatric and neonatal intensive care admissions are within scope, and the population consists of acutely and critically ill patients'. human_subject_research.notes: 'a target of more than 100,000 critically ill patients across the project'. subsets: all 9 have is_subpopulation=false (they are modality partitions). Absent: any age, sex, race, ethnicity or geographic distribution; per-subpopulation counts; inclusion/exclusion criteria; missing_data_documentation. Human subjects are clearly identified with an aggregate count, three named care-setting strata and at-risk population flags — comfortably band 3. It does not advance materially beyond it: the three 'subpopulations' are identified solely 'by the care setting of the admission', which restates the description without adding characterization, and carry no counts. Both band-5 elements — detailed demographics and inclusion/exclusion criteria — are entirely absent, as is missing_data_documentation. The absence of demographics is not a neutral omission here; it is in tension with the record's own claims. The title is 'for Equitable AI', purposes promises 'the most diverse... data set', and keywords include 'social determinants of health' — yet no demographic composition is reported for the released 50,000 admissions, so the diversity claim is unverifiable from the datasheet and no fairness analysis is possible (this also caps Q20). sampling_strategies concedes that inclusion criteria and any verification of representativeness are undocumented, confirming the gap rather than offsetting it. Scored 3 rather than 4 because the subgroup description present is a re-labelling of the care settings already given, not population characterization.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page: 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; id: 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; external_resources: 'https://chorus4ai.org/', 'https://github.com/chorus-ai', 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus'; extension_mechanism.contribution_url: 'https://github.com/chorus-ai'; conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'. doi: absent. Passes: multiple well-formed external URLs are present, including a documentation site and a substantial code organization, plus a w3id.org schema URI which is itself a persistent-identifier service. Passes on links while failing on persistence. No DOI, ARK or Handle identifies the dataset; id and page are the same project homepage, which source_caveats reports is under review for potential modification, so the primary locator is documented as unstable. One external resource, 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus', lacks a URI scheme and is not resolvable as written (logged low-severity correctness). The pass/fail form records findability as achieved; the persistence deficit is reflected where the rubric provides graduated room, in Q13.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Controlled access to all data types. Participants must sign a licensing agreement, included in the registration form, before gaining access to the dataset; under the training program route a ".edu" email address is required to gain access... and program administrators will assist with this access if needed.' data_governance.access_review_process: 'Access requests are directed to the contacts published in the chorus-ai GitHub README: dbold@emory.edu or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org. Under the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program, participants complete a registration form giving name, email and institution, and receive an email once access is granted and compute has been provisioned.' distribution_formats: 5 entries, each noting controlled access and, for OMOP/telemetry, that data are 'held in the cloud enclave'. download_url: absent. The access tier is unambiguous — signed licensing agreement plus approval, with data delivered into a provisioned compute enclave rather than downloaded — and the process is described end to end for the training-program route, with named human contacts for the general route. Held below 5 because no download or application URL exists and the general (non-training-program) pathway resolves to two email addresses in a GitHub README rather than a documented application process. The record avoids the error the rubric specifically warns against: it never describes the dataset as 'public' or 'open', and consistently pairs availability with the signed agreement and enclave provisioning, so the access tier cannot be misread. The enclave model is also correctly reflected in the absence of a download_url — for analysis-in-place data, no download URL should exist, and treating its absence purely as a defect would misread the delivery model. What is genuinely missing is an application or portal URL for the standing access route: a prospective user outside AIM-AHEAD Cohort 2 learns whom to email but not what to submit or against what criteria a request is judged.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms present (controlled access, signed licensing agreement). intended_uses (3 categories with examples): 'Clinical AI/ML model development' — 'Building machine-learning and AI-derived models that characterize acute and critical care illness, predict complications, and measure treatment response'; 'External model validation' — 'Validating externally developed models against a sequestered holdout dataset'; 'Education and workforce development' — hands-on AI/ML training, with usage_notes clarifying that as of 9 September 2025 'the Cohort 2 application deadline had not passed and no trainees had been selected; this is an announced program rather than a use in progress'. future_use_impacts (2): catalyzing 'biomedical research and expertise needed to promote patient-focused deployment of AI in acute and critical care'; and pairing future use with 'transformations that limit re-identification, community-facing ethics focus groups on what data is appropriate for public sharing, and analysis of the legal and regulatory landscape to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'. other_tasks and existing_uses also populated. Absent: prohibited_uses; discouraged_uses. License plus richly categorized intended uses plus a genuine social-impact statement that names mitigations rather than only benefits — clearly above band 3. Capped at 4 because use guidance is one-sided: for a controlled-access PHI dataset, neither prohibited nor discouraged uses are stated anywhere, so the constraints a signatory presumably accepts are invisible in the datasheet. The second future_use_impacts entry is what distinguishes this from boilerplate: it explicitly ties anticipated benefit to identified risk (critically ill patients' data) and names three mitigation mechanisms, which is the CROISSANT RAI-style analysis band 5 asks for. The usage_notes on the training cohort is a further mark of accuracy — an announced programme is labelled as announced rather than counted as a use in progress. The missing prohibitions are the substantive gap and are logged: no anti-re-identification clause, no redistribution restriction, and no caution against clinical deployment of models trained on a cohort whose representativeness is undocumented.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: was_derived_from: 'Routine clinical documentation and device data from the electronic health record, PACS imaging archives, bedside monitor gateway/middleware, and hospital EEG databases of 14 contributing hospitals.' raw_data_sources (5) each with source_description, source_type, raw_data_format and access_details. acquisition_methods with was_directly_observed / was_inferred_derived flags. preprocessing_strategies (5) tracing each modality's transformation: source EHR → OMOP via validated semantic mappings; notes → OHNLP tokens; monitor capture → WFDB via chorus_waveform scripts; OMOP Location → geocoded via DeGauss; imaging → de-identification. cleaning_strategies describing characterization reports returned to sites. subsets.is_data_split=false across all 9 subsets; splits describing a planned sequestered holdout. Absent: version_access; errata; parent_datasets; missing_data_documentation. The rubric permits provenance as text, and the textual lineage here is substantially complete: entities (five raw sources per modality), activities (extraction, standardization, tokenization, waveform conversion, geocoding, de-identification), and agents (14 contributing hospitals, site data managers, and named tools/repositories) are all identifiable and connected modality by modality. Held at 4 rather than 5 because the version/integrity limb is largely empty and the derivation paths are narrative rather than systematically linked. This record inverts the usual pattern the bands assume: it is weak on version history (no version_access, no errata) yet strong on lineage, so band 3's description does not fit it well. Assessed on substance, the entity-activity-agent triad is genuinely present and each modality's path from source system to released form can be traced by a reader. What blocks 5 is that the lineage cannot be traced mechanically — no released artifact is linked to the specific activity that produced it, no parent_datasets exist, and there is no identifier on which a provenance graph could be reconstructed. missing_data_documentation is absent despite obvious incompleteness in the data (imaging de-identification and EEG extraction both in process), which is a quality-documentation gap on top of the provenance one.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases (1): bias_type 'selection_bias'; bias_description 'The cohort is assembled from 14 data contributing hospitals within a collaboration of 20 academic centers, so patient case mix reflects the populations served by those centers'; mitigation_strategy 'Federated access is intended to enable sampling methods that ensure a balanced and diverse cohort; the project additionally samples to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies, and patient-focused efforts determine ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'; source_caveats 'it does not report a measured bias assessment for the released data'. future_use_impacts references managing 'privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'. known_limitations (5) with limitation_type enum values supply coverage and scope context. A BiasTypeEnum value is correctly applied with a substantive, specific description and a mitigation strategy — more than band 3's 'basic bias identification without taxonomy'. But coverage is a single category, and band 5's other limb, fairness analysis, is explicitly absent by the record's own admission. Scored 3 on the balance of one correctly-taxonomized entry against substantial uncovered ground. The selection-bias entry is accurate and appropriately scoped to academic medical centers. Several bias types plainly applicable to this dataset are undocumented: measurement bias across heterogeneous EHR vendors, monitor manufacturers and EEG systems at 14 sites; informative-censoring and missing-data bias, unaddressed and compounded by missing_data_documentation being absent; and imaging-cohort bias, given that de-identified imaging covers only a fraction of admissions. No AIO mappings are present. The mitigation strategy is stated as intent ('is intended to enable') rather than executed practice, and the record's own source_caveats concedes no measured assessment exists — consistent with Q15, since without demographics no fairness analysis of the released cohort is possible. The honest caveat is credited as transparency but does not substitute for the analysis.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated (10 of 14): id 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; title 'Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI'; description (~1,900 chars); keywords (12); license_and_use_terms.license_terms 'Access to the dataset is controlled...'; page 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; creators (6, each with affiliations); purposes (5 responses); instances (11 entries, 3 with counts); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted'. Absent (4): doi; resources (nested sub-resources — external_resources is a distinct field per the rubric field reference); parent_datasets; variables. 10/14 = 71.4%, squarely on the 3 band. The populated fields are not merely present but substantive — instances carries eleven typed entries with B2AI substrate and topic codes, creators carry institutional affiliations. The four absences are not cosmetic: no doi removes the persistent identifier the rest of the FAIR questions depend on, and no variables means the 1.6 billion OMOP rows are described at modality granularity with no variable-level metadata, which is the level an AI/ML consumer needs. Correctness: id and page hold the identical string, so id does not function as an independent identifier — the nominal 10/14 overstates distinct identifying content. Consistency: parent_datasets and related_datasets are both absent, which the top-level source_caveats explains ('names no sibling dataset, so no dataset relationships are recorded') — a defensible extraction decision that nonetheless leaves the count at 3.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description ≈1,900 characters, covering programme context, access model, released volumes (50,000 admissions, 1.6 billion OMOP rows, 7,642 imaging admissions, 23 Tb waveform), the competing 45K figure, the anticipated 100,000-admission target, and an enumeration of all nine modalities. purposes holds five responses of ~150–250 characters each, e.g. 'To provision a holdout test set accessible for external validation of models, aiding marketplace adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical care.' Average narrative length well above the 200-character threshold. Comfortably exceeds the top band, and length here is carrying information rather than padding: the description alone supplies the modality inventory, the volume figures, the access model and the source disagreement. Semantic density is high — the description is specific (named modalities, named counts, named standards) rather than generic programme boilerplate. One semantic caution: the description asserts a 'currently released dataset' while status says 'Partially released', and three of nine modalities were incomplete at the snapshot; the description does surface the webinar's contrary figure, so the tension is disclosed rather than hidden.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: 12 unique keywords: critical care; acute illness; intensive care unit; electronic health records; OMOP Common Data Model; waveform telemetry; electroencephalography; medical imaging; social determinants of health; artificial intelligence; machine learning; Bridge2AI. Twelve distinct terms, none duplicated, spanning clinical domain, data modality, standard, and programme — good discoverability coverage across the axes a searcher would use. Keywords are semantically accurate against the content: every modality keyword (waveform telemetry, electroencephalography, medical imaging, electronic health records) has a corresponding instances entry and distribution_formats entry, and 'OMOP Common Data Model' matches conforms_to_standard. 'social determinants of health' is corroborated by sensitive_elements and other_tasks. Programme context is inferable from the quoted keyword 'Bridge2AI' and from funders.grantor, as required, without recourse to the filename. Minor gap: no keyword names the pediatric/neonatal scope that subpopulations and human_subject_research.special_populations document.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists five entries with per-format notes: 'OMOP Common Data Model relational tables' (with OMOP schema extensions for nursing flowsheets); 'OHNLP open-source schema (tokenized clinical notes)'; 'DICOM'; 'WFDB' (extended PhysioNet schema); 'EDF+ and Persyst'. file_collections and total_file_count are absent. Five distinct formats, well above the >3 threshold, and each is annotated with which modality it carries and what its metadata-publication status was. Format variety is genuinely corroborated as multi-modal by description ('nine data modalities'), keywords and the eleven instances entries, rather than being an unsupported list. Correctness: each format is the appropriate standard for its substrate (DICOM for PACS, WFDB for physiologic waveforms, EDF+/Persyst for EEG, OMOP for structured EHR), so the variety is technically coherent rather than nominal. Consistency issue carried to the issues list: these are in-enclave working formats, since regulatory_restrictions states data are not distributed as files and no download_url exists. Absence of total_file_count and file_collections limits enumeration to type variety only, which is what this question scores.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: instances.counts: 50000 (ICU/PICU/NICU patient admissions), 1600000000 (rows of OMOP-standardized EHR data), 7642 (admissions with radiology data). Size figure in instances.notes for waveform telemetry: 'The project website reports 23 Tb of waveform data in the current released dataset.' subpopulations populated (ICU/PICU/NICU); splits populated (holdout intention). total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes absent. Passes on numeric instance counts at three granularities plus one modality-level byte magnitude. Note that sample size only supports an estimate of overall size, and the top-level source_caveats explicitly declines to record a dataset-wide size because 23 Tb covers waveforms only — so no aggregate volume is available. Content accuracy: two of the three counts are qualified in the record itself — 50000 is disputed by a 45K webinar figure, and 1600000000 is the record's own expansion of a rounded '1.6 Billion' claim. Pass/fail is unaffected since meaningful numeric metadata is present, but the precision implied by the serialized integers exceeds source support (raised as separate issues).

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: page: 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; id: 'https://chorus4ai.org/' (identical string). doi: absent. rrid: absent. publisher: absent (created_by 'CHoRUS Consortium' and data_governance.accountable_organization 'Massachusetts General Hospital' are the nearest equivalents). Additional links: extension_mechanism.contribution_url 'https://github.com/chorus-ai'; conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'. Passes on the stated fail condition ('No persistent ID or link') because a resolvable project link exists — but this is the weakest possible pass. There is no DOI, ARK, Handle or RRID, and the id is a duplicate of the landing-page URL rather than an independent identifier. Correctness: DOI format validation is not_present, not invalid — there is nothing to validate. Semantic understanding: id and page holding the same project-homepage string means the record has no dataset-level identifier distinct from the organization's website, so a citation to this dataset cannot distinguish it from the project. This binary pass materially overstates identification quality; the deficiency is carried into Q13 (sustainability) and Q19 (provenance anchoring) where it is scored rather than thresholded.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health, Common Fund Bridge2AI program'; grants[0].grant_number 'OT2OD032701' with notes 'project number for the funded application is 1OT2OD032701-01, NIH application ID 10472824. Award amount 5,880,300 US dollars for fiscal year 2022; project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30. The awardee organization is Massachusetts General Hospital.' Plus the NIH disclaimer in funders.notes. creators: six named leaders each with affiliations — Eric S. Rosenthal (Massachusetts General Hospital), Azra Bihorac (University of Florida), Xiaoqian Jiang (UTHealth Houston), Yulia Strekalova (University of Florida), Parisa Rashidi (University of Florida), Manlik Kwong (Tufts University). Meets the top band on both limbs and exceeds the minimum: grant number, application number, application ID, award amount, project period, awardee organization, funder disclaimer, and six creators each with an institution and a stable id URI. Correctness: OT2OD032701 validates against the NIH pattern — OT2 is a legitimate Other Transactions activity code, OD correctly denotes the Office of the Director which administers the Common Fund, and the 1OT2OD032701-01 expansion is the correct application form of the core number. Consistency: the awardee organization (MGH) matches the PI's affiliation and data_governance.accountable_organization; funders align with purposes, which restate Bridge2AI's stated goals of ethically sourced AI-ready data. Semantic caveat noted and not penalized: source_caveats explains that all six leaders are carried under principal_investigator because it is the only person-valued field the Creator class declares, so the role assignment is a schema artifact, not a claim that all six hold the award — only Rosenthal is independently attested.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: Present: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects true, with regulatory_compliance ('establishes a legal framework for collecting data at scale and analyzes the existing legal and regulatory landscape') and special_populations (PICU and NICU patients). is_deidentified.method ('Data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification; unstructured EHR text is tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit...') with deidentification_details. participant_privacy.anonymization_method and .privacy_techniques ('Local retention of clinical note text at contributing sites, with only tokens shared. Controlled access to all modalities within a cloud enclave.'). at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included true. ethical_reviews (two entries: community-facing ethics focus groups; community-perspective evaluation of clinical care AI). sensitive_elements and confidential_elements both populated. Absent: informed_consent (no field); participant_compensation; data_protection_impacts; participant_privacy.reidentification_risk; regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant; regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance; regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact; and no named IRB or approval number (human_subject_research.source_caveats: 'The bundle does not name an IRB or ethics review board, nor state an approval number, for the dataset.'). Roughly half the twelve ethics fields carry content, and the content present is genuine rather than boilerplate — the tokenization-and-local-retention architecture is a real, specific privacy control. But the 3 band is defined as IRB plus deidentification, and here the IRB limb fails outright: no review board, no approval number, and the ethical_reviews entries describe community engagement rather than regulatory review. Deidentification is documented but unspecified as to standard. For a dataset of 50,000 critical-care admissions including neonates, the simultaneous absence of IRB identification, any consent or waiver documentation, and any HIPAA determination is a serious deficiency that caps this well below the top bands. Scored 3 rather than 2 because deidentification, privacy techniques, at-risk identification, sensitive/confidential element declarations and ethics-activity documentation are all substantively present; scored no higher because the three load-bearing regulatory elements are all missing. Four consistency failures were detected here and are recorded in issues_detected: involves_human_subjects=true without IRB; involves_human_subjects=true without informed_consent or a documented waiver; is_deidentified without reidentification_risk or a named standard; and PHI-derived restricted data without a HIPAA determination. A fifth, medium-severity concern is method appropriateness: geocoding of OMOP Location entities via DeGauss appears under preprocessing_strategies and increases re-identification risk, with no offsetting protection recorded in participant_privacy. A sixth: at_risk_groups_included=true with no assent or guardian-permission procedures. These semantic failures, not mere field absence, are what hold the score at 3 — the record's own source_caveats correctly flag several of them, which is good documentation practice but does not substitute for the missing protections.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Access to the dataset is controlled. Participants in the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program must sign a licensing agreement included in the registration form before gaining access to the dataset.' regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: 'restricted'. regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions: 'All nine documented data types are marked as controlled for access control, and access requires a signed licensing agreement and an institutional (".edu") email address. Data are worked with inside a cloud enclave rather than distributed as files.' data_governance.accountable_organization 'Massachusetts General Hospital' and a detailed access_review_process naming contacts dbold@emory.edu and jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org, the registration flow, the .edu requirement and compute provisioning. license_and_use_terms.notes distinguishes MIT/Apache-2.0 software licensing from the clinical dataset. Absent: ip_restrictions; data_protection_impacts; hipaa_compliant; other_compliance; governance_committee_contact. All three elements of the top band are nominally present — access terms, restrictions and a confidentiality classification — and the governance narrative goes further than most, naming an accountable organization, two access contacts, the credential requirement and the enclave model. Held at 4 rather than 5 because the licence instrument governing the data is never named or reproduced (the record's own source_caveats concede this), no regulatory compliance determination is recorded, and data_governance.source_caveats notes there is no named access committee, decision timeframe or appeal process. A prospective user learns whom to email but not the terms they would be agreeing to. Content accuracy: the restrictiveness of the access terms is well aligned with the sensitivity declarations — sensitive_elements and confidential_elements both true, confidentiality_level 'restricted', all nine modalities controlled, analysis-in-place in an enclave. That alignment is a genuine consistency pass. The residual inconsistency, recorded as an issue, is scope: the only licence described is embedded in a training-programme registration form, while third_party_sharing.is_shared=true implies a general sharing route whose terms are undocumented. The MIT/Apache-2.0 note is correctly scoped to software and explicitly disclaimed as covering the clinical dataset, which avoids a common licence-conflation error.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to (prose): structured EHR standardized to OMOP CDM 'with published OMOP-schema metadata and OMOP schema extensions for nursing flowsheets'; notes follow 'the OHNLP open-source schema'; imaging 'the DICOM schema'; telemetry 'WFDB with an extended PhysioNet schema'; EEG 'the open-source EDF+ and Persyst schemas'. conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]. conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; conforms_to_class: 'Dataset'. distribution_formats: five standard formats. Integration: preprocessing_strategies cites 'validated semantic mappings that connect clinical data in various source formats to international standards; pooled tabular mappings and their documentation are maintained in the chorus-mapping repository'; collection_mechanisms cites 'the OHDSI tool stack'; instances carry B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC ontology codes. Absent: related_datasets (no typed relationships); no common cross-dataset linking identifier. Two of the three top-band elements are exemplary. Standard formats are correct per substrate; schema conformance is stated at a level of detail (named extensions, named schema URIs) that is rare in these records. Integration capability across the 14 contributing hospitals is real and operationalized — OMOP CDM plus validated semantic mappings plus the OHDSI tool stack is precisely a harmonization procedure, and the ontology-coded instances support machine interpretation. Held at 4 because the question also calls for cross-platform dataset linkages with typed relationships: related_datasets is empty, no common identifier for linking to other datasets is described, and the record's own source_caveats confirm that although CHoRUS collaborates with three sibling Bridge2AI projects, no dataset relationship is recorded. Secondary drag: metadata publication was only 'planned' for notes, imaging and EEG, so schema conformance is asserted but not yet realized for a third of the modalities. Correctness: every named standard is real and correctly matched to its substrate; the w3id.org schema URI is well formed. Consistency: conforms_to prose, conforms_to_standard enums and distribution_formats agree with each other modality by modality — a clean three-way check. Semantic caution: interoperability is documented as harmonization *into* the enclave rather than interoperability *out of* it, since no files are distributed; combined with the absent related_datasets this means the dataset is internally harmonized but externally unlinked, which is what separates 4 from 5 here.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies (five entries): OMOP standardization with validated semantic mappings in chorus-mapping; OHNLP-toolkit extraction and tokenization; 'Transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification, including de-identification of imaging'; WFDB conversion 'using the waveform conversion scripts'; 'Geocoding of OMOP Location entities via DeGauss, using the open source UF-Geocoding code'. cleaning_strategies: 'Characterization reports are produced and returned to contributing sites following their data submissions, and site status tracking is used to identify and resolve blocking issues'. labeling_strategies: annotation environment (future tense) with data_annotation_protocol 'Clinical collaborators contribute to semantic mapping and validation under a clinical validation SOP'. machine_annotation_tools: tools ['OHNLP toolkit'] with tool_descriptions. missing_data_documentation: detailed patterns and causes. Named tools overall: OHNLP toolkit, OHDSI tool stack, DeGauss, chorus-mapping, chorus_waveform, chorus-extract-upload, chorus-container-apps, privacy_scan_tool, CTP-deid, UF-Geocoding, CHoRUSReports, Azure. Absent: annotation_analyses; imputation_protocols; any version number. Five of seven fields populated, with strategies documented per modality rather than generically, and roughly a dozen named tools with an organization-level URL (https://github.com/chorus-ai) plus a stated package status page tracking 'versions, maintainers and other package metadata'. That is strong transparency. Held at 4 because the top band requires software versions or URLs at tool granularity: not a single version number appears anywhere, individual repositories are named in prose without their own URLs, and imputation_protocols and annotation_analyses are absent entirely — so a reader cannot reproduce the pipeline as configured. Consistency pass: the preprocessing tools map coherently onto the declared outputs — OHNLP tokenization produces the OHNLP-schema tokens in distribution_formats, and the waveform conversion scripts produce the WFDB format. Consistency gap carried to the issues list: privacy_scan_tool and CTP-deid are listed as existing repositories, but is_deidentified.source_caveats explicitly states the bundle does not say either was applied to the released data — so a de-identification tool is named without a verified link to the artifact it supposedly processed. Semantic caution: labeling_strategies is written in the future tense and its own source_caveats confirm 'the bundle does not report labels present in the released data', so the labeling limb describes intent rather than a realized pipeline.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: 'Retrospective collection: clinical data generated during routine care are extracted at contributing hospitals, standardized, tokenized, stored, visualized and labeled through a multi-center network, then delivered as a CHoRUS data extract to the shared cloud enclave.' collection_mechanisms: six entries, one per modality plus site tooling (OMOP extraction via the OHDSI tool stack; OHNLP tokenization with text remaining on site; PACS retrieval in DICOM; telemetry capture via gateway/middleware converted to WFDB; EEG as EDF+/Persyst; chorus-extract-upload and dockerized container apps on Azure). data_collectors: two entries — 'Fourteen data acquisition centers, drawn from a collaboration spanning 20 academic centers... Site data managers follow the step-by-step extraction and contribution workflow documented in the Chorus_SOP repository' (role: Data contributing sites) and consortium sub-teams for Standards, Data Acquisition and Tooling. raw_data_sources: five typed sources with native formats and access details. direct_collection.is_direct false with rationale. sampling_strategies present. collection_timeframes: 'Data collection is retrospective. As of August 2025 the assembled dataset covered 14 different hospitals. The funded project period runs from 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30', with source_caveats 'The bundle does not state the calendar range of the clinical encounters represented in the data'. All five fields populated, and the methods and collectors limbs are as detailed as this rubric's top band asks for — per-modality mechanisms, named SOP repository, named tooling, typed source systems, and an explicit statement that collection was not direct. The timeframes limb, however, does not deliver a data collection timeframe: what is recorded is the award period and an August 2025 status snapshot, not the calendar range of the ICU admissions represented. For a retrospective EHR dataset the encounter date range is load-bearing — it determines comparability of coding practice, care protocols and any COVID-era effects — so its absence is a substantive reusability gap, not a formality. Scored 4: two of three top-band limbs fully met, the third only nominally. Consistency pass: collection_mechanisms and raw_data_sources agree modality by modality on origin system and native format, and both agree with distribution_formats on the resulting format. The '14 hospitals within a collaboration of 20 academic centers' figure is stated consistently in data_collectors, known_limitations and description. Semantic caution: sampling_strategies asserts 'sampling methods intended to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort' while its own notes concede the bundle 'does not describe the sampling frame or selection criteria in operational detail' — so the selection mechanism that determines which of a hospital's ICU admissions entered the 50,000 is undocumented, which compounds the timeframe gap and is directly relevant to the selection bias not documented under Q20.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: Present: updates.update_details 'The released dataset is being expanded toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals. As of August 2025, de-identification of a larger imaging cohort and extraction of EEG were in process, and metadata publication for clinical notes, imaging and EEG was planned', with source_caveats 'The bundle does not state an update frequency or a versioning policy.' maintainers: three entries — Ciera McCrary, Program Manager, MGH; access contacts at Emory and Tufts Medicine; and the chorus-ai organization maintaining 28 repositories with 'versions, maintainers and other package metadata... tracked on a package status page'. status describes the release state and the award period. Absent: version; version_access; errata; doi; publisher. Well below the 3 band, which requires a version number plus basic access info plus a persistent ID — of those three, only access info exists. Against the four sustainability criteria: (1) persistent identifier — absent; (2) long-term governance plan — partial only, via data_governance's accountable organization and access process, with no preservation commitment; (3) domain-appropriate repository — no; the holding is a project cloud enclave, not a persistent domain repository such as PhysioNet, notwithstanding that the waveform schema derives from PhysioNet; (4) institutional commitment — partial, limited to the OT2OD032701 award period ending 2026-11-30 with nothing stated beyond it. Scored 2 rather than 0 because maintainers are named with working roles and contacts, a substantive forward-looking update plan exists, and package-level version tracking is at least asserted for the software; scored no higher because a dataset that is actively changing — 50,000 now, 100,000 anticipated, three modalities incomplete — with no version identifier and no DOI cannot be cited reproducibly at all. This is the sharpest sustainability exposure in the record, and two independent signals compound it. First, the award period ends 2026-11-30 with no stated successor arrangement for hosting or preservation. Second, the record faithfully captures a site-wide banner in notes: 'This repoitory is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives' (typo as printed on the source site), which is an explicit governance-continuity risk sitting alongside an absent preservation plan. Consistency: the record does not overclaim — updates.source_caveats concedes the missing versioning policy rather than inventing one, which is honest documentation of a genuine deficiency.

name: Associated Publications
text: external_resources holds nine entries, of which the distinct references include: the CHoRUS project website (https://chorus4ai.org/); the chorus-ai GitHub organization (https://github.com/chorus-ai, 28 repositories); Chorus_SOP (centralized SOP documentation site with interactive workflow diagram); chorus-mapping; chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources; chorus-extract-upload and chorus-container-apps; privacy_scan_tool, CTP-deid and UF-Geocoding; CHoRUSReports; and the Bridge2AI project page (www.bridge2ai.org/chorus) plus the AIM-AHEAD call for applications. citation: absent. doi: absent. existing_uses notes only that 'As of August 2025, the datasets are being used for training activities and publications' without naming any publication. Well past the two-distinct-references threshold — there are at least nine distinct non-publication references, all genuinely distinct resources rather than repeated links to the same target. But the 5 band additionally requires a formal citation for this dataset, and none exists: there is no citation field, no dataset DOI, and no entry that identifies the dataset by title together with its authors or publishing organization in citable form. Per the Q14 rule this is exactly the documented case of multiple non-publication resources without a formal citation, which earns 3. No peer-reviewed publication is cited either, despite existing_uses alluding to publications in the abstract. Correctness: URLs are mostly well formed; 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' is recorded without a scheme and several named repositories (Chorus_SOP, chorus-mapping, CHoRUSReports) appear in prose without individual URLs, so they resolve only by navigating the organization page. Consistency: the absence of a citation is coherent with the absence of a DOI — the record has no citable identifier to cite with, so Q14's ceiling here is a direct downstream consequence of the Q6/Q13 identifier gap rather than an independent omission.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances: 'Patient admission from an intensive care unit (ICU), pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)', counts 50000; a 'Demographics record' modality standardized to OMOP; 7,642 admissions with radiology data. subpopulations: subpopulation_elements_present true, identification 'Released admissions are identified by care setting as adult intensive care (ICU), pediatric intensive care (PICU) and neonatal intensive care (NICU) admissions', with source_caveats 'The bundle does not report the distribution of admissions across these settings.' at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included true (minors via PICU/NICU). splits: holdout intention, size and composition unstated. missing_data_documentation: uneven modality coverage. sampling_strategies: aim of 'a balanced and diverse cohort'. Above the 3 floor in that subgroups are identified at all — care setting, and by implication a pediatric and neonatal population — and the at-risk flag is derived from the data rather than asserted. But the top band requires detailed demographics and inclusion/exclusion criteria, and neither exists: no age, sex, race, ethnicity or payer distributions are reported even though a demographics modality is part of the dataset; the split across ICU/PICU/NICU is explicitly unreported; and no inclusion or exclusion criteria for admissions are stated anywhere. A reader cannot assess whether the cohort is representative of the population they intend to deploy a model on. Consistency pass: PICU/NICU appear coherently across subpopulations, human_subject_research.special_populations and at_risk_populations, so the vulnerable-population identification is internally sound. Semantic gap with direct downstream effect: the record contains a demographics modality and keywords 'social determinants of health', and sampling_strategies claims an aim of a diverse cohort — yet no demographic characterization is reported, so the diversity claim is unverifiable from the datasheet. That unverifiability is the same deficiency that makes the Q20 fairness analysis impossible, and the two should be remedied together.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; id 'https://chorus4ai.org/'; extension_mechanism.contribution_url 'https://github.com/chorus-ai'; conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; external_resources also cite 'https://github.com/chorus-ai' and 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus'. download_url and doi absent. Passes on the stated criterion of at least one external URL — several are present, structurally sound and on plausible domains, and the w3id.org URI is itself a persistent-identifier service. Correctness: one URL is schemeless ('www.bridge2ai.org/chorus') and several named repositories lack individual URLs, hence the some_invalid url_validity flag; these do not defeat the pass. Semantic caution worth recording: none of these links is a persistent identifier for the dataset itself — they point at a project website, a code organization and a schema. 'Findable' is satisfied here in the weak sense of reachable-today, not in the FAIR sense of a globally unique persistent identifier, which the binary criterion cannot distinguish and which Q6, Q13 and Q19 penalize instead.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: license_and_use_terms: controlled access; signing a licensing agreement in the registration form is a precondition. data_governance.access_review_process: 'Access requests are directed to named CHoRUS contacts (dbold@emory.edu or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org). For the AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program, participants complete a registration form giving name, email and institution and sign the licensing agreement included in that form; once access is granted and compute is provisioned, an email is sent to the participant. A ".edu" email address is required.' third_party_sharing: Cohort 2 runs 2025-11-17 to 2026-07-31 for up to 30 trainees working 'on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud'. regulatory_restrictions: analysis inside a cloud enclave, not file distribution. distribution_formats: five in-enclave formats. download_url absent. The three components of a fully defined access path are each partly present: platform (the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud, Azure-hosted enclave), login/credential gate (institutional .edu email plus signed licensing agreement, with provisioning confirmation by email), and policy (controlled access across all nine modalities). For the training-programme route this is genuinely actionable — a reader knows what to do. Held at 4 because the general route is only 'email one of two people': no application portal, no DUA document, no eligibility criteria outside the programme, and data_governance.source_caveats confirms no access committee, no decision timeframe and no appeal process. The formats also cannot be obtained as files at all, which the distribution_formats listing does not itself convey. Consistency pass: the access mechanism is coherent with confidentiality_level 'restricted', with all modalities marked controlled, and with the absence of a download_url — the record does not claim downloadability anywhere. Consistency gap raised as an issue: license_and_use_terms describes terms only for training-programme participants while third_party_sharing asserts general availability, so the terms attaching to the general route are undocumented. Semantic note: the enclave model is appropriate for PHI-derived critical-care data, so the restriction is well matched to the sensitivity — the deduction concerns documentation completeness, not excessive restriction.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: intended_uses: three categories with examples and usage_notes — 'Clinical AI/ML model development' (characterizing critical illness, predicting complications and deterioration, measuring treatment response); 'External validation of clinical AI models' (evaluating externally developed models against a sequestered holdout dataset); 'Workforce training and AI literacy' (trainee research on the Collaborative Cloud, canonical Jupyter notebooks, OHDSI/OMOP workshops, clinical deep learning exercises). future_use_impacts: three entries covering marketplace adoption via the holdout set; 'privacy, accountability and clinical benefit as conditions on future use, with patient-focused work determining the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'; and community ethics focus groups determining 'what data is appropriate for public sharing, so the shareable scope of future releases depends on those findings'. license_and_use_terms present but the dataset licence is unnamed. Absent: prohibited_uses; discouraged_uses. Three of five named fields populated, two of them well. intended_uses is genuinely comprehensive — three distinct categories, each with concrete examples and a usage note — and future_use_impacts contains real social-impact reasoning rather than a platitude, notably the point that community consultation determines the shareable scope of future releases. But the top band needs comprehensive use guidance plus a social impact analysis with mitigation strategies, and two limbs fail: prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses are entirely absent, so the boundaries of acceptable use are nowhere stated for a restricted dataset of critically ill patients' records including neonates; and no mitigation strategies are articulated as such — the enclave and tokenization function as controls but are never presented as risk mitigations tied to identified risks. The licence limb is also weak, since license_and_use_terms.source_caveats concedes no data use licence is named. Scored strictly against the five named fields, as the rubric directs. Adjacent content exists elsewhere and was noted but not credited here: known_limitations records that 'analyses requiring full note text cannot be performed on the shared data', which is a de facto use limitation, and regulatory_restrictions confines work to the enclave. Their placement outside Q18's fields means a consumer reading the use-guidance block alone would find no statement of what must not be done — for example, no prohibition on re-identification attempts, on linkage to external identified data, or on clinical deployment without prospective validation, all of which are standard for a dataset of this type. The gap is one of guidance, not of intent: the record's ethics narrative is plainly protective.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: Present: raw_data_sources — five typed origin systems with native formats ('Structured electronic health record systems at 14 data contributing hospitals'; unstructured notes; 'Hospital picture archiving and communication systems (PACS)' in DICOM; 'Bedside physiologic monitors and their gateway/middleware'; 'Hospital EEG databases' as EDF+/Persyst). updates.update_details (expansion plan). missing_data_documentation with both missing_data_patterns and missing_data_causes. splits (holdout intention, composition unstated). Quality control via cleaning_strategies: 'Characterization reports are produced and returned to contributing sites following their data submissions'. Absent: version_access; errata; was_derived_from; parent_datasets. An unusual profile: lineage is strong where versioning is absent. Read across raw_data_sources → acquisition_methods → collection_mechanisms → preprocessing_strategies → cleaning_strategies → distribution_formats, the record does supply entities (source systems, site extracts, the enclave holdings), activities (extraction, OMOP mapping, OHNLP tokenization, WFDB conversion, de-identification, DeGauss geocoding) and agents (14 acquisition centers, site data managers, Standards/Data Acquisition/Tooling sub-teams) — which is the textual form of provenance the question expressly permits. What prevents a higher score is that this lineage is not anchored to any identified released artifact: there is no version, no version_access, no errata, no was_derived_from and no parent_datasets, so derivation paths terminate in an unversioned, unidentified 'current release'. Equally, the 3 band's own descriptor — version history — is itself not met, since no version number or erratum exists. Scored 3 as the balance of a well-documented process lineage against an absent integrity and versioning layer. Consistency pass: the lineage is internally coherent at every hop — each raw source's native format matches the mechanism that extracts it and the preprocessing that transforms it into the stated output format. Quality signals are real: CHoRUSReports characterization returned to sites is a genuine data-quality feedback loop, and missing_data_documentation distinguishes data availability from metadata publication per modality, which is precisely the integrity information an AI/ML user needs. Structural gap: was_derived_from is unpopulated even though raw_data_sources contains exactly the derivation content it would carry, so the provenance is human-readable but not machine-traversable. Compounding issue already raised: with no DOI and no version, no analysis performed on this data can be pinned to a reproducible state of it.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases: absent entirely. future_use_impacts contains one bias-adjacent clause: 'patient-focused work determining the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health'. Related content sits outside Q20's named fields — known_limitations includes a representativeness_limitation ('Data come from 14 data contributing hospitals within a collaboration of 20 academic centers and cover acute and critical care admissions only, so the population is not a general hospital or general population sample') and two coverage_limitations on incomplete imaging and EEG; sampling_strategies states an aim of 'a balanced and diverse cohort'. No bias is typed, no BiasTypeEnum or AIO mapping appears, and no fairness analysis across any subgroup is reported. Above zero because bias is named as an object of management in future_use_impacts and because the record does acknowledge representativeness constraints, but well short of the 3 band, which requires basic bias identification: no bias is actually identified as a bias in the designated field. This is the record's weakest area relative to its own framing — the dataset is titled '...for Equitable AI', carries 'social determinants of health' as a keyword, and is explicitly intended for clinical AI model development and marketplace adoption, all of which raise the expected standard for bias documentation rather than lowering it. The obvious candidates are all documentable from material already in the record: selection bias from 14 academic critical-care centers; measurement bias across heterogeneous site EHR instrumentation and monitor vendors; and differential missingness, which missing_data_documentation already quantifies qualitatively across modalities. Completeness issue of high severity, recorded in issues_detected. The gap also interacts with Q15: because no demographic distribution is reported and the ICU/PICU/NICU split is explicitly unreported, a fairness analysis could not be substantiated even if attempted — the two deficiencies are causally linked. Consistency note: nothing here is inconsistent, and the record does not overclaim fairness; it simply omits the analysis. Scoring was driven by the named fields (known_biases, future_use_impacts) as the rubric directs, with the known_limitations content acknowledged as mitigating but not sufficient to reach the 3 band.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated: id 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; title 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description (~1,290 chars); keywords (30 terms); license_and_use_terms (full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 terms plus data_use_permission 'no_commercial_use' and a named contact); doi '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; page 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; creators (46, mostly with ORCID and affiliation); purposes (3 responses); instances (5 typed instance descriptions with substrate/topic CURIEs); resources (10 enumerated under six file_collections, each with format, media_type, md5, issued). Absent: variables (no variable-level documentation anywhere); parent_datasets (unpopulated — related_datasets carries only an is_new_version_of link to doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level (no classification value; confidential_elements narrates an embargo instead). Eleven of the fourteen enumerated fields are populated and the populated ones carry real content rather than placeholders, putting the record near the top of the 70% band but short of the ≥90% needed for 5. The three gaps are not cosmetic: no variable-level documentation exists for any of the four modalities, provenance to prior releases is expressed only as a sibling relationship rather than a parent link, and confidentiality is described in prose without a classification value a system could act on. Populated fields are mutually coherent — id, doi and page resolve to the same Dataverse object, and the citation repeats the same DOI and version. The missing variables field is the most consequential gap semantically: a record claiming AI-ready multi-modal data with no variable documentation cannot support the variable-level reuse it advertises. No credit was withheld for field presence alone; each counted field was checked for meaningful content.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description runs ~1,290 characters and is substantive throughout: it names the program role ('the Functional Genomics Grand Challenge of the NIH Bridge2AI program'), the three modalities ('protein-protein interaction, spatial protein localization, and genetic perturbation'), the biological systems ('MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (with or without paclitaxel or vorinostat) and in KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cells'), the delivery channel ('ten ZIP archives through the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData)'), a per-modality inventory, and the interim status ('computed cell maps are not included, and some component datasets remain under temporary pre-publication embargo'). The three purposes responses run ~290, ~230 and ~280 characters respectively. Every narrative field exceeds the 200-character threshold by a wide margin, and the length is carried by specifics — named compounds, named cell lines, named repository, an explicit statement of what is absent — rather than by padding. Length here correlates with information density rather than diluting it. The description's closing admission that the release is 'explicitly interim' is a rare instance of a narrative field spending its length on a limitation; it aligns with known_limitations and with the Beta status field rather than contradicting them.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: 30 unique keywords spanning assay modalities ('AP-MS', 'SEC-MS', 'perturb-seq', 'scRNAseq', 'size exclusion chromatography', 'affinity purification', 'mass spectroscopy', 'subcellular imaging'), biological systems ('MDA-MB-468', 'KOLF2.1J', 'iPSC', 'neural progenitor cell', 'cardiomyocyte', 'neuron', 'breast cancer'), perturbagens ('paclitaxel', 'vorinostat', 'CRISPR/Cas9'), analysis targets ('protein-protein interaction', 'protein localization'), program identifiers ('Bridge2AI', 'CM4AI') and a subject classification ('Medicine, Health and Life Sciences'). Nearly four times the ≥8 threshold, and the set is genuinely diverse across facets rather than being one concept restated. Both spelled-out and abbreviated forms are supplied for several concepts (perturbation sequencing/perturb-seq; single-cell RNA sequencing/scRNAseq; neural progenitor cell/NPC), which is a deliberate discoverability choice. Every keyword is corroborated elsewhere in the record — each named modality appears in collection_mechanisms, each cell line in raw_data_sources, each drug in the description — so the keyword set inflates neither scope nor coverage. 'mass spectroscopy' is a minor terminological slip for 'mass spectrometry' but does not affect matching, since the correct forms AP-MS and SEC-MS are also present.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats contains exactly one entry: 'format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip'. Every one of the ten enumerated resources repeats 'format: ZIP', 'media_type: application/zip', 'compression: zip'. The only typing distinction is file_type 'data_file' (9 resources) versus 'metadata_file' (cm4ai_release_metadata.zip), and collection_type 'raw_data'/'metadata' on two collections. total_file_count is 10 and matches the enumeration; file_collections groups the ten into six named collections with per-collection descriptions and sizes (AP-MS 113.3 KB / 135.8 KB; IF images 4.6 GB / 3.8 GB / 4.2 GB; SEC-MS 171.8 KB / 93.9 KB; perturb-seq atlas 30.2 KB; perturb-seq raw 73.3 KB; metadata 1.1 MB). The enumeration half of this question is done about as well as it can be — ten files named individually, grouped into meaningful collections, each with MD5, issue date and size. The variety half fails outright: one container format for the entire release, with no statement of what formats lie inside the archives. The rubric band for a single file type is 0; 1 rather than 0 credits the complete, checksummed, per-collection enumeration, which is real evidence of file-level documentation even though it yields no format diversity. The rubric's note asks for unified participant/sample identifiers across modalities as the marker of multimodality; none exist here. Cross-modality linkage is implicit in the cell-line names (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J) embedded in filenames, which is a weak join key and cannot distinguish treatment arms without parsing the filename. Semantically this matters more than the format count: a reuser cannot tell from this record how to align an immunofluorescence image with a SEC-MS elution profile for the same condition. The ZIP-only declaration also sits awkwardly against the record's RO-Crate and AI-ready claims, which is recorded as a separate semantic_understanding issue.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: Per-archive sizes appear in every file_collections description: '113.3 KB', '135.8 KB', '4.6 GB', '3.8 GB', '4.2 GB', '171.8 KB', '93.9 KB', '30.2 KB', '73.3 KB', '1.1 MB'. Counts: total_file_count 10; file_count per collection (2, 3, 2, 1, 1, 1). notes gives project-scale figures: '1,374 protein interactions, 53,788 immunofluorescent images, 7,023 total proteins investigated, 11,739 genes targeted and 21.4 TB of data volume'. distribution_formats notes a '1.9 GB' web download limit. Passes comfortably on the presence test: numeric sizes exist for all ten deliverables and instance-scale counts exist at project level. Two qualifications, neither defeating the pass. First, sizes live in free-text descriptions rather than in total_size_bytes or file_collections.total_bytes, so they are human-readable but not machine-computable and no release-level total is given. Second, and more serious, several stated sizes are implausible for their described contents — a 30.2 KB 'cell atlas' for an 11,739-gene screen — which is recorded as a content_accuracy issue; the size metadata is present, but its plausibility is in question. The 21.4 TB figure is project-cumulative by the record's own flagged inference and must not be read as this release's volume.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; id 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; page 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; citation resolves the same DOI as 'https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; version_access.latest_version_doi repeats it and lists prior release DOIs 10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, 10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, 10.18130/V3/B35XWX; resource-level identifiers use DOI-anchored fragments (e.g. 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C#file-apms-paclitaxel'); cell lines carry RRID:CVCL_0419 and RRID:CVCL_B5P3; creators carry ORCIDs. Well past the pass threshold — a registered dataset DOI, a resolving landing page, per-release DOIs for the version series, and locally consistent fragment identifiers for each of the ten files. The 10.18130 prefix is the University of Virginia Dataverse registrant and is consistent with the LibraData landing page and with the citation's stated publisher, so the identifier is not merely well-formed but correctly attributed. Fragment-style resource ids are a sensible local convention though not independently resolvable. No explicit publisher field is set; the publisher is recoverable from the citation and maintainers, which is a small structural gap that does not affect the pass.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders lists grantor 'National Institutes of Health' with grant_number '1OT2OD032742-01' (annotated with RePORTER detail: 'core project number as OT2OD032742, with application 11211616 / project number 3OT2OD032742-01S2 for fiscal year 2025, an award amount of 5,289,382, and a project period of 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31') and grant_number '5U54HG012513-02' ('Bridge2AI Bridge Center award'), plus grantor 'University of Virginia' with 'Frederick Thomas Fund'. PI attribution is recorded: 'NIH RePORTER records Trey Ideker, University of California, San Diego, as principal investigator'. creators lists 46 people, the large majority with both ORCID and named affiliation (University of Virginia, UCSD, UCSF, Stanford, KTH, Yale, UAB, University of Texas at Austin, Simon Fraser, University of Montreal). Both halves of the 5-band are satisfied with room to spare: funders carry award numbers rather than agency names alone, and creators carry institutional affiliations rather than bare names. The award period and amount go beyond what the band asks. Award numbers are checked for pattern and for role plausibility: 1OT2OD032742-01 is a well-formed OT2 Other Transaction through the NIH Office of the Director — the correct instrument for a Bridge2AI Data Generation Project — and 5U54HG012513-02 is a well-formed U54 through NHGRI, the correct instrument for the Bridge2AI Bridge Center; the two roles are stated and match. The award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31 is consistent with a June 2026 release and with the updates field's 'through the end of the project in November 2026'. One low-severity defect: 'Frederick Thomas Fund' occupies a grant_number slot while the note concedes no numeric identifier exists. Creator affiliations corroborate data_collectors, with UCSF, Stanford, UCSD and UVA all represented among named people. No score reduction was applied; the grant_number misuse is disclosed and immaterial to the band.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects false with regulatory_compliance 'The release record states "Human Subjects: No" and "FDA Regulated: No"'. is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present false with deidentification_details: 'The release record answers "De-identified Samples: Yes"... CM4AI data are non-clinical, from tissue cultures, and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.' ethical_reviews names two review contacts with ORCIDs and emails (Vardit Ravitsky, ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801; Jean-Christophe Bélisle-Pipon, ORCID:0000-0002-8965-8153), each 'per the Data Governance and Ethics section of the release record'. data_governance gives committee_name 'Data Governance Committee' and a contact with ORCID (Jillian Parker, UCSD), and notes a planned Data Access Committee to 'supervise ethical matters related to dataset distribution and potential dual licensing'. sensitive_elements_present false with rationale. confidential_elements_present true, documenting the pre-publication embargo. purposes commit to producing 'ethical, AI-ready datasets'. Absent: informed_consent (no donor consent provenance for either line), data_protection_impacts, participant_compensation, at_risk_populations, HIPAA or other named compliance framework, reidentification_risk assessment.
