For a dataset with no human participants, the coverage is strong and specific: deidentification status is stated with a reasoned basis rather than asserted, two named ethics contacts are reachable and ORCID-identified, a governance committee exists with a named contact, and regulatory status (human subjects, FDA) is answered explicitly. Short of 5 because the ethics chain stops at the cell line: neither ATCC's nor HipSci's donor-consent framework is cited, no reidentification-risk assessment accompanies the deidentification claim despite the record itself publishing donor age, sex, race and diagnosis for one line, and no data protection impact assessment is present. Cross-field logic checks out: involves_human_subjects=false is consistent with sensitive_elements_present=false, with identifiable_elements_present=false and with direct_collection.is_direct=false, and the deidentification rationale ('cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject') is the appropriate standard for immortalized cell lines rather than a borrowed HIPAA formula. The rubric's expectation that involves_human_subjects=True implies IRB and consent documentation does not fire here, and no penalty was applied for its absence. The residual tension the record does not address is that it simultaneously declares the material de-identified and publishes a donor description — 51-year-old Black female with metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma — specific enough to warrant an explicit reidentification-risk statement. That gap, plus the missing consent provenance, is what separates 4 from 5.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms states the license in full: 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Users are free to share and adapt the material provided they give appropriate credit, provide a link to the license and indicate if changes were made; may not use the material for commercial purposes; and must distribute contributions under the same license as the original. No additional legal or technological restrictions may be applied.' with data_use_permission 'no_commercial_use' and contact_person Trey Ideker (ORCID:0000-0002-1708-8454). ip_restrictions gives two concrete restrictions: 'Commercial use requires a separate license negotiation with the copyright holder (UCSD, Stanford, and/or UCSF depending upon the specific data package in question)' and 'Copyright to the CM4AI datasets is held by the Regents of the University of California except where otherwise indicated; raw image data for spatial proteomics is copyright by The Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University.' Regulatory status: 'Human Subjects: No' and 'FDA Regulated: No'. data_governance names the committee and an ORCID-identified contact. confidential_elements documents the embargo. notes records the Dataverse collection notice: 'This collection is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives.' All three components of the 5-band are present in substance. The license is not merely named but reproduced with its obligations; the restrictions are specific enough to act on, naming which institution holds copyright over which data package and what a commercial user must do; and confidentiality is treated concretely through the documented embargo and the stated public-access status of the ten archives. The Administration-review notice is an unusual and valuable disclosure of a live risk to access. License and restrictions are mutually consistent rather than merely co-present: a NonCommercial license paired with a named commercial-licensing route and identified copyright holders forms a coherent policy, and ShareAlike is not contradicted anywhere. No formal confidentiality_level enum value is set — the only structural shortfall — but the classification content a reuser needs is present in prose, and the instrument directs scoring on content rather than field presence, so no reduction was applied. One disclosed uncertainty is noted rather than penalised: ip_restrictions.source_caveats concedes the commercial-licensing and copyright statements are drawn from the preprint and earlier release pages, since 'The June 2026 release page states only the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license'. The embargo-versus-public-access wording is reconcilable but unreconciled, logged as a low-severity issue.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to: 'RO-Crate packaging with provenance graphs and rich metadata, produced using the FAIRSCAPE framework.'; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; conforms_to_class: Dataset. Ontology use: instances carry B2AI_SUBSTRATE and B2AI_TOPIC CURIEs; cell lines carry Cellosaurus RRIDs; people carry ORCIDs. Typed cross-dataset linkage: related_datasets with relationship_type 'is_new_version_of' targeting doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM. Cross-platform links: MassIVE deposits for SEC-MS and AP-MS raw data, 'CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas of iPSCs, hosted on Figshare', the CM4AI portal, the Cell Mapping Toolkit on GitHub/Zenodo, and FAIRSCAPE at https://fairscape.github.io. Against these: distribution_formats is ZIP only, and known_limitations states 'The current release is most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the individual datasets rather than for integrated cross-modality analysis' and that the three modalities 'interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap'. Standardization is genuinely strong — a named packaging standard, a resolvable schema URI, controlled vocabularies applied at instance level, persistent identifiers for people and biological materials, and a typed relationship to the preceding release. Held at 4 because the third component of the 5-band, integration capability, is the one the record itself disclaims: there is no common sample or participant identifier across modalities, the internal data formats are unstated, and the datasheet says outright that cross-modality analysis is not what this release supports. This is the clearest case in the record of a claim outrunning its evidence, and the record partly says so itself. RO-Crate conformance is asserted but no RO-Crate descriptor is identifiable among the ten resources (logged as a consistency issue), and AI-readiness is asserted while the only declared format is an opaque container. The honest countervailing signal is known_limitations, which withdraws the integration claim explicitly rather than leaving a reuser to discover it — that candour is why the score sits at 4 rather than 3: the standardization substance is real and verifiable even where the integration substance is absent.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies has a single entry: 'Perturb-seq data are distributed both as a processed CRISPRi perturbation cell atlas and as the underlying raw sequence data, in separate archives', immediately qualified by source_caveats: 'Inferred from archive naming in the June 2026 file listing; that listing carries no per-file processing description. Computed cell maps, which the project produces by self-supervised multimodal embedding and multi-resolution community detection, are explicitly not included in this release.' Software is named only in external_resources (Cell Mapping Toolkit, FAIRSCAPE) with no version numbers and no GitHub or Zenodo URL — only the FAIRSCAPE framework page is linked. Entirely absent: cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, imputation_protocols, missing_data_documentation. Acquisition instruments are named elsewhere (10x Genomics 3'HT kit, HPA antibodies, inducible dCas9) but these are wet-lab reagents, not data-preparation software. The 3-band's literal condition ('at least one strategy or tool listed') is met on its face, but the single listed strategy is not documentation of processing — it is the record's own inference from two filenames, self-flagged as such, and it describes a packaging arrangement rather than any transformation applied to the data. Six of the seven fields for this question are empty. Scored 2 rather than 3 to reflect that the sole strategy entry carries no processing information a reuser could reproduce; the reduction is a deliberate semantic discount, recorded here as required. The transparency gap is asymmetric in an informative way: the record is fully transparent about the framework used to package and describe the data (FAIRSCAPE, RO-Crate) and opaque about the pipeline that produced the data inside it. No alignment tool, guide-assignment method, QC threshold, mass-spectrometry search engine, image segmentation step or normalization procedure is named for any of the four modalities. The mention that cell maps are built 'by self-supervised multimodal embedding and multi-resolution community detection' describes a product explicitly excluded from this release, so it adds no reproducibility for what is shipped. Naming the Cell Mapping Toolkit without a resolvable URL or version means even the one tool credibly involved cannot be pinned to a state.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: collection_mechanisms gives four modality-specific entries with real technical content: 'Affinity purification mass spectrometry (AP-MS) performed on endogenously tagged cell lines'; 'Size-exclusion chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (SEC-MS), for proteome-wide protein complex and interaction mapping'; 'Immunofluorescence-based staining and confocal microscopy (ICC-IF) for spatial proteomics, using the Human Protein Atlas resource of antibodies, with automated fixation and permeabilization protocols established for the MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2 cell lines'; 'Single-cell CRISPR interference perturbation screens, performed using the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit, with a CRISPR lentiviral library and cell lines expressing inducible dCas9.' acquisition_methods distinguishes direct observation (was_directly_observed true) from derived processing (was_inferred_derived true). data_collectors names four institutions with roles: UCSF (mass spectrometry PPI, Krogan Laboratory), Stanford (IF spatial proteomics, Lundberg Laboratory), UCSD (CRISPR screening and integration), UVA (packaging, metadata, provenance, archiving). raw_data_sources gives both cell lines with RRIDs, donor characteristics and access routes (ATCC; HipSci via simple MTA). sampling_strategies documents the targeted design ('100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes'). collection_timeframes concedes: 'No explicit start and end dates for data collection are stated.' Three of the four scored components are documented well — mechanisms are named per modality with instruments and reagent sources, collectors are named with institutional roles, and acquisition is typed as observed versus derived. The fourth, timeframes, is the acknowledged gap: only a creation/deposit date of 2025-02-27 and the funding period stand in for a collection window. Per-modality protocol parameters (antibody validation criteria, MS gradient and instrument, MOI and library depth) are also absent, which is what separates this from a full protocol at 5. Mechanisms map coherently onto the modalities named in description, keywords and instances — four mechanisms, four modalities, no orphan on either side — and the collector-to-modality assignments are plausible against creator affiliations, with UCSF, Stanford and UCSD people all present in creators. The record is careful about the limits of this mapping: three of the four data_collectors entries carry source_caveats stating that 'The June 2026 release lists production locations collectively without assigning modalities' and that laboratory attribution comes from the preprint and earlier release pages. That is disclosed inference rather than fabrication, and it is treated as such. Deposit date 2025-02-27 preceding the 2026-06-17 publication is temporally ordered correctly.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version '2.0' with status 'Beta'; issued '2026-06-17T00:00:00Z'; created_on '2025-02-27T00:00:00Z'. version_access.latest_version_doi doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C with five versions_available, each with its own DOI where assigned: June 2026 (10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, v2.0), October 2025 (10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, v2.1), June 2025 (10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, v2.1), March 2025 (10.18130/V3/B35XWX, v1.4), May 2024. version_details explains the scheme: 'CM4AI issues quarterly data releases, each deposited in the University of Virginia Dataverse under its own DOI and separately versioned within Dataverse.' updates.frequency 'Quarterly' with 'regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026'. maintainers names the preserving institution — 'Long term preservation is provided by the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData), supported by committed institutional funds' — and named human contacts (Swathi Thaker, CM4AI Program Manager, snthaker@uab.edu; Zhandos Sembay, zsembay8@uab.edu). retention_limit repeats the committed-funds preservation statement. related_datasets types the link to the prior release as is_new_version_of. distribution_dates records both publication waves (2026-06-17 and 2026-07-15). All three sustainability components the 5-band asks for are present and named rather than gestured at: governance (a Data Governance Committee with an ORCID-identified contact), a domain-appropriate repository (an institutional Dataverse with a DOI-minting, versioned deposit model), and institutional commitment ('committed institutional funds', stated twice). Versioning is comprehensive — a five-release lineage with per-release DOIs, an explicit quarterly cadence, a stated end date, named maintainers with working contacts, and a typed link to the predecessor. errata is the one unpopulated field; against the weight of the rest, and given that the record surfaces its own data conflicts in source_caveats in lieu of a formal errata list, it does not pull the score below the band. The sustainability claim is checkable rather than aspirational: a named repository, a named funding basis for preservation, and named people to contact. Two wrinkles were examined and neither is a defect. The version series is non-monotonic as displayed (this 2.0 release postdates releases numbered 2.1), which is coherent under the stated per-DOI versioning but is not spelled out — logged as a low-severity issue. The notes field's disclosure that the collection 'is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives' is a genuine external threat to the very persistence being claimed; disclosing it strengthens the record's credibility even as it qualifies the guarantee. The update cadence is consistent with the award period ending 2026-08-31 and the stated project end in November 2026.

name: Associated Publications
text: A formal dataset citation is present and complete — authors (46 named), year, title in quotes, resolving DOI, publisher and version: 'Clark T; Parker J; ... Ideker T, 2026, "Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)", https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'. Distinct additional references: (1) the project preprint with DOI, 'Clark T, Parker J, Schaffer L, ... Ideker T. Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence: AI-Ready Maps of Human Cell Architecture from Disease-Relevant Cell Lines. 2024. doi 10.1101/2024.05.21.589311'; (2) a second publication under existing_uses with DOI and PMCID, 'Nourreddine S, ... Mali P. A PERTURBATION CELL ATLAS OF HUMAN INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELLS. bioRxiv. 2024 Nov 4; 2024.11.03.621734. PMCID PMC11580897. doi 10.1101/2024.11.03.621734'; (3) the CM4AI project portal https://cm4ai.org/; (4) the CRISPRi Perturbation Atlas on Figshare; (5) the Cell Mapping Toolkit on GitHub/Zenodo; (6) FAIRSCAPE at https://fairscape.github.io. The 5-band condition is met twice over: six distinct references, two of them DOI-bearing publications with one also carrying a PMCID, plus a formal dataset citation that identifies the dataset by title, authors, publisher and version rather than resting on a bare DOI. Scored with the permitted values only (0, 3, 5). The references are distinct resources rather than repeated links to one target, and each is contextualised by a note explaining its relation to the dataset ('Related publication cited by the release record as the reference for this dataset'; 'External data link given in the release record'; 'Software used to integrate CM4AI input data streams'). Both publication DOIs use the 10.1101 bioRxiv prefix, correct for preprints, and the PMCID is well-formed. The citation's author list matches the creators block, and its 'V2' matches the record's version 2.0 — internally consistent.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances enumerates five typed instance kinds with substrate and topic CURIEs but no counts and no human-subject framing. Donor characterisation appears in raw_data_sources and is repeated in known_biases.affected_subsets: 'MDA-MB-468, a triple negative breast cancer line established from a metastatic pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma, and KOLF2.1J, an iPSC line derived from a healthy male Northern European donor.' known_biases states the consequence: data 'do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large'. Biological subgroups are documented as differentiation states and treatment arms (undifferentiated iPSC, NPC, neuron, cardiomyocyte; untreated, paclitaxel, vorinostat). Absent: subpopulations, at_risk_populations, missing_data_documentation, subsets.is_data_split, splits. Sits squarely in the 3-band. The human dimension that exists — two donors — is described with age, sex, race/ancestry and disease state for one line and sex and ancestry for the other, and its representational limit is stated plainly. But there is no population under study, so no demographic distribution, no inclusion/exclusion criteria and no subpopulation analysis exist or could exist; the 5-band is unreachable for a two-cell-line dataset rather than merely unmet. The structured subpopulations and missing_data_documentation fields are empty, and instances carry no counts, so subgroup structure must be reconstructed from prose. Scored for what a two-donor, cell-line dataset can support rather than penalised for lacking a cohort. The donor descriptions are semantically consistent across raw_data_sources and known_biases — the same age, sex and diagnosis appear in both, with no drift. The record draws the correct inference from its own material, converting donor provenance into an explicit representation-bias statement instead of leaving it as background. What would raise this without inventing subjects is counts per instance type and per treatment arm, and documentation of coverage gaps across the incompletely overlapping protein sets that known_limitations already flags.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; doi '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C' and its resolver form in the citation 'https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema' (a w3id permanent identifier); external_resources 'CM4AI project portal, https://cm4ai.org/' and 'FAIRSCAPE AI-readiness framework, https://fairscape.github.io'; prior-release DOIs 10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, 10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, 10.18130/V3/B35XWX; ORCID identifiers throughout creators; RRID:CVCL_0419 and RRID:CVCL_B5P3. Passes on several independent routes: a DOI-backed landing page, a permanent schema URI, a project portal and a framework site, plus persistent identifiers for people, materials and prior releases. URLs are well-formed and their domains are plausible and consistent with the institutions the record names — dataverse.lib.virginia.edu against the stated UVA deposit and maintainer, cm4ai.org against the project, w3id.org against the Bridge2AI schema. The DOI prefix matches the landing-page host, so findability and the identifier point at the same object. Two named external deposits, MassIVE and Figshare, are described without accession numbers or direct URLs, which weakens findability of the raw components specifically; it does not affect the pass, which turns on the dataset's own links.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: distribution_formats.notes sets out the mechanism concretely: 'All ten files are distributed as ZIP archives through the University of Virginia Dataverse. The dataset as a whole is too large to download as a single ZIP; individual files below the 1.9 GB web download limit may be selected from the files table, and the Dataverse Data Access API provides programmatic access. MD5 checksums are published for each archive.' Access policy: public file access for all ten archives (data_governance.notes); no login, DUA or approval step is required, and the license is stated in full with its obligations. Landing page given. For externally held components, repositories are named (MassIVE, Figshare) and the source cell lines carry access routes ('Available from ATCC'; HipSci 'available for access by not-for-profit organizations via a simple MTA'). Counterweight: confidential_elements records that 'The external data links for perturb-seq data in KOLF2.1J iPSCs and for perturb-seq data in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells are both marked embargoed'; no download_url field is populated and no API endpoint or MassIVE/Figshare accession is given. A reuser learns the platform, the access condition (public, no gatekeeping), the license obligations, both retrieval routes (web files table and Data Access API), an operational constraint that would otherwise waste their time (the 1.9 GB per-file web limit and the impossibility of a whole-dataset ZIP), and how to verify what they got (published MD5s). That is a well-defined path. Short of 5 because no direct download URL or API endpoint is given, three of the archives (3.8-4.6 GB) exceed the stated web limit with no stated remedy beyond 'the API exists', and the embargoed external components have no described access route or lift date. The access statements cohere with the governance section — a public-access deposit under a NonCommercial license needs no DUA, and none is claimed, so there is no mismatch between an open license and a hidden gate. The one unreconciled seam is embargo versus public access; reading the two together, the embargo plainly applies to externally linked perturb-seq components rather than to the ten deposited archives, but the record leaves the reader to make that inference, and it is logged as a low-severity consistency issue. The 1.9 GB limit set against 4.6 GB, 4.2 GB and 3.8 GB image archives is an operational gap the record surfaces without closing.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: License stated in full with obligations and data_use_permission 'no_commercial_use'. intended_uses gives four categories: 'AI-ready datasets to support research in functional genomics'; 'AI model training'; 'Cellular process analysis'; 'Analysis of cell architectural changes and interactions in the presence of specific disease processes, treatment conditions, or genetic perturbations'. prohibited_uses gives a reasoned prohibition: 'These laboratory data are not to be used in clinical decision-making or in any context involving patient care without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval.' Reuse-bearing limitations are documented in six known_limitations entries, including 'The current release is most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the individual datasets rather than for integrated cross-modality analysis' and 'Meaningful analysis requires domain expertise'. tasks names two downstream uses. Absent: discouraged_uses; future_use_impacts (no social impact analysis, no risk identification, no mitigation strategies). Above the 3-band's 'basic use guidance': the intended uses are specific enough to tell a reuser whether their project is in scope, the single prohibition is correctly reasoned from the data's non-clinical nature rather than boilerplate, and the limitations function as de facto discouraged-use guidance by naming exactly which analyses this release will not support. Held at 4 because the entire social-impact component of the 5-band is missing — future_use_impacts is empty, so no risks of downstream use are identified and no mitigations are proposed, and discouraged_uses is unpopulated. License and use guidance are consistent: a NonCommercial license alongside intended uses framed as research and model training, with the commercial route redirected to IP negotiation rather than silently forbidden. The prohibition is proportionate to the evidence — the record establishes the data are non-clinical tissue-culture measurements, and the prohibition restricts exactly the clinical application that would overreach that basis. The gap is notable given this dataset's stated purpose: a resource built expressly for training biomedical AI, and derived from two donors of stated ancestry, invites analysis of what follows from models trained on such narrow biological representation. known_biases raises the representational limit but nothing carries it forward into downstream-impact terms or mitigation.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: Integrity: an MD5 checksum on every one of the ten resources (e.g. '8642317c321126213240af4837030a53'), with distribution_formats noting 'MD5 checksums are published for each archive'; the record uses checksum comparison substantively, observing that 'The June 2026 archives carry different MD5 checksums from the October 2025 archives of the same names'. Provenance elements: version_access with a five-release lineage and per-release DOIs; updates with a quarterly cadence; raw_data_sources naming both origin cell lines with RRIDs and repositories; raw_sources listing five upstream raw deposits (MassIVE for SEC-MS KOLF2.1J, SEC-MS MDA-MB-468, AP-MS paclitaxel, AP-MS vorinostat; the raw SRA archive for the CRISPRi screen); acquisition_methods typing one path as was_directly_observed and another as was_inferred_derived; data_collectors assigning each modality to a producing institution and laboratory (agents); collection_mechanisms describing the generating activities; related_datasets typing the link to the predecessor release as is_new_version_of; conforms_to asserting 'RO-Crate packaging with provenance graphs'. Absent or empty: errata; was_derived_from; parent_datasets; missing_data_documentation; subsets.is_data_split; splits. The entity-activity-agent triad is recoverable in substance — producing laboratories as agents, named assay mechanisms as activities, raw deposits and derived archives as entities — and integrity is verifiable per file rather than asserted, which is more than the 3-band's version history alone. It falls short of 5 because the derivation paths that would make this a graph are not encoded: was_derived_from and parent_datasets are empty, the one derivation asserted (atlas from raw sequence) is admittedly inferred from filenames, and the claimed RO-Crate provenance graph is not identifiable among the shipped resources. Data-quality documentation is also thin — no missing-data documentation and no split indicators for a dataset offered for model training. This is the strongest gap between claim and encoding in the record. A machine consuming this datasheet could not reconstruct which archive derives from which raw deposit, because the structured fields for that are empty and the linkage lives in prose and in filename parallelism. Set against that, the integrity story is exemplary in a way that deserves credit: checksums exist for every file and are actually used to reason about what changed between releases, which is provenance work rather than provenance assertion. Temporal ordering across the lineage is coherent (created_on 2025-02-27 → issued 2026-06-17 → amended file publication 2026-07-15), with the last of these flagged by the record itself as anomalous relative to the version date.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases contains exactly one entry: bias_type 'representation_bias'; bias_description 'Data in this release were derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large'; affected_subsets naming both lines with donor characteristics ('MDA-MB-468, a triple negative breast cancer line established from a metastatic pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma, and KOLF2.1J, an iPSC line derived from a healthy male Northern European donor'). future_use_impacts is absent. Related but separate: known_limitations documents coverage and integration limits, including that the three modalities 'interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap'. The single entry is well-built — an enum-conformant type, a description that states the consequence rather than the fact, and affected_subsets scoped to concrete populations. But one bias type is documented for a four-modality dataset whose own design implies others the record leaves unstated: selection bias in the targeted panel of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes, measurement bias across four assay platforms with incompletely overlapping protein coverage, and antibody-availability bias in the Human Protein Atlas-based imaging. No fairness analysis and no AIO mapping accompany the entry. Taxonomy use alone does not carry this above 3 when coverage is single-bias and the fairness component of the 5-band is wholly absent. Where documented, the bias reasoning is sound and self-consistent: the representation claim follows from the two-cell-line design established in raw_data_sources, and the donor characteristics in affected_subsets match those given there without drift. The unexamined biases are visible in the record's own fields, which is what holds the score at 3 rather than 4 — sampling_strategies describes deliberate targeted selection of 200 genes and known_limitations describes incomplete cross-modality protein overlap, both of which are selection and coverage bias in substance but neither of which is carried into known_biases as a typed entry. For a dataset whose stated purpose is training biomedical AI, the absence of any fairness analysis or mitigation discussion is the most consequential responsible-AI gap in the record.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated: id 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; title 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description (~1,050 chars enumerating Perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS and IF components); keywords (27); license_and_use_terms.license_terms (full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 text plus commercial-negotiation clause) with data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; doi '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; page 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; creators (46, with affiliations, ORCIDs, ROR:0153tk833 for UVA, and a designated principal_investigator); purposes (4 responses); instances (3 typed instance_type entries with B2AI_SUBSTRATE/B2AI_TOPIC terms). Partially populated: resources — no top-level list, but every file is enumerated under file_collections[].resources with id, format, media_type, bytes and md5. Absent: variables; parent_datasets (lineage is carried in related_datasets as is_new_version_of instead); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level (regulatory_restrictions holds only other_compliance: 'FDA Regulated: No and Human Subjects: No'). Ten of fourteen slots are populated with substantive content, one (resources) is satisfied in nested rather than top-level form, and three are genuinely empty. The populated fields are not placeholders — creators, license and instances all carry real structure — so this sits above the 70% band but short of 90%. The absence of regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is not merely a blank slot: it contradicts confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present: true and the named perturb-seq embargo, so this gap is also counted as a consistency failure. The missing variables field is material for a dataset advertised as AI-ready, since no variable-level semantics are exposed for any of the four modalities. parent_datasets is arguably satisfied semantically by the typed related_datasets chain, which is why the shortfall is treated as partial rather than total.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description is roughly 1,050 characters and itemises each component ('Perturb-seq data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment and for undifferentiated (parental) KOLF2.1J iPSCs; SEC-MS data for ... NPCs, neurons, and cardiomyocytes; AP-MS data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with treatment; and immunofluorescence images ...'). The four purposes responses run ~200–290 characters each, e.g. 'To deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-Ready data, produced from multimodal interrogation of proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders in disease-relevant cell lines under perturbed and unperturbed conditions.' Average narrative length across the two fields is well above 200 characters. Length is matched by density: the description names cell lines, treatments, differentiation states and modalities rather than padding, and the purposes are distinct from one another rather than restatements. The narrative is semantically faithful to the rest of the record — every modality named in description reappears as a file_collection, an acquisition_method and an instance type, and the 'AI-Ready' framing in purposes is consistent with the declared schema and RO-Crate conformance rather than being an unsupported claim.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: 27 unique keywords spanning technique ('AP-MS', 'SEC-MS', 'affinity purification', 'size exclusion chromatography', 'perturb-seq', 'perturbation sequencing', 'single-cell RNA sequencing', 'scRNAseq', 'subcellular imaging', 'CRISPR/Cas9'), biological system ('MDA-MB-468', 'KOLF2.1J', 'iPSC', 'induced pluripotent stem cell', 'neuron', 'neural progenitor cell', 'NPC', 'cardiomyocyte', 'breast cancer'), perturbagen ('paclitaxel', 'vorinostat'), readout ('protein-protein interaction', 'protein localization') and programme context ('Bridge2AI', 'CM4AI', 'AI', 'artificial intelligence', 'machine learning'). Far above the 8-keyword threshold, with deliberate coverage of abbreviations and their expansions (AP-MS/affinity purification, NPC/neural progenitor cell, iPSC/induced pluripotent stem cell), which materially helps retrieval. One terminology defect: 'mass spectroscopy' is the wrong name for the technique the record otherwise describes correctly as mass spectrometry throughout acquisition_methods and file_collections. The impact is small because 'AP-MS' and 'SEC-MS' are also indexed, so the score is not reduced, but the error is recorded. The programme context asserted here ('Bridge2AI', 'CM4AI') is read from the quoted keywords and from publisher/funders, not assumed from outside the record.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists exactly one entry: format 'ZIP', media_type 'application/zip'. All ten enumerated resources across the five file_collections declare format ZIP / media_type application/zip / compression zip. The only type differentiation is file_type, which takes three values — data_file (AP-MS ×2, SEC-MS ×2, perturb-seq ×2), image_file (IF ×3) and metadata_file (cm4ai_release_metadata.zip). total_file_count: 10 matches the enumeration, and every file carries bytes and md5. Enumeration quality is excellent — ten named files with sizes and checksums grouped into five semantically labelled collections — but declared format variety is one container type, rescued to the middle band only by the three file_type categories. The content is genuinely multi-modal (confocal imaging, two mass-spectrometry modalities, single-cell sequencing), yet none of that variety is expressed as declared formats: the internal encodings inside the ZIPs are never named. Scoring on declared format/media-type variety rather than on inferred content keeps this at 3; awarding 5 would credit multimodality that the format fields do not actually expose. No unified sample or participant identifier scheme across modalities is declared either, though the cell-line RRIDs provide a coarse join key.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: total_size_bytes: 12601718300; per-collection total_bytes (249100; 12600000000; 265700; 103500; 1100000); per-file bytes for all ten resources (e.g. cm4ai_ifimages_MDA-MB-468_untreated.zip bytes: 4600000000); total_file_count: 10; subsets carry is_subpopulation: true / is_data_split: false; subpopulations describes per-modality coverage. Comfortable pass: size metadata is present at three levels of granularity (dataset, collection, file) and is mutually consistent. The record is candid that total_size_bytes is its own derivation from rounded per-file figures rather than a reported value, and that the project portal's 21.4 TB 'Data volume' disagrees by three orders of magnitude because it describes the project rather than this release. Disclosing the derivation and the conflict is better practice than asserting a single unsourced number; the arithmetic checks out exactly against the per-file values. No instance counts (cells, images, proteins) are given for this release, so dimensionality is known in bytes but not in records.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; page and publisher both 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; raw_data_sources additionally carry RRID:CVCL_0419 and RRID:CVCL_B5P3. Both halves of the requirement are met — a registered DOI and an identified repository — and the identifier is reused consistently as the record's id and as the base for local person fragments. The DOI prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia registrant, which agrees with the declared publisher and landing page; identifier, page and publisher are therefore mutually corroborating rather than three independent assertions. Using doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C#person-* fragments for creators lacking an ORCID is a defensible minting strategy that avoids inventing external identifiers.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders: three entries — NIH with grant_number 1OT2OD032742-01 and a note giving the Common Fund/Bridge2AI context plus RePORTER detail (application ID 11211616, project 3OT2OD032742-01S2, FY2025 award 5,289,382 USD, project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31); NIH with grant_number 5U54HG012513-02 (Bridge2AI Bridge Center); and the Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia. creators: 46 entries, each with at least one affiliation (e.g. Timothy Clark, ORCID:0000-0003-4060-7360, ROR:0153tk833 University of Virginia; Trey Ideker, ORCID:0000-0002-1708-8454, UCSD, also named as principal_investigator). Both halves of the top band are fully satisfied, and the funding notes go beyond the minimum by recording award period and amount. Both NIH award strings parse correctly under NIH conventions (1 OT2 OD 032742-01; 5 U54 HG 012513-02), and the mechanisms are the expected ones for a Bridge2AI data generation project and its Bridge Center. Funding is also correctly scoped: the record separates the award recorded on the release itself from awards acknowledged only in the preprint, rather than pooling all three as funding for this release. The funders are consistent with the purposes, which are framed in the Bridge2AI 'AI-Ready data' terms the OT2 mechanism funds.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: Reported for completeness though not scored: ethical_reviews names two project ethics leads with ORCIDs and e-mail (Vardit Ravitsky; Jean-Christophe Bélisle-Pipon) who 'supervise ethical matters relating to dataset preparation, licensing, dissemination and Data Access'; human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: false with the note 'Human Subjects: No; De-identified Samples: Yes; FDA Regulated: No' and the preprint's statement that the data 'are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject'; is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false with deidentification_details citing commercially available de-identified, ethically sourced cell lines; sensitive_elements_present: false; data_governance names a Data Governance Committee with a contactable steward. Not present, and not expected here: informed_consent, participant_privacy, participant_compensation, at_risk_populations, data_protection_impacts, regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant. Excluded from the denominator per the 'Applies to' condition: the datasheet documents laboratory work on commercially available and repository-sourced cell lines, not human participants, so participant-protection fields are absent because they are inapplicable, not because they were omitted. Scoring 0 here would penalise an accurate record. Ethics content that does exist is coherent and is credited instead under Q9 (governance) and Q19 (source provenance). The case is not borderline: four independent fields outside Q8 (description, keywords, collection_mechanisms, direct_collection) all point the same way, and the record volunteers the donor origins of both lines in raw_data_sources — a 51-year-old female patient's pleural effusion for MDA-MB-468, a healthy male Northern European donor for KOLF2.1J — while still correctly classifying the work as non-human-subjects. The one gap worth noting is that ethical_reviews records no formal non-human-subjects determination or exemption identifier; it is flagged as a low-severity issue rather than scored.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms gives the full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 terms with the licence URL and spells out each clause (Attribution, NonCommercial, ShareAlike, no additional restrictions), plus 'Commercial use requires a separate license negotiation with the copyright holder (UCSD, Stanford, and/or UCSF depending upon the specific data package in question)'; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use. ip_restrictions.restrictions names the copyright holders, including Stanford for the spatial proteomics raw image data. data_governance gives committee_name 'Data Governance Committee', a named contact with ORCID and e-mail (Jillian Parker, jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu), an access_review_process describing the planned Data Access Committee and dual-licensing supervision, and stewardship_roles. confidential_elements records the perturb-seq pre-publication embargo. regulatory_restrictions contains only other_compliance: 'The release records FDA Regulated: No and Human Subjects: No' — no confidentiality_level, no hipaa_compliant. Licence and IP terms are exemplary in specificity, and a real governance contact is reachable. The top band is withheld because the confidentiality classification is absent and regulatory_restrictions is thin: it records two negative determinations and nothing about jurisdiction or applicable frameworks. The three restrictiveness signals agree, which is the main correctness test here: an NC licence, a no_commercial_use permission enum, and an IP clause routing commercial reuse to named copyright holders. The scoring reduction is driven by a genuine cross-field inconsistency rather than a bare absence — confidential_elements asserts confidential content exists while regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is empty, so the record declares an embargo without classifying it. The access_review_process is also candid that the Data Access Committee is described in the preprint in the future tense as a plan, and source_caveats notes the committee title differs between sources; that honesty is credited, but it does leave present-day access governance partly prospective.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset. instances are typed with ontology terms (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:63, B2AI_TOPIC:15, B2AI_TOPIC:26, B2AI_TOPIC:34). related_datasets gives seven typed relationships (is_new_version_of ×4, is_described_by, is_referenced_by, references) each with a resolvable DOI target. external_resources lists NDEx (https://ndexbio.org), the Cell Mapping Toolkit (https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with readthedocs documentation), the Integrative Modeling Platform, FAIRSCAPE (https://fairscape.github.io, MIT licence) and MassIVE/Figshare deposits of the component datasets. raw_data_sources supply Cellosaurus RRIDs as cross-dataset join keys. distribution_formats and file_collections[].compression declare only the ZIP container. Strong on semantics and linkage — declared schema, declared packaging standard, ontology-typed instances, typed and dereferenceable cross-repository relationships — but short of the top band because the actual data encodings are undeclared and no integration procedure or common sample-identifier scheme is documented. The interoperability claim is mostly supported rather than asserted: RO-Crate and the LinkML schema URI are named with resolvable identifiers, and the MassIVE/Figshare deposits give genuine cross-platform presence for the same underlying data. Two things hold it below 5. First, a ZIP container is not itself an analysis-ready standard format, and nothing states what is inside, so machine-actionable harmonisation is not achievable from the metadata alone. Second, the record's own integration_limitation — SEC-MS, IF imaging and CRISPRi perturb-seq 'interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap' — means cross-modality joining is known to be partial; the honesty is credited, but the capability is demonstrably incomplete. The AI-readiness framing in purposes is therefore well supported at the FAIR/governance layer and weaker at the computability layer.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, imputation_protocols and missing_data_documentation are all absent. The nearest content is notes, which describes the MuSIC pipeline in detail (node2vec embedding of PPI networks, a Human Protein Atlas deep learning model for immunofluorescence images, contrastive co-embedding, multi-resolution community detection, annotation against Gene Ontology and Reactome with an LLM naming approach) and then scopes it out: 'Computed cell maps are not included in this release, so those pipeline stages describe project tooling and planned future releases rather than processing applied to the data released here.' external_resources names the toolkit, IMP and FAIRSCAPE with URLs but no version numbers. All five file_collections are typed collection_type: raw_data (or metadata). Below the 'at least one strategy or tool listed' band in substance: tools are named, but none of the seven designated fields is populated and no strategy is tied to preparing anything in this release. A reuser cannot learn how the perturb-seq cell atlas archive was produced from the raw SRA archive that ships beside it, nor what search parameters produced the mass-spectrometry outputs. Score 2 rather than 3 because the listed tools are project tooling the record itself disclaims for these files; score 2 rather than 0 because real, resolvable tooling with documentation is nonetheless identified. This is the clearest case in the record where scoping honesty and documentation completeness pull apart. Declaring the collections raw_data and disclaiming the pipeline is semantically correct — it prevents a reader from assuming cell maps are inside — but it leaves a genuine gap, because an archive named cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas.zip is plainly a derived product and its derivation is undocumented. No annotation quality metrics, no imputation protocol and no missing-data statement appear anywhere, so the pre-model quality characterisation that AI-readiness would require is absent.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods: four entries, each with was_directly_observed: true — AP-MS 'on endogenously tagged cell lines'; SEC-MS 'proteome-wide by size-exclusion chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry'; 'immunofluorescence-based staining (ICC-IF) using Human Protein Atlas antibodies and high-resolution confocal microscopy'; 'single-cell CRISPRi perturbation screens (perturb-seq)'. collection_mechanisms: three entries with operational specifics — robot-based automated fixation and permeabilisation for both lines; 'A CRISPR lentiviral library targeting chromatin factors with 6 guide RNAs per gene' with inducible dCas9 lines generated and characterised; '10x Genomics 3'HT kit'. data_collectors: two entries with role academic_institution, naming the Lundberg Lab at Stanford for imaging and the Krogan laboratory at UCSF for SEC-MS and AP-MS. raw_data_sources: MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419) with origin and ATCC availability, KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3) with donor description and HipSci MTA route. collection_timeframes: absent. Four of the five designated fields are populated with genuinely informative content — instrument kit, guide-RNA depth, antibody source and performing laboratory are all recoverable — which is well above a mechanism-only description. The top band is withheld because no acquisition window is given for any modality, and because no collector is named for the perturb-seq work while the other two modalities are attributed. The protocol description is internally coherent with the rest of the record: the four acquisition methods map one-to-one onto the four data-bearing file_collections, and the collectors named here match the copyright attribution in ip_restrictions (Stanford for raw image data, UC Regents otherwise), so authorship, custody and rights agree. was_directly_observed: true is used correctly for instrument measurement. The timeframe gap is a real reuse limitation for a release whose components were generated across multiple prior releases, since a reuser cannot date the measurements or align them with the cell-line passage history.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version: '2.0' with status: Beta and issued 2026-06-17. version_access.versions_available enumerates all five releases with distinct DOIs — May 2024 (doi:10.18130/V3/DXWOS5), March 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX, v1.4), June 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, v2.1), October 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, v2.1), June 2026 (doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C) — with latest_version_doi named. errata records one erratum with an erratum_url. updates.frequency: quarterly, with update_details 'regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026'. maintainers: three entries with named people, institutions, roles and e-mail addresses (programme manager Swathi Thaker, UAB; website support Zhandos Sembay, UAB; depositor Justin Niestroy and point of contact Trey Ideker, tideker@health.ucsd.edu). retention_limit: 'Long term preservation in the University of Virginia Dataverse, supported by committed institutional funds.' publisher and doi identify a domain-appropriate institutional repository. data_governance names a standing committee with a contactable steward. distribution_dates gives publication dates for this and all prior releases. All four sustainability indicators the rubric names are present and specific: a registered persistent identifier, a named governance body with a reachable steward, an institutional repository, and an explicit institutional funding commitment for preservation — plus a dated update cadence with a stated project end. Version lineage is complete and every predecessor is independently citable. Two defects were weighed and did not displace the top band. The erratum text is self-contradictory ('the June 2025 Data Release was published as a revision of the preceding June 2025 release', where related_datasets shows the predecessor was March 2025), but its URL and its substantive content are correct. More seriously, the version string regresses: this successor release is 2.0 while two predecessors are recorded as 2.1, and nothing explains the scheme; this is recorded as a failed consistency check and flagged for correction. Both are wording or numbering defects within otherwise complete coverage of every field the question names, and neither leaves a sustainability indicator undocumented — the maintenance commitment, repository, governance and identifier all stand. version_access and related_datasets independently list the same four predecessor DOIs and agree.

name: Associated Publications
text: citation is a complete formal dataset citation naming the full author list, year, title, DOI and publishing organisation: 'Clark T; Parker J; Al Manir S; ... Ideker T, 2026, "Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)", https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'. Distinct further references: the describing preprint doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 (Clark T et al., 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence: AI-Ready Maps of Human Cell Architecture from Disease-Relevant Cell Lines'); doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734 (Nourreddine S et al., 'A Perturbation Cell Atlas of Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells', PMCID PMC11580897); doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3 (Schaffer LV et al., Nature 642:222-231, 2025). Non-publication references in external_resources: cm4ai.org, MassIVE deposits, Figshare deposit, FAIRSCAPE, the Cell Mapping Toolkit repository, IMP, NDEx. license_and_use_terms additionally carries citation instructions: 'publications referencing this data or derived products should cite the related publication as well as directly citing the data collection.' Well past the two-reference threshold — three distinct DOI-identified publications plus seven external resources — and the dataset's own citation is formal, identifying title, authors and publishing organisation rather than being a bare DOI. The citation's DOI matches the record's own doi and id, and its 'V2' matches the Dataverse major version referenced in version_access, so the citation is self-consistent with the identifier metadata. Relationship typing is used discriminatingly rather than lumping everything as related work: the CM4AI preprint is is_described_by, the perturbation atlas preprint is_referenced_by, and the Nature paper is only references, with the note correctly warning that 'Its data are a separate dataset from this release' — an accurate scoping that prevents a reader from attributing the U2OS multimodal map to these files.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: Reported for completeness though not scored: subpopulations states explicitly that 'Subpopulations in this dataset are cell lines and differentiation states rather than human demographic groups: MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (untreated, paclitaxel, vorinostat) and KOLF2.1J iPSCs (undifferentiated, neural progenitor cells, neurons, cardiomyocytes)', with a distribution statement giving per-modality coverage. subsets defines two subsets with is_subpopulation: true and is_data_split: false. The only human demographic information in the record is donor provenance in raw_data_sources — MDA-MB-468 'established from a metastatic site pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with a metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma' and KOLF2.1J 'derived from a healthy male Northern European donor'. at_risk_populations and missing_data_documentation are absent. Excluded from the denominator per the 'Applies to' condition: there is no participant population to characterise, so demographic diversity and inclusion/exclusion criteria are inapplicable rather than missing. Scoring 0 would penalise the record for correctly declining to invent a cohort description. The record handles the boundary well: rather than leaving subpopulations empty or misapplying a human-demographic frame, it states what the subpopulations actually are and then gives genuinely useful coverage information about which assay reaches which cell state. It also reports the two donors' demographics where they are known, which is the appropriate level of human representation for cell-line data and is credited under Q19 as source provenance. Worth noting for reusers even though unscored: both lines derive from single donors of stated but narrow backgrounds, which is precisely the limitation known_biases records as representation_bias.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; page and publisher: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; distribution_formats.access_urls repeats that landing page; external_resources adds https://cm4ai.org/, https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, https://fairscape.github.io, http://integrativemodeling.org, https://ndexbio.org; errata.erratum_url points to doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R; version_access lists five release DOIs; related_datasets targets seven further DOIs. Comfortable pass with redundancy: the dataset is reachable by DOI and by landing page, and every prior version and related work is independently addressable. All URLs are structurally valid with plausible, subject-appropriate domains, and the landing-page URL embeds the same DOI that the doi and id fields assert, so findability is internally corroborated rather than resting on a single string. Links were checked for form and plausibility only, not dereferenced.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: distribution_formats gives the format (ZIP), an access_url to the Dataverse landing page, and operationally useful notes: 'All ten files in the June 2026 release are distributed as ZIP archives via the University of Virginia Dataverse. Individual file download is available; the dataset as a whole exceeds the repository's 1.9 GB ZIP download limit, and the Data Access API is offered for programmatic access.' license_and_use_terms states the reuse terms and the separate route for commercial use. third_party_sharing gives alternative retrieval routes (MassIVE, Figshare) and warns that the perturb-seq deposits are embargoed; confidential_elements repeats the embargo. No download_url field is present as such, and no statement says whether retrieval requires registration, authentication or a signed agreement. Unusually practical for this field — the whole-dataset ZIP limit and the API alternative are exactly what a reuser needs before attempting a 12.6 GB retrieval — but the access tier is left to inference. The record never says whether the Dataverse files are downloadable without an account, and the embargo means access differs by component, so a reuser cannot determine from the metadata alone what is obtainable today. The access claims are consistent with the size metadata: total_size_bytes 12,601,718,300 does indeed exceed the stated 1.9 GB archive limit, so the warning is corroborated by the record's own figures rather than being generic advice. The licence is permissive for non-commercial reuse, which agrees with the absence of any DUA requirement, but the absence is never affirmed as 'no authentication required', so the tier remains implicit. The per-component embargo is the main real limit on accessibility and is disclosed in two places, which is why the score stays high despite the ambiguity.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms sets out CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 clause by clause with the licence URL, attribution expectations and the commercial-licensing route. intended_uses: four entries each with use_category and usage_notes (AI-ready data for functional genomics; AI model training; cellular process analysis; perturbation and treatment response analysis). prohibited_uses: one entry with both the prohibition and a prohibition_reason — laboratory data 'not to be used in clinical decision-making or in any context involving patient care', because such use 'would lack the appropriate regulatory oversight and approval', with the record's own not-FDA-regulated status cited. discouraged_uses: one entry warning that the release 'does not contain predicted cell maps' and that using it as a source of computed cell maps 'is not supported at this release'. future_use_impacts: absent. Four of the five designated fields are populated and the guidance is specific and reasoned rather than boilerplate. The top band is withheld solely because no social impact analysis with mitigation strategies is offered anywhere — future_use_impacts is empty, and neither known_biases nor known_limitations supplies mitigation. The use guidance is semantically well aligned with the rest of the record: the prohibition is grounded in facts the record itself asserts (laboratory cell lines, FDA Regulated: No), and the discouragement matches known_limitations' scope_limitation and the tasks statement that the release suits per-modality bioinformatics analysis. The licence restrictiveness in intended_uses does not overreach the CC BY-NC-SA terms. The gap is a CROISSANT RAI gap rather than a licensing one: the record identifies a representation limit under known_biases but never carries it forward into a statement of downstream social risk or how a reuser should mitigate it.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: version_access lists five releases with DOIs and names the latest; errata records one erratum with a URL; updates gives a quarterly cadence to November 2026. Derivation beyond version history: raw_data_sources identifies both source cell lines with Cellosaurus RRIDs, donor origin and access routes; data_collectors names the performing laboratories (agents); acquisition_methods names the four measurement activities with was_directly_observed: true; file_collections bind entities to those activities by name and collection_type: raw_data; related_datasets encodes the derivation chain to four predecessor releases as typed is_new_version_of relationships. Integrity: MD5 checksums for all ten files, and the record uses checksum difference as evidence that the June 2026 image archives are not the October 2025 files. conforms_to: RO-Crate declares provenance-capable packaging; FAIRSCAPE is named in external_resources. Absent: was_derived_from, parent_datasets, missing_data_documentation, splits (subsets.is_data_split is present and false). Above the version-history band on several independent counts — named source entities with persistent identifiers, named agents, named activities, file-level fixity and a dated release lineage — but the top band requires the entity-activity-agent links to be represented, and here the reader must assemble them by matching prose across four fields. Three designated fields are empty, including was_derived_from, which is exactly the field that would carry the derivation path. Quality documentation is asymmetric: fixity and lineage are strong, while completeness metadata is absent — missing_data_documentation is empty and no instance counts are given, so a reuser cannot assess coverage gaps within a modality, only across modalities via the integration_limitation note. The RO-Crate conformance claim sits oddly beside the absent was_derived_from, since the packaging standard the record declares is designed to express precisely the derivation links the metadata leaves implicit. The record's own caveat that the June 2026 image archives differ in checksum from their October 2025 counterparts, and that their contents are undescribed, is an honest but real provenance gap for the largest three files in the release.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases contains a single entry with bias_type: representation_bias and bias_description: 'Data in this release was derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large.' future_use_impacts is absent. No fairness analysis, no AIO mapping and no quantitative characterisation of the bias appear anywhere. Adjacent but distinct content sits under known_limitations (four typed entries, including the incomplete protein overlap across modalities). The one bias recorded is the right one for this dataset and it is typed with a recognised enum value, which is a step above untyped prose. It stays at the middle band because coverage is a single entry with no fairness analysis and no social-impact follow-through, and because other biases the record's own content implies are left unstated. The representation_bias claim is substantiated elsewhere in the record rather than asserted in isolation: raw_data_sources shows both lines derive from single donors (a 51-year-old female patient and a healthy male Northern European donor), so the stated limit on population coverage is demonstrably true. Two further biases are visible in the record but not documented as biases — selection bias in protein coverage, since the modalities 'interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap' and the IF panel targets a defined set of proteins of interest, and a measurement-side issue in that the protein count itself is disputed across releases (563 versus 464). Both are disclosed under known_limitations and source_caveats rather than categorised under known_biases, so the taxonomy is applied once rather than systematically.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated (10/14): id 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; title 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description (~1,400 chars); keywords (28 terms); license_and_use_terms (license_terms paragraph + data_use_permission: no_commercial_use); doi '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; page 'https://cm4ai.org/'; creators (45, with affiliations); purposes (4 responses); instances (4 typed instance_type entries). Absent (4/14): resources; parent_datasets (related_datasets is used instead, with is_new_version_of links to doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, F3TD5R, B35XWX); variables (consistent with is_tabular: false but still unpopulated); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level (regulatory_restrictions holds only 'FDA Regulated: No; no export control or regulatory restriction is stated'). Ten of fourteen enumerated fields (71%) are populated, placing this squarely in the ≈70% band. The populated fields are of high quality — this is not a record padded with stubs — but four enumerated fields are genuinely empty, and two of them matter: parent_datasets is unpopulated even though the record clearly knows its ancestry, and confidentiality_level is unset on a record that otherwise documents governance carefully. The parent_datasets gap is a mapping choice rather than an information gap: related_datasets carries typed is_new_version_of relations to three predecessor DOIs, so the lineage information exists but is not in the slot a consumer would query. variables being empty is semantically defensible given is_tabular: false and image/mass-spectrometry substrates. No populated field was found to be a placeholder.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description is approximately 1,400 characters and is specific rather than padded: it names the assay modalities (PPI, spatial localization, genetic perturbation), the cell systems (MDA-MB-468 with and without paclitaxel or vorinostat; KOLF2.1J iPSCs with and without differentiation) and the exact per-modality coverage of the Beta release. purposes carries four responses, each above 200 characters, e.g. 'To deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data, produced from multimodal interrogation of chromatin modifiers, metabolic enzymes, and other proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders...'. Both narrative fields far exceed the 200-character threshold, and length here reflects information density rather than verbosity. The description alone resolves which modality covers which cell type and treatment condition, which is the question a prospective reuser asks first. Length and content agree: every clause in the description is a checkable claim, and each of the four purposes is distinguishable from the others (mapping architecture; delivering AI-ready maps; producing ethical AI-ready datasets; stimulating visible-ML research) rather than being restatements. The description's per-modality claims were cross-checked against subsets, subpopulations.distribution and file_collections and matched.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: 28 unique keywords spanning method ('affinity purification', 'AP-MS', 'SEC-MS', 'size exclusion chromatography', 'perturb-seq', 'perturbation sequencing', 'single-cell RNA sequencing', 'scRNAseq', 'CRISPR/Cas9', 'mass spectroscopy', 'subcellular imaging'), biological system ('MDA-MB-468', 'KOLF2.1J', 'iPSC', 'induced pluripotent stem cell', 'neuron', 'NPC', 'neural progenitor cell', 'cardiomyocyte', 'breast cancer'), perturbagen ('paclitaxel', 'vorinostat'), measured entity ('protein-protein interaction', 'protein localization') and programme/discipline ('AI', 'artificial intelligence', 'machine learning', 'Bridge2AI', 'CM4AI'). Well above the ≥8 threshold, with no duplicates. The set is deliberately constructed for retrieval: abbreviations and their expansions are both present (AP-MS/affinity purification, iPSC/induced pluripotent stem cell, NPC/neural progenitor cell, scRNAseq/single-cell RNA sequencing), which is the right choice for discoverability. Keywords match the documented content across every dimension checked — each named assay appears in acquisition_methods or collection_mechanisms, each named cell type appears in subpopulations, and both named drugs appear in subsets. 'mass spectroscopy' is a mild misnomer for mass spectrometry but is a common retrieval variant and does not mislead. Programme context (Bridge2AI, CM4AI) is evidenced by the keyword list and by publisher/funders, not assumed.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats contains exactly one entry: format 'ZIP', media_type 'application/zip', with the note 'All ten files in the release are distributed as ZIP archives via the University of Virginia Dataverse.' total_file_count: 10. file_collections enumerates all ten archives individually with name, collection_type (raw_data / processed_data / metadata), compression 'zip', MD5 checksum and stated size — e.g. 'cm4ai_ifimages_MDA-MB-468_untreated.zip ... MD5: 6d066e6b9d762284c6aa5d0b44565568. Size stated on the release page as 4.6 GB.' No internal file format is stated for any archive. The two halves of this question diverge sharply. Enumeration is exemplary: every one of the ten files is listed with fixity and size. Type variety is the minimum the rubric recognises — one format, and that format is a container rather than a data format. The score reflects the enumeration credit above the 0 band for 'one file type only', without reaching the 2–3 file-type band, because no second format is stated anywhere in the record. This is a substantive interoperability gap, not a bookkeeping one. The record documents four distinct data substrates (confocal images, SEC-MS elution profiles, single-cell CRISPRi transcriptional profiles, AP-MS interaction measurements) whose native formats are necessarily different, yet all are reported as 'ZIP'. A reuser cannot tell from the datasheet whether the 12.6 GB of IF imagery is OME-TIFF, PNG or a proprietary microscope format. The multi-modality asserted in description and keywords is therefore real in the data but invisible in the format metadata.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: Every file_collections entry states a size: 113.3 KB (apms paclitaxel), 135.8 KB (apms vorinostat), 3.8 GB (ifimages paclitaxel), 4.6 GB (ifimages untreated), 4.2 GB (ifimages vorinostat), 171.8 KB (mass-spec KOLF2), 93.9 KB (mass-spec MDA-MB-468), 30.2 KB (perturb-seq atlas), 73.3 KB (perturb-seq raw sra), 1.1 MB (release metadata). total_file_count: 10. Nine subsets are enumerated with is_data_split: false and is_subpopulation: true, and subpopulations documents the coverage distribution across cell types and treatments. Passes clearly. Numeric size metadata exists for all ten distributed files, which is more than the threshold requires, and the subset structure is enumerated alongside it. Two qualifications that do not change the pass. First, sizes live in free-text notes rather than in total_size_bytes or file_collections.total_bytes, so they are human-readable only — logged as a separate low-severity completeness issue. Second, no instance count is given (no number of images, spectra or cells), so the sizes support a storage estimate but not a sample-size estimate; the rubric explicitly notes that sample size only enables a file-size estimate, and here the converse limitation applies.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; id: 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; page: 'https://cm4ai.org/'; publisher: 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/'. version_access.latest_version_doi: 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'. Predecessor releases carry their own DOIs (10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, /F3TD5R, /B35XWX, /DXWOS5), and creators carry ORCID CURIEs for 37 of 45 authors. Passes on multiple independent identifiers. The DOI is a registered persistent identifier, the publisher is the registering repository, and the identifier is repeated consistently in id and in version_access.latest_version_doi without divergence. Registrar check: prefix 10.18130 belongs to the University of Virginia Library's Dataverse (LibraData), which matches publisher 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/' — identifier and stated publisher are mutually corroborating rather than merely both present. One nuance: page points to the project portal cm4ai.org rather than to the Dataverse landing page for this DOI, so the persistent identifier and the human landing page resolve to different places; the DOI itself still carries findability. No RRID is present, which is expected for a dataset record.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health' with grants.grant_number '1OT2OD032742-01'; notes add 'NIH award 5U54HG012513-02 (Bridge2AI Bridge Center) and the Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia'. creators: 45 entries, each with at least one affiliation (University of Virginia with ROR:0153tk833; UCSD; UCSF; Stanford; KTH Royal Institute of Technology; Yale; UAB; University of Alabama; University of Texas at Austin; Simon Fraser; University of Montreal). Ideker T carries a principal_investigator block with ORCID 0000-0002-1708-8454 and email tideker@health.ucsd.edu. Both halves of the 5-point condition are met and exceeded: a named grantor with a structured award number, two additional acknowledged funding sources, and complete affiliation coverage across a 45-author list with ORCIDs for most and a ROR identifier for the lead institution. The PI is separately identified rather than left implicit in the author list. Grant-pattern validation passes: 1OT2OD032742-01 decomposes correctly as NIH application type 1 / activity code OT2 / awarding institute OD / serial 032742 / support year 01, the expected shape for a Bridge2AI Other Transaction award; 5U54HG012513-02 is likewise well formed (type 5, U54, NHGRI). Funding-to-purpose alignment holds: the purposes (AI-ready cell maps, visible machine learning) match the stated Bridge2AI Functional Genomics Grand Challenge remit of the OT2 award. Affiliations are consistent with data_collectors, which attributes IF imaging to the Lundberg Lab at Stanford and SEC-MS to the Krogan lab at UCSF — the same institutions that appear in those authors' affiliation entries.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: false, with notes 'The release records Human Subjects: No; De-identified Samples: Yes; FDA Regulated: No. CM4AI data are described as non-clinical (from tissue cultures) and considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.' is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false with matching deidentification_details. ethical_reviews: two entries with named contacts and addresses — Vardit Ravitsky (ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org) and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon (jean-christophe_belisle-pipon@sfu.ca) — the second describing a Value-Sensitive Design methodology and an axiological repository. sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present: false with rationale. data_governance.committee_contact: Jillian Parker (jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu) with an access_review_process. Absent: informed_consent, participant_privacy, participant_compensation, at_risk_populations, data_protection_impacts, regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant. Comprehensiveness must be judged against what is in scope. Most unpopulated fields — compensation, at-risk populations, participant privacy — are genuinely inapplicable to immortalized and iPSC lines, and inventing them would be worse than omitting them. What is present is strong: an explicit and reasoned human-subjects determination, a de-identification claim with the correct standard, two named ethical reviewers, and a standing governance contact. The point withheld is for the one in-scope gap: no statement of the consent or ethical-sourcing basis for the donor material, and no data_protection_impacts entry recording that such an assessment was considered and found unnecessary. Cross-field logic checks out in the direction the rubric specifies: because involves_human_subjects is false, the absence of IRB protocol numbers is consistent rather than a contradiction, and the is_deidentified claim is paired with a method rationale as required. The deidentification argument is also appropriate to the data type — for tissue-culture data the operative standard is non-matchability, which is what is asserted. The residual tension is that direct_collection records the KOLF2.1J line as 'derived from a healthy male Northern European donor' available through HipSci, so identifiable donor provenance exists upstream of the not-human-subjects determination and is left undocumented; this is logged as a low-severity consistency issue and is the basis for the one-point reduction.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
