text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms gives CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 in full operative detail ('free to share ... and adapt ... under the conditions that appropriate credit is given with a link to the license and an indication of changes; that the material is not used for commercial purposes; and that contributions built upon the material are distributed under the same license'), with data_use_permission: no_commercial_use. ip_restrictions states 'Copyright for CM4AI data is held by the Regents of the University of California except where otherwise noted; raw image data for spatial proteomics is copyright by The Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University', plus commercial relicensing via UCSD/Stanford/UCSF and a Data Access Committee. data_governance provides a named committee_contact with email, an access_review_process and stewardship_roles. regulatory_restrictions records only 'FDA Regulated: No; no export control or regulatory restriction is stated'. regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is absent, as are hipaa_compliant, other_compliance and data_protection_impacts. License and restrictions are documented to a standard well beyond 'license only' — the copyright split between UC and Stanford for different data types is the kind of detail that actually governs downstream reuse, and a named governance contact with a review process makes the policy actionable. The fifth point is withheld solely because the confidentiality classification, which the 5-point condition names explicitly, is never set. Restrictiveness is coherent across fields: a non-commercial share-alike license, a reserved commercial-licensing pathway, and a Data Access Committee together describe a consistent posture of open academic reuse with commercialization held back. That posture is also consistent with the ethics fields — because no human subjects and no sensitive elements are declared, the absence of HIPAA and DPIA content is logically expected rather than a contradiction. The one incongruity is that a record this careful about governance leaves confidentiality_level unstated when the obvious value (public/open) follows directly from its own CC BY-NC-SA distribution.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema' with conforms_to_class: 'Dataset'. conforms_to_standard: RO_CRATE, with conforms_to narrating FAIRSCAPE RO-Crate packaging and provenance graphs. instances are typed with ontology term IDs (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19, :58, :59, :64; B2AI_TOPIC:15, :26, :34). related_datasets carries typed relationships — is_new_version_of (three predecessor DOIs), is_described_by (doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311), is_referenced_by (doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734), references (doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3). external_resources names NDEx with Cytoscape/HiView/ndex2 access, the Cell Mapping Toolkit at github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, FAIRSCAPE and IMP. notes describes ARK persistent identifiers and the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology, and GO/Reactome alignment of assemblies. distribution_formats: ZIP only. Integration capability is real and specific: a LinkML schema URI with a declared class, ontology-typed instances, four distinct relationship predicates linking this release to its predecessors and to three publications, and named cross-platform endpoints (NDEx, MassIVE, Figshare) with tooling to consume them. That is materially beyond 'standard format but no schema reference'. Full marks are withheld because the distribution layer itself is a bare ZIP container with no internal format declared, so harmonization with another dataset still requires opening the archives to discover what is inside. The RO-Crate conformance claim is the weak link and the record itself flags it: conforms_to states that the June 2026 release page 'does not itself restate the packaging format', yet conforms_to_standard asserts RO_CRATE unqualified, so the structured standards claim outruns its evidence. That mismatch is logged as a medium consistency issue and contributes to the one-point reduction alongside the format gap. Cross-platform linkage is otherwise genuine rather than nominal — the external endpoints are named with the tools that read them, and the typed related_datasets predicates are used correctly (is_new_version_of for prior releases of the same collection, references for the distinct U2OS cell map).

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: All seven scoring fields are unpopulated: preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, imputation_protocols, missing_data_documentation. Tool documentation exists only outside them — external_resources gives the three repository URLs above, and notes describes 'the Multi-Scale Integrated Cell (MuSIC) pipeline, which integrates protein-protein interaction and immunofluorescence image data by node2vec and Human Protein Atlas deep learning embeddings, contrastive co-embedding, and multi-resolution community detection, and which annotates resulting assemblies by alignment to Gene Ontology and Reactome and by a large language model naming approach'. No version number is given for any tool. Seven of the ten archives are labelled collection_type: processed_data. Named tools with resolvable repositories and documentation sites earn credit above the 0 band, but this falls short of 'at least one strategy or tool listed' in the sense the question intends, because the tooling that is described is not the tooling that produced these files. The MuSIC pipeline builds the computed cell maps, which known_limitations states are explicitly absent from this release. How the seven processed_data archives were derived from the raw acquisitions — search engines, databases, QC thresholds, guide calling, image processing — is nowhere documented. This is the record's largest substantive gap and it is a reproducibility gap, not a formatting one. The internal inconsistency is telling: the record labels seven archives processed_data, which asserts that processing occurred, while documenting none of it. No software versions appear anywhere, so even the tools that are named cannot be pinned to a state. Missing-data handling and annotation quality are likewise undocumented, which matters for the perturb-seq atlas in particular. Logged as a high-severity completeness issue.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods gives three entries with was_directly_observed: true, e.g. 'Genetic perturbation data acquired by single-cell CRISPR (CRISPRi) perturbation screens by cell type, using a CRISPR lentiviral library targeting chromatin factors with 6 guide RNAs per gene, in cell lines expressing inducible dCas9, read out with the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit.' collection_mechanisms adds channel-level imaging detail: 'DAPI for nuclei (blue), calreticulin antibody for endoplasmic reticulum (yellow), tubulin antibody for microtubules (red), and antibody against the protein of interest (green)'. data_collectors names the performing laboratories — 'Immunofluorescence imaging was performed in the Lundberg Lab at Stanford University', 'Size exclusion chromatography-mass spectrometry was performed in the Nevan Krogan laboratory at the University of California San Francisco' — plus four production institutions. raw_data_sources lists seven upstream sources with access_details. direct_collection and sampling_strategies document the cell-line sourcing (ATCC; HipSci KOLF2.1J). collection_timeframes is absent. Three of the four named field groups are documented at a level that would let a domain reader reconstruct the assay design: specific reagents, specific kits, specific antibody channels, guides per gene, and the named laboratory responsible for each modality. The missing element is the fourth: no collection_timeframes, so the period over which the acquisitions ran is unknown. Deposit and publication dates exist elsewhere but describe the record's lifecycle, not the data's collection window. Technical terminology is used correctly and consistently throughout — AP-MS, SEC-MS, ICC-IF, CRISPRi, dCas9, 10x 3'HT are each deployed in the right context and each maps to a matching instances entry with its Bridge2AI substrate term. Attribution of modalities to laboratories is consistent with the creators' affiliations (Lundberg at Stanford, Krogan at UCSF). The timeframe gap compounds the created_on problem noted in the temporal issue: with created_on inherited verbatim from an earlier release, there is no reliable statement anywhere of when this release's data were generated.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version: '2.0'; status: Beta. version_access.versions_available enumerates the full release lineage with identifiers — 'May 2024, March 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX, Version 1.4), June 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, Version 2.1), and October 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, Version 2.1)' — with latest_version_doi set. updates.frequency: 'Quarterly', update_details: 'regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis'. maintainers names four people with roles and working emails (Swathi Thaker snthaker@uab.edu, programme manager; Zhandos Sembay zsembay8@uab.edu, web support; Trey Ideker, point of contact; Justin Niestroy, depositor). retention_limit: 'Long term preservation in the University of Virginia Dataverse, supported by committed institutional funds.' distribution_dates records per-tranche release dates (Jun 17 2026 and Jul 15 2026). errata is absent. All four sustainability indicators the question enumerates are present and evidenced rather than gestured at: a persistent DOI, a long-term governance arrangement (Data Access Committee plus named stewardship roles), a domain-appropriate institutional repository, and an explicit institutional funding commitment for preservation. Versioning is equally complete — every predecessor release is named with its own DOI, the update cadence has a stated end point, and four maintainers are individually contactable. The absent errata field is the only shortfall and does not offset documentation this thorough; nothing suggests errata exist and are being withheld. One semantic defect does not reduce the score but is recorded: the declared version '2.0' is lower than the '2.1' recorded for both the June 2025 and October 2025 predecessors that this release supersedes, so the version strings do not order the series. This is almost certainly an artifact of per-deposit Dataverse numbering rather than an error of fact, and the record supplies DOIs and dates that do order the series correctly — but a consumer sorting on version alone would misread the lineage. Logged as a medium consistency issue. The repository choice is domain-appropriate and the preservation commitment is specific about its funding basis, which is rarer than the claim itself.

name: Associated Publications
text: A formal dataset citation is present and complete, identifying authors, title, DOI, publisher and version: 'Clark T; Parker J; Al Manir S; ... Ideker T, 2026, "Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)", https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'. Distinct additional references: doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 (CM4AI preprint, recorded as the Related Publication); doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734 (Nourreddine et al., perturbation cell atlas of human iPSCs, PMCID PMC11580897); doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3 (Schaffer et al., Nature 642, 222-231, 2025). Seven external_resources entries add cm4ai.org, MassIVE, Figshare, NDEx, the Cell Mapping Toolkit repository and docs, FAIRSCAPE and IMP. The 5-point condition is met with margin: three distinct DOI-identified publications plus seven external resources, and a formal citation that names the dataset by title and identifies both its authors and its publishing organization — not a bare DOI. Each reference is annotated with what it contains and how it relates to this release, so a reader can tell which publication describes the data and which merely overlaps in authorship. Reference DOIs validate by registrar: 10.1101 is bioRxiv for the two preprints, 10.1038 is Springer Nature for the journal article. The relationship typing is semantically precise — the CM4AI preprint is is_described_by, the iPSC atlas preprint is is_referenced_by, and the Nature U2OS paper is references with an explicit note that it concerns 'a separate multimodal cell map of U2OS osteosarcoma cells produced by overlapping investigators', which correctly prevents a reader from attributing that dataset to this release. That distinction is exactly the kind of over-claim this question can otherwise reward, and the record declines to make it.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: subpopulations.identification: 'Cell type and treatment condition. The release spans MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells under untreated, paclitaxel-treated, and vorinostat-treated conditions; undifferentiated (parental) KOLF2.1J iPSCs; and iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells (NPCs), neurons, and cardiomyocytes', with a distribution statement giving per-modality coverage. Nine subsets carry is_subpopulation: true and is_data_split: false. instances lists four typed measurement types. direct_collection records the only donor-level fact in the record: 'the KOLF2.1J iPSC line was derived from a healthy male Northern European donor and is available from the Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells Initiative (HipSci) resource', and MDA-MB-468 as ATCC-sourced. known_biases records that the data 'does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large'. at_risk_populations and missing_data_documentation are absent. Subgroup characterization is detailed and well structured, but the subgroups are biological (cell line, differentiation state, treatment arm) rather than human-demographic. Donor demographics amount to a single line — sex, health status and broad ancestry for one of the two lines, nothing for the other — and there are no inclusion/exclusion criteria because there was no participant selection. A 3 reflects general human-derived data whose population characterization is thin, while crediting the precise and internally consistent subgroup structure the record does provide. Scoring here must not penalize the record for lacking demographics it could not have: with no human participants, detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria would be semantically inappropriate. What is properly expected — provenance and representativeness of the human-derived material — is partly met. The record is candid that the sample is non-representative (sampling_strategies.is_representative: false with why_not_representative, echoed in known_biases), which is the honest statement for two cell lines. The gap is that donor characteristics for MDA-MB-468 are absent entirely and KOLF2.1J's are minimal, so a reuser assessing ancestry coverage for a model has almost nothing to work with.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: doi '10.18130/V3/HIGT4C' and id 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C'; page 'https://cm4ai.org/'; publisher 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/'; distribution_formats.access_urls 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/'; conforms_to_schema 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema'; external_resources 'https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline', 'https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/', 'https://fairscape.github.io', 'http://integrativemodeling.org'. Passes comfortably. A registered DOI, a project landing page, a repository publisher URL, a w3id schema URI and four resolvable tool/documentation URLs give several independent routes to the dataset and its context. All URLs are structurally well formed and point to plausible, well-known domains for this field; w3id.org is a persistence service and github.com/readthedocs are stable hosting for the named toolkit. Two minor notes that do not affect the pass: integrativemodeling.org is given as http rather than https, and the DOI's own Dataverse landing page is never given as a URL, with page instead pointing at the project portal.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: distribution_formats: format ZIP, media_type application/zip, access_urls 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/', notes 'All ten files in the release are distributed as ZIP archives via the University of Virginia Dataverse. Files above the 1.9 GB browser download limit are obtained through the Data Access API.' license_and_use_terms sets CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with no_commercial_use, implying open access without a DUA or login for the non-embargoed material. third_party_sharing.is_shared: true, with MassIVE and Figshare as alternative sources. raw_data_sources marks two perturb-seq sources 'Embargoed'. No download_url field. The access path is largely defined: the hosting platform is named, the retrieval mechanism is specified, and the record anticipates the practical obstacle a reuser will actually hit — the 1.9 GB browser limit that affects the three multi-gigabyte image archives — and gives the API workaround. Access policy follows unambiguously from an open CC license with no registration requirement stated. Full marks are withheld because the API endpoint is a bare stem with no file identifiers, and because the embargoed subsets are flagged without any route to request them. Consistency between license and access holds: an open reuse license is matched by an open retrieval mechanism with no DUA, which is the coherent pairing. The practical shortfall is that the documented path stops one step short of retrieval — a consumer following 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/' without a file ID reaches nothing, and the record supplies file names and MD5s but never the Dataverse file identifiers that would complete the URL. Naming MassIVE and Figshare as alternative sources without accessions has the same shape: an access route stated but not made actionable.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms sets out CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 operatively, including the attribution, non-commercial and share-alike conditions, the no-further-restrictions clause and a requirement to cite both the related publication and the data collection. intended_uses gives four use_category entries with examples ('AI-ready data for functional genomics research', 'AI model training', 'Cellular process analysis', 'Analysis of cell architecture under perturbation'). prohibited_uses gives two entries with reasons: clinical decision-making and patient care 'without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval', and commercial use, tied to both the NC clause and the separate-negotiation requirement. known_limitations adds four scoped caveats including the absence of computed cell maps and the need for domain expertise. discouraged_uses and future_use_impacts are both absent. License plus use guidance is met well beyond the 3-point band — prohibitions carry reasons rather than bare assertions, intended uses are categorized with examples, and the limitations section tells a reuser what the release cannot support. The fifth point requires social impact analysis with mitigation strategies, and that is absent: future_use_impacts is empty, so no downstream risk is identified and no mitigation proposed. The nearest thing to impact analysis sits in fields belonging to other questions — data_governance describes an Ethics team plan for 'ethical preparation, licensing, dissemination, and Data Access supervision' and a 'CM4AI Life Cycle' governance framework, and ethical_reviews describes a Value-Sensitive Design methodology. These are governance processes for producing the data, not an analysis of the societal risks of reusing it, so they do not substitute. The clinical-use prohibition is the one place where a downstream harm is named, and it is correctly reasoned from the absence of regulatory approval for laboratory data.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: version_access lists the full predecessor lineage with DOIs and latest_version_doi. updates gives a quarterly cadence through November 2026. raw_data_sources enumerates seven upstream sources with type and access_details, mapping each released modality to its origin repository (MassIVE, Figshare) or embargo state. related_datasets supplies typed lineage (three is_new_version_of links, is_described_by, is_referenced_by, references). subsets record is_data_split: false explicitly for all nine entries, and each subset names the file_collection that distributes it while each file_collection names the subset it contains. Every file_collection carries an MD5 checksum. conforms_to describes FAIRSCAPE RO-Crate packaging with 'provenance graphs and rich metadata', and notes describes ARK identifiers with 'provenance entailments expressed in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology'. Absent: errata, was_derived_from, parent_datasets, missing_data_documentation, splits. This goes well past 'version history only'. Derivation is documented in two directions — upstream to the raw acquisitions and their repositories, and laterally to predecessor releases through typed relations — and file-level MD5 fixity gives integrity checking that most records omit entirely. The elements of an entity-activity-agent structure are all present but scattered across fields: entities in subsets and file_collections, activities in acquisition_methods, agents in data_collectors and creators. Full marks require a provenance graph with those relationships expressed as such, and this record describes one rather than containing one: the RO-Crate and EVI Evidence Graph claims are narrative, carried from the preprint and earlier releases, and the record itself concedes that the June 2026 release page does not restate the packaging format. The explicit subset↔file_collection ID linkage is a genuine in-record graph fragment and is why this sits at 4 rather than 3. Quality documentation is the weaker half: missing_data_documentation is empty and no QC metrics are reported for any modality, so integrity is well evidenced at the byte level and unevidenced at the measurement level.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases contains exactly one entry: bias_type 'representation_bias', bias_description 'Data in this release was derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large.' future_use_impacts is absent. Related but separately located material: sampling_strategies records is_random: false, is_representative: false and why_not_representative repeating the same sentence, plus 'Targeted selection of cell lines and perturbation targets rather than random sampling'; known_limitations records that 'Protein-protein interaction (SEC-MS), protein localization (IF imaging), and CRISPRi perturb-seq data interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap.' The single bias is correctly identified, correctly typed against a taxonomy enum value, and explained in terms a modeller can act on. But one entry is thin coverage for a multi-modal release, there is no fairness analysis of any kind, no AIO mapping, and no statement of downstream impact. This sits at the 3-point 'basic bias identification' band, lifted to the top of that band by the correct use of a taxonomy term rather than free text. The record documents two further biases without categorizing them, which is the substantive shortfall. Its own sampling_strategies field describes non-random targeted selection of cell lines and perturbation targets — a textbook selection bias — and known_limitations describes incompletely overlapping protein coverage across the three modalities, which will systematically bias any integrative model toward the intersection. Both are stated as facts elsewhere and omitted from known_biases, so a consumer reading the bias field alone receives an incomplete picture. Logged as a medium consistency issue.

name: Field Completeness
text: Populated: id 'doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; title 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description (~1,100 chars); keywords (4); license_and_use_terms.license_terms (Registered Access License, credentialing, DUA, fee statement) with data_use_permission 'general_research_use'; doi '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; page 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; creators (16 entries, all with affiliations, one with PI block and email); purposes (3); instances (2 types, counts 833); resources (11 named file resources nested under file_collections[0].resources, each with id, file_type and description); variables (4: participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames with data_type and is_identifier); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted'. Absent: parent_datasets (derivation instead carried by was_derived_from and related_datasets derives_from 'syn72370534'). 13 of 14 named fields are populated (~93%) and the content is substantive rather than placeholder: creators carry institutional affiliations individually, variables carry types and identifier flags, and the license field describes an actual access procedure rather than naming a license. Only parent_datasets is unpopulated. Field values are semantically appropriate to their slots: id and doi agree; page resolves to the version-specific PhysioNet landing page matching version '3.1.0'; confidentiality_level 'restricted' is consistent with a registered-access license rather than overstated. The missing parent_datasets is a placement issue, not missing information, since the parent is named in two other fields.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description runs approximately 1,100 characters and is specific: '833 adult participants recruited at five North American sites', an enumeration of the four condition families, the collection modality ('standardized protocol of acoustic tasks on a tablet application, with a headset where possible'), and an explicit statement of what is and is not distributed ('spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, pitch and periodicity traces, Speech Articulatory Coding articulatory estimates, phonetic posteriorgrams, openSMILE, Praat and parselmouth static features ... rather than the original waveforms'). purposes has three responses averaging roughly 200 characters each. Both narrative fields are far above the >200 character band, and length here reflects information density rather than padding: the description alone supplies participant count, site count, cohort structure, instrument, and release scope. The description's claims are corroborated elsewhere in the record rather than free-standing: 833 matches instances.counts, the feature list matches the eleven enumerated resources, and the waveform exclusion matches is_deidentified.deidentification_details and known_limitations.scope_limitation. Length is therefore backed by verifiable content.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: keywords: ['health', 'biomarkers', 'bridge2ai', 'voice'] — four unique terms. Supplementary topical coverage exists outside the keywords field: instances carry ontology CURIEs B2AI_TOPIC:25, B2AI_TOPIC:36, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30, and the phenotype file_collection description enumerates roughly eighteen conditions (airway stenosis, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, anxiety, benign lesions, bipolar disorder, cognitive impairment, COPD and asthma, depression, glottic insufficiency, laryngeal cancer, laryngeal dystonia, laryngitis, muscle tension dysphonia, Parkinson's disease, precancerous lesions, unexplained chronic cough, unilateral vocal fold paralysis) plus thirteen named instruments. Four keywords sits at the low end of the 3-7 band and the terms are broad; none names a condition, a modality beyond 'voice', or a method. The rubric's note permitting supplementation by condition lists and ontology references was applied, but the supplementary condition terms appear inside a prose folder description rather than as indexable metadata, and the ontology references amount to two coded topic terms, so the supplementation does not reach the >=8 threshold. The keywords are individually accurate and none is misleading, but as a discovery surface they under-describe the record: a researcher searching for 'dysphonia', 'Parkinson', 'speech', 'acoustic features' or 'machine learning' would not retrieve this dataset on keywords alone, despite all of those being central to its content as documented elsewhere in the same record. This is an indexing gap rather than a correctness defect.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats lists three: TSV (media_type 'text/tab-separated-values'), JSON (media_type 'application/json'), Parquet (no media type, with the note 'No IANA media type for Parquet is stated by the sources, so none is recorded'), each with access_urls. file_collections enumerates three collections (features, phenotype, metadata) and eleven individually named resources with dimensions and record counts, e.g. 'torchaudio_spectrogram.parquet ... Spectrograms of dimension 201 by T ... 29,278 records'; 'sparc_ema.parquet ... dimension T by 12 ... 28,640 records'; 'static_features.tsv'; 'audio_quality_metrics.tsv'. total_file_count is absent. Exactly three distinct formats places the count in the 2-3 band. The score is lifted one point because the question also weighs file enumeration, and the enumeration here is exceptional: every dense feature file is named, dimensioned and counted, and every data file is documented as paired with a JSON data dictionary. It does not reach 5 because there is no fourth format and no total_file_count. Format choice is semantically coherent with content type: Parquet for dense variable-length tensors, TSV for per-recording scalar tables and phenotype data, JSON for data dictionaries. The refusal to invent a media type for Parquet is correct behaviour rather than an omission. The three formats reflect a single-modality feature release, consistent with known_limitations.integration_limitation stating that imaging, genomic and spirometry data are not part of this release, so low format variety is an accurate signal about scope rather than a documentation failure.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: instances[0].counts: 833. instances[1].notes gives per-feature record counts: 'torchaudio pitch 32,522; sparc periodicity and sparc pitch 31,872 each; sparc loudness 31,855; phonetic posteriorgrams 29,289; spectrogram, Mel spectrogram and MFCC 29,278 each; sparc EMA 28,640'. Each file resource repeats its own count. subpopulations and splits are present (splits: 'No recommended train, validation or test splits are predefined'). total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes are both absent. Passes on instance and record counts, which are numerous and file-specific. Byte sizes are entirely absent, so the criterion is met by the count route only. Counts are internally consistent across three places (instances.notes, individual resource descriptions, and the description's scope statement), and the record explains why counts differ between features rather than leaving the discrepancy unexplained: 'representations derived from sensitive records and audio checks were withheld, and ... some files could not generate certain features'. It also declines to compute a total the sources do not state. As the rubric notes, sample size supports only an estimate of file size, so download planning remains approximate.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66; page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; publisher: https://physionet.org/; citation carries RRID:SCR_007345. Sibling and predecessor DOIs are also given (10.13026/k81f-qr68, 10.13026/h995-bt35, 10.13026/249v-w155, 10.57764/qb6h-em84). Passes comfortably: a DOI, an RRID, a version-specific landing page and a named hosting platform are all present, exceeding the single-identifier threshold. The 10.13026 prefix is PhysioNet's actual DataCite prefix and matches the named publisher, so identifier and platform corroborate one another rather than merely coexisting. RRID:SCR_007345 matches the RRID:SCR_ pattern. One defect is noted against Q13 rather than here, since it concerns version pointing rather than identification of this record: version_access.latest_version_doi names 10.13026/37yb-1t42, which is not this DOI and appears nowhere else.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders[0].grantor: 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund, Bridge2AI Program' with two grants: '3OT2OD032720-01S1' (the acknowledgement in the PhysioNet release) and 'OT2OD032720' (the RePORTER core project, 'held at the University of South Florida with Yael Emilie Bensoussan as principal investigator, running from 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 with a fiscal year 2025 award amount of 4,660,942 US dollars'). All 16 creators carry affiliations (USF, Weill Cornell, Vanderbilt, SickKids, WashU, OHSU, Simon Fraser, The Hastings Center, MIT, Toronto, Sinai Health, University of Florida); the consortium entry carries a principal_investigator block with name, email and department-level affiliation. maintainers separately names NIH support under OT2OD032720. Meets the 5 band fully and then exceeds it: grant numbers are accompanied by award period, host institution, PI and dollar amount, and every creator carries an institutional affiliation rather than a bare name list. Both grant strings parse correctly against NIH conventions (activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032720; the type-3 prefix and -01S1 suffix denote a supplement to support year 01), and the award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 brackets the 2026-05-01 issue date consistently. Where sources disagree the record says so rather than choosing silently: funders.source_caveats records that RePORTER lists application -01S3 while PhysioNet acknowledges -01S1, and the top-level caveat identifies two further transcriptions ('3Tf-OTOD03272001S2', '3TF-OT2ActfOD032720Projectf01S1') as corrupted. Recording an unresolved identifier conflict explicitly is stronger evidence practice than presenting one variant as settled, and no score reduction is warranted.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: USF IRB, with subsite IRBs through the Single IRB process and Canadian institutions applying to their own REBs. human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects true, irb_approval, ethics_review_board, regulatory_compliance (HIPAA de-identification, Certificate of Confidentiality assertable against subpoenas, no DMC, not a drug/device study), special_populations (adults 18-120; assent option; cohorts including mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's and other dementias). is_deidentified: method 'HIPAA Safe Harbor, supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers ... and by withholding of all raw audio', a full identifiers_removed enumeration, and deidentification_details ending 'K-anonymization with k of two or more is not achieved'. participant_privacy: anonymization_method, four privacy_techniques, reidentification_risk, data_linkage. informed_consent: consent_obtained true, three consent modalities, documentation retained five years, consent_scope, withdrawal_mechanism; plus collection_consents, consent_revocations, collection_notifications. participant_compensation: gift cards, '40 US dollars ... 80 US dollars ... maximum compensation of 120 US dollars', adults only. at_risk_populations: three special_protections and assent_procedures. regulatory_restrictions: hipaa_compliant 'compliant', other_compliance, and a governance contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org via data_governance. data_protection_impacts: 'no analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted'. Every ethics field in the rubric's list is populated, most with operational specificity (dollar amounts, retention periods, breach-reporting windows, named board). The score stops at 4 because the 5 band requires DPIA alongside the other protections, and the record states plainly that no impact analysis on data subjects was performed. The honest negative answer is better documentation than an empty field, but it does not supply the protection the band asks for. Consistency logic passes throughout: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by populated ethical_reviews and informed_consent; is_deidentified is matched by a stated method and by participant_privacy protections; sensitive_elements flagging voice as a biometric is matched by the raw-audio withholding and the separate controlled-access tier. The de-identification method is appropriate to the data type, and unusually the record states where it fails (k-anonymity not achieved; voice 'cannot be fully de-identified'), which is what makes the residual-risk claim credible. One content-accuracy tension is logged separately: hipaa_compliant='compliant' sits against the record's own quotation of the DTUA describing the data as 'not covered under HIPAA, FERPA, or similar laws'. Because the record discloses rather than conceals the conflict, it is treated as a flagged inconsistency and is reflected in the Q9 and Q8 reasoning without a further deduction here.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license_and_use_terms.license_terms sets out the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, the requirement to sign the Registered Access Agreement, the PhysioNet policy from version 3.0.0 that 'only credentialed users who sign the data use agreement can access the files; no additional training is required', the separate raw-audio regime (Data Access Request Form, DUA, DACO review, DTUA signed by an authorized institutional official), permitted duplication, prohibited sale, and 'There are no fees associated with these restrictions'; data_use_permission 'general_research_use'. ip_restrictions gives four clauses covering non-transfer of IP, non-blocking of downstream access, downstream IP with Fort Lauderdale Agreement obligations, and absence of third-party restrictions. regulatory_restrictions: export controls ('No export controls apply'), confidentiality_level 'restricted', hipaa_compliant 'compliant', other_compliance (HIPAA de-identification, Certificate of Confidentiality, safeguards, authorized-persons restriction, 'report any unauthorized use or disclosure to the provider within five business days'). data_governance names the Data Access Compliance Office, the accountable organization 'University of South Florida Board of Trustees', a step-by-step access_review_process, five stewardship_roles, and the contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org. All four components of the 5 band are present and operational rather than nominal: the confidentiality classification is a coded value, the governance contact is an actual address, and the access process names each document and its signatory. Multi-jurisdiction coverage is evidenced by US federal (HIPAA, Certificate of Confidentiality, OMB M-07-16) and Canadian REB routes. Restrictiveness is proportionate to sensitivity and is consistent across fields: confidentiality_level 'restricted' matches a registered-access licence, and the escalation to committee review for raw audio matches sensitive_elements identifying voice as biometric. The ip_restrictions clauses are semantically consistent with prohibited_uses, which bars using IP protection to restrict access. The one flaw is the HIPAA characterisation conflict the record itself quotes; it is disclosed with both statements recorded, affects the interpretation of a single enum rather than the access path a user must follow, and is logged as a medium-severity content-accuracy issue rather than scored down here, since the question asks whether access and governance terms are clearly defined and they are.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: distribution_formats: TSV, JSON, Parquet, described as 'Apache Parquet, an open-source column-oriented data file format'. conforms_to_schema: 'https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema' with conforms_to_class 'Dataset'. Ontology terms: B2AI_TOPIC:25, B2AI_TOPIC:36, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30. related_datasets carries four typed relationships: is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68, derives_from syn72370534, references 10.13026/h995-bt35 (pediatric release), is_documented_by 10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926. external_resources names b2aiprep and SenseLab (Apache-2.0), the REDCap data dictionary (MIT, Zenodo-archived), the documentation source (MIT, Zenodo-archived), and 'Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker'. Integration keys: variables define participant_id and session_id as identifiers, file_collections states 'Each element carries participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames', and participant_privacy.data_linkage confirms linkage 'across sessions and across feature and phenotype files by a study participant identifier'. Every data file is paired with a JSON data dictionary 'sharing its file stem ... giving a description of each column, the question asked of the participant where applicable, and the data type'. conforms_to (data standard) and file_collections.compression are absent. Formats are open and appropriate, typed cross-platform relationships are present with resolvable identifiers, and integration capability is concretely documented through shared keys and column-level dictionaries. The score stops short of 5 because no data-level standard or ontology conformance is asserted for this release: conforms_to_schema points at the datasheet schema rather than the data, ontology use amounts to two coded topic terms, the FHIR profiles are cited as supporting material rather than as a conformance claim, and compression is unstated. The abstention from a standards claim is deliberate and correct, not an oversight: source_caveats records that the documentation asserts BIDS v1.9.0 conformance for a b2ai-voice-audio layout with 'dataset_description.json, phenotype and sub-<id>/ses-<id>/audio directories', while 'the PhysioNet 3.1.0 release described here has a features, metadata and phenotype layout and does not state conformance to any data standard, so no standard is asserted'. Declining to carry a claim across releases where the layout differs is the semantically accurate choice, and the record is scored on what this release documents. The per-file JSON dictionaries and stable participant/session keys mean machine ingestion is well supported in practice despite the absent formal standard.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
text: preprocessing_strategies (6) give exact parameters: 'converting to monaural and resampling to 16 kHz with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter'; 'short-time Fast Fourier Transform with a 25 ms window size, 10 ms hop length and a 400-point FFT, then downsampled by a factor of two'; '60 Mel bins'; sparc kinematics 'all gathered at 50 Hz'; ppgs 'at 100 Hz across 40 phoneme categories'; openSMILE, Parselmouth and Praat for prosodic measures; 'Transcriptions were generated using OpenAI's Whisper Large model'. cleaning_strategies give an audit protocol (missingness tables, distribution and outlier checks, schema validation of categorical responses, audio QC, silence and duration checks, produced-versus-intended speech checks) performed 'with the b2aiprep and SenseLab toolkits', plus the released audio_quality_metrics.tsv. labeling_strategies give clinician gold standards, annotations_per_item 1, annotator_demographics, data_annotation_protocol 'Per Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10 codes', and platform. machine_annotation_tools lists nine tools with descriptions and a tool_accuracy caveat: 'off-the-shelf models that have not been audited for correctness'. missing_data_documentation gives patterns, causes and handling_strategy. Versions: only 'b2aiprep ... version 3.0.0 generated this release'. imputation_protocols and annotation_analyses are absent. Strategy documentation is comprehensive and parameterised well beyond the 3 band, and repository URLs with licences are supplied for the pipeline code. Two elements of the 5 band are missing: versions for eight of nine tools (openSMILE, Praat, parselmouth, torchaudio, sparc, ppgs, SenseLab unversioned; Whisper given only as 'Large'), and any imputation protocol. Annotation quality is partially covered by annotations_per_item and the accuracy caveat but there is no annotation_analyses entry such as inter-rater agreement. Tools are correctly matched to the outputs they produce and the mapping is verifiable against the file names (torchaudio_* for spectral and pitch features, sparc_* for articulatory and source measures, ppgs for posteriorgrams, openSMILE/Praat/parselmouth for static features), so the pipeline description is coherent rather than a generic tool list. The stated parameters are internally consistent: a 25 ms window at 16 kHz with a 400-point FFT yields the 201-bin spectrogram dimension given in the resource description. The missing versions matter substantively rather than formally, since feature extractors change output across releases; annotations_per_item=1 is also a genuine limitation the record does not hide, as single-annotator labels admit no agreement statistics.

name: Collection Protocol Clarity
text: acquisition_methods (2) with provenance flags: a standardized session where 'diagnoses were confirmed by clinicians reviewing audio and/or imaging data, electronic health records, or medication prescriptions' (was_directly_observed, was_reported_by_subjects, was_validated_verified all true), and a derived-features entry (was_inferred_derived true). collection_mechanisms names the custom tablet application and the exact hardware: 'iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) with an Avid AE-36 microphone connected through an Apple dongle; distinct iPad devices were used at each site', plus REDCap for instruments. data_collectors (3 roles) distinguish research teams ('data was collected in the clinic with the assistance of a trained research assistant'), clinicians ('listed under the IRB as co-investigators ... provided the clinical diagnoses used as gold standard labels') and hospital staff. collection_timeframes: 'data was collected over a period of 12 months', with a caveat that no start or end dates are stated. raw_data_sources (2) give source_type, raw_data_format (WAV audio; REDCap export) and access_details including the Synapse location and DACO contact. Supported by sampling_strategies, direct_collection and collection_consents. All three named components of the 5 band are present, and methods and collectors are documented at a level well above typical: named microphone model, per-site device distinction, role-differentiated collector responsibilities, and a screening step against 'per-diagnosis inclusion and exclusion criteria before the clinic visit'. The timeframe is the weakest element and is scored as adequate rather than perfect, but the overall protocol description is complete enough to reconstruct the collection. The acquisition provenance flags are used correctly and discriminatingly: observed/reported/validated for the session, inferred/derived for the computed features, which is exactly the distinction the schema encodes. The per-site device detail is not incidental; the record itself draws the inference through to known_biases.measurement_bias, noting that distinct iPads per site confound label with apparatus. The timeframe is the one soft point, carrying an explicit warning that the 12-month figure comes from a healthsheet written against an earlier release and 'may not cover the whole of the collection behind version 3.1.0'; this is logged as a low-severity temporal warning rather than scored down, since the caveat prevents a reader from over-relying on it.

name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
text: version '3.1.0'. version_access.versions_available lists five releases with dates and, for three of them, DOIs ('1.1 - 17 January 2025 - doi:10.13026/249v-w155'; '2.0.0 - 16 April 2025'; '2.0.1 - 18 August 2025'; '3.0.0 - 16 December 2025 - doi:10.13026/k81f-qr68'; '3.1.0 - 1 May 2026 - doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66'), with version_details noting that older versions remain supported by default, that 'The files for version 1.1 are no longer available from PhysioNet', and that version 1.0 sits on Health Data Nexus under doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84. errata records per-version corrections (v2.0 spectrogram reprocessing and free-speech removals; v2.0.1 authorship correction; v3.1.0 broken parquet fixes, back-filled diagnoses, renamed gold standard variables). updates states a semi-annual plan, explicitly labelled 'a plan written against the Health Data Nexus platform and an earlier release, not an observed cadence'. maintainers names PhysioNet/MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology, NIH support under OT2OD032720, and the consortium with the DACO contact. distribution_dates repeats the release sequence; retention_limit states indefinite retention for the published dataset. Defect: version_access.latest_version_doi is 'doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42'. Sustainability is documented on all four indicators the rubric names: persistent identifiers per version, a governance plan through DACO and the accountable institution, a domain-appropriate biomedical repository (PhysioNet), and institutional commitment via MIT LCP hosting plus NIH award support. Versioning is otherwise comprehensive. One point is deducted for the latest_version_doi defect, which is a functional error in exactly the field a consumer uses to find the current release, compounded by two listed versions lacking DOIs. Temporal ordering across the record is coherent: the release sequence Nov 2024 -> Jan 2025 -> Apr 2025 -> Aug 2025 -> Dec 2025 -> May 2026 is monotonic, the issued date 2026-05-01 matches the 3.1.0 entry, and the award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 encloses all of it. Against that, latest_version_doi 10.13026/37yb-1t42 is unresolvable from within the record: it matches no entry in versions_available, is not the top-level doi, and is not the 3.0.0 or pediatric DOI. The prefix is well formed and PhysioNet-registered, so this is a pointing error rather than a format error, but it contradicts the record's own statement that 3.1.0 is the latest version and is the single clearest internal inconsistency in the datasheet. The candour elsewhere is notable in the opposite direction: stating that v1.1 files are no longer retrievable is an admission against interest that improves the sustainability picture's reliability.

name: Associated Publications
text: citation is a formal dataset citation identifying the dataset by title, authors and publisher: 'Bensoussan, Y., Sigaras, A., Rameau, A., Elemento, O., ... Ghosh, S. (2026). Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66'. Distinct additional references: the Interspeech 2024 protocol-development paper (external_resources, with URL https://www.isca-archive.org/interspeech_2024/bensoussan24_interspeech.html, and independently in related_datasets as is_documented_by 10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926); the b2aiprep and SenseLab repositories; the REDCap data dictionary archived at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12760724; the documentation source archived at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653; the Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles. Well past the 5 threshold: a formal dataset citation is present and there are at least five distinct further references, four of them DOI-linked. The Interspeech paper appearing in both external_resources and related_datasets is counted once. Each DOI prefix matches its registrar: 10.13026 PhysioNet, 10.5281 Zenodo, 10.21437 ISCA. The citation's author order is consistent with creators (Bensoussan first, Ghosh described in creators as 'senior author of the version 3.1.0 release' and appearing last), and the version in the citation matches the version field. Placing the RRID inside the citation string is conventional for PhysioNet deposits. The record notes that the project documentation calls the dataset 'self-contained' and gives no guarantees about external resources, then supplies the supporting references anyway with that qualification attached, which is the right handling.

name: Human Subject Representation
text: instances[0]: instance_type 'human participant', counts 833, label true with a label_description explaining clinician-assigned diagnosis and the EHR/prescription route for the psychiatric cohort, and two missing_information entries. subpopulations: subpopulation_elements_present true; identification 'Age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status are recorded, and participants are assigned to disease cohort categories - voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders - or to the control group'; distribution 'The public data releases do not contain an equal distribution of the disease categories, and the dataset has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors'. at_risk_populations: adults only, 'minimum age is 18 years and the maximum age is 120 years', assent_procedures, and cohort-specific distress risks. missing_data_documentation gives patterns, causes and handling. Eligibility constraints appear in known_limitations.coverage_limitation ('eligibility required the ability to read and speak English') and sampling_strategies ('screened against per-diagnosis inclusion and exclusion criteria'). splits records that no splits are predefined. Well above the 3 band: subgroups are named, the demographic axes collected are enumerated, vulnerable-population handling is described and skew is acknowledged. It falls short of 5 because no numbers accompany any of it - no age or sex distribution, no race or ethnicity breakdown, no per-cohort participant counts - and the per-diagnosis inclusion and exclusion criteria are referenced rather than listed. The record is consistent in scoping itself to adults: the 18-120 range, the adults-only compensation note, and the routing of pediatric participants to the separate release identified as 10.13026/h995-bt35 all agree, so the 833 count is unambiguously the adult cohort. The absence of distribution figures interacts with Q20: the record documents representation bias qualitatively and tells users to 'consider the multivariate distribution', but supplies no distribution to consider, so a fairness audit cannot be performed from the datasheet alone. This is a real limitation on reuse rather than a presentational one, and is the basis for withholding the fifth point here and in Q20.

name: Findability (Persistent Links)
text: page 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/' (repeated as access_urls on all three distribution formats); doi 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; id doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66; publisher https://physionet.org/; external URLs to github.com/sensein/b2aiprep, github.com/sensein/senselab, github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap, github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-docs, zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12760724, zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653, www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/, docs.b2ai-voice.org, isca-archive.org, w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema. Passes decisively. Findability rests on several independent, resolvable, version-specific handles rather than a single link. All URLs are structurally well formed with plausible, verifiable domains, and the landing page is version-pinned so it will continue to denote 3.1.0 after later releases. Zenodo URLs use the concept-DOI form (zenodo.org/doi/...), which resolves to the latest archived version of each repository - appropriate for code archives. The Synapse accession is given as an identifier with an explanation that no DOI exists for it, rather than a DOI being invented.

name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
text: Each distribution_formats entry carries access_urls 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'. license_and_use_terms states the tier explicitly: 'From version 3.0.0 the PhysioNet access policy is that only credentialed users who sign the data use agreement can access the files; no additional training is required', with 'no fees'. The second tier is separated cleanly: 'Raw audio is governed separately, requiring a Data Access Request Form, a Data Use Agreement, review by the Data Access Compliance Office and a Data Use and Transfer Agreement signed by an authorized official at the recipient institution.' data_governance.access_review_process walks the whole path for both tiers and notes 'The agreement takes effect only upon review and approval by the Data Access Compliance Office, which requires a distinct application', with requests to DACO@b2ai-voice.org and audio served through Synapse. raw_data_sources repeats the Synapse URL and contact. A separate download_url field is not used. Meets the 5 band without reservation. A prospective user can determine which artifact they need, which tier governs it, which documents they must sign, who reviews the application, where to write, and that no fee applies - all from this record. The record avoids the misleading 'public/open' framing the rubric warns against: it is explicit that registered access still requires credentialing and a signed agreement, and it does not describe the release as open. Tier assignment is semantically coherent with sensitivity, escalating from credentialed registration for derived features to committee review for the biometric raw audio, and matches confidentiality_level 'restricted'. The absence of a bare download_url is correct rather than a gap, since no unauthenticated download exists and publishing one would misrepresent the access model.

name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
text: license_and_use_terms as quoted at Q9 and Q17. intended_uses (2): research use for 'the development of AI and machine-learning models for healthcare' with examples ['AI model pretraining', 'fine-tuning', 'benchmarking', 'validation'], and the agreement scope 'solely for commercial and non-commercial research purposes by Authorized Researchers'. prohibited_uses (3) with reasons: re-identification attempts and 'any actions that could reasonably lead to re-identification'; uses causing 'harm or stigmatization to research participants, their families, communities or specific populations'; use of IP protection to restrict access to the data or conclusions. discouraged_uses (1): 'hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustments, or any form of surveillance that could lead to discrimination or harm'. future_use_impacts (2): distributional skew such that 'unexamined use could result in unfair treatment of individuals or groups', and non-research use producing 'discrimination or harm on the basis of health conditions or voice characteristics'. The licence and use-guidance half of the band is fully met and would support 5 on its own: intended, prohibited and discouraged uses are all populated, each with reasoning rather than bare assertion, and the commercial-use position is stated unambiguously. The social-impact half is thinner. future_use_impacts has two short entries whose mitigations are either advisory ('users should consider the multivariate distribution') or restated as contractual exclusion, and the record's own data_protection_impacts states that no analysis of impact on data subjects was conducted. 'Comprehensive social impact analysis with mitigation strategies' is therefore not demonstrated. Use guidance is internally consistent and enforceable-looking: the prohibition on re-identification matches the reidentification_risk analysis and the contractual bar on contacting subjects, and the discouraged surveillance and insurance uses are echoed in future_use_impacts as the reason those applications are excluded by the agreement, so the two fields reinforce rather than duplicate. One tension is that consent_scope records the consent does not restrict commercial use while intended_uses permits commercial research - these agree, which is worth noting as a passed check rather than a conflict. The impact gap is substantive: mitigation for the documented skew depends on users assessing a distribution the record does not publish, which is the same limitation identified at Q15 and Q20.

name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
text: was_derived_from: 'Raw audio recordings of standardized acoustic tasks captured by the Bridge2AI-Voice tablet application, together with questionnaire and clinical data captured in REDCap, collected under the Bridge2AI Voice Data Acquisition protocol.' Entities: raw_data_sources gives WAV audio (Synapse syn72370534, controlled access) and REDCap exports; file_collections names the eleven derived outputs. Activities: preprocessing_strategies give the ordered transformation chain (mono conversion and 16 kHz resampling with Butterworth filter -> STFT spectrogram at 25 ms/10 ms/400-point -> Mel and MFCC -> sparc articulatory estimates at 50 Hz -> ppgs at 100 Hz -> openSMILE/Praat/parselmouth static features -> Whisper transcription), with cleaning_strategies giving the audit activity. Agents: b2aiprep 'version 3.0.0 generated this release', SenseLab, the data release team, and clinicians as labelling agents. Derivation path: related_datasets derives_from syn72370534 and is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68; version_access, errata and updates give version lineage; missing_data_documentation gives patterns, causes and handling; splits records that none are predefined. Meets the 5 band on the textual route the rubric expressly permits. The lineage is complete in both directions: upstream to the named raw-audio and REDCap sources with their access regimes, and downstream to specific named output files, with the transforming software and its version identified for the orchestrating tool. Version-history elements (errata, updates, version_access) are present in addition to, not instead of, the derivation graph. The lineage can be traversed file by file rather than only in the abstract, which is what distinguishes it from version history alone: file names encode their producing tool (torchaudio_*, sparc_*, ppgs) and each corresponding preprocessing_strategies entry supplies that tool's parameters, so a reader can reconstruct which activity produced which entity. Quality is carried through the same graph: audio_quality_metrics.tsv is itself released as a derived entity, and the reasons some entities are absent are stated (sensitive-record and free-speech exclusions, generation failures). The absence of a machine-readable PROV-O serialisation and of a top-level parent_datasets entry are noted as issues but do not reduce the score, since the rubric accepts complete textual lineage and the derivation targets are given as resolvable identifiers.

name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
text: known_biases (3), each typed from the controlled vocabulary: selection_bias ('recruited at a small number of high volume expert clinics; groups that have less trust in the medical system or in AI, or who are less proximal to the collection sites, would have been less likely to be recruited') with mitigation_strategy; representation_bias ('skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors') with mitigation_strategy; measurement_bias ('participants with different labels also had their data collected on different devices, confounding label with recording apparatus and site') with affected_subsets. future_use_impacts adds fairness framing: 'unexamined use could result in unfair treatment of individuals or groups' and discrimination risk in hiring, insurance and surveillance. Reinforced by known_limitations (representativeness, coverage, scope, temporal, integration), anomalies (3), sampling_strategies.why_not_representative and subpopulations.distribution. Clearly beyond the 3 band: biases are categorised with BiasTypeEnum-style terms rather than described loosely, two of three carry mitigations and one identifies affected subsets. The fifth point is withheld because there are no AIO or CROISSANT RAI ontology mappings, and the fairness analysis is entirely qualitative - no subgroup performance or distribution statistics, and indeed no demographic distribution anywhere in the record against which fairness could be assessed. The bias types are applied correctly rather than as labels of convenience: the confounding of diagnostic label with site-specific iPad hardware is a genuine measurement bias and is a non-obvious finding that follows from the per-site device detail given in collection_mechanisms, so the taxonomy term and the evidence agree. Bias documentation is also consistent with sampling_strategies (is_representative false, with why_not_representative) and with known_limitations, so the record does not claim representativeness anywhere while conceding skew elsewhere. The weakness is circular in effect: representation_bias is documented and users are told to weigh the multivariate distribution, but because Q15's distribution figures are absent the recommended mitigation cannot actually be carried out from this datasheet.

name: Field Completeness
text: id: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; title: 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description ~1,900 chars; keywords: 4 terms; license_and_use_terms with data_use_permission: general_research_use; doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; page: https://b2ai-voice.org/; creators: 3 entries with PIs and 12 affiliations; purposes: 3 responses; instances: 3 instance types including counts: 833; variables: participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames; regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted. Twelve of the fourteen named slots are populated with substantive content. The two absent slots have populated equivalents: external_resources carries six sub-resources in place of `resources`, and parent lineage is carried by was_derived_from, raw_sources and related_datasets (derives_from syn72370534, is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68) in place of `parent_datasets`. Semantic coverage is therefore ≈93%. No field is populated with a placeholder. keywords is the one slot whose content, while present, is thin enough to be scored against separately at Q3; it is not counted as unpopulated here.

name: Entry Length Adequacy
text: description is a single block of roughly 1,900 characters naming the cohort (833 adults, five North American sites), the four adult disorder categories, the derived-feature inventory (spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, SPARC articulatory and source measures, PPGs, pitch contours, openSMILE/Praat/parselmouth statics), the phenotype directory contents, the recording setup and the credentialed access model. purposes holds three responses of roughly 190, 230 and 220 characters. Well past the >200 character band on both fields, and the length is carrying information rather than padding: the description alone answers what, who, how many, how collected, what is withheld and how to get it. Narrative content matches the claimed dataset type throughout; terms such as Mel-frequency cepstral coefficient, phonetic posteriorgram and electromagnetic articulography are used in their standard senses and at consistent sampling rates.

name: Keyword Diversity
text: keywords: health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice — four unique terms. Four keywords places this squarely in the 3–7 band. The terms are accurate but generic; three of the four would apply to any Bridge2AI voice artefact, and none discriminates this release from the pediatric companion or from the raw-audio distribution. The rubric permits supplementing keywords with schema-defined condition lists or ontology references. Conditions are in fact enumerated, but only inside file_collections.phenotype prose and instances CURIEs (B2AI_TOPIC:36/37, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30/80), not as retrievable keywords, and no ICD-10 or SNOMED CURIEs are exposed despite labeling_strategies stating that labeling followed ICD-10 codes. The supplement therefore does not lift the score above the counted band.

name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
text: distribution_formats: 'Parquet' and 'Tab-separated values with JSON data dictionaries', each with access_urls to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/. file_collections names nine Parquet feature files (ppgs, sparc_ema, sparc_loudness, sparc_periodicity, sparc_pitch, torchaudio_spectrogram, torchaudio_mfcc, torchaudio_pitch, torchaudio_mel_spectrogram), two TSV files (static_features.tsv, audio_quality_metrics.tsv), a Parquet metadata file, and a phenotype tree of tab-delimited tables each paired with a JSON dictionary. total_file_count absent. Three distinct types (Parquet, TSV, JSON) puts this in the 2–3 band. Enumeration quality is well above what the band implies — individual files are named and their contents described — but the count of types is what the question measures, and no media_type, encoding or compression is declared. The narrow format range is semantically appropriate rather than a defect: a feature-only release of dense tensors plus tabular phenotypes has no reason to carry DICOM, imaging or waveform containers, and the record explains that the waveforms ship elsewhere. Multimodality is achieved by shared participant_id/session_id keys across feature, metadata and phenotype tables, which the rubric's Q4 note treats as the integration signal.

name: Data File Size Availability
text: instances: counts: 833 participants; per-feature record counts '29,278 spectrogram, Mel spectrogram and MFCC records; 32,522 torchaudio pitch records; 28,640 articulatory records; 31,855 loudness records; 31,872 periodicity and Speech Articulatory Coding pitch records; and 29,289 phonetic posteriorgram records'; variables.n_frames documents per-recording time-frame counts; splits present (user-defined); subpopulations present. Passes on instance counts, which are given at both participant and recording granularity and per feature family. No byte figure exists anywhere (total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes both absent), so size is only estimable from record counts times frame counts times feature dimensionality — a weak proxy for nine dense Parquet tensors. Pass/fail cannot express that gap, so it is recorded as a completeness issue instead.

name: Dataset Identification Metadata
text: doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; id: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; page: https://b2ai-voice.org/; publisher: https://physionet.org/; citation carries RRID:SCR_007345; version_access.latest_version_doi and related_datasets carry the concept DOI 10.13026/37yb-1t42 and the predecessor 10.13026/k81f-qr68. Passes comfortably: a version DOI, a concept DOI, a resolvable landing page, a project page and a named domain repository are all present. Prefix 10.13026 is PhysioNet's and is consistent with publisher. Two defects noted elsewhere do not defeat the pass: latest_version_doi holds the concept rather than the 3.1.0 DOI, and RRID:SCR_007345 denotes PhysioNet rather than the dataset.

name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
text: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund, Bridge2AI Program' with grants 3OT2OD032720-01S1 and OT2OD032720, each annotated with its source, plus source_caveats reconciling PhysioNet, NIH RePORTER (3OT2OD032720-01S3, core OT2OD032720, FY2025 award 4,660,942, period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30), the feasibility publication and garbled documentation forms. creators: University of South Florida with PI Yael Bensoussan (USF Health Morsani College of Medicine), Weill Cornell Medicine with PI Olivier Elemento (Englander Institute for Precision Medicine), and the consortium with twelve named affiliations. maintainers additionally credit U24EB037545 and R01EB030362 for PhysioNet. Top band on both limbs: grant numbers are attached to a named grantor, and creators carry institutional affiliations down to department level for the two co-PIs. Both grant strings parse as NIH identifiers (OT2 activity code, OD institute, six-digit serial; 3…-01S1 as an application number with supplement suffix). The award-number divergence across sources is disclosed with a stated preference rule rather than concealed, which increases rather than reduces confidence. Funding purpose (Bridge2AI Common Fund, voice as a biomarker) aligns with the stated purposes and tasks.

name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
text: ethical_reviews: University of South Florida IRB with Single IRB subsite approvals. human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects true, ethics_review_board named, irb_approval narrative, regulatory_compliance (HIPAA, Certificate of Confidentiality, Single IRB), special_populations listing neurodegenerative and psychiatric cohorts. is_deidentified: HIPAA Safe Harbor plus indirect-identifier removal, an explicit eighteen-item identifiers_removed list, and deidentification_details ending 'k-anonymization with k of at least two was not achieved'. participant_privacy: anonymization_method, privacy_techniques (HIPAA firewall, password-protected REDCap, HTTPS to NIH STRIDES cloud, trained personnel), reidentification_risk ('a person's voice is unique to them'), data_linkage (EHR access under consent). participant_compensation: gift cards, $40/$80 per session, cap $120. informed_consent: written/electronic/video consent, five-year documentation retention, scope, withdrawal_mechanism. regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant: compliant; other_compliance: Certificate of Confidentiality, OMB M-07-16. Nine of the eleven protection areas are documented to a high standard, several beyond the usual depth (per-modality withholding rules, transcript review for external voices, consent re-administration for longitudinal visits). Two things hold it off the top band: no data_protection_impacts entry or equivalent DPIA, and an identifiability claim that the record's own other_compliance and k-anonymity statements contradict. Ethics claims are plausible against scope: credentialed access plus an RAA for low-risk derived features, escalating to DACO review and an institution-signed DTUA for the waveforms, is proportionate to voice's biometric character. The deidentification method suits the data type. Against that, identifiable_elements_present=false sits beside a DTUA designation of the data as PII and an admitted k<2, and sensitive_elements_present=true conflicts with the statement that REDCap-flagged sensitive fields were removed at 3.0.0. Both contradictions are partly caveated but neither is resolved for 3.1.0, and the deduction to 4 reflects them together with the missing DPIA. Canadian collection with no Canadian ethics or privacy instrument cited is recorded at Q9.

name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
text: license: 'Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License'; license_and_use_terms: data_use_permission general_research_use, credentialed PhysioNet access with signed Registered Access Agreement, no additional training, separate controlled-access path for raw audio (Data Access Request Form, DUA, DACO review, institution-signed DTUA), commercial and non-commercial research both permitted, per-organisation application required. ip_restrictions: five clauses covering copyright non-transfer, duplication-but-not-sale, no IP claims blocking access, downstream licensing under the Fort Lauderdale Agreement, and no third-party IP restrictions. regulatory_restrictions: confidentiality_level restricted, hipaa_compliant compliant, no export controls, credentialed-access restriction, other_compliance (Certificate of Confidentiality, OMB M-07-16, PhysioNet requirements). Governance contact DACO@b2ai-voice.org appears in maintainers. retention_limit gives both hosting and recipient obligations. Every limb of the question is addressed and the IP clauses are unusually specific. The top band in the rubric text additionally requires multi-jurisdiction compliance, and that limb is not met. Restrictiveness is internally coherent: a restricted classification, a signed RAA and a two-tier access model match the sensitivity of clinically labelled voice-derived data. Two semantic gaps reduce the score. First, collection occurred in the United States and Canada, yet only United States instruments are cited for the adult cohort. Second, the governance contact lives in maintainers rather than regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact, so a consumer reading the governance block alone finds no contact. The confidentiality_level value is the record's own inference, which it flags honestly.

name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
text: distribution_formats: Parquet ('an open-source column-oriented data file format', loadable by any Parquet library) and tab-delimited text with companion JSON data dictionaries whose 'keys match the column names of the table'. conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to omitted by explicit decision recorded in source_caveats. related_datasets: four typed relationships (is_supplemented_by 10.13026/h995-bt35, is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68, is_version_of 10.13026/37yb-1t42, derives_from syn72370534). external_resources: docs site, b2aiprep (Apache-2.0), senselab, bridge2ai-redcap (MIT), bridge2ai-docs (MIT), Synapse raw audio. Integration keys declared in variables (participant_id, session_id, task_name) and stated to be 'shared across the feature, metadata and phenotype tables'. Ontology CURIEs in instances (B2AI_TOPIC:36/37, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30/80); labels follow ICD-10. Formats are open and AI/ML-friendly, every table ships a machine-readable dictionary, cross-dataset links are typed and DOI-resolvable, and join keys with their cardinality are documented — which is what harmonisation actually requires. Short of the top band because no schema governs the released files themselves. conforms_to_schema names the datasheet metamodel, not a data schema, so the apparent schema conformance does not bear on the distributed artefacts; the BIDS 1.9.0 conversion is correctly scoped to the audio dataset's folder layout and deliberately not asserted here, which is semantically honest but leaves the gap open. file_collections.compression is absent for nine dense Parquet tensors. Ontology use is real but partial: B2AI CURIEs appear at instance level while the eighteen diagnosis tables and ICD-10 labels carry no codes in the record.

name: Tool and Software Transparency
